author: Binoy Kampark
title: Unmasked agendas: Macron, youth protests and blocking social media
content:
Finally, the ill-fitting mask on the ugly face of government policy comes off. In the sunset of his administration, French President Emmanuel Macron is facing a boiling, indignant movement that began with the protests of disgruntled students and has burgeoned into something much more significant.

Teachers at the Antoine de Saint-Exupéry High School in the southeastern Parisian suburb of Créteil went on strike over severe staff shortages, on September 17. Students and parents added themselves to the strike. The school entrance was blocked, videos taken and social media platforms used to disseminate the message.

A blooming followed through to October, drawing in some 3700 schools and hundreds and thousands of protesters. Social, economic and political angst had been stirred, with grievances focused on inadequate provision of teaching, packed classrooms, overburdened schedules and the dilapidation of school infrastructure. The university admissions platform Parcoursup also came in for criticism.

As part of the response to the protests, Macron has, as is traditional with a smug incumbent caught off guard, identified an aggravating, foreign influence steering matters. Conveniently for him, the fault seems to lie with the progenitors of the social media world, those United States Big Tech beasts and platforms that have turned users into anything from bovine consumers to adept, resourceful users of technology. It’s the resourceful aspect of the technology that is proving particularly troubling for government officialdom.

As one of the last acts of his administration, France’s desperate leader has attempted to impose age-restrictions on users of social media platforms ostensibly as a therapeutic exercise.

In doing so, he has joined a wide tent of invigilating governments keen to use the alleged malignancies of social media as an alibi for controlling access to certain online platforms, a mood captured by the efforts of the European Union to advance the all suppressing EU Kids Act. (Australia was the first to bolt out of the stables last December with its Online Safety Amendment (Social Media Minimum Age) Act 2024, paraded as a noble effort to limit the use of social platforms by those under 16 years of age. Unsurprisingly, it is showing itself to be a foolish legislative bauble, weak and circumvented.)

On July 21, the French parliament adopted the “Loi visant à protéger les mineurs face aux risques associés à l’usage des réseaux sociaux” (Law aiming to protect minors from the risks associated with social media usage), an alleged palliative for the ills (examples include anxiety, depression and sleep disorders) of using social media for those under 15. This exaggerated sense of moral success did not last long.

In August, France’s Constitutional Council poured cold water on the government’s grand strategy, striking down the legislation as needlessly broad and hopelessly excessive. The access to the platforms, for instance, was “not subject to any condition relating to the functionalities or content offered, the dangers they expose users, and the inadequacy of the safeguards with which they are provided.”

Saliently, the Council noted that the ban encumbered the rights of young people to access information and engage in the democratic system. This meant retarding the useful instruction of children to meaningfully engage the political process on ceasing to be minors. Social networking platforms were not inherently wicked things; they could also serve as educational tools, promote civic engagement and aid in building communities.

A chastened Macron proceeded to direct Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu to make the necessary adjustments in line with the Council’s decision.

The response from Macron to these youth-inspired protests, in light of his stuttering efforts against the corruptions of social media, is a more candid reflection on why governments seek to restrict any platform that adds vim to dissent and disagreement.

In remarks made to members of law enforcement during his October 26 visit to Marseille City Hall, the president scorned social media sites for “damaging our democracies” and being “tools for mobilising the worst impulses”. They had brought “young and not-so-young people to places where criminal acts, attacks and looting were taking place.”

This imprecise, misleading assessment proved most telling.

In the week leading up to October 24, recent reports reveal that the French interior ministry was putting …

author: April Holcombe
title: China’s forgotten miracle makers
content:
History has no parallel for modern China’s economic transformation. To what do we owe the China “miracle”, in which annual GDP growth averaged 9 percent over 40 years, wages up roughly tenfold in 30 years, and more high-speed rail built in ten years than the rest of the world in all time?

In the heyday of globalisation, people said China proved the magic of free markets and free trade. These days, people are more likely to attribute the country’s success to some special Chinese characteristic, such as its state-directed investment or its “Communist” dictatorship. 

These perspectives share in common a wilful or ignorant blindness to capitalism’s real wealth creators. Economic value comes neither from the market’s “invisible hand” nor the state’s “guiding hand”, but plain old everyday hands. The secret to China’s “miracle” is the not-so-miraculous condition of its working class.

Beginning in the 1990s, the greatest ever number of wage labourers was assembled through the collusion of profit-hungry foreign capital with millions of venal bureaucrats and their repressive state machine. Three hundred million people decamped from rural poverty to seek better lives in China’s cities, while urban compatriots in state-owned mines and mills lost their livelihoods through merciless privatisation.

China’s working class is legally stratified into “migrant” and “resident”, subject to the severest dictatorship of their bosses, and deprived of political rights to speak out or unionise. Apply hundreds of billions in Western and Taiwanese investments, lather, rinse, repeat for decades, and voilà! You have the most “miraculous” economic growth in capitalist history. 

China’s migrant workforce

We are used to hearing about how important migrants are to Western economies, but migration—the internal kind from village to city, not country-to-country—has been even more critical to China’s boom. In the 1990s, the government enticed young villagers with the prospect of independence, new experiences and better pay in newly established, deregulated Special Economic Zones with low wages and low taxes.

Lu Qingmin first left her family’s half-acre farm and came to Dongguan, a burgeoning megacity in the southern manufacturing heartland of the Pearl River Delta, in the early 2000s. Bosses preferred migrant women like her, considering them doubly docile. Writer Leslie Chang, in her 2008 book

Factory Girls

, described Lu’s experiences at her first job in a Hong Kong-owned alarm clock factory:

“A day on the assembly line stretched from eight in the morning until midnight—thirteen hours on the job plus two breaks for meals—and workers labored every day for weeks on end. From the moment she entered the factory she wanted to leave.”

The Pearl River Delta opened wide to investment in such sweatshops, and American-style hyper-individualism flowed in with it. Self-help books, life-coaching gurus, pyramid schemes, talent markets, unregulated colleges: each refracted through the false prism of empowerment what migrant workers already felt in their bones:

you are on your own

.

Hukou

: China’s internal visa system

Every migrant who left for the cities took the same thing with them: their rural

hukou

(户口), a residential registration that acts like an internal passport. Originally designed under Mao Zedong in 1958 to prohibit rural-to-urban movement altogether, the

hukou

household registration system was repurposed to create a pliant, defenceless workforce with second-class citizenship wherever it went.

Out-of-town

hukou

holders, also called the “floating population”, now represent just under half of the country’s workforce. Registered to villages far away, they are denied health insurance and pensions by the local government where they actually live. Many cities bar them from buying property, and local schools charge significant sums to teach their children. 

Think of them like the United States’ undocumented immigrants, who can get driver’s licences but not Social Security, who work in practically every key industry, but technically are not supposed to be there at all. Except there are now as many in China as the entire US population.

China does not offer the equivalent of America’s birthright citizenship: children inherit their parents’

hukou

author: Mat Ward
title: 10 new underrated protest albums that should be topping the charts
content:
Do you think there’s no good protest music these days? So did I, until I started looking for it. Every month, I listen to it all, then select the best that relates to that month’s political news. Here’s the round-up for October.

New South Wales' Labor government backed Queensland's ban on Palestine freedom slogans on October 1. The move came as Jewish US protest singer David Rovics released probably his catchiest album yet, containing songs "all about the US-Israeli Epstein Empire", before touring Australia. On album opener "The Holocaust Is Now", featuring backing vocals from Green Left writer Kamala Emanuel, he sings: "Can you spend two hundred dollars to buy a loaf of bread? Neither can the Palestinians, they’re dying instead." The LP was released while donkey prices in Gaza surged from $US1000 to $US30,000 "due to the virtual elimination of motorised private transport". As Israel's election loomed on October 28, the album's title track, "Rise", called for Israelis to rise up against Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who was being endorsed by US President Donald Trump as a "great warrior" who must be re-elected so they could "finish the job" in their disastrous war on Iran. "Overthrow your theocratic state, before it is too late," sings Rovics. "Reject your leaders and their lies. Rise, Israelis, rise!" LISTEN>>>

One of the seemingly few Israelis rising up is pop-rock musician Regev Baruch, with his scathing new album, Super Sparta. Its title is a phrase coined by Netanyahu last year to describe his commitment to eternal war. Discussing the LP, which likens Israelis to Nazis, Baruch said: “There’s this graffiti that says, ‘Grandma, what were you doing during the genocide?’ I was looking for a good answer to that — something I could do to prove I wasn’t part of the silent majority... In the end, I said, ‘OK, there are journalists; they’re investigating. There are lawyers; they’re fighting a legal battle. You’re a musician — just make music.’ That’s the most powerful thing I can do.” Of course, Baruch is far from the only Jewish person publicly condemning Israel's genocide against Palestinians, as shown by the countless Jews who attended vigils marking three years of the war on October 7. Meanwhile, pro-Palestine punks Amyl and the Sniffers, whose new live LP blasts fascistic leaders, said they were donating proceeds from an upcoming Bondi gig to "extend our love" to Jews affected by the Bondi attack. LISTEN>>>

English feminist rage musician Delilah Bon, who paints her body with slogans such as "Free Palestine", also released a new live album on October 16 as her Australian tour loomed. The LP documents a show she played to reach out to American fans after she had to cancel a US tour due to fears about the country's Immigration and Customs Enforcement agency. The event, which raised £8,000 for organisations supporting people affected by ICE, opens with the apt "Illegal Aliens" and powers through fan favourites such as "Dead Men Don't Rape", "War On Women" and "Princeless Princess". On the excoriating "Not The President", she sings: "That's not the president, that's just some man, who has abused so many women and children... There's so much love in this world, I'm holding hands with every girl that cries alone in her room, that fears this world is so fucking doomed." She then gets her British fans to chant "fuck Trump" for their peers in the US. The explosive power of her dayglo-daubed live show, in which she goes from pitch-perfect singing to razor-sharp rapping and searing screaming, is inspiring. LISTEN>>>

Also condemning ICE is the new LP from Grammy-winning folk musician Mary Gauthier, released days before an agent in New York shot into a car with a child inside. On "Soldier Of Fortune" she cites ICE victims Renée Good and Alex Pretti as she sings: "You're nothing but a gun for hire, hiding behind a mask. You didn't care if she was somebody's mother, when you shot her in the face through the window glass. A VA nurse on a city street, full of the courage you lack. An angel of mercy, helping a stranger and you fired 10 bullets into his back." That preceded the October 16 LP from Heavens To Betsy, the kind of riot grrrl pioneers who paved the way for the likes of Delilah Bon. The LP, a long-lost 1992 demo released to mark their reformation, centres on "My Secret" in which singer Corin Tucker blasts an abuser. "It turned the tables on everything, and it let go of everything, and it also freaked everyone out," …

author: Unknown
title: Emeklilerin üçte ikisi çalışmak zorunda, ileri yaşta iş cinayetleri tırmanıyor
content:
Andaç Aydın Arıduru [email protected]

Cumhurbaşkanı Erdoğan 26 Ekim tarihli kabine toplantısının ardından yaptığı açıklamada, “Sosyal adalet ilkemiz gereği, devletimizin şefkat elini ihtiyacı olan her bir vatandaşımıza ulaştırmak boynumuzun borcudur” ifadelerini kullandı. Erdoğan’ın açıklamalarının ardından AKP kanadından emekli maaşlarında “refah payı” veya “seyyanen zam” seçeneklerinin değerlendirildiği açıklamaları geldi. Milyonlarca emekli açlık sınırının altında, asgari ücretin gerisinde aylıklara mahkum. AKP’li yıllarda emekli olup çalışmaya devam etmek zorunda kalanların sayısı 4 kattan fazla arttı. Emekli aylığıyla geçim, ülkenin en yoksul kesiminin verdiği geçim mücadelesi haline geldi.

En düşük emekli aylığı 23 bin 552 TL seviyesinde. Her ay Türk-İş tarafından açıklanan ve 4 kişilik bir ailenin sadece beslenebilmek için gıda masraflarını içeren açlık sınırı Ekim ayında 38 bin 24 TL oldu. Emekli aylığı, açlık sınırının yüzde 38 altında kalıyor. Gıda ile birlikte diğer tüm temel harcamalar için haneye girmesi gereken toplam gelir tutarı olan yoksulluk sınırı ise 123 bin 856 TL. Emekli aylığı yoksulluk sınırının yüzde 81 altında kalıyor.

Zam senaryoları en düşük emekli aylığını dahi açlık sınırına ulaştırmıyor. Gündemdeki zam senaryolarına göre seçeneklerden biri tüm emekli aylıklarına seyyanen zam, diğeri ise enflasyon artışının üzerinde refah payı verilmesi. Sabah Gazetesi yazarı Faruk Erdem, emeklilere yönelik hazırlıkların detaylarını aktarırken ocak ayında refah payı artışının da gündemde olduğunu ileri sürdü. Haberde verilen örnek hesaba göre, 3 bin liralık seyyanen zam yapılırsa 23 bin 552 TL olan en düşük emekli aylığı 26 bin 552 TL'ye yükselecek. En düşük emekli maaşı (23 bin 552 TL) ocak ayında yüzde 10 zam yapılması durumunda aylık 25 bin 907 TL'ye yükselir. Yüzde 5 refah payı verilmesi durumunda emekli aylığı 27 bin 202 TL'ye, yüzde 20 refah payı verilmesi durumunda 31 bin 88 TL olabilir.

3 bin liralık seyyanen zam yapılsa bile en düşük emekli aylığı açlık sınırının yalnızca yüzde 69.8'ine ulaşacak. Yüzde 10 zamda bu oran yüzde 68.1, yüzde 5 refah payında yüzde 71.5, yüzde 20 refah payında ise yüzde 81.8 olacak. En yüksek senaryoda dahi emekli aylığı açlık sınırının 6 bin 936 TL altında kalacak. Yoksulluk sınırı karşısındaki tablo ise daha ağır: En yüksek, yani yüzde 20 refah payı senaryosunda bile aylık yoksulluk sınırının yalnızca yüzde 25.1'ine ulaşacak ve 92 bin 768 TL altında kalacak.

Emekli aylıklarının Gayrisafi Yurtiçi Hasıla (GSYH) karşısındaki kaybı da derinleşti. 2002’de ortalama emekli aylığının kişi başına milli gelire oranı yüzde 46.4 iken 2025’te yüzde 31.6’ya düştü. 2019’da ortalama emekli aylığı en düşük aylığın yüzde 91.7 üzerindeyken, bu fark 2025’te yüzde 18’e indi.

2025 yılı için 14 bin 469 TL olarak uygulanan taban aylık dikkate alındığında 14 bin 469 TL olan en düşük emekli aylığıyla geçinen bir hanenin yıllık geliri 173 bin 628 TL’de kaldı. Bu tutar, en yoksul yüzde 20’lik kesimin 200 bin 100 TL’lik ortalama yıllık gelirinin de altında kaldı.

TÜİK verilerine göre emekli hanelerinin konut ve kira harcamalarının bütçedeki payı 2018’de yüzde 28.55’ten 2025’te yüzde 38.66’ya çıktı. Kira yükü artarken gıdanın payı yüzde 25.52’den yüzde 22.66’ya geriledi. En yoksul hanelerin gelirinde emekli aylığının payı da 2018’de yüzde 13.70’ten 2025’te yüzde 20.29’a yükseldi. Böylece emekli aylığının en yoksul hanelerin bütçesindeki ağırlığı yüzde 50’den fazla arttı.

TÜİK’in 2025 verileri, temel geçim kaynağı emekli aylığı olan hanelerin tüketim harcamalarının en yoksul yüzde 20’lik kesimle eşitlendiğini ve yer yer gerisine düştüğünü gösteriyor. Her iki grubun bütçesinin yaklaşık yüzde 39’u konut ve kiraya giderken, eğlence, kültür ve giyim harcamaları yüzde 1-3 bandında kalıyor. Gıdanın payı ise artan gıda enflasyonu nedeniyle emekli hanelerinde yüzde 22.66’ya kadar düşüyor.

Emekli aylıklarının erimesi ve artan barınma giderleri, milyonlarca emekliyi yeniden çalışmaya zorladı. DİSK-AR’ın SGK ve TÜİK verilerine göre 2002’de 4.3 milyon emeklinin 1.6 milyonu (yüzde 36.6'sı) çalışırken, 2025’te 12.3 milyon emeklinin 8.5 milyonu (yüzde 69’u) çalışıyor veya iş arıyor. Yani her üç emekliden ikisi emeklilik hakkını fiilen kullanamaz hale geldi.

TÜİK işgücü göstergeleriyle yapılan karşılaştırmalı hesaplama, emeklilerin genel işgücü içindeki ağırlığının tarihi bir sıçrama yaptığını gösteriyor: 2005 yılında çalışan veya iş arayan 1.9 milyon emeklinin, Türkiye'de işgücü olarak ölçülen 21.3 …

author: Jake Johnson
title: UK Bars Entry to Swedish Climate Scholar Who Advocates for Palestinian Rights
content:
Andreas Malm was scheduled to speak at a conference that will also feature a co-founder of Palestine Action.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

The United Kingdom’s Labour government has barred Swedish climate scholar and Palestinian rights advocate Andreas Malm from entering the country, without explanation, just days before he was scheduled to speak at a conference that will also feature a co-founder of Palestine Action — an organization banned by the UK government on highly dubious grounds.

Malm, an author and associate professor of human ecology at Sweden’s Lund University, said Friday that he was “dismayed” by the UK Home Office’s decision this week to cancel his Electronic Travel Authorization, noting that he has “been going to the UK for decades — this is where I did my archival research for my PhD dissertation and lectured at dozens of universities and participated in even more conferences.”

Malm said the UK government’s move was “nothing short of scandalous,” and he linked the decision to his scheduled appearance at the conference organized by the socialist magazine Tribune. The event was billed as a discussion of “domination and resistance in the age of [US President Donald] Trump,” featuring Malm and Palestine Action co-founder Huda Ammori.

“This is a drift toward authoritarianism that didn’t begin with me, and it’s not going to end with me either,” Malm told Al Jazeera. “If I’m now being deemed a threat to the public good because I’m supposed to have a conversation with someone from Palestine Action, this is guilt by association.”

Verso Books, Malm’s publisher — including of his 2025 book The Destruction of Palestine Is the Destruction of the Earth — said in a statement Friday that it is “shocked and disturbed by the Labour government’s decision to ban one of our leading authors.”

“Never in over 55 years of publishing has a British government revoked the right of one of our authors to enter the country,” said Tariq Ali, the chair of Verso’s board of directors. “We can only assume, since no reasons have been given for banning him, that Andreas’ positions on Palestine, no different from the [International Criminal Court] and UN commissions, is the cause.”

“Verso Books condemns the silencing of critical voices and stands in support of writers and scholars who continue to speak out about important issues and contribute to open intellectual discourse,” Ali added. “We urge the government to restore Andreas Malm’s electronic travel authorisation immediately and allow him entry into the country.”

Jeremy Corbyn, the former UK Labour leader who now serves as the Your Party MP for Islington North, joined the chorus denouncing the cancellation of Malm’s travel authorization.

“This is an absurd and outrageous decision,” Corbyn wrote on social media. “What kind of society are we living in where world-renowned authors and campaigners are treated as enemies and threats? The real threat is this government’s assault on freedom of expression.”

“This is not an isolated incident — and the government should know that it is gaining a bad reputation for censorship and repression,” added Corbyn. “We know why the government has taken this decision: because it wants to silence criticism of Israel, as well as its own complicity in genocide. It will not succeed.”

As Trump cracks down on political speech, independent media is increasingly necessary.

Truthout produces reporting you won’t see in the mainstream: journalism from the frontlines of global conflict, interviews with grassroots movement leaders, high-quality legal analysis and more.

author: Clare Hymer
title: ‘Major Opportunity’ for UK Unions to Recruit Workers As New Rules Take Effect
content:
Trade unions could see a boost in membership due to

new workplace rights

 that come into force today.


As of 30 October, union representatives have the right to request in-person or digital access to workplaces where at least 21 people are employed – even if the union isn’t recognised by the employer or it has no members there.


This will make it easier for organisers to reach workers shut out of collective representation in order to speak to them about demanding better pay and conditions.


Until today, bosses could keep unions out of many workplaces by simply refusing access. Now, if talks to negotiate an access agreement fail, the Central Arbitration Committee – an independent government body – can force employers to agree, with penalties for breaches reaching £500,000.

 


Andrea Egan, general secretary of Unison – Britain’s largest trade union – said the new laws presented “a major organising opportunity”.


“For decades, employers have used every trick in the book to prevent unions getting into workplaces,”

she wrote in a blog post

 earlier this month. “They know organised workplaces shift the power dynamic so that workers have a real voice through recognition and collective bargaining and they don’t want that to spread. 


“The new access rights provide a significant reset of industrial relations.”


After peaking at 13.2 million in 1979, union membership in the UK plummeted as a result of deindustrialisation and anti-union legislation introduced by Margaret Thatcher’s government.


The new rules, which form part of Labour’s Employment Rights Act 2025, could be particularly helpful for unions wanting to reach workers in the private sector, where

just 12% of employees

 are unionised.


Other reforms taking effect today strengthen protections for workers taking part in industrial action. 


A separate requirement for bosses to inform staff of their right to join a union is due to come into force on 1 January 2027.

author: CNT Madrid
title: Recomendaciones de cara a la huelga del 11N en el sector de la comunicación
content:
Como seguramente sepas a estas alturas, la clase trabajadora de este país está convocada a una

huelga general el próximo 11 de noviembre

. CNT es una de las organizaciones convocantes del paro con el lema

‘Bajemos los alquileres, subamos los salarios’

.


Por otro lado, en nuestro sector, el de los medios de Comunicación (Prensa, televisión, radio, publicidad…) se dan una serie de particularidades que pueden generar dudas entre quienes formamos parte de él y queremos participar de manera activa en la jornada de paro y movilización, por lo que desde la

sección de Prensa y Comunicación de CNT

 queremos compartir algunas cuestiones básicas:


1. Tradicionalmente en prensa escrita de periodicidad diaria, la huelga se legalizaba para el día anterior a la general:    los redactores no escribían nada para la edición del día siguiente, las rotativas no imprimían… El día de huelga que amanecía sin prensa en la calle ya era sinónimo de éxito. Hoy, con el papel como algo testimonial y los periodistas realizando su trabajo para la edición online o papel indistintamente, ese acto forma ya parte del pasado y

la huelga se convoca para todo el sector a partir de las 0:00 horas del día 11 de noviembre.


2.

Los servicios mínimos no son aplicables a los medios privados y no se pueden imponer

. Se

podrán fijar sólo en medios de titularidad pública

 y bajo condiciones muy estrictas, amparando el derecho de la ciudadanía a la información.

Pero, en todo caso, deberán ser negociados con Comité de Huelga o la representación de los y las trabajadoras en cada centro de trabajo o los sindicatos convocantes en cada empresa.


3. Emitir programas enlatados o de catálogo por parte de radios, televisiones, etc es legal, pero

adelantar grabaciones de programas que suelen ser en directo con el objetivo de contrarrestar el efecto de la huelga es ilegal.


4.

No tenemos obligación de comunicar a la empresa si vamos a secundar la huelga

; Y si estoy acogiéndome a mi derecho a parar,

mi puesto no puede ser ocupado por nadie

, tampoco a través de personal externo contratado para ese objetivo.; es ilegal.


5. Finalmente,

cualquier acción de la empresa dirigida a


disimular o minimizar el paro

 estará atentando contra el derecho de huelga y

es por tanto denunciable,

 por lo que recomendamos documentar esa actuación.


Si tienes más dudas, consulta nuestras

preguntas frecuentes sobre el derecho a la huelga

. Y ante cualquier duda adicional,

contacta con nosotr@s a través del correo: prensa_medios@madrid.cnt.es

title: Tuncay Yılmaz: We want to build a united front of resistance in Europe - Part One
content:
As the rise of the far right, war policies, hostility towards migrants and attacks on democratic rights continue across Europe, political and social organisations from Turkey and Kurdistan are strengthening their efforts to build a common struggle. On 17 October, 25 organisations gathered in Cologne, Germany, and decided to establish a new alliance to unite their struggles for peace, democracy, equality and freedom. At the meeting, 20 organisations representing different political traditions declared their willingness to become founding members. The democratic resolution of the Kurdish question and the Peace and Democratic Society Process were also among the main issues discussed.


ANF spoke to Tuncay Yılmaz, founding co-chair of the Socialist Refoundation Party (SYKP), about the outcomes of the Cologne meeting, the need for a common struggle, the situation of left-wing and democratic forces in the face of the rising far right in Europe, and the roadmap for the proposed alliance.


On 17 October, 25 organisations from different political traditions came together in Cologne. Similar attempts to build alliances have been made in Europe before. Why has the need to establish a common platform for struggle emerged again today? What distinguishes this meeting from previous initiatives?


As you said, organisations from different political traditions and social groups in Europe have come together at various times. Previously, there was the European Assembly for Peace and Democracy (ABDEM). We then extended the organisation of the Peoples' Democratic Congress (HDK) in Turkey to Europe, establishing a broad organisation under the name HDK Europe. This organisation later became the European Democratic Forces Union (ADGB) and continued its activities under that name. Most recently, ahead of the NATO summit, a joint initiative called PANEV was established against imperialist aggression, wars and the NATO.


All these initiatives emerged from efforts to find ways for the forces of democracy, peace, equality and freedom to become better organised in Europe and pursue more effective political action against the enormous aggressive power confronting us.


The alliances we established at different times sometimes lost their effectiveness, both because of changes in the objective conditions in which they were formed and, to speak frankly, because of our own shortcomings. This is a reality, and we are aware of it. Indeed, this was one of the issues on the agenda of our meeting. We want to learn from our previous experiences.


However, the mistakes we made in the past or the changes we have experienced should not prevent us from bringing democratic forces together again and carrying out a common struggle. And indeed, they are not preventing us. One of the main motivations that brought us together at this meeting was the growing hostility towards migrants in the European countries where we live, the rise of the right, fascist movements coming to power and increasing state violence. The fact that laws targeting asylum seekers have reached almost inhumane proportions is also deeply concerning to all of us. We want to build a united front of resistance against all of this.


At the same time, however, all our attention, thoughts and concerns are focused on developments in Turkey. Looking at Turkey, we see a totalitarian regime being built step by step. Everyone who opposes it becomes a target. Presidential candidates are arrested. Selahattin Demirtaş has been imprisoned for years, as has Figen Yüksekdağ. Ekrem İmamoğlu was subsequently arrested. The Republican People's Party (CHP), which prides itself on being the founding party of the state, is also under serious pressure. Attempts are being made to divide the party, and many of its representatives have been arrested.


Alongside all this, a negotiation process has begun. It has not yet reached the stage of a peace process. However, this negotiation process has the potential to generate a collective strength capable of pushing back attacks on democracy through the positive developments it could bring to the country's political life. Despite this, we see that the political authorities are acting with appalling arbitrariness in this process as well.


To speak frankly, this process has been made possible by the determination and goodwill of Abdullah Öcalan and the Kurdish Freedom Movement. After all, decisions were taken to lay down arms and dissolve the organisation. These decisions …

author: Maríangeles Guerrero
title: Rosa Amorim: "Hablar de reforma agraria en Brasil es hablar de un proyecto de dignidad de vida"
content:
“Com a barriga vazia não consigo dormir,

E com o bucho mais cheio, comecei a pensar.

Que eu me organizando posso desorganizar

Que eu desorganizando posso me organizar

Que eu me organizando posso desorganizar”.

Da lama ao caos, Nação Zumbi - Chico Science


“Con la panza vacía no puedo dormir,

Con el buche más lleno, empecé a pensar.

Que desorganizándome puedo organizar

Que organizando me puedo desorganizar

Que desorganizándome puedo organizar”


Por Mariángeles Guerrero y Carla Perelló

Desde Brasil


Rosa Amorim es la primera mujer del Movimiento de los Trabajadores Rurales sin Tierra (MST) en ser electa diputada nacional en Brasil. Es negra, lesbiana, oriunda de Pernambuco, nordeste del país, y tiene 29 años. Integra el Partido de los Trabajadores (PT). Durante la pandemia, mientras gobernaba Jair Bolsonaro, fue una de las impulsoras de la red de cocinas solidarias que enfrentaron el hambre en los barrios populares de las ciudades. La reelección de Lula da Silva significa una victoria popular y una esperanza, pero la conformación de un Congreso con mayoría de la extrema derecha plantea sus propios desafíos. En ese escenario, sostiene que la “lucha parlamentaria” será vital. “Queremos que Brasil deje de ser uno de los países que más venenos y agrotóxicos consume”, afirma.


Hija de la lucha por la reforma agraria, Amorim creció en las filas del MST y también fue dirigente estudiantil. Desde sus orígenes, el movimiento campesino mantuvo su autonomía aunque apoyó candidaturas del PT. Pero, en 2022, tras el retroceso en materia de derechos que significó el gobierno de Jair Bolsonario, presentó sus propios candidatos. Ese año, ella fue electa diputada del estado de Pernambuco.

El pasado 5 de octubre fue electa diputada nacional; una de lxs 38 legisladorxs LGBT+ que obtuvieron un escaño y una de los cuatro integrantes del MST que estarán en el Congreso brasileño

.


En el histórico proceso electoral que consolidó a Luíz Inácio Lula da Silva como presidente por los próximos cuatro años, Amorim fue una de las jóvenes que acompañó la campaña para revertir la derrota que el PT obtuvo en la primera vuelta.

Llevará las banderas de la reforma agraria y la soberanía alimentaria al Poder Legislativo. Allí el agronegocio presiona, de la mano de la bancada ruralista, para obtener beneficios y seguir extendiendo la frontera agropecuaria

, causando deforestación y contaminación.


En contraste, el MST lleva cuatro décadas de lucha por la tierra para la producción de alimentos sanos.

“Alimentamos al pueblo porque con comida en la panza podemos tener mentes pensantes y con mentes pensantes podemos organizarnos”

, sostuvo en entrevista con Tierra Viva, haciendo honor a la histórica banda nordestina Nação Zumbi liderada por Chico Science.


Foto: Prensa PT


Las cocinas solidarias, que define como “una tecnología social para organizar al pueblo”, se convirtieron en política pública en 2023, durante el gobierno de Da Silva. Su objetivo es vincular el campo con la ciudad, llevando alimentos sanos a espacios comunitarios de los barrios populares. En esos ámbitos se brinda un plato de comida pero también escucha, alfabetización, contención y cuidados. Para la diputada, comer es el primer paso para cuestionar por qué existe el hambre y la pobreza.


—¿En qué situación está hoy la soberanía alimentaria en Brasil?

—Hablar del hambre no es solamente hablar de si el pueblo come por la mañana, por la tarde y por la noche. Es más profundo. Combatir el hambre también significa hablar de la calidad de lo que se come. Y para eso vamos a tener que librar una lucha muy grande. Ya la estamos librando, pero va a ser todavía mayor: la lucha contra el agronegocio, contra el modelo de producción vigente que hace que las personas se enfermen por lo que consumen todos los días. Queremos que Brasil deje de ser uno de los países que más venenos y agrotóxicos consume. Y esto tiene una relación directa con la lucha parlamentaria. Vamos a tener que librar una enorme disputa contra el agronegocio en el Congreso para reducir la cantidad de agrotóxicos que se autorizan en Brasil. author: rezgar2
title: The Brazilian Victory: Left Unity and Digital Autonomy
content:
Rezgar Akrawi : Lula's victory offers an experience worth studying and learning from. It demonstrates the possibility of cooperation among left-wing forces despite their differences, while recognizing the other factors that contributed to the result.


The left does not need to erase its diversity in order to unite. It needs to turn that diversity into an organized and effective force, strengthen its independence across all five pillars, and pursue the struggle for freedom, equality, and social justice while developing democratic, humanist socialist alternatives to capitalism.


Author


Rezgar Akrawi


رزكار عقراوي


    Submitted by

rezgar2

 on October 29, 2026


Rezgar Akrawi


The leftist leader Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva secured a historic victory in Brazil’s presidential election on October 25, 2026. The result came amid intense political and social polarization and the growing influence of the far right in Brazil and across Latin America, backed by the American far right led by Donald Trump.


The significance of this electoral victory extends beyond Lula securing a fourth term. It also lies in the political and organizational experience that helped make it possible, above all the ability of diverse left-wing and progressive forces, with different programs and ideological outlooks, to forge a broad electoral alliance around common ground in confronting the far right.


A Broad Left-Wing and Progressive Alliance Despite Differences


Lula contested the election with the support of the ‘Brazil Ready for More’ alliance, comprising seven left-wing and progressive parties organized into two party federations and two separate parties. The ‘Brazil of Hope’ federation brought together Lula’s Workers’ Party, the Communist Party of Brazil, and the Green Party. The second federation united the Socialism and Liberty Party, which includes socialist and radical-left currents, with the Sustainability Network. The Brazilian Socialist Party and the Democratic Labour Party also joined the alliance, alongside supportive social movements and trade unions. Lula ran with Geraldo Alckmin of the Brazilian Socialist Party as his vice-presidential candidate.


The importance of this alliance lies in its ability to bring together communists, socialists, the radical left, social democrats, and Greens despite their disagreements over capitalism, the role of the state, and the limits of social reform. These forces agreed on common electoral objectives while preserving their identities and organizational autonomy.


This is one of the most important lessons of the Brazilian experience. Left unity does not require ideological or organizational uniformity. It means being able to work together on common ground while respecting pluralism and differences.

 Disagreements over Lula’s economic and social policies will naturally persist, including among the forces that supported him at the ballot box.


Unity Does Not Mean Abandoning Criticism or Autonomy


The Brazilian experience raises an important question for left-wing forces around the world. Why do ideological and organizational differences become barriers to cooperation, despite so much common ground, even when these forces face shared political and class challenges?


Pluralism among communists, social democrats, the radical left, environmentalist and feminist currents, and independent leftists can be a source of strength and intellectual and political richness, provided it is managed democratically and constructively, without monopolization, exclusion, or claims to possess the absolute truth.

 Unity does not require abandoning criticism or offering unconditional acceptance of the policies of governments led by left-wing and progressive alliances.


Confronting Capitalism and the Far Right Requires a Broad Social Front


The victory demonstrated the importance of connecting the defense of democracy, rights, and freedoms with the economic and social demands of working classes and poor and marginalized communities.


Lula drew broad support from lower-income groups and proposed expanding social assistance, improving living conditions, and defending democratic institutions.


Confronting capitalism and the far right therefore cannot be confined to elections and party alliances. It requires sustained mass organizations in workplaces, neighborhoods, universities, trade unions, and social movements, together with policies that tackle class inequality and improve the lives of the majority …

author: Mary Stuart
title: How the Far-Right Uses Climate Disasters to Build Political Power
content:
Naomi Klein and Astra Taylor’s

End Times Fascism and the Fight for the Living World

 is critical reading for anyone seeking to understand and push back against the far-right coalitions wielding considerable state and corporate power around the world.


Klein and Taylor posit that today’s fascists believe that end times have arrived, and have made it their mission to profit from cascading global crises, while hunkering down and protecting themselves as the world burns around them.


The book details three factions of end times fascists, united by their shared apocalypticism. The religious fundamentalists believe end times are upon us, but they will be saved by their messiah. The Silicon Valley technologists are building technologies they say could be world-ending, that in the meantime are killing jobs, consuming vast resources, and polluting communities. The ethno-nationalists espouse conspiratorial ideas about cultural replacement and treat immigration as an existential threat.


DeSmog Canada editor/reporter Mary Stuart spoke with Astra Taylor about how climate change fits into end times fascism, the importance of AI data centre fights, and how we can understand Canadian Prime Minister Carney’s neoliberal moves in response to U.S. President Donald Trump.


Taylor is a writer, documentarian, and activist. She co-founded the

Debt Collective

, a membership-based union for debtors, and is the author of several books, including

The Age of Insecurity

 and

Democracy May Not Exist But We’ll Miss It When It is Gone

.


This interview was conducted by phone and has been edited for length and clarity.


Mary Stuart:

 

I


want to start by


asking how your book can help us understand some recent elections. Jair Bolsonaro’s son Flávio won the first round of voting in Brazil’s election and


nearly


became president. The far-right AfD recently won in Saxony-Anhalt.


How do these wins fit into your analysis of end times fascism?


Astra Taylor:

 One phenomena we describe in End Times Fascism relevant here is the role of Pentecostal religious communities in turning out the vote. To paraphrase reporting from Brazil, a voter said “my heart’s with Lula, but my pastor told me to vote for Flávio”.


The incredibly difficult conditions that we’re living under created fertile terrain for prophecy and religion, for kinds of pentecostalism, a faith that is focused on prosperity, individual advancement and banking on the idea that life is suffering here on earth, but you will be rewarded in the afterlife.


There’s also interference from Tech oligarchs. We don’t know the half of it at this moment, but the way the platform [Meta] refused to run ads for Lula’s party and beyond is certainly a factor. And the Trump regime [is playing a role] as well.


AfD is a similar. Naomi and I wrote a piece in the

Financial Times

 and we open with the images that went viral this summer of the Danube River drying, and Nazi warships emerging. Hundreds of Nazi warships sank during WWII, and as the river receded, this paraphernalia was coming out of the mud. We thought it was a powerful metaphor for today. What’s really striking is the riverbed— the fact that it’s drying because of climate change. Our point is that fascism always emerges from crises. And we cannot separate the ecological and economic crises people are facing.


People are really struggling with affordability. People are feeling that they don’t have a future. And actually quite strikingly, rates of immigration are quite low, right? So [Saxony-Anhalt is] one of the places with the least immigration, but [the AfD] step in and say “the problem is the immigrants, it’s not a larger economic system.” This is a classic fascist move that we describe throughout the book.


MS:


What role do climate change and climate denial play in end times fascism?


AT:

 Naomi and I are insistent that the planet is a player in our politics. Fascism always surges in moments of crisis.


We are in a world that is being roiled by disasters and shocks. We’ve reached a point where the consequences [of climate change] are undeniable. You cannot deny a heat dome when you’re inside it. You cannot deny a hurricane when it’s blowing the roof off your house. Of course, you can still deny why the storm is coming. You can embrace a Marjorie Taylor Greene perspective and say that it’s due to space lasers or you can say “the climate has always chained, this is nothing new, we don’t know if it’s human causing it.” …

author: nodes of resistance
title: Rechenzentren, „KI“ und Strategien für emanzipatorischen Widerstand
content:
Im Vorfeld der bundesweiten Konferenz zur Vernetzung von Widerstand gegen „KI“ und Rechenzentren. am 7.11.26 in Berlin veröffentlichen wir folgendes Diskussionspapier


Es regt sich Widerstand gegen Rechenzentren und das, wofür sie stehen. Damit dieser Widerstand möglichst weit trägt, halten wir eine Diskussion zu drei Themen für wichtig:


1) Der enge Zusammenhang von Rechenzentren und „KI“


2) Gemeinsam kämpfen für Klima- und soziale Gerechtigkeit, gegen Faschismus und Militarisierung


3) Wirksamer Widerstand durch Vielfalt und Unberechenbarkeit


1) Der enge Zusammenhang von Rechenzentren und „KI“


Der massive Ausbau von Rechenzentren und der Hype um „KI“ hängen unmittelbar zusammen. Denn: Der Hype um „KI“ mobilisiert die finanziellen Ressourcen und die politisch einstimmige Unterstützung für einen in Geschwindigkeit und Umfang beispiellosen Ausbau materieller Infrastruktur. Der Zusammenhang umfasst die technische, ökonomische und politische Dimension.


• Der technische Zusammenhang: Rechenzentren sind gewissermaßen die Fabriken von „KI“. Während es schon länger Rechenzentren gibt (seit dem Aufkommen von „Cloud“ als zentral verwaltete Rechenkapazitäten), macht „KI“ noch viel mehr und größere Rechenzentren erforderlich: Manche Rechenzentren dienen primär dem Training von „KI“-Modellen (diese brauchen besonders teure Halbleiter-Chips und liegen oft eher ländlich), andere primär der Inferenz, also dem Errechnen von „KI“-Outputs basierend auf trainierten Modellen (diese liegen meist möglichst nah an Internetknotenpunkten, oft urban). Rechenzentren liegen am Ende einer komplexen globalen Lieferkette: Besonders deutlich ist die erhöhte Nachfrage nach seltenen Erden und Metallen sowie nach Wasser und (fossiler) Energie, die an vielen Stellen dieser Lieferkette benötigt werden: Bei der Herstellung der Lithografiemaschinen, die wiederum nötig sind, um Chips zu produzieren zu können, die wiederum nötig sind, um ein Rechenzentrum zu betreiben. Die Infrastruktur rund um Rechenzentren und „KI“ ist seit einigen Jahren in erheblichem Aufbau und schließt zunehmend auch Endgeräte ein, deren Funktionieren an eine kontinuierliche Anbindung nicht nur an Internetkonnektivität, sondern auch an „KI“ und Cloud gebunden ist (von Heimgeräten über industrielle Produktion hin zu Kampfjets).


• Der finanzielle Zusammenhang: Der Finanzierung von Rechenzentren liegt ein quasi-religiöser Glaube an die Unausweichlichkeit und die Spekulation auf zukünftige Profitabilität von „KI“ zugrunde. „KI“-Unternehmen fahren jährlich Milliardenverluste ein, weil ihre Ausgaben in Form von Kosten von Rechenkapazitäten, Energie und Löhnen über den Einnahmen liegen. Rechenzentren sind dabei der Knotenpunkt für finanzielle Risiken: Die Chipherstellung ist (bisher) profitabel (siehe Bilanzen von Nvidia, TSMC, SK Hynix), das gleiche gilt für die Bereitstellung von Rechenkapazitäten als Dienstleistung, die vor allem die drei Hyperscaler-Unternehmen Amazon, Microsoft und Google anbieten. Rechenzentren sitzen zwischen der Chipherstellung und der Bereitstellung von Rechenkapazitäten und werden häufig nur angemietet von denjenigen, die dann wiederum Rechenleistung nutzen oder verkaufen. Rechenzentren sind extrem kapitalintensiv (bis zu mehreren Milliarden Euro pro Rechenzentrum) und hochspekulativ, sodass auch Menschen aus der Rechenzentrumsbranche (anonym/vertraulich) sagen: „Wer das Risiko versteht, wird nicht investieren.“ Das Risiko (also die Wahrscheinlichkeit von Verlusten) ergibt sich u.a. aus einer kurzen Lebensdauer von Chips (je nach Quelle ein, zwei oder max. sieben Jahre), der langfristigen Finanzierung von Rechenzentrumsbau (oft 15-20 Jahre), einer hohen Unsicherheit über die Verfügbarkeit und den Preis von Chips, Energie und Wasser und einer ebenfalls hohen Unsicherheit über die Nachfrage nach „KI“-Rechenkapazitäten. Diese Risiken werden aktuell immer neu verschachtelt durch komplexe Zirkelkäufe zwischen „KI“-Unternehmen, Chipherstellern und Rechenzentrumsbetreibern, was selbst Finanzanalyst*innen kritisch bewerten. Bereits seit mehreren Jahren attestieren u.a. Analyst*innen von Goldman Sachs das Vorliegen einer „Blase“.


• Der politische Zusammenhang: Die vermeintliche Unausweichlichkeit von „KI“ wird politisch verknüpft mit einem Wettbewerb um geopolitische Vorherrschaft (v.a. zwischen USA und China), einem Streben nach „Souveränität“ (z.B. durch Chipherstellung und Rechenzentren in Europa) und dem (Un-)Heilsversprechen immer mächtigerer …

author: La Zarzamora
title: Anarquistas pela anarquia sobre as eleições no Brasil/ Anarquistas por la anarquía sobre las elecciones en Brasil
content:
Enviado a La Zarzamora/ *Traducción al español al final.

Contra o fascismo todas as ações são úteis! Encontra teu lugar na luta. Revolte-se!

São os dizeres de um cartaz que apareceu nas ruas de Porto Alegre em 2019, e que são dizeres vigentes, antes de 2019, depois de 2019, nestes dias e que serão vigente ainda muito depois.

Nestes tempos em que o apelo anti fascista tende a afunilar-se no voto diante de um contexto em que o resultado das eleições no Brasil podem consolidar o neo fascismo a nível continental, nos é importante compartilhar um olhar anárquico que nos possibilite sair do pânico e construir antagonismos aos fascismos atuais, apesar de que nada seja tão simples assim. Para isso inicialmente vamos a entender que enquanto anárquicos e anarquistas, fazemos parte de coletividades, redes, e grupos dentro da sociedade que não compartilham nossa posição política, para depois apontar e precisar que nossas posições políticas não são sinônimos de pertencimentos ou identidades.

Cientes de que habitamos territórios felizmente diversos e com pessoas que tem maior ou menor apego à autonomia e a auto determinação, pensarmos nos diferentes lugares de luta contra o fascismo, consiste precisamente em aceitarmos dentro dessa diversidade, mutuamente, o que quer dizer horizontalmente, longe das tentativas uniformizadoras. Então podemos respeitar e entender que os cidadãos votantes “lutem” por não ter um presidente fascista, mediante o voto. Ao final é uma vergonha andar pelo mundo com a imposição majoritária de governantes misóginos, racistas, e aquele longo etc que bem sabemos sobre as famílias com tendência monarquista e miliciana. E mais profundamente, é respeitável o ódio que sentem por um personagem desse naipe. Quando trata-se de pessoas que não compartilham o local ácrata de luta contra o sistema, seu lugar na “luta” é nas urnas e é entendível.

Agora quando falamos de pessoas que escolhem a anarquia como posição política, e seus locais de luta é que nos debruçamos com um debate que a cada eleição nos faz perder companheiros e que a cada eleição nos joga diante de acusações de supostos purismos, falta de tática, falta de solidariedade, indiferença e outro longo etc. No entanto, o que no fundo incomoda a cada eleição é o fato de que os mesmos anarquistas chamem a fazer campanha por um candidato e façam apelo ao chamado “voto tático”.

Independentemente dos argumentos, isso incomoda não apenas quem escuta esses apelos e decide que sendo anarquista não tem como votar, mas acredito que incomoda também a quem vai na campanha, faz o apelo e tem que pensar, argumentar, escrever, fazer vídeo ou responder que apesar de… segue sendo anarquista. É nessa mesma justificativa que pode ser percebido que votar não forma parte do repertório das práticas anarquistas.

Ao nos perguntarmos sobre nosso lugar na luta contra o fascismo o que evidencia que somos anarquistas? Qual é a diferença com os demais? O apelo ao voto anarquista já nos indica que somos reconhecidos por não votar. Então pedem-nos, diante do desespero, o favor de abdicar de uma de nossas práticas e isso não é pouca coisa.

Um dos nossos fundamentos, enquanto anárquicos e anarquistas, é o rechaço ao Estado. Odiamos ele porque enxergamos nele a cristalização de todos os processos opressivos, mas mesmo odiando o Estado ele nos afeta, e as pautas que possam resultar do circo dos horrores que foi eleito, vão nos afetar com politicas que procuram devolver forças para o patriarcado, ao militarismo, ao extrativismo, a moralidade religiosa, ao conservadorismo. De fato é por isso que odiamos o Estado, porque ele nos afeta, porque nos impõe.

Para além desse fundamento, o que do anarquismo fez com que nosso coração batesse e escolhêssemos esse caminho? Se há algo que fazemos sem nenhuma obrigação é ser parte das agitações e movimentos anarquistas, então sendo uma escolha tão livre, o que dessa proposta nos tocou o coração?

A autonomia, a autogestão, a horizontalidade, o apoio mútuo, a solidariedade, são práticas anarquistas que também são fundamentais e que, inegavelmente, são também incompatíveis com a existência dos Estados, porque cada Estado pretende anular essas práticas. Se sustenta no discurso de que as pessoas não sobreviveríamos sem o Estado, apesar de que catástrofes já demonstraram a efetividade da organização horizontal, apesar de que a história social e coletiva tem se desenvolvido majoritariamente sem Estado se pensamos nela historicamente e fora do eurocentrismo …

content:
Le 31 octobre, c'est Halloween – la fête des morts. Généralement ils reviennent exiger des bonbons ou des sorts. Le 17 octobre, le gouvernement a choisi les sorts. Résultat : on vient de quitter l'époque contemporaine et, depuis, Bismillah, c'est les ténèbres. Mais ces ténèbres, elles sont super drôles.


Jamais autant de créatures multiformes n'avaient déferlé dans nos insurrections. Il nous a fallu analyser cet étrange phénomène. Alors on a invité deux experts des ténèbres joyeuses : le philosophe Norman Ajari et l'essayiste Pacôme Thiellement. La brèche entre les mondes vient de s'ouvrir, elle n'est pas près de se refermer. C'est la première fois que la révolution s'apparente à la chorégraphie du Thriller de Michaël Jackson. Si le Gilet Jaune de 2018 s'est ajouté au k-way noir de 2016, désormais : c'est l'intégralité du multiverse qui se fait costume. title: On en a marre - en Suisse aussi!
content:
Wir haben es satt. Alle am 31. Oktober nach Zürich in den Kreis 4.


Seit drei Jahren offener Genozid. Kriege überall. Bilder von Polizei und Faschist*innen, die Hand in Hand die Jugend ihrer Länder verstümmeln.

 La police mutile les lycéen-s!

 Unterdrückung, Polizeistaat und Faschismus, so sichbar wie schon lange nicht mehr.


An diesen Punkt sind wir nicht ohne Grund gekommen. Denn die Herrschenden nutzen ihre Macht, um die Ressourcen dieser Welt nach ihrem Kalkül einzusetzen. Das heisst, das Geld geht ins Militär, anstatt in die Schulen. Das heisst das Geld geht in KI, anstatt in den Klimaschutz. Das heisst das Geld wird in die Polizei investiet, anstatt in antipatriarchale Projekte. Das heisst offene Grenzen für Kapital und geschlossene Grenzen für all diejenigen, die durch die Kriege des Kapitals ihre Lebenswelt verlieren. Kurz, der Status Quo ist nicht einfach so passiert.

Die Herrschenden haben sich - wenn auch nicht als homogener Block - für ihn entschieden.


In der Summe haben sie den Krieg der Pflege und Care, die Polizei der Gerechtigkeit, KI der Ökologie und Genozid der Erinnerung und

Reparation

 vorgezogen haben. Hervorheben wollen wir dabei auch, dass die genannten Probleme nicht isoliert betrachtet werden können. Die Herrschenden finanzieren ihre Kriege und Genozide mit dem Geld, dass dann anderswo fehlt.

Es ist ein und dieselbe Rechnung.

 Und aus eigener Tasche bezahlen sie es sicher NIE! Aka, wir alle bezahlen es. In der heilen Schweiz immerhin (noch) nicht mit unserem Leben. Und die Verantwortlichen sitzen tagtäglich vor unseren Nasen. Was eine Gesamtscheisse! Zum Glück findet der Kampf dagegen gerade wieder Wege in die Festung Europa.

The kids are alright after all!


Wir lehne dabei das Narrativ ab, es handle sich einach um Schüler*innenproteste. Erstens geht es schon lange nicht mehr um "Protest" es geht um Konfrontation und die Weigerung, sich zu unterwerfen.

Der Geist des Aufstands geht um in Europa.

 Zweitens waren es von Beginn an nicht einfach Schüler*innenproteste, sondern eine viel breitere Bewegung, die ihre Lebensrealität nicht mehr akzeptieren wollte. Und die Poteste waren von Beginn an militant. Wehe all denen, die Denken, die

Casseurs

 hätten die Bewegung unterwandert. Nein, die

Casseurs

 sind Teil der Bewegung und es gilt, sich uneingeschränkt mit ihnen zu solidarisieren. Ihre Handlungen verstehen wir als revolutionäre Akte der Kollektivierung, Vorboten einer möglichen Welt. Ein kleines bisschen Gerechtigkeit blitzt auf in jeder zerbrochenen Scheibe der sonst für uns unbezahlbaren Innenstädte. Solidarität mit allen

Zerbrecher*innen

 dieser Welt!

Wir haben euch lieb.


Solidarität mit den aktuellen Unruhen in Europa kann dabei nicht nur bedeuten, Soli-Posts zu veröffentlichen. Echte Solidarität muss materiell spürbar sein. Echte Solidarität bedeutet, wenn unsere Geschwister auf die Stasse gehen, dann gehen wir auch. Echte Solidarität bedeutet, wenn

die Anderen

 auf die Fresse bekommen, dann auch wir. Solidarität bedeutet, wir stehen zusammen auf, lassen einander nicht allein und kämpfen Seite an Seite. Auch wenn es ungemütlich wird.

Denn niemand ist frei, sind wir nicht alle frei!


In diesem Sinn:

On en a marre - en Suisse aussi!

 Let's join the fight. 31. Oktober 22Uhr Kreis 4, Zürich. Weitere Daten werden Folgen.

Wir möchten mit diesem Aufruf keine avantgardistische Position in der aktuellen Bewegung einnehmen. Wir haben lediglich entschieden, dass wir nicht mehr warten können und die Initative ergriffen. content:
Οι αντιφασίστες της Θεσσαλονίκης έδωσαν το παρόν στο άγαλμα Βενιζέλου επί της Εγνατίας όπου είχε καλεστεί συγκέντρωση ενάντια στη φασιστοσύναξη του νεοναζί Κασιδιάρη σε ξενοδοχείου του Βαρδαρίου. Όμως τα κυβερνητικά σχέδια προστασίας του προσφάτως αποφυλακισθέντα χρυσαυγίτη, ακολούθησαν η απαγόρευση της συγκέντρωσης από την αστυνομία και τελικά η εκτεταμμένη χρήση βίας από τα ΜΑΤ που είχαν ζώσει την περιοχή.


Οι αντιφασίστες πολίτες ανταποκρίθηκαν στα καλέσματα σωματείων, συλλόγων, οργανώσεων, συλλογικοτήτων και προήλθαν από  ευρύ πολιτικό φάσμα: τον αντιεξουσιαστικό χώρο, τη ριζοσπαστική αριστερά, το ΚΚΕ. Έδειξαν δε μεγάλη αποφασιστικότητα στην πραγματοποίηση της συγκέντρωσης και παρέμειναν στο χώρο παρά τα χημικά, τα δακρυγόνα, τις κρότου λάμψης που έπεσαν σωρηδόν από την ελληνική αστυνομία και τις δύο προσαγωγές.


Χαρακτηριστικά του δυναμισμού και παλμού της αντιφασιστικής συγκέντρωσης ήταν και συνθήματα που καταγράφηκαν: Μπλόκο στους φασίστες, καμιά ανοχή στα τσιράκια των αφεντικών. Είστε η σαπίλα όλου του ντουνιά, μπλόκο στους φασίστες σε κάθε γειτονιά. Φασίστες από το λαό θα τη βρείτε. Το φασισμό τσακίζουν αγώνες λαϊκοί. Έξω οι νεοναζί από τη Θεσσαλονίκη. Στη φυλακή οι νεοναζί. Φασίστες, χίτες, μαυραγορίτες. Ούτε σπιθαμή γής στους φασίστες. Ούτε με φυλακές, ούτε με νόμους, ο φασισμός τσακίζεται στους δρόμους.

title: “Nos falta una maestra”
content:
Foto: CTERA


Paro nacional de docentes y auxiliares por justicia para Nanci Godoy


Mario Hernandez


La Confederación de Trabajadores de la Educación de la República Argentina (CTERA) convocó a un paro nacional docente para este jueves 29 de octubre, acompañado por una jornada de duelo, movilizaciones y acciones públicas tras el hallazgo sin vida de Nanci Estela Godoy, la maestra rural que trabajaba como directora suplente en la Escuela Rural Nº 626 de Paraje El Malezal en la localidad de Esquina (Corrientes) y se encontraba desaparecida desde el 7 de octubre. La medida de lucha exige el esclarecimiento el femicidio y reclamar responsabilidades por las condiciones de precariedad, aislamiento y desprotección en las que la docente desarrollaba su trabajo.


La convocatoria central será en la Ciudad de Buenos Aires, donde la CTERA y otros gremios, como SUTEBA Multicolor, Ademys y la agrupación Isadora –que también movilizaron el pasado martes– convocaron a concentrar nuevamente desde las 8:30 en la Casa de la provincia de Corrientes, en Maipú 271.


La adhesión comprende a distintos sectores de la educación pública y privada. En la provincia de Buenos Aires, el Frente de Unidad Docente Bonaerense (FUDB) –integrado por el Sindicato Unificado de Trabajadores de la Educación de Buenos Aires (SUTEBA), la Federación de Educadores Bonaerenses (FEB), el Sindicato Argentino de Docentes Privados (SADOP), la Unión de Docentes de la Provincia de Buenos Aires (UDOCBA) y la Asociación del Magisterio de Enseñanza Técnica (AMET)– confirmó su participación. También se suman el frente Multicolor de SUTEBA -que ya viene realizando un paro desde el día de ayer en reclamo de aumento salarial y mejoras en las condiciones laborales-, la Unión Docentes Argentinos (UDA), la Asociación de Maestrxs de la Provincia de Buenos Aires. Además, adhieren organizaciones de los sectores de auxiliares y estatales, como la Asociación Trabajadores del Estado (ATE), el Sindicato de Obreros y Empleados de Minoridad y Educación (SOEME) y la Unión del Personal Civil de la Nación (UPCN).


En las provincias, las adhesiones incluyen al Sindicato Único de Trabajadores de la Educación de Corrientes (SUTECO), que declaró jornadas de duelo escolar y laboral y convocó a parar en todo el territorio provincial; la Asociación Gremial del Magisterio de Entre Ríos (AGMER); la Unión de Educadores de la Provincia de Córdoba (UEPC); la Asociación del Magisterio de Santa Fe (AMSAFE), junto con SADOP y UDA en esa provincia; y la Unión Docentes Agremiados Provinciales (UDAP), UDA y AMET en San Juan. El Sindicato Unificado de Trabajadoras y Trabajadores de la Educación Fueguina (SUTEF) también adhirió al paro nacional y mantuvo, además, la jornada de lucha que había previsto para el viernes 30. La modalidad de las protestas y la afectación de las clases varían según cada organización y establecimiento.


El reclamo por justicia se enlaza con una discusión más amplia sobre las condiciones en las que trabajan quienes sostienen la educación pública. Dos meses antes de desaparecer, Godoy había denunciado por escrito el abandono de la Escuela Rural Nº 626, sin agua, con baños inutilizables, techos deteriorados y rastros de roedores y murciélagos, y con un docente titular que llevaba años sin asistir regularmente a dar clases. Ahora, su muerte vuelve a poner en primer plano la desprotección de las trabajadoras de la educación rural y la necesidad de investigar tanto el crimen como las circunstancias en las que desarrollaba su labor.


El pueblo de Esquina realizó una multitudinaria marcha en reclamo de justicia para Nanci


Este miércoles 28 por la tarde, una multitudinaria marcha llevó el reclamo de justicia para Nanci hasta la fiscalía local, luego de confirmarse de que el cuerpo hallado pertenece a la maestra rural que era intensamente buscada. Allí, familiares, amigos y vecinos se concentraron frente a la Fiscalía para exigir justicia y respuestas sobre lo ocurrido. Uno de los momentos más conmovedores se vivió cuando los vecinos se acercaron a abrazar y acompañar al hijo de Nancy, en medio del profundo dolor que atraviesa toda la familia.


El cuerpo de la docente fue hallado el miércoles 28 de octubre en un bañado de una zona de monte dentro de la estancia El Curupí, en el departamento correntino de Esquina. Según las informaciones judiciales publicadas este jueves, hay cinco personas detenidas con prisión preventiva. Ireneo Antonio Zarza y Felipe Dionisio Sandoval, capataces …

title: Attacker who shot Rojda Odabaşı cites ‘noise’ as motive
content:
Rojda Odabaşı, who was seriously wounded when Mazlum Çelebi shot her with a shotgun on the night of 23 August in Diyarbakır (Amed), continues her fight for justice. Odabaşı is still receiving treatment for injuries sustained in the armed attack by Çelebi, reportedly her downstairs neighbour. However, the attacker, who was arrested on the day of the incident, was released after 58 days in detention. Reacting to the release of Çelebi, who was indicted on charges of "intentional injury" and "damage to property", Odabaşı asked, "Did I have to die for him to be punished?"


First hearing scheduled for 8 April 2027


Mazlum Çelebi, who shot and wounded Rojda Odabaşı and damaged her vehicle, was detained on 23 August and remanded in custody the same day. The indictment prepared in connection with the incident seeks his punishment on charges of "intentional injury" and "damage to property". Çelebi reportedly justified the attack in his statement by saying, "They were making noise."


Following the preparation of the indictment, the court ordered Çelebi's release in a preliminary procedural decision issued on 23 October. Odabaşı subsequently requested a restraining order and protective measures, stating that her personal safety was at risk. The first hearing in the case is scheduled for 8 April 2027 at Diyarbakır 2nd Criminal Court of First Instance.


‘My client was struck by 100 shotgun pellets in her legs’


Arif Altunkalem, the lawyer representing Odabaşı, criticised the release decision, saying that the case file contained evidence indicating intent to kill.


Altunkalem said that noise had been cited as the justification for the attack, adding: "You know how the incident unfolded. Noise is being given as the reason. Because of noise, 16 shotgun rounds were fired at a home in the middle of the night. My client was struck by 100 shotgun pellets in both legs. We maintain that releasing the defendant after just 58 days in a case containing elements indicating intent to kill is contrary both to the law and to the evidence in the case file. We have submitted our objection to the release decision. We will continue to follow the case."


‘I will continue my fight for justice’


Rojda Odabaşı criticised the release decision and spoke about the impact of the attack and her concerns for her personal safety. Odabaşı said: "The person who shot me with a shotgun in my own home, wounded my legs and damaged my car is no longer in custody. Yet I am still living with the consequences of the attack and concerns about my safety. What will happen to my personal safety? Far from easing my fears, the release decision has increased my concerns about the future. How am I supposed to feel safe in my home, on my street and in my daily life? Who can guarantee that I will not be attacked again?"


Odabaşı underlined the severity of the attack she had suffered and continued: "Did I have to die for him to be punished? The fact that I survived does not diminish the seriousness of the attack I experienced. It is unacceptable to disregard the safety concerns of a woman who has been subjected to an armed attack in her own home. Of course, the legal grounds for judicial decisions must be examined. However, as a victim of violence, it is my most fundamental right to demand that my safety be ensured, that my questions be answered and that my demand for justice be taken seriously."


Odabaşı said that they would challenge the release decision and called on the authorities to immediately implement the necessary protective measures to ensure her safety, clarify the legal grounds for the release decision and ensure that the available appeal procedures are effectively pursued.

title: Remembering Legendary Farmworker Organizer and Activist Dolores Huerta
content:
Huerta wasn’t just an organizer — she also loved life, says journalist Maria Hinojosa.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

Immigrant rights and labor icon Dolores Huerta died Wednesday at the age of 96. Huerta co-founded the National Farm Workers Association in 1962 and then the United Farm Workers of America, working with Cesar Chavez. From 1965 to 1970, the union organized the historic Delano grape strike, which ended in major gains for farmworkers’ labor rights.

In the years that followed, Huerta became heavily involved in the women’s liberation and immigrant rights movements and became a major supporter of the Democratic Party. In March, The New York Times published an investigation into Cesar Chavez’s history of sexual abuse of women and girls in the farmworkers’ movement, prompting Huerta to reveal that she, too, had been raped by Chavez. Huerta said the assaults led to the births of two of her children.

Dolores Huerta appeared on Democracy Now! many times over the years. We remember her legacy with Pulitzer Prize-winning journalist Maria Hinojosa, who says, “Dolores was not only a labor organizer, a civil rights organizer, a feminist, committed, always optimistic about the possibilities of this country, but she loved life, and I want people to remember that.”

AMY GOODMAN: This is Democracy Now!, democracynow.org, The War and Peace Report. I’m Amy Goodman.

The legendary labor organizer, feminist and civil rights activist Dolores Huerta has died at the age of 96. She was co-founder of the National Farm Workers Association in 1962 and then the United Farm Workers of America. She worked with Cesar Chavez at both groups. The United Farm Workers grew out of a merger between the National Farm Workers Association and the Filipino-led Agricultural Workers Organizing Committee.

Dolores Huerta coined the phrase ”¡Sí se puede!,” “Yes, we can!” It became a rallying cry for farmworkers, a lasting slogan for social justice movements.

title: The Cornell Case and the Left's Betrayal of Itself
content:
Here's an article about the feminist reaction to the "Cornell 7" case that has been in the news recently (October 2026). A version of it was published in "Compact." (The hyperlinks have been deleted, unfortunately.) The general point is that contemporary feminism has become an albatross for the left, and is also contributing to destructive social and cultural trends.

In the 1960s, feminists demanded that women and men have legal equality, that women be treated as mature adults who are free to make their own choices be it with regard to sex or their careers, that patriarchal paternalism be dismantled. In the 2020s, feminists demand that women be constantly protected against men, that patriarchal paternalism be resurrected, that women be legally treated as not responsible for decisions they’ve made because, in certain contexts, only men have agency. And men, they argue, are inveterate misogynists, abusers, and rapists, so the agency they manifest is almost invariably malign.

The reaction to the “Cornell 7” case is the latest example. A remarkable wave of hysteria has swept liberal and left culture, from mass media and social media to university campuses. Misandry is drenching the discourse; mobs are going after anyone who questions the dominant narrative; the guilt of the accused is automatically assumed, because the accused are men and men are by definition guilty. Is it any wonder that millions of men in recent years have turned away from the left—which seems to hate them—and fallen into the clutches of the far-right and the “manosphere”?

Consider what has transpired. Far from condemning the wildly irresponsible comments of public figures like Governor Hochul and Attorney General Letitia James, which treat as established fact accusations made in a civil lawsuit, leftists themselves, including Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and Zohran Mamdani, have talked as though the case has already been decided. This is despite the highly ambiguous evidence that has been presented, much of which tends to exonerate the alleged perpetrators of the “gang-rape.” Not only is presumption of innocence thrown out the window; it is obvious that even if the accused end up being found innocent, most liberals and leftists will remain sure of their guilt.

Lynch mobs have been out for blood. A few weeks ago, it was easy to find thousands of people “liking” public demands to kill the accused. Even innocent bystanders were victimized. The campaign of overwhelming harassment to which the journalist Michael Tracey has been subjected for questioning the “guilty until proven innocent” narrative led to his father receiving “thousands of nonstop crazed texts/calls/voicemails” threatening him with brutal violence. The current owners of Tracey’s childhood home were “inundated” with “crazed threats,” and received suspicious packages at their house. Friends and family of the accused men were harassed by thousands. So was the family of an innocent man who happens to have the same name as one of the accused.

Since liberals and leftists are refusing to stand up for decency and the rule of law, it is left to conservatives to do so—which enables them to claim the moral high ground against “lunatic” leftists and thereby score political points. It turns out that many conservatives take women more seriously as (potentially) responsible adults and moral agents than most leftists do.

Feminist moral panics may seem well-intentioned in that they’re allegedly motivated by concern for the safety of women, but these episodes illustrate the extent to which the (so-called) “left” has been corrupted and co-opted by neoliberal dynamics, particularly in the era of social media. The atomized, polarized, siloed, anti-intellectual, narcissistic soundbite culture of social media—itself a reflection of capitalist tendencies—has helped produce a liberal-left that dehumanizes others, reflexively assumes the worst of men, exploits controversies for social media clout, and contributes to the very social breakdown that leftists rightly attack neoliberalism for engendering. After all, a feminism that teaches women to hate and fear men, and to view themselves as being on a higher moral plane, doesn’t exactly promote healthy relationships. It exacerbates gender wars and culture wars, thus, again, gifting the right wing with talking points and grievances to rally around.

author: Sara Fayyazi
title: Making Women’s History Part of the Curriculum
content:
Two teachers from Sacred Heart Preparatory School in California, Kristen Kelly and Serene Williams, have proposed an Advanced Placement U.S. Women’s History course in response to the issue of students not learning about women’s history. The courses would allow studying women’s experiences and contributions in greater depth. Establishing this course would create a better understanding of American history as it includes the diverse experiences of women and would help students connect the historical struggles for equality to gender issues today.

Women have contributed to shaping the nation’s politics, economy, and social movements, yet their participation is often overlooked by traditional history classes. From fighting for the right to vote, challenging discrimination, and advocating for female autonomy, women have had a significant role in building the foundation of the United States today.

One of the main arguments for WAPUSH is that women’s experiences are not explored in the classroom. In the article Educational Activism: Creating an AP U.S. Women’s History Course, Serene Williams, Kristen Kelly, and Clara Robinson explain that topics such as women’s suffrage and reproductive rights receive limited attention in the current AP U.S. History curriculum. The women’s suffrage movement involved decades of organizing, political campaigning, and resistance. However, teachers may not introduce this topic to students or have enough time to examine its strategies and leaders in detail. A dedicated course would allow students to study these movements more thoroughly and understand how women helped shape American democracy.

Women’s history is much broader than the fight for voting rights. The proposed WAPUSH curriculum includes women’s labor, politics, religion, culture, war, and violence against women. It also examines how race, class, sexuality, religion, and other identities shaped women’s experiences. This approach is important because women throughout the years have never shared one universal experience. Indigenous women, Black women, Immigrant women, etc., have faced different opportunities and forms of discrimination. Studying these differences would help students develop a greater understanding of American history and that America was not built on just our founding fathers, but by women who paved the path for opportunity and development through blood, sweat, and tears.

An AP course would also help students recognize the connection between historical events and current issues. The debate over reproductive rights and other feminist struggles today cannot be fully understood without examining the laws and political movements that shaped access to contraceptives, abortion, and female economic support. Studying topics from the suffrage movement to the Equal Rights Amendment can help students understand the political equality that has developed through activism and engage in feminist discussion. Learning this history would give students the context needed to evaluate debates instead of viewing them as different events.

Establishing this course would show that women’s history is worthy of advanced academic study. The WAPUSH campaign began in 2022, and according to its website, the campaign gathered more than 4,000 petition signatures and received encouragement from College Board leadership as it worked toward launching this course. Its proposal has also received university support, while the campaign continues seeking letters from high schools willing to offer the course. This continued support brings women closer to bringing light to women’s history and giving women a space in school systems and curricula. This petition is one step closer every day to its goal to educate and inform people all across America of women’s contributions.

An AP U.S. Women’s History course would make education more comprehensive, inform students even more about the history of the U.S., and connect past struggles to present issues. Women have influenced American politics, economics, culture, and social movements, yet their experiences are not always given sufficient attention in existing courses. By offering students an opportunity to examine these experiences, the College Board could help create a more inclusive and accurate understanding of the nation’s past. Women’s history is not separate from American history but instead an essential part of it.
