author: Tam Saavedra
title: The UN CRPD Guidelines on Intersectionality are Here!
content:
Ver versión en español


The UN CRPD Guidelines on Intersectionality Just Changed the Game for Disability Rights—Here’s What You Need to Know 


Big news for women with disabilities and all feminist disabled advocates, allies, and organizations worldwide!

 


During its 35th Session in August 2026, the

UN Committee on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities

 (UN CRPD)

 officially adopted the historic

Guidelines on Identifying and Addressing Intersectional Discrimination Against Girls, Adolescents, Women, and Older Women with Disabilities

.

 


This milestone represents a monumental step forward for disability rights. For the first time, States have explicit, actionable guidance to support their obligations at the intersection of gender and disability.

 


Read the official CRPD Guidelines here

 


What Are the CRPD Guidelines on Intersectional Discrimination?


The Guidelines serve as an authoritative framework developed by the UN


CRPD Committee to help States better prevent, monitor, and address intersectional discrimination.

 


Throughout years of UN CRPD country review processes, the Committee identified a persistent, critical gap:

the specific rights of women with disabilities and the complex, intersectional discrimination they experience are rarely understood or adequately addressed by governments.

 


As the UN CRPD celebrates its 20th anniversary, these Guidelines were issued to bridge that gap—ensuring the convention is implemented to benefit

all

 women, girls, and gender-diverse people with disabilities across their lifespans.

 


Why Are These Guidelines a Game


–

Changer?

 


International documents rarely explicitly focus on the detailed, lived experiences and rights of women with disabilities. These Guidelines clearly name and elaborate on the systemic barriers

 women and gender-diverse people with disabilities face daily across the globe, including:

 


Sexual & Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR):

 Addressing and preventing enforced sterilization, forced contraception, lack of accessible healthcare, restrictions on abortion, and lack of perinatal, menstrual, and menopause care.

 


Gender-Based & Disability-Based Violence:

 Exposing institutional violence, digital/online abuse, and the widespread lack of support services for victims.

 


Caregiving Recognition:

 Validating women with disabilities as active caregivers and mothers, rather than only recipients of care.

 


Economic & Educational Exclusion:

 Highlighting barriers in the labor market, economic and exclusion from education during puberty.

 


Crisis & Climate Response:

 Tackling compounded exclusion during environmental disasters, climate emergencies, and humanitarian relief efforts.

 


…just to name a few.

 


7 Key Breakthroughs in the Framing of the Guidelines 

 


What makes this document uniquely transformative is its progressive, structural approach:

 


Explicit Inclusion of Gender Diversity:

 The Guidelines explicitly encompass the rights of transgender, intersex, non-binary, and other gender-diverse people with disabilities and ask for gender diversity – inclusive interpretation of all obligations described.

 


Recognition of Historical Root Causes:

 The Committee explicitly addresses the legacy and ongoing impacts of

colonialism and enslavement

, establishing that States benefiting from these historical systems bear a particular responsibility to remedy their ongoing effects.

 


An Open Catalogue of Diversity:

 The text recognizes that women with disabilities belong to multi-marginalized communities—including Indigenous, Black, Dalit, Adivasi, refugee, asylum-seeking, religious minority, and pastoralist groups or people living in informal settings, among others —while leaving space for all intersecting identities.

 


Structural & Preventive Approach:

 Moving beyond a strictly punitive, reactive model, the Guidelines demand the dismantling of systemic oppression (such as ableism, audism, racism, and patriarchy) through early intervention, education, and public policy reform. 

 


Decriminalization

 is also a disability issue:

The guidelines recognize impacts of criminalization of abortion, homosexuality, gender identity and expression as well as

restricting marriage or consensual relationships as an important intersectional disability rights issue.

 


Holding digital platforms accountable:

author: Dominique Gené - Local Journalism Initiative Reporter
title: Nunavik school board to pilot sex-education program
content:
Kativik Ilisarniliriniq, Nunavik’s school board, will test a sexuality education program in Kuujjuaq and Umiujaq in November.


The pilot program was developed with the Nunavik Regional Board of Health and Social Services and is intended to help children understand personal boundaries and how to stay safe in sexual situations, said Sarah Aloupa, president of Kativik Ilisarniliriniq, in an interview.


“It’s important for parents to take this very seriously. This program is for the students’ well being,” she said.


Aloupa said the initiative responds to a need raised by Nunavik residents and parents. The school board’s council of commissioners heard a presentation from the health board about the proposed program in June.


The program will cover students from kindergarten to Grade 11, with information packages for different age groups.


Aloupa declined to share the teaching material.


The pilot is scheduled to run Nov. 2 to 6 at Jaanimmarik School and Pitakallak School in Kuujjuaq and Nov. 16 to 20 at Kiluutaq School in Umiujaq. The schools were chosen in part because they were ready to take part and have staff with relevant experience, said Jade Duchesneau-Bernier, spokesperson for the school board.


During those weeks, staff will participate in training and parents can review material and ask questions at evening information sessions.


Their feedback will help shape the final program. While the board has not yet clarified how parents can do so, they can opt their children out, Aloupa said.


Information about the sessions is being sent to parents through school letters and posted on Facebook.


Aloupa pointed to sexual abuse cases in the region as part of the broader need for education on the subject.


In February 2025, Nicolas Cyr, a physical education teacher at Jaanimmarik School, was

charged

 with sexual assault of a minor, sexual interference of a minor and assault.


The pilot is intended to help the Nunavik school board and the region’s health board assess the program before considering whether to expand it to the other 18 schools Kativik Ilisarniliriniq operates, Aloupa said.


The organizations have not yet set a timeline for a region-wide rollout.

Trans sensitivity question!

Is the term ‘dead naming’ reserved for trans people, or can it be used for people who changed their name for other reasons? Thank you in advance.


I’m fine with anyone using 'dead naming’ for themselves. People have many reasons to have a painful association with their past name and if having a term that says ’

do not fucking use this name

’ is convenient for you: go for it.

But also, I may be an outlier, as I am trans and I hate the term 'dead naming’ and would never use it for myself.

I’m not dead. Nothing about me died. My past name isn’t a horrible memory that must never be uttered, it’s just a name I once used. It’s as mundane as my pre-transition pictures, which are still on my wall because my transness is not a dirty secret to be hidden.

Someone who uses my past name for me deliberately is being a transphobic asshole, but they don’t hold any power over me. I will not cry myself to sleep because they used the secret spell of trans pain. I’ll just think they’re a transphobic asshole and I’ll move on.

author: Pinko Collective
title: Letter in Support of the Dolls of Berlin, Casa Kuá and Trans and Queer People Facing State Repression Worldwide
content:
We reprint the open letter below in support of the Dolls of Berlin. To add your name as a signatory, follow the link at the bottom of the page.

On the afternoon of Sunday 18 October a large police squad forcibly entered Casa Kuá, a queer community center in Berlin, Germany, where at that point The Dolls of Berlin, a transfem social collective, was gathering. Police detained several women for hours while ransacking Casa Kuá. We, the undersigned, stand in support with The Dolls of Berlin, Casa Kuá, and queer and trans people facing state violence, repression and erasure everywhere. We are demanding that the German State drop the case and immediately stop the criminalization of trans spaces and solidarities. We are urging everyone to contribute to the fundraiser, to help our comrades continue their essential work and activities, and keep

nourishing much needed survival spaces for the most vulnerable communities

. 

The attack against the Berlin Dolls comes at a time of unprecedented rise of state fascism, both in Germany where the AfD recently won local elections in Saxony-Anhalt, in neighbouring European countries, and in India, Brazil, Argentina, the United States and elsewhere. This rise of the far right has been accompanied by a massive increase on attacks on queer and trans people. In Turkey between 12-14 September, in coordinated overnight raids across five cities, Turkish police targeted seven LGBTQI+ rights organizations, two groups supporting people living with HIV, and 13 bars and clubs where queer people gather. Board members of some of the country’s oldest LGBTQI+ associations, including Kaos GL and Lambda Istanbul, were

taken from their homes

. Human Rights Watch reports that at least

112 people were arrested and that 82 remain in detention

 by court order. On 3/4 October Taiwan police

raided a Taipei queer bar

 detaining 51 persons and abusing disabled customers.

At the same time, increasingly authoritarian states, including Germany, are seeking to erase trans existence through administrative violence, putting barriers in front of access to trans healthcare. As European governments divert public spending to remilitarisation efforts, access to housing, welfare, jobs and education become circumscribed. In the UK, the drastically curtailed access to trans healthcare in recent years has led to trans suicides on an

unprecedented scale

. Recent government guidelines on so-called 'single sex spaces' are likely to cause more deaths such as that of trans woman, Joelle, who died after being

denied cancer care for 16 days

. A stark example of the hypocrisy on the part of the ruling elite came on 21 October when openly gay Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jette and his partner celebrated the expected arrival of their child, while his government

denies queer refugees the right to family reunification

. The attacks on queer and trans people are accompanied by attacks on, and further marginalisation of the disabled, migrants and refugees, precarious workers, poor Black, Brown and Indigenous communities, the unhoused and incarcerated, compounded for those in multiple of these categories. It is a tell-tale sign of fascism when particular communities are rendered vulnerable, disposable and presented as scapegoats for the various harmful effects of racialised capitalism. 

That the relatively small community of queer and trans people, and racialised trans femmes in particular, has become a target for (proto-)fascist and authoritarian regimes globally is no surprise. Transness especially stands out as a visible transgression of cis hetero patriarchal norms on which fascist authority is built. It forms a thorn in the eye of regimes dependent on popular internalisation of its structural "truths". Transness thus becomes a powerful wedge issue that allows states to whip up fear and distrust of trans people which is consolidated through state carceral and administrative violence. It is also no surprise that state attacks on queer and trans people are on the rise globally at a time when Gen Z, along with older social movements are rising up in France, Albania, Brazil, India, Argentina, Indonesia, Greece and across the planet. Time and again, queer and trans people have stood at the helm of

social movements and popular struggles for liberation

.


The 18 October attack on The Dolls of Berlin at Casa Kuá is historic. Coming at this conjuncture in history, it is signaling the moment that demands we all stand up not only …

Κάλεσμα/Αφίσα από

Η τόσο μεγάλη συμμετοχή των γυναικών στον Δημοκρατικό Στρατο αποτέλεσε ένα ανατρεπτικό γεγονός για όλη την ελληνική κοινωνία, το οποίο ήταν δύσκολο να το κατανοήσει, να το ερμηνεύσει και να το εντάξει -ακόμα και σήμερα- στη συλλογιστική της. author: Andrea DiP
title: Um beijo em uma mulher trans
content:
A cena toda deve ter durado cerca de três segundos: A deputada federal Erika Hilton (Psol-SP) faz um vídeo comemorando a eleição de Lula após a contagem das urnas, no dia 25 de outubro. Ele passa por ela, pega seu rosto, tasca um beijo carinhoso em sua bochecha e sai do quadro. Um gesto simples, espontâneo, terno, um carinho. 


Eu não sei se Lula tem noção do tamanho da declaração que fez pro mundo.

 O presidente de um país, que acaba de ser reeleito em um processo histórico e inédito em tantos níveis – com participação popular e engajamento sociais sem igual, em uma virada épica que acontece apesar de todo tipo de sabotagem das

Big Techs

 ao governo Trump, de tentativas de boicote ao

transporte público

 para que as pessoas não chegassem às urnas a uma grande imprensa tacanha jogando contra –

um homem de 81 anos, que tem os olhos do mundo virados para si, mostra publicamente afeto a uma mulher trans. 


Trecho de vídeo publicado por Erika Hilton


Essa cena me emociona por diferentes motivos. Tenho passado os últimos anos me infiltrando em eventos da extrema direita pelo mundo e entrevistando essas figuras. Posso afirmar que não houve um desses congressos sequer, nenhuma dessas conversas, que não passou por discursos ultraviolentos contra pessoas trans. 


Já escrevi bastante sobre isso, inclusive sobre como no governo Trump essa violência levou a resoluções e políticas públicas desde seu primeiro dia de mandato. Não vou me repetir aqui sobre a maneira como essas narrativas são construídas com base no pânico moral e na ideia da destruição da família e de valores sagrados. O que quero ressaltar é que

a demonização de pessoas trans está hoje no epicentro político da extrema direita. É um tema de consenso entre eles, usado para mobilizar o medo, o ressentimento e o ódio e que tem efeitos concretos na vida de milhares de pessoas. 


E a mobilização desses afetos não é exclusiva da extrema direita, também é importante dizer. Não sei dizer quantas vezes eu mesma fui perseguida, ameaçada e exposta por mulheres que se dizem feministas radicais trans excludentes ou quantas vezes o Pauta Pública foi alvo de ódio quando apontamos nosso microfone para pessoas trans. Tudo bem. Como me disse Judith Butler, ser perseguida por essas pessoas é um distintivo de coragem. 


Um outro ponto importante é que

o Brasil é um dos países que mais mata transexuais no mundo

. Quando Lula faz esse gesto, que mensagem ele manda para o povo? E que mensagem ele manda para as pessoas trans?


A cena me lembrou o relato de Suzanne Hommel, uma alemã nascida em 1938 que falou no documentário “Encontro com Lacan” sobre o tempo em que foi paciente do psicanalista francês. Ela carregava traumas profundos de sua vivência durante a Segunda Guerra Mundial, mas, em uma de suas sessões com Lacan, contou de um sonho recorrente que a acordava sob forte angústia todos os dias pontualmente às 5h da manhã. Acrescentou o contexto histórico de sua infância: “Era às 5h da manhã que a Gestapo vinha buscar os judeus em suas casas”. Ao ouvir a palavra “Gestapo” (polícia secreta oficial da Alemanha Nazista) o psicanalista levantou-se rapidamente da poltrona e fez um carinho suave em seu rosto. Quando ela conta isso no documentário, imediatamente leva a mão ao rosto imitando o gesto. 


Através desse ato físico e verbal, Lacan transformou a palavra “Gestapo” em “geste à peau”, que em francês significa “gesto na pele”, e introduziu ternura onde antes habitava apenas o horror e o trauma. No documentário, ela se emociona ao dizer que isso não apagou seu sofrimento mas o modificou de forma definitiva e que mesmo décadas depois, ela ainda sentia aquele toque que mudou a forma como olhava para a própria história e sua própria dor. 


O “geste à peau” de Lula em Erika Hilton neste momento da nossa história, me parece muito poderoso, simbólico, um marco de posição diante do mundo, que pode ressignificar um monte de afetos pra muita gente. E ao mesmo tempo é tão bonito precisamente porque foi um afago espontâneo em um país que está ressignificando sua relação com a política, que ainda sofre com o trauma dos quatro anos sob o governo genocida de Bolsonaro – e que escolheu neste domingo apostar na ternura ao invés do horror.


Aliás, que fique marcado aqui: Erika Hilton foi reeleita como a mulher mais votada da história para a Câmara dos Deputados e, com 1,5 milhão de votos conquistados em São Paulo, é a segunda parlamentar no país a romper a barreira de 1 milhão de votos …

Queer/Feminist Alternatives to Both Historical Anarchism and State Systems

Benevolent State Control vs. Community Care

Cindy Barukh Milstein. 2024. Constellations of Care: Anarcha-Feminism in Practice. London: Pluto Press.

Constellations of Care is an anthology of answers to a fundamental question: what do people do to survive and thrive from the margins of society? According to the volume’s editor, Cindy Barukh Milstein, the goal of state-based systems is not to provide prosperity and security for all. Rather, they strategically reserve material and political protections for those who conform to a masculine and heteronormative model of the ‘good citizen’. The various authors of this anthology, all members of various anarcha-feminist collectives, employ the praxis of anarcha-feminism to suggest that resistance to state-based exclusion depends first and foremost on the practice of care, sustaining and building relationships that give life to those without political and economic power or opportunities, who unwittingly or willingly do not conform to the standards desired by the state. Empowerment and social transformation are not driven by massive state projects, but by interpersonal and highly specific interventions managed by those who share the ontological experience of exclusion through inhabiting queer or feminine bodies.

What follows is a collection of histories, reflections, conversations, and artwork that reflect collective, anti-hierarchical, and locally organized efforts to care for a global network of the excluded. Whether written by underground abortion care providers in Poland, communal kitchen collectives that sustained anti-government protests in Colombia, or unhoused and precarious sex workers in Philadelphia who hold weekly needle exchanges, each of its thirty-seven entries offers an approach to creating communities by and for the marginalized.

In some ways, Milstein’s work sits at odds with a strictly academic style of writing. One of the first entries in the book, written by members of the Nightshade collective in Philadelphia, actively denounces the ability of formal academia to understand and advance anarchist theory, suggesting that academia is inherently hierarchical, focuses on creating grand universalist theory rather than accepting theoretical plurality, and gatekeeps legitimacy through economically restricting access to academic credentials (p. 24). Constellations of Care is based on the idea that theory is created, interpreted, and used not by researchers, but by the everyday stakeholders in the political processes that it analyzes. The book emphasizes alternatives to academic style in some of its editorial choices. For example, each section’s author biography veers away from listing degrees or institutional affiliations, and rather briefly chronicles the author’s skill sets and political positions, as well as their close relationships to both communities and geographies, often defined by a city or an Indigenous land designation, rather than a nationality …

author: CMI Argentina
title: Denuncian la continuidad de mujeres alojadas en una comisaría clausurada
content:
El Juzgado de Ejecución N° 2 de La Plata a cargo de Juan José Ruiz, ordenó mantener la prohibición de alojamiento en la Comisaría 3

a

 de Los Hornos, La Plata, y que se traslade a las mujeres detenidas a dependencias habilitadas y con condiciones dignas de alojamiento. La Comisión Provincial por la Memoria (CPM) presentó una acción de habeas corpus colectivo, en su calidad de Mecanismo Local de Prevención de la Tortura, cuando relevó en una de las inspecciones que realiza regularmente en lugares de encierro, que había seis mujeres alojadas irregularmente, en condiciones inhumanas y sin acceso a derechos básicos.


A partir de las tareas de monitoreo que realiza la CPM en su calidad de Mecanismo Local de Prevención de la Tortura de la Provincia de Buenos Aires, se realizó una inspección en la comisaría tercera de Los Hornos, La Plata, donde se relevaron seis mujeres alojadas en los calabozos, pese a que la dependencia cuenta con una clausura administrativa y judicial vigente para el alojamiento de personas.


Las condiciones de detención además eran tortuosas: hacinadas en celdas pequeñas y sucias, con insectos, materia fecal de roedores y olor a pis, sin ventanas y con la luz encendida 24 horas. Los baños estaban tapados y a punto de desbordarse, por lo que debían orinar en botellas y no contaban con agua caliente para higienizarse.


El Juzgado de Ejecución Penal N° 1 de La Plata, a cargo de Juan José Ruiz, ordenó mantener la prohibición de ingreso de personas privadas de libertad a esa comisaría, y dispuso el traslado inmediato de las mujeres que a la fecha se encontraban allí alojadas hacia ámbitos habilitados y en condiciones dignas de detención.


Se ordenó también a los titulares del Ministerio de Justicia y Derechos Humanos y del Ministerio de Seguridad de la provincia de Buenos Aires que realicen tareas de mantenimiento y limpieza en celdas, reparación de sanitarios, desobstrucción de desagües cloacales, fumigación y desinfección de celdas e instalación de un termotanque para la provisión de agua caliente. Además, ordenó que se garantice la inmediata atención médica y psicológica de las detenidas frente a la situación de falta de acceso a la salud que padecían, hecho que refirieron en entrevistas con el equipo de monitoreo.


En su fallo subrayó que “resulta claro la aflicción de derechos humanos específicos -personas privadas de libertad-, condiciones dignas de vida y de acuerdo a parámetros de derechos humanos en alojamiento”, y consideró que “los lugares de alojamiento en donde los privados de la libertad deben llevar adelante su respectiva sanción punitiva, necesariamente deben reunir condiciones de infraestructura dignas y humanitarias para un efectivo y real cumplimiento del fin perseguido con aquella sanción, pues de lo contrario, ese fin se convierte en una mera ficción. Considero que el tratamiento institucional es sencillamente el trato que se les brinda en la institución a las personas privadas de la libertad”.


De acuerdo a los datos recabados y publicados por la CPM en su sitio Datos abiertos, en el año 2025 un 33% de las comisarías se encontraban clausuradas, ya sea a través de la justicia o administrativamente, y aun así alojaban el 12% de las personas detenidas en dependencias policiales. Para más información acerca de las comisarías bonaerenses, ver: 

https://www.comisionporlamemoria.org/datosabiertos/comisarias-datos/

author: Paul Gregoire
title: Allega Spender pushes to remove religious exemptions against LGBTIQ students, teachers
content:
The Sex Discrimination and Fair Work Amendment (Equality in Treatment in Religious Schools) Bill 2026, introduced on October 12, seeks to repeal the offending exemptions in federal sex discrimination law as well as removing the related provisions in federal workplace relations law. It also extends protections to associates of those who are captured under the current exemptions.

Section 38 of the Sex Discrimination Act 1984 (SDA) makes it lawful for religious education institutions to discriminate against a teacher, student or contract worker due to their “sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital or relationship status or pregnancy”.

The proposal took centre stage in 2018, as the national religious freedoms debate took off prior to then-Coalition Prime Minister Scott Morrison shooting it down.

Morrison’s push to establish a religious freedoms regime in 2018 uncovered their existence. His years-long religious crusade was defeated after debate on these exemptions.

Labor PM Anthony Albanese promised to progress the reform in 2022, but changed his mind.

Spender, independent MP for Wentworth, is pushing popular reforms, despite far-right commentators claiming it as an attack on religious freedom.

“These exemptions have already been removed in state and territory law, to varying degrees, but there are no national standards,” Spender told NSW Parliament on October 12.

“The Australian Law Reform Commission’s 2024 review found that religious schools could still maintain their ethos without this exemption.

“At its heart, section 38 of the Sex Discrimination Act is repealed in its entirety and replaced with a far narrower provision,” Spender said in her second reading speech on her private member’s bill.

“Protections are also extended to a person’s associates ... This means a child cannot be treated differently just because she has two mums.”

The bill repeals the current provisions affecting students, teachers and contract workers in section 38, replacing it with a provision that allows institutions to preference staff based on faith in two ways — at their initial employment and in the promotion of senior leadership roles such as “principal, vice-principal, religious education teacher, chaplain” or any other comparable role.

The bill inserts section 7AAA into the SDA, which makes it unlawful to discriminate against an associate, such as a spouse or relative, of a person protected under the Act. It removes provisions that permitted discrimination based on sex, sexuality or gender.

It also repeals provisions in the Fair Work Act 2009 that extend discrimination into workplace agreements.

“But preferencing is not a licence to discriminate,” Spender said. “A school can choose a candidate because of their faith. It cannot fire someone because of their sexuality. Many students have wonderful, formative experiences at religious schools. Many LGBTQIA+ students come out to their friends and teachers in these schools and are accepted. But … this is not everyone’s experience.”

The exemptions in section 38 of the SDA relating to sexual orientation and gender identity, were inserted into the Act when a 2013 bill added anti-discrimination provisions into the law that related to sexual orientation, gender identity and intersex characteristics. The exemptions in respect of gay and transgender individuals joined pre-existing ones that permitted discrimination based on sex.

The October 2018 Ruddock review into religious freedoms recommended tightening these exemptions in federal law, which drew attention to and then condemnation of the laws.

While Morrison initially tried to downplay the outcry, he reversed course and promised to repeal the discriminatory measures targeting students. But Morrison, a Pentecostal, attempted to progress three versions of the Religious Freedoms Bill — two in 2019 and one in 2022 — and the removal of any exemptions was forgotten.

Each version of the religious freedoms legislation was increasingly watered down.

Three years of debate on these laws made it clear that his measures sought religious privileges.

The public debate over religious concerns is different to the present, with the conservative push to insert the controversial International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance definition of antisemitism into all levels of government to curb criticism of Israel and its genocide.

author: Brooke Migdon
title: Ballot Measures Will Impact LGBTQ+ Rights in 7 States This Election
content:
Voters will decide how trans youth can participate in school sports, access gender-affirming health care, and more.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

Voters in seven states this fall will weigh more than half a dozen ballot initiatives with direct bearings on LGBTQ+ people — disproportionately on transgender youth. They come as LGBTQ+ rights issues feature heavily in campaigns for candidates on either side of the aisle in the final stretch of November’s midterm elections, which will determine party control of Congress and several key governorships.

Nearly half of LGBTQ+-related ballot initiatives this year would restrict trans student-athletes from competing in line with their gender identity, an issue championed overwhelmingly by Republicans and by a rising share of Democrats. Others would ban certain transition-related treatments for minors — another focus of conservative candidates and President Donald Trump’s second administration.

Since 2021, more than half the nation has adopted laws barring trans students from playing on school sports teams matching their gender identity, and 27 states have banned gender-affirming care for trans youth. Nationally, the number of trans students who participate in school sports is unknown, but is believed to be relatively low: The Williams Institute estimates that just over 300,000 13- to 17-year-olds in the United States are trans, and not all of them will play sports.

In Washington state, where voters will decide this fall whether to ban trans student-athletes from teams matching their gender identity, the organization governing high school sports told The 19th that it is aware of about 10 trans middle and high schoolers who play sports out of more than 200,000 students who compete statewide.

Other ballot initiatives appearing before voters this fall include measures to change the state constitution to expand nondiscrimination protections for LGBTQ+ people; formally repeal language against same-sex marriages and modify students’ and parents’ rights in schools.

Here’s where LGBTQ+ rights are on the ballot this November.

Arizona voters will decide this fall whether trans student-athletes may continue to compete on school sports teams that align with their gender identity. A ballot initiative introduced late last year by state Rep. Selina Bliss, a Republican running for reelection, would effectively restore a 2022 state law restricting trans athletes’ participation that a federal appeals court had blocked in 2024.

Kris Mayes, Arizona’s Democratic attorney general, has declined to defend the law in court.

Bliss’ proposal would require public and qualifying private schools to designate K-12 sports teams as exclusively “male,” “female” or “coeducational” based on participating students’ “biological status at birth.” It would also bar trans students from using restrooms, locker rooms and other spaces “integral to athletic engagement” that match their gender identity.

In July, a lawsuit challenging the measure claimed it violated a requirement that Arizona ballot initiatives address only a single subject and was “misleading to the point of fraud.” A state superior court judge later ruled that the initiative could remain on the November 3 ballot.

Colorado voters will decide whether to bar trans student-athletes from competing in line with their gender identity by designating K-12 and collegiate sports teams based on students’ “biological reproductive systems.” The ballot initiative qualified for the general election after Protect Kids Colorado, the organization behind it, collected more than 168,000 signatures statewide.

Voters will also decide whether to ban transition-related surgeries for minors, and whether state or federal funds, Medicaid reimbursements or insurance coverage can be used to help pay for them. Such surgeries are already rare. The measure, also introduced by Protect Kids Colorado, does not directly mention nonsurgical care.

State medical organizations, including the Colorado Academy of Family Physicians and the Colorado Medical Society (CMS), the state’s largest organized group of practitioners, have publicly opposed the healthcare-related initiative. “CMS members hold diverse political views but share a core principle: medical decisions belong in the exam room,” Brigitta Robinson, the organization’s president, said in September.

author: Jillian Kestler-D’Amours
title: Masked White Supremacists Are Stoking Residential School Denialism in Canada
content:
“We have endured fear, and we will not be intimidated,” one Indigenous leader said.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

It was 3:00 am when Doug George-Kanentiio first arrived at the Mohawk Institute Residential School in Brantford, Ontario, in 1967.

He was 11 years old, and he would go on to spend 18 months at the abusive institution, which was Canada’s longest-running residential school. The notorious school operated for more than 140 years before it closed in 1970.

“They weren’t places of learning, they were places of confinement,” George-Kanentiio said.

Decades later, he still remembers the hunger, fear, and brutality that he and the other Indigenous children who were forced to attend the Mohawk Institute endured there every day.

“Anything you could imagine [being done] to a child, when it comes to abuse, that’s what these individuals did,” said George-Kanentiio, who is from Akwesasne, a Kanien’kehá:ka (Mohawk) community on the U.S.-Canada border, between New York state and the provinces of Ontario and Quebec.

“It was physically painful and extraordinarily cruel,” he told Truthout.

More than 150,000 First Nations, Metis, and Inuit children were separated from their families and forced to attend residential schools across Canada between the 1870s and the mid-1990s.

The institutions — which aimed to forcibly assimilate Indigenous children into the country’s predominantly white European culture — were rife with physical, sexual, and psychological abuse.

The children were barred from speaking their languages, and thousands are believed to have died while in attendance due to abuse, malnutrition, and rampant disease that resulted from squalid conditions. In 2015, a federal commission of inquiry said the system amounted to “cultural genocide.”

Yet while George-Kanentiio and other survivors have spoken about their abuse for years, efforts to downplay, minimize, and distort facts about the residential school system are getting louder in Canada.

The rising wave of residential school denialism has drawn widespread alarm as Indigenous community leaders and other experts say right-wing figures are trying to derail truth and reconciliation — the process of investigating and redressing the devastating impacts of Canada’s colonial policies, including its residential school system — while harming survivors in the process.

Niigaanwewidam Sinclair, an Indigenous studies professor at the University of Manitoba, likened residential school denialism to Holocaust denialism.

“They’ll say, ‘We’re just asking questions, it’s free speech, we’re trying to just tell the other side,’” he told Truthout.

“They weren’t places of learning, they were places of confinement.”

But he emphasized that residential school denialists are not really interested in a “good-faith conversation.” Instead, Sinclair said, they have two main goals: to “monetize ignorance” and to gain public attention.

“They’re trying to profit off of the fact that for 150 years Canadians were miseducated about Indigenous peoples and residential schools in particular,” he explained.

The issue came to a very public head last month when a group of about two dozen masked men affiliated with white nationalist group Second Sons Canada gathered on the lands of Tk̓emlúps te Secwépemc, an Indigenous (First Nation) community in the province of British Columbia.

Tk̓emlúps te Secwépemc has faced years of pressure from denialists since it announced in 2021 that a preliminary radar search of the grounds of the former Kamloops Indian Residential School had uncovered the potential remains of more than 200 children.

The discovery sparked a reckoning across Canada as people demanded justice for the myriad crimes committed at residential schools, which were funded by the government but run by various churches.

But the findings in Tk̓emlúps te Secwépemc also fueled denialism, with far right activists and politicians seizing on early reporting errors to accuse the community and media outlets of lying.

“The entire country is motivated and moving towards implementing truth and reconciliation,” whereas denialists are “trying to slow things down, and they’re trying to profit,” said Sinclair.

The men who entered Tk̓emlúps te Secwépemc in late September hung a banner on an overpass that day reading, “Got bones?” — a reference to the 2021 discovery of possible remains …

author: Unknown
title: Fransa'da ırkçılık ve İslamofobi karşıtı gösteriler düzenlendi
content:
Fransa'da farklı sendika, dernek ve kitle örgütü kuruluşlarının çağrısıyla Paris, Strazburg, Roubaix, Stains, Nanterre, La Courneuve dahil farklı kentlerde ırkçılık karşıtları bir araya geldi.

Ülkede artan ırkçılığa ve İslamofobiye tepki verilen gösterilerde, 23 Ekim'de Yvelines ilinde düzenlenen terör saldırısında hayatını kaybeden Kongo asıllı Fransız Pengo Bossio Wangi anıldı.

Gösterilerde, söz konusu ırkçı saldırıda yaralanan 1'i çocuk olmak üzere 5 kişiye yönelik destek mesajları da dile getirildi.

Başkent Paris'te Stalingrad Muharebesi Meydanı'nda yerel saatle 19.00'da başlayan gösteriye yüzlerce kişi katıldı.

Göstericiler, "Irkçılık bir görüş değil, hayatları paramparça eden bir suçtur", "Paramparça olan hayatlardan ziyade kırılan vitrinlere şefkat gösteriyorlar" ve "Irkçılık öldürür" yazılı pankartlar taşıdı.

Göstericiler, ırkçı söylemleri yaymakla suçlanan CNews kanalında çalışan bir gazetecinin gösteriye katılmasına "CNews dışarı" ve "CNews katil, (Cumhurbaşkanı Emmanuel) Macron suç ortağı" sloganları atarak tepki gösterdi.

Irkçılıkla mücadele derneği SOS Racisme'in Başkanı Dominique Sopo, burada yaptığı konuşmada, birkaç yıldır ülkede ırkçı saikli suçların yeniden işlenmeye başlandığını söyledi.

Sopo, bazı medya organlarının bünyelerinde ırkçı söylemlerin sarf edilmesine izin verdiğini belirterek, bu söylemin son derece "ciddi" olduğuna dikkati çekti.

Yvelines'e bağlı Trappes kentindeki saldırıyı yapan teröristin "siyahilere ve Araplara saldırarak 17 Ekim'deki gösterilerinde, dükkanı yağmalanan esnafın öcünü almak istediğini" dile getirdiğini aktaran Sopo, terör saldırısından birkaç gün önce Fransız televizyon kanallarında eylemlerdeki yağma olaylarıyla ilgili ırkçı bir çerçeve kullanıldığını belirtti.

Trappes Belediye Başkanı Ali Rabeh ise Ulusal Birlik (RN) Partisi Başkanı Jordan Bardella'nın daha önce Trappes kentini "Paris'e 30 dakika mesafedeki Kabil'e" benzettiğini hatırlattı.

Rabeh, Trappes'a yönelik damgalayıcı sözler kullananları terör saldırısının failine silah vermekle suçlayarak, "Kanallarda durmaksızın aktarılan yabancılara, göçmenlere, Müslümanlara karşı sarf edilen nefret söylemleri, Fransızların bir kısmının insanlıktan çıkarılmasına neden oldu." dedi.

Bu durumun, bu kişilerin "iç düşmanlar" gibi gösterilmesine sebebiyet verdiğini kaydeden Rabeh, ırkçılık zehrinin tüm ülkeye bulaştığını dile getirdi.

Irkçılık Karşıtı Koalisyon'dan yapılan açıklamaya göre, Paris'te Cumhuriyet Meydanı'nda düzenlenmesi planlanan bir diğer gösteri, Paris Emniyet Müdürlüğünce yasaklandı.

Sosyal medyaya yansıyan görüntülere göre, bazı göstericiler, yasağa rağmen Cumhuriyet Meydanı yakınlarında toplandı.

Sokakta yere oturan göstericiler, Fransa'nın ulusal marşı La Marseillaise'i okudu.

Polis, eylemi dağıtmak için kalkanlarıyla göstericileri iterek bölgeden uzaklaştırmaya çalıştı.

Yvelines ilinde 23 Ekim'de bir kişi, bulunduğu araçtan etraftakilere ateş açmıştı. Saldırıda 1 kişi hayatını kaybetmiş, 5 kişi ağır yaralanmıştı.

39 yaşındaki saldırgan Kevin T, olay yerinde gözaltına alınmıştı.

Fransa Cumhurbaşkanı Emmanuel Macron, saldırının ırkçı nitelikte bir terör saldırısı olduğunu duyurmuştu.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: anonerror
title: [Valladolid] Apertura de nuevo local de CNT
content:
Antifascistas, antirracistas, anticapitalistas, transfeministas e internacionalistas. En medio de una convocatoria de huelga general por la vivienda y contra todos los poderes que viven de desangrar a la clase trabajadora, CNT Valladolid inaugura un nuevo local en calle Merced, 6, de Valladolid, entre las plazas de Santa Cruz y Circular.


Hace más de dos años empezamos un proyecto muy ilusionante. Nuestro local se quedaba pequeño y teníamos que buscar otro. Hicimos un proceso de reflexión colectiva, para tener claras nuestras necesidades presentes y futuras. Una tienda de fontanería se ha convertido en un sindicato como el nuestro, con más salas donde reunirse, un salón amplio en el que convocar actos… Un nuevo espacio en Valladolid a disposición de todas las personas trabajadoras.


A pesar de que quedan retoques, el pasado 17 de octubre nos decidimos a abrir puertas en un acto en el que nos reunimos la afiliacIón con personas afines del presente y del futuro. Contamos con las actuaciones de Jesús Puebla Mimo, de Rubén Ruiz, Rosa Vicente y José Luis Alonso, de Chusma y de Juguillos, de Astrolabio, y tuvimos ocasión de mover el esqueleto con las aportaciones de Eva DJ. No faltaron el recorrido por el nuevo local, el picoteo hecho a mano en comida y bebida, y sobre todo las ganas de llenar de vida esta nueva casa para la rebeldía y la defensa frente a empresaurios y politicastros de todos nuestros derechos actuales y los que nos inventemos en el futuro. Para todo ello y más, contad con CNT, vuestra herramienta de lucha, vuestro sindicato de clase, vuestra alternativa sindical.


A continuación hemos puesto en marcha unas jornadas de inauguración de las que tenéis información en las redes y web de CNT.


Reproducimos a continuación el manifiesto que refleja esta nueva etapa:


Hoy, sábado, 17 de octubre, inauguramos una nueva etapa en CNT Valladolid.


Estrenamos un espacio más amplio. Un espacio donde pueda entrar más gente, donde podamos encontrarnos, organizarnos y construir juntas una respuesta colectiva a la realidad que vivimos.


Porque este local no es solamente un lugar nuevo. Es un espacio de encuentro para quienes entendemos que nuestros derechos no son concesiones, que la dignidad no se negocia y que nuestra fuerza está en la lucha obrera.


Y cuando decimos clase trabajadora, no hablamos solo de quienes tienen un contrato o un empleo. También hablamos de quienes trabajan sin derechos, de quienes sostienen los cuidados y de quienes encuentran las puertas cerradas al empleo por su identidad o su condición.


Porque si el sistema utiliza esas diferencias para dividirnos y para colocar a unas personas en posiciones de mayor vulnerabilidad, el sindicalismo tiene que hacer justamente lo contrario:

reconocernos como parte de una misma clase y organizarnos juntas.


Por eso abrimos este espacio.


Para que haya más gente, más organización y más lucha.


Porque somos CNT.


CNT tiene una historia profundamente ligada a la organización de la clase trabajadora y a la lucha por los derechos laborales y sociales.


Antes que este local, CNT tuvo varios, cada uno con su historia: desahucios, asaltos policiales, atentados… Desde la calle Francisco Zarandona multiplicó por diez su afiliación en tiempos de la segunda republica; desde los pactos de la moncloa, superando multiples dificultades, hemos crecido en varios locales en Valladolid que han ido abriendo cada vez más brecha en la provincia y en la ciudad. Hasta llegar a este en el que nos encontramos


Somos anarcosindicalistas. Entendemos que quienes vivimos de nuestro trabajo tenemos capacidad para defender nuestros derechos colectivamente y para construir otras formas de relacionarnos y organizarnos frente a la explotación.


Tenemos una memoria sindical fuerte y combativa. Pero no queremos convertir esa memoria en una fotografía, ni mirar hacia atrás únicamente para recordar lo que fuimos.

Nuestra memoria nos obliga a mirar hacia delante.


Porque el sistema contra el que se organizaron quienes nos precedieron no ha desaparecido. La explotación adopta nuevas formas. La precariedad se normaliza. Trabajar ya no garantiza unas condiciones de vida dignas. Y quienes acumulan riqueza siguen teniendo capacidad para decidir sobre nuestras vidas.


Por eso estamos aquí.


Porque la lucha sigue.


Y esa lucha sigue hoy en múltiples frentes que se complementan.


Una de ellas es la

lucha antifascista

.


Estamos viendo crecer discursos que alimentan el odio y el miedo …

author: dev
title: Quelques mots sur Trappes, la nécropolitique et le traitement des « pillages »
content:
L'attentat raciste du 23 octobre, qui a tué Pengo Bossio Wangi et blessé cinq autres personnes dont une enfant de 12 ans, on aurait pu le prévoir, et on aurait dû l'empêcher. Malgré la violence et le harcèlement auxquels leurs luttes les exposent, c'est contre une telle actualisation de la violence raciste que se mobilisent chaque jour les militant.es antiracistes. Par son abjection monstrueuse, l'assassinat déchire la réalité mais il n'est pas moins le produit de cette réalité, et de tout ce qui en elle relève, jusque dans l'apparente normalité des discours quotidiens, de la mécanique organisée du racisme.


Que le racisme soit en cours d'intensification en France, et qu'il tue, on le savait. Que tous les discours, politiques, intellectuels, médiatiques, qui relativisent ou nient l'existence du racisme - allant même jusqu'à remettre en question le terme d'

islamophobie

author: Elliot Downes
title: NT government closes Darwin’s largest homelessness shelter
content:
Residents of Darwin’s largest homelessness shelter were evicted by the Northern Territory government on 12 October, and relocated to Batchelor, a town 100 kilometres away.

Yilli Short Stay Accommodation (YiSSA), which is run by Yilli Rreung Housing Aboriginal Corporation, was home to hundreds of people, mostly Aboriginal. Many have experienced domestic violence and are living with serious health conditions, including kidney conditions requiring dialysis. 

Residents from communities across the territory would stay at YiSSA while accessing medical care or other services in Darwin. Nearly 400 people were directly affected by the closure of the facility, including 160 children.

YiSSA’s closure will place more pressure on remaining homelessness services in Darwin. Meanwhile, the minority of residents transferred to the smaller facility in Batchelor will not have the same access to support networks, food, healthcare and education. Batchelor is a town with a population of around 500, a small health clinic and no public transport. 

The closure of a key homelessness service is particularly egregious given the Northern Territory has the highest rate of homelessness in the country. According to data released last year by the Australian Institute of Health and Welfare, 

one in every 25 Territorians requires homelessness assistance

, and Aboriginal people make up 89 percent of those accessing homelessness services in the Northern Territory.

As the biggest landlord in the territory, the Northern Territory government is largely to blame for this situation. Territorians on the emergency public housing waiting list can expect to 

wait up to a decade for a roof over their head

. The government is also responsible for the apartheid-like conditions in Aboriginal town camps on the outskirts of places like Darwin and Alice Springs, as well as the overcrowding in remote communities.

The closure of YiSSA was announced by the ruling Country Liberal Party (CLP) in July. Ostensibly, it was due to a failure to secure a deal with Ausco, the owner of the buildings and other infrastructure on the Crown land site. But in reality, it was a political decision. 

After years of renting the demountable buildings, the government offered to buy them for $3 million—the equivalent of just one year’s rent. When this offer was rejected by Ausco, the federal government proposed to cover the cost of the purchase on the condition that Yilli Rreung continue running the service.

The CLP rejected the offer of federal funding, with Chief Minister Lia Finocchiaro calling it a 

“waste of taxpayers’ hard-earned money”

. Yet it has cost 

$16.25 million to establish and fund the Batchelor facility

, run by Mission Australia.

The announcement of YiSSA’s closure sparked a campaign by the activist group, Justice Not Jails (JNJ). It culminated in a 200-strong rally outside of the Australian Homelessness Conference in Darwin just days before residents were to be evicted. 

Anna, an activist with JNJ, told 

Red Flag

 that the decision doesn’t make sense “unless you approach it from an ideological viewpoint. Some of the YiSSA residents have said that [the government] just don’t want Aboriginal people to have a nice, secure place to live.”

The YiSSA closure is symptomatic of a Trumpian government that has targeted Aboriginal people in particular. Since coming to power in 2024, the CLP have lowered the age of criminal responsibility to 10, reintroduced spit hoods in detention, and made it easier for Aboriginal children to be removed from their families and placed into long-term state care.

This has involved a significant expansion in the carceral state, with the prison population 

increasing by 24 percent between 2024 and 2025

, and the Finocchiaro government announcing earlier this year the construction of a new private prison in Darwin. 

The Northern Territory is one of the most incarcerated places in the world, 

second only to El Salvador

, with more than 1 percent of the entire population behind bars. Increasingly, this includes people on remand, who are awaiting trial or sentencing.

According to Anna, the next phase of the campaign will involve putting pressure on the federal Labor government. “There’s been a lot of disagreement between the CLP and Labor about what was actually promised. It’s all really immature and I think disrespectful to the people whose lives are actually being affected,” she told 

Red Flag.

title: El nuevo local de CNT en Valladolid abre sus puertas
content:
Antifascistas, antirracistas, anticapitalistas, transfeministas e internacionalistas. En medio de una convocatoria de huelga general por la vivienda y contra todos los poderes que viven de desangrar a la clase trabajadora, CNT Valladolid inaugura un nuevo local en calle Merced, 6, de Valladolid, entre las plazas de Santa Cruz y Circular.


Hace más de dos años empezamos un proyecto muy ilusionante. Nuestro local se quedaba pequeño y teníamos que buscar otro. Hicimos un proceso de reflexión colectiva, para tener claras nuestras necesidades presentes y futuras. Una tienda de fontanería se ha convertido en un sindicato como el nuestro, con más salas donde reunirse, un salón amplio en el que convocar actos… Un nuevo espacio en Valladolid a disposición de todas las personas trabajadoras.


A pesar de que quedan retoques, el pasado 17 de octubre nos decidimos a abrir puertas en un acto en el que nos reunimos la afiliacIón con personas afines del presente y del futuro. Contamos con las actuaciones de Jesús Puebla MImo, de Rubén Ruiz, Rosa Vicente y José Luis Alonso, de Chusma y de Juguillos, de Astrolabio, y tuvimos ocasión de mover el esqueleto con las aportaciones de Eva DJ. No faltaron el recorrido por el nuevo local, el picoteo hecho a mano en comida y bebida, y sobre todo las ganas de llenar de vida esta nueva casa para la rebeldía y la defensa frente a empresaurios y politicastros de todos nuestros derechos actuales y los que nos inventemos en el futuro. Para todo ello y más, contad con CNT, vuestra herramienta de lucha, vuestro sindicato de clase, vuestra alternativa sindical.


A continuación hemos puesto en marcha unas jornadas de inauguración de las que tenéis información en inauguracion.cntvalladolid.es

Hoy, sábado, 17 de octubre, inauguramos una nueva etapa en CNT Valladolid.


Estrenamos un espacio más amplio. Un espacio donde pueda entrar más gente, donde podamos encontrarnos, organizarnos y construir juntas una respuesta colectiva a la realidad que vivimos.


Porque este local no es solamente un lugar nuevo. Es un espacio de encuentro para quienes entendemos que nuestros derechos no son concesiones, que la dignidad no se negocia y que nuestra fuerza está en la lucha obrera.


Y cuando decimos clase trabajadora, no hablamos solo de quienes tienen un contrato o un empleo. También hablamos de quienes trabajan sin derechos, de quienes sostienen los cuidados y de quienes encuentran las puertas cerradas al empleo por su identidad o su condición.


Porque si el sistema utiliza esas diferencias para dividirnos y para colocar a unas personas en posiciones de mayor vulnerabilidad, el sindicalismo tiene que hacer justamente lo contrario:

reconocernos como parte de una misma clase y organizarnos juntas.


Por eso abrimos este espacio.


Para que haya más gente, más organización y más lucha.


Porque somos CNT


CNT tiene una historia profundamente ligada a la organización de la clase trabajadora y a la lucha por los derechos laborales y sociales.


Antes que este local, CNT tuvo varios, cada uno con su historia: desahucios, asaltos policiales, atentados… Desde la calle Francisco Zarandona multiplicó por diez su afiliación en tiempos de la segunda republica; desde los pactos de la moncloa, superando multiples dificultades, hemos crecido en varios locales en Valladolid que han ido abriendo cada vez más brecha en la provincia y en la ciudad. Hasta llegar a este en el que nos encontramos


Somos anarcosindicalistas. Entendemos que quienes vivimos de nuestro trabajo tenemos capacidad para defender nuestros derechos colectivamente y para construir otras formas de relacionarnos y organizarnos frente a la explotación.


Tenemos una memoria sindical fuerte y combativa. Pero no queremos convertir esa memoria en una fotografía, ni mirar hacia atrás únicamente para recordar lo que fuimos.

Nuestra memoria nos obliga a mirar hacia delante.

author: Sharon Zhang
title: Trump Suggests Ilhan Omar, a US Citizen, Doesn’t Have Constitutional Rights
content:
“She goes, ‘I have constitutional rights.’ The arrogance,” Trump said at a rally in Texas.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

President Donald Trump suggested that Rep. Ilhan Omar (D-Minnesota), a U.S. citizen, should not have constitutional rights because of where she’s from in racist remarks at a rally this week.

“She was from Somalia and she came over and right away she started opening her mouth, ‘I have constitutional rights,’” Trump said mockingly, in the middle of a three-and-a-half minute rant about Omar in Lubbock, Texas, on Tuesday night. “She comes from a country with no government, no counsel, no police, no anything. It’s not even a country. It’s just a piece of land.”

“She goes, ‘I have constitutional rights.’ The arrogance,” Trump said. He then transitioned into making Islamophobic comments about Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed.

Trump has consistently targeted Omar with racist remarks, and has previously called Somalia a “garbage country.”

Trump’s comments on Tuesday suggest that he believes Omar should not be afforded basic rights laid out in the U.S. Constitution, like freedom of speech and religion or the right to a fair trial. Notably, these protections are supposed to apply to everyone within the United States, not just citizens.

Trump has repeatedly remarked on Omar’s right to constitutional protections. He has said some iteration of these comments at many rallies this midterm cycle — including just after Homeland Security Investigations’ pre-dawn raid on her house earlier this month. However, Tuesday’s version is the clearest he’s been about suggesting that Omar doesn’t deserve such rights.

The president’s rant comes as his administration is attempting to denaturalize and deport Omar — part of a mass deportation campaign that critics say has already drastically eroded or is directly violating numerous constitutional liberties.

This is a remarkable rebuke of the Constitution coming from the leader of the party that is attacking people like Omar and El-Sayed as un-American.

Indeed, Republicans in Congress and in Trump’s orbit have repeatedly made comments suggesting that only Christians should be allowed to be in Congress, and that Muslims specifically should be barred from holding office.

At a rally in Ohio on Wednesday night, for instance, Sen. Bernie Moreno (R-Ohio) said that El-Sayed, who was born in Michigan, is an “affront to me as a naturalized citizen of this country” and “can be nowhere near D.C.” His reasoning was that El-Sayed doesn’t understand “that our rights come from God Almighty” and that “Jesus came here for our salvation.”

The GOP’s racist and Islamophobic remarks have become increasingly incendiary as the election has neared. On Wednesday, Sen. Ted Cruz (R-Texas) said that, if El-Sayed were to gain access to classified information, “there is a very real risk that Americans will die as a result” — a remark that critics noted was open incitement to violence.

Just days before the raid on Omar’s house, Trump called for a race war against Somalis in Omar’s home state of Minnesota. In a post on Truth Social, Trump said “The people of Minnesota must fight back” against Somali immigrants in the state.

content:
Fransa’da ırkçı Ulusal Birlik Partisi’nin lideri Marine Le Pen, 15 Ekim’de Brüksel’de düzenlenen Avrupa Birliği liderler zirvesi öncesinde yaptığı açıklamada, Türkiye’ye yönelik AB politikalarının sona erdirilmesini istedi.

Euronews’ün haberine göre Le Pen, Türkiye’ye sağlanan mali desteğin yanı sıra üyelik öncesi politikaların ve kalkınma programlarının da bitirilmesi gerektiğini savundu.

Le Pen, “Üyelik öncesi politikalar, Türkiye’ye destek ve kalkınma programları sona ermeli” ifadelerini kullandı.

Le Pen, açıklamasında Avrupa Komisyonu’nun mevcut yetkilerini de hedef aldı. Komisyonun yetki alanını aştığını öne süren ırkçı lider, kurumun rolünün üye ülkelere hizmet veren bir sekretaryayla sınırlandırılması gerektiğini savundu.

Sağlık ve iç güvenlik gibi alanlarda Komisyonun kendi yetki sınırlarının dışına çıktığını ileri süren Le Pen, Avrupa Birliği’nin ortak karar mekanizmalarının ulusal egemenlikleri zayıflattığını iddia etti.

Avrupa’nın ulusal egemenliklerini koruması, sınır güvenliğini sağlaması ve bağımsız hareket edebilmesi gerektiğini söyleyen Le Pen, mevcut AB politikalarının bu hedefleri karşılamadığını ileri sürdü.

Fransa’nın AB kurumlarının diplomasi, askeri konular ve istihbarat alanlarında daha fazla yetki üstlenmesini kabul etmeyeceğini belirten Le Pen’in açıklamaları, Avrupa Birliği’nin yetki alanı ve Türkiye ile ilişkiler konusunda aşırı sağın yaklaşımını bir kez daha gündeme taşıdı.

Le Pen’in çağrısı, Türkiye’nin AB üyelik süreci ve Birlik tarafından sağlanan mali desteklerin geleceğine ilişkin siyasi tartışmaların sürdüğü bir dönemde geldi.

author: Simón Rodríguez
title: Dominican Republic Cozies Up to Israel Amid Right Wing Surge in Latin America
content:
The government recently adopted the IHRA definition of antisemitism while escalating its ethnic cleansing of Haitians.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

On August 24, the Dominican government adopted the International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance (IHRA) working definition of antisemitism, infamous for equating opposition to Israeli apartheid and Zionist colonialism with antisemitism. President Luis Abinader made the announcement in Santo Domingo, while speaking at an event organized by the U.S. Zionist organization Combat Antisemitism Movement. In 1938, the racist and genocidal Trujillo dictatorship was in power. Just as the Israeli regime pushes for the redefinition of antisemitism to shield itself, in Orwellian fashion, Abinader is rewriting the past to accommodate the neo-Trujilloist present.

It is not surprising that the Dominican government, led by Abinader, would uphold the Trujilloist legacy. This is a government that has denied the significance of slavery during the Spanish colonial period that preceded the formation of the Dominican state, that does not officially commemorate the genocide against Haitians in 1937, known as the Parsley Massacre, and that denies the existence of widespread racism in the Dominican Republic while keeping more than 200,000 Dominicans of Haitian descent stateless. President Abinader boasts of following the ideas of dictator Joaquín Balaguer, one of the Trujillo era’s main ideologues. Abinader follows in Trujillo’s footsteps regarding what Dominican racists dub “the Haitian problem,” as shown by his policy of mass deportations and the construction of a border wall — an aggiornamento of the Trujillo-era political program known as the “Dominicanization of the border.”

Today’s neo-Trujilloist regime, with its apartheid policies of racial mass deportations, denationalization and statelessness, is coherent in its support of the genocidal Israeli regime and in claiming the legacy of the dictatorship. This is the true significance of the Dominican endorsement of the IHRA definition through a statement that upholds the legacy of a totalitarian regime that extorted and killed Jewish refugees.

In the context of the ongoing genocide in Gaza, the Dominican government has signed agreements with Israel on issues such as water management and has acquired Israeli weapons. By adopting the IHRA’s working definition of antisemitism, Abinader now threatens to further erode the weak democratic rights that still exist in this Caribbean country by moving in the direction of weaponizing accusations of antisemitism to criminalize solidarity with Palestine.

Abinader’s total subordination to Trump is another key driver of his support for Israel. The Dominican government has aligned itself with the pro-Trump “Shield of the Americas” regional coalition and has made its airports available for U.S. military operations in the Caribbean and against Venezuela; it has even agreed to accept deportees from third countries arriving from the U.S.

The Dominican government’s alliance with Israel is part of this broader trend, and one of the clearest indicators of the region’s shift to the right is the intensification of ties with Israeli apartheid.

author: Sharon Zhang
title: 98 Percent of Trump’s Refugee Admissions Have Been White South Africans
content:
The openly white supremacist policy is poised to continue through 2027, the administration has said.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

The Trump administration is blocking admissions for nearly every type of refugee — except for white South Africans, who make up nearly all of those admitted under President Donald Trump’s second term so far, data shows.

According to State Department data compiled by economist Steve Rattner, white South Africans make up 98 percent of refugee admissions between February 2025 and July 2026. Of 10,764 refugees admitted in that time, 10,597 originated from South Africa, while only 167 were from other countries.

Most of those from other countries were approved prior to Trump’s executive order last year to prioritize admissions of Afrikaners, per Rattner. Trump and his allies falsely claim the group is being subject to persecution and “white genocide,” which has been repeatedly debunked by experts. In fact, Afrikaners are largely faring fine in the country, owning the vast majority of land in South Africa despite making up only roughly 7 percent of the population.

The State Department’s raw data is even more stark. According to the State Department’s Bureau of Population, Refugees, and Migration, only five refugees out of 16,292 total arrived from Afghanistan, while South Africans made up the remainder in fiscal year 2026, which ranges from October 2025 to September 2026.

Meanwhile, Trump is barring admissions from nearly every other country. Trump capped refugee admissions for fiscal year 2026 at 17,500, near record lows that were previously set during his first term.

By contrast, as Rattner noted, 100,034 refugees were admitted in fiscal year 2024 under President Joe Biden. Roughly a third were from Africa, while 30 percent were from the Near East or South Asia, and another 25 percent were from Latin America or the Caribbean.

The Trump administration is poised to continue this openly white supremacist policy next year. The administration notified Congress last month that it is intending to cap refugee admissions to 17,500 once again in 2027, limited to mostly white South Africans. The notification says that white South Africans are facing land seizures and persecution, while noting that they would be likely to assimilate in the U.S.

The policy comes as the Trump administration has openly embraced racist rhetoric and carried out a mass deportation campaign in which immigration agents are racially profiling their targets. Those originating from Latin American countries have been targeted the most with deportation orders in fiscal year 2026.

Last month, the White House bragged in a post on X that it had cut legal immigration and refugee admissions from majority-Muslim countries by 96 percent between December 2024 and February 2026. Meanwhile, Republicans and Trump administration officials have openly and repeatedly spewed vile Islamophobic rhetoric, including against Somali Muslim Rep. Ilhan Omar (D-Minnesota), who the administration is reportedly attempting to denaturalize and deport.

author: By Dan Feidt, Unicorn Riot
title: ‘Icepick’ Leak Exposes Thousands of Homeland Security Personnel, Groups and More
content:
Washington, DC — There’s been yet another major security breach among federal agencies. The Department of Homeland Security’s ‘single sign-on’ (SSO) login system was reportedly subverted by a hacker going by “Department of Peace” (DoP), which has revealed thousands upon thousands of federal employee records. Around one-fifth of Homeland Security’s personnel have been exposed. Offices and locations are identified in great detail, from Canadian airports to agents in U.S. embassies around the world. Groups assigned within the SSO system, going back at least to 2011, are also exposed, showing the names of globe-spanning activities, and management personnel handling undercover operations.


Thousands of personnel records include supervisors and subordinates, which enabled generating gigantic organizational charts automatically across these agencies.
