title: Henry aus dem Antifa-Ost Verfahren ist gestorben!
content:
Henry Aulich ist tot. Er wurde 38 Jahre und starb heute in den frühen Morgenstunden, nachdem schon vor einigen Tagen die die lebenserhaltenden Maschinen abgeschaltet worden waren. Seit seinem Suizidversuch am 15. August 2026, bei dem er von einer S-Bahn erfasst und schwerst verletzt wurde, war er nicht mehr aus dem Koma erwacht.


Es war ein sonniger Dienstag im August, zu mehreren saßen wir zusammen, nach einem weiteren von über 50 Prozesstagen im Dresdner Antifa-Ost-Verfahren. Thema war auch Henry. Er war an diesem Tag nicht zum Prozess erschienen, denn wegen akuter Suizidalität war er in eine Psychiatrie eingewiesen worden. Vier Tage später sollte er von einer S-Bahn überrollt werden.


Seit 2013 im Visier des Staatsschutzes


Henry war seit 2013 im Visier der sächsischen Repressionsbehörden. Im Zusammenhang mit Ermittlungen gegen die Fanszene der BSG Chemie Leipzig wurde über Jahre gegen ihn wegen des Verdachts der Bildung einer kriminellen Vereinigung ermittelt. Seine Telefone wurden überwacht, er wurde observiert, seine Kontakte erfasst. Auch besonders geschützte Gespräche wurden aufgezeichnet. 2016 wurde das Verfahren eingestellt. Der sächsische Datenschutzbeauftragte beanstandete später das Vorgehen des LKA und der Staatsanwaltschaft Dresden.


Doch damit endete die staatliche Verfolgung nicht. Immer weitere Ermittlungen folgten, und die Wohnung seiner damaligen Partnerin und ihm wurde wiederholt durchsucht, einmal über 14 Stunden lang. Zu Anklagen kam es damals nicht.


Als Henry schließlich 2025 im Antifa-Ost-Verfahren angeklagt wurde, lagen bereits mehr als zwölf Jahre staatlicher Ermittlungen hinter ihm. Jahre, in denen es seinerseits immer auch immer wieder den Wunsch gab zu sterben.


Mehr als 50 Prozesstage und kein Ende


Henry saß nicht in Untersuchungshaft und kam er seit November 2025 zuverlässig zu den Verhandlungen nach Dresden. Über 50 Prozesstage, obwohl ihn nur ein vergleichsweise kleiner Teil der Anklage betraf. Die Verteidigung beantragte wiederholt vergeblich, sein Verfahren abzutrennen.


Auch der Versuch seiner Anwält:innen, einzelne Verhandlungstage früher enden zu lassen, damit Henry an einer notwendigen Therapie teilnehmen konnte, scheiterte am Gericht. Der Senat verwies auf das Beschleunigungsgebot, weil andere Angeklagte in Untersuchungshaft saßen.


Im Juli wurde Henry wegen akuter Selbstgefährdung in eine geschlossene Psychiatrie eingewiesen. Ein behandelnder Arzt empfahl eine dreimonatige Prozesspause für Henry, ein anderer Psychiater hielt ihn für verhandlungsfähig.


Am 12. August wurde Henry von der Polizei aus der Psychiatrie zur Verhandlung gebracht. Wie ein Möbelstück. So saß er dann da, von Tavor, einem starken Psychopharmakon etwas benommen wirkend die wenigen Stunden den verbleibenden Prozesstages an seinem Platz. Drei Tage später, am 15. August, wurde er in Leipzig von einer

S-Bahn erfasst

.


Selbst als Henry dann im Koma lag, wollte der OLG-Senat erst noch ein Gutachten über seine Verhandlungsfähigkeit einholen. Erst am 2. September wurde sein Verfahren schließlich abgetrennt.


Eine Frage der (Mit-)Verantwortung


Die Frage, welche Verantwortung die Richter:innen des Staatsschutzsenats des Oberlandesgerichts Dresden für den Umgang mit einem Menschen tragen, dessen akute Suizidgefährdung bekannt war, bleibt. Ebenso die Frage, was es mit einem Menschen macht, wenn er über mehr als ein Jahrzehnt immer wieder ins Visier staatlicher Ermittlungsbehörden gerät.


Jetzt also ist Henry tot


Henry galt einigen als ein gelinde gesagt schwieriger Mensch, wie es in einer differenzierten

Stellungnahme

 vom September beschrieben wird.


Zugleich gibt es jene die davon erzählen, er habe ihnen aus der Patsche geholfen, wenn es nötig war. Bei der

BSG Chemie Leipzig

 engagierte er sich über Jahre, wurde 2011 in den Aufsichtsrat gewählt und gehörte von 2012 bis 2015 dem Vorstand an. In ihrem

Nachruf

 vom 24. Oktober schreibt die BSG, Henry habe die positive Entwicklung des Vereins maßgeblich mitgestaltet.


Nach seinem Suizidversuch vom 15. August zeigte sich die

Rote Hilfe e.V.

 erschüttert und wütend.


Henry war eben nicht nur jener streitbarer Mensch, der über mehr als ein Jahrzehnt immer wieder ins Visier des sächsischen Staatsschutzes geriet. Es bleiben seine Freund:innen, seine Familie, darunter seine Kinder, und Weggefährt:innen.


Nach seinem Suizidversuch im August breitete sich eine

merkwürdige Stille

 aus. Nur hinter vorgehaltener Hand wurde darüber gesprochen …

author: Wir bleiben alle Friedrichshain
title: Was tun, wenn die Eigenbedarfskündigung ins Haus flattert?
content:
Einladung zum Nachbarschaftstreffen!


Am 27.10.2026 ab 19.00 Uhr in der Villa Felix


(Schreinerstr. 47)


Was tun, wenn die Eigenbedarfs- kündigung ins Haus flattert? Diese Frage müssen sich gerade sehr viele NachbarInnen stellen. Deswegen haben wir die Gruppe „Eigenbedarf kennt keine Kündigung“ (E3K) zu Gast.


E3K kämpft seit über sieben Jahren gemeinsam mit MieterInnen gegen Eigenbedarfs- kündigungen. Die Gruppe informiert, unterstützt Betroffene,


bereitet Gerichtsprozesse vor und organisiert solidarische Begleitungen zu Gerichts- terminen. Dabei konnten in den vergangenen Jahren zahlreiche Prozesse gemeinsam gewonnen werden.


Eigenbedarfskündigungen treffen selten eine einzelne Person. Sie können das ganze soziale Umfeld eines Hauses oder eines Kiezes verändern.


Kommt vorbei, bringt Eure Fragen und Erfahrungen mit – egal, ob ihr selbst betroffen seid oder einfach wissen wollt, was man tun kann. Wir freuen uns auf Euch!

author: Clare Hymer
title: Police Threaten to Arrest Anyone Helping Protesters at Palestine Action Demo
content:
The Metropolitan police has said it will arrest anyone providing “logistical support” to those protesting the Palestine Action ban in London on Saturday. 


This means people could be arrested for bringing water to elderly and disabled people holding placards, organisers Defend Our Juries (DOJ) said.


Commander Adam Slonecki, who is

leading the policing operation

 outside the US embassy, said: “I want to be clear – it is not just those who hold up placards who should expect to be arrested.


“Anyone officers consider to be playing a key role in organising the event, giving instructions to others and/or providing logistical support will very likely be committing an offence and face enforcement action.”


DOJ also raised concerns that this could also include their own media liaisons.


When approached by Novara Media for clarification, a Met spokesperson said: “

Section 44 of the Serious Crime Act 2007 makes it an offence to intentionally encourage or assist an offence.


“We are not going to define the terms we’ve used in our press release beyond their plain English meanings. Each incident is assessed on its own merits, and it is for officers to form the reasonable grounds to suspect an offence has taken place.”


A spokesperson for DOJ said in a statement: “How can the Met possibly justify arresting people who are not defying the ban themselves, who are simply providing logistical support to the peaceful protesters, many of whom are elderly or disabled and in need of support?


“It is also reckless and irresponsible, putting the safety of elderly and disabled people at risk… The moral bankruptcy of the Met is complete.”


The London protest is due to be held at the same time as another in Edinburgh, just days before the start of a supreme court challenge to the ban on Palestine Action. 


Both protests hope to draw attention to

questions over whether

 Keir Starmer’s government announced the proscription under pressure from US president Donald Trump, following the spray-painting of Trump’s Scottish golf course by Palestine Action protesters in March 2025.


Palestine Action became the first direct action group in British history to be proscribed as a terror organisation in July 2025. Over 3,300 people have since been arrested for peacefully defying the ban on expressing support for the group.

title: Kurdish protester wounded by IRGC sentenced to prison and fined
content:
Milad Ebrahimi, a 31-year-old Kurdish man from Kamyaran, Kurdistan Province, who was shot and wounded by Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) forces during the December 2025–January 2026 protests, has been sentenced to one year in prison and fined four billion rials on charges of “disturbing public order”.


The Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN) has reported that Branch 101 of the Kamyaran Criminal Court Two tried Ebrahimi in mid-October. He was notified of the verdict on 25 October.


IRGC forces shot Ebrahimi in the lower back with live ammunition during protests in Kamyaran on the evening of 8 January 2026.


He was taken to a medical facility in Sanandaj, the provincial capital, where he underwent surgery before returning home to recover.


Ministry of Intelligence forces arrested him on 1 February, despite his need for further hospitalisation because of an infection caused by his gunshot wound, and took him to the ministry’s detention facility in Sanandaj.


He was denied access to a lawyer and medical care during his detention and was provisionally released on bail on 27 February.

content:

Hallo,

Es hängt von einer Entscheidung des Oberlandesgerichts (OLG) Frankfurt, 8. Wer einen Redebeitrag auf der Kundgebung halten möchte, sagt uns bitte rechtzeitig Bescheid.


Eine weitere Kundgebung wird es am 17. Dezember geben. Geichzeitig findet in Frankfurt am Main vor dem US-Konsulat die Kundgebung zu Mumia Abu Jamal statt. Daniela ist die Solidarität zu Mumia sehr wichtig. Er wurde am 9.12.1981 festgenommen. Sollte Daniela aber doch schon in Preungesheim einsitzen, findet dann vorher dort diese Kundgebung statt mit einer anschließenden Demo zum US-Konsulat.


Das Foto (siehe Anhang) ist von der Demo/Kundgebung „FREE THE ULM 5“ am 26. Otober 2026 in Stuttgart. Einige Genoss*innen von uns waren da.


Den Aufruf zur Veranstaltung am 7. November in Zürich veröffentlichen wir hier noch einmal.


Gruppe: Solidarität mit Daniela


solidarisch-mit-daniela@t-online.de / www.solidarisch-mit-Daniela.de


Solidarität mit Daniela

am 5. November 2026 um 15 Uhr


Vechta, Franziskanerplatz/Kleine Kirchstraße


Daniela Klette hat am 5. November Geburtstag. Aus diesem Anlass wird es eine weitere Kundgebung/Demo geben. Daniela lebte über 30 Jahre in der Illegalität, sie wurde nach ihrer Verhaftung Ende Februar 2024 in Berlin in die JVA Vechta gebracht. Dort war sie in den ersten sieben Wochen in Einzelisolation gewesen, dies bedeutete: 24 Stunden wurde die Zelle videoüberwacht, eine Metallblende war vor dem Fenster angebracht, so dass kein Sonnenlicht in die Zelle drang, Einzelhofgang, keinen Kontakt zu anderen gefangenen Frauen. Dies ist Folter! Nur durch Öffentlichkeitsarbeit wie z. B. die ersten beiden Kundgebungen im März und April 2024 wurden die Haftbedingungen für Daniela gelockert. Seitdem hat sie „normale“ Haftbedingungen.


Am 27. Mai 2026 ist Daniela vom Landgericht Verden – im ersten Prozess u.a. wegen acht Geldbeschaffungsaktionen – zu 13 Jahren verurteilt worden. Die Verteidiger von Daniela und auch die Staatsanwaltschaft haben Revision eingelegt, über die der Bundesgerichtshof in den nächsten Monaten dann entscheiden wird. Ein zweiter möglicher Prozess gegen Daniela wird vor dem Oberlandesgericht Frankfurt/M stattfinden. Die Anklageschrift der Bundesanwaltschaft (BAW) u.a. wegen zwei Aktionen der Roten Armee Fraktion (RAF) in 1991 und 1993 sowie einer dritten einer Kämpfenden Einheit in 1990, an denen laut BAW Daniela angeblich beteiligt gewesen sein soll, wird höchstwahrscheinlich in den nächsten Monaten vom OLG zugelassen werden. Auf jedem Fall wird dann Daniela nach der Zulassung der Anklageschrift nach Frankfurt verlegt. Im Frauenknast Frankfurt-Preungesheim sind die Haftbedingungen schlechter als in Vechta, z. B. hier hat sie 4x im Monat Besuch, in Frankfurt nur 2x.

author: Rizomatica
title: 534 años de resistencia: a propósito de la marcha histórica del 12 de octubre en la ciudad de Temuco 2026
content:
Por: Cheuquelen Ñancucheo Ñanculeo


Empatía y solidaridad con la resistencia Mapuche y las diferentes Luchas.

El pasado 12 de octubre se realizó la marcha por la resistencia Mapuche en la ciudad de Temuco convocada por los familiares de los presos políticos Mapuche de la cárcel de dicha ciudad y comunidades en resistencia, en conmemoración a los 534 años de invasión española.

La denominada Marcha por la Resistencia Mapuche del año 2026 fue una marcha histórica por diversos motivos: el primero es la gran convocatoria que tuvo y que se vio reflejado en varios centenares de personas que marcharon por el centro de la cuidad de Temuco. Autoridades tradicionales del pueblo Mapuche, así como diferentes representantes de los diversos Lof en resistencia; hogares estudiantiles de distintas regiones, así como colectivos e individualidades, tanto mapuche como del pueblo chileno.


El segundo: lo emotivo de dicha marcha no solo por la fecha, sino por el trabajo realizado previamente, el cual se vio reflejado en las más de un centenar de banderas azules con sus respectivos colihues, las que representaban cada una con su propio número a los más de 113 presos políticos Mapuche que se encuentran recluidos en las diferentes cárceles del estado Chileno.


Lo tercero: es la mezcla de la primera y la segunda, vale decir, en la impronta de una marcha tan masiva cargada de simbolismos en varios aspectos, como por ejemplo: la visualización de las demandas del movimiento Mapuche, la que se vio reflejada en múltiples y coloridos lienzos , el primero de estos se llevó en el frontis de la marcha y representaba al módulo de presos políticos Mapuche de la cárcel de Temuco; el segundo lienzo, representando a los prisioneros políticos Mapuche de la cárcel de Angol, ambos con la frase: Kiñewaiñ Weichan mew, unidad en la lucha; el tercero , fue uno que decía relación con la exigencias al término del estado de excepción constitucional de emergencia, el que a la fecha lleva 4 años y cinco meses, lo que significa netamente una segunda ocupación militar del territorio Mapuche, está vez en el siglo XXI. Así sucesivamente, diferentes lienzos y consignas hasta el final de dicha marcha.


Además de lo anterior, las 113 y una banderas realizadas por los familiares de presos políticos Mapuche de la cárcel de Temuco, dieron una impronta y un simbolismo emocional como pocas veces vistos. Ver la marcha cargadas de banderas azules flameando al viento – sobre todo en la parte final de esta- dio un toque emotivo importante, porque no solamente era una bandera azul con un colihue, cosa que ya es simbólico en una cuidad como Temuco, sino que además cada bandera llevaba el nombre de un preso y Presa Política Mapuche recluidos en diferentes cárceles de Wallmapu; Cada bandera representaba a ese peñi o esa lamgen que está tras las rejas, pero además representaba a una familia de un Lof en lucha y el conjunto de aquello, a un pueblo en resistencia.

Visualizar personas de diferentes partes del Gulumapu, además de los diferentes Lof y autoridades del pueblo Mapuche que se hicieron presentes ese día, hace reflexionar una sola cosa : cuando un pueblo apuesta por la unidad en su legítima lucha y se trabaja socialmente por aquello, respetando las diferencias de cada pensamiento que compone dicho movimiento, tarde o temprano se va haber reflejado en algo. No es de un día para otro, porque detrás de esto hubo un trabajo y porque la diferencia es algo inherente a todo pueblo y todo movimiento.

No olvidar que la ‘Marcha del 12 de octubre’ o la «Marcha por la Resistencia Mapuche» como se conoce comúnmente, representa para los diferentes gobiernos de turnos- sobre todo para el de Bachelet, Piñera, Boric y Kast- la expresión social del principal enemigo interno del estado de Chile, el Movimiento Mapuche en Resistencia o Autonomista, criminalizado históricamente por los medios de comunicación burgueses, sobre todo los últimos 30 años.

Pero ahí estaba nuestra gente, representada en niños y niñas, jóvenes, adultos y adultos mayores, tanto del pueblo Mapuche como también del pueblo Chileno que llegaron ese dia; los hijos e hijas de los presos políticos Mapuche; los jóvenes y adultos de comunidades en resistencia que han crecido bajo los patrullajes mixtos y que han tenido que soportar los más de 730 mil controles de identidad, además de la adultez mayor, la que permanentemente junto a la infancia, tienen que soportar los más de 6 tipos de ruidos que asedian Wallmapu: el dron …

author: Unknown
title: La culture entre en scène : appel à la mobilisation
content:
Après un mois de répression meurtrière et proto-fasciste à l'encontre du mouvement lycéen, exigeant des conditions décentes d'apprentissage, les étudiant•es et travailleur•euses de la culture luttent toujours contre la casse capitaliste du service public.


Malgré les réformes lointaines proposées en réponse à la lutte lycéenne, le Gouvernement ne renonce pas à sa politique économique austéritaire et sa dévastation sans précédent de nos conditions de vie.


En rêvant la privatisation générale des moyens de production culturelle et de leur récupération par l'extrême-droite, le Gouvernement incendie un à un les étages de la société.


Nous défendons une culture non-marchande, collective, populaire et inclusive, qui s'oppose radicalement aux idéologies réactionnaires qui abritent les dominations les plus graves et les plus destructions les plus violentes.


Nous appelons les étudiant•es et travailleureu•ses de la culture à continuer de se rassembler, à rejoindre nos canaux d'information, à se mobiliser ensemble dès ce samedi 31 octobre, à se réunir de nouveau en Assemblée Générale lundi prochain 2 novembre, et à construire la grève générale.

title: SUTEBA Multicolor vuelve al paro, con protestas y movilizaciones en distintos puntos de la provincia
content:
Las seccionales y agrupaciones de SUTEBA Multicolor convocaron a nuevas medidas de fuerza para este martes 27 y miércoles 28 de octubre en rechazo al acuerdo salarial del 6%, dividido en dos tramos del 3% para octubre y noviembre, alcanzado entre el gobierno de Axel Kicillof y la mayoría de los gremios que integran el Frente de Unidad Docente Bonaerense. Las agrupaciones opositoras denuncian que la propuesta fue acordada sin consultar a las escuelas y que no alcanza para recomponer los salarios. Las modalidades de la protesta varían según el distrito: La Matanza, Tigre y General Pueyrredón anunciaron dos jornadas de paro; en Marcos Paz habrá huelga este martes y una jornada de protesta el miércoles; mientras que en Bahía Blanca se realizarán actividades de protesta durante ambos días. La nueva convocatoria da continuidad a las medidas de lucha de la semana pasada, que incluyeron paros, una olla popular y una movilización a la Dirección General de Cultura y Educación (DGCyE). La Multicolor reclama un salario de $1.700.000 por cargo testigo, rechaza las sumas no remunerativas y exige el cese de los descuentos por paro, mejores prestaciones de IOMA y medidas frente a la violencia en las escuelas. También reclama la aparición con vida de la docente correntina Nanci Godoy, desaparecida desde el 7 de octubre.

title: Hatimoğulları: Alevis should play an active role in the peace process
content:
DEM Party Co-Chair Tülay Hatimoğulları called on the Alevi community to actively participate in the peace and democratization process in Turkey. At a meeting with representatives of Alevi organizations in Istanbul, she criticized the exclusion of Alevis from parliamentary deliberations and warned against leaving the future of the process solely in the hands of the government. Lasting peace, she argued, could only be achieved on the basis of equal citizenship, legally guaranteed fundamental freedoms, and the democratic restructuring of the republic.


The meeting took place at the Kazım Karabekir Cemevi in Istanbul’s Ümraniye district. Alongside representatives of Alevi associations and institutions, numerous other guests attended the event. Speaking here, Hatimoğulları emphasized that the process initiated by Abdullah Öcalan must not be understood as a power struggle between political camps. “We do not view peace in terms of one side winning and the other losing. Peace means building a shared life and giving one another our consent to do so. Genuine peace can only emerge when all 86 million citizens of this country can live in justice, freedom, and peace.”


Criticism of the exclusion of the Alevi community


The DEM Party co-chair recalled the decades of persecution, massacres, and assimilation policies targeting Alevis. Despite these experiences, she said, the Alevi community expanded its social and political organization in Turkey and Europe. Rather than allowing the history of injustices it suffered to paralyze it, the Alevi community drew strength from these experiences for its resistance and self-organization, she underlined. Hatimoğulları also addressed the massacres of Alevis in Syria by the Islamist forces of HTS, which have ruled the country since late 2024. She noted that international solidarity actions against this violence was warmly welcomed by the affected population.


Regarding the peace process, she particularly criticized the Turkish parliament speaker’s refusal to hear representatives of the Alevi community. “We have repeatedly asked the government why Alevis are not being heard. A faith community to which millions of people in this country belong cannot be ignored. Peace cannot be built without speaking to Alevis.” Remarking that the DEM Party has repeatedly insisted on their participation, she described Parliament Speaker Numan Kurtulmuş’s rejection of this demand as politically unacceptable.


Peace process amid state repression


Hatimoğulları spoke at length about the contradictions between the government’s official declarations of commitment to peace and its continued policies of repression. She pointed out that restrictions on freedom of expression, the persecution of opposition politicians, the imprisonment of critical voices, and the appointment of state trustees to opposition-run municipalities stood in the way of credible democratization. She also addressed questions that Alevi organizations had raised with the DEM Party: How can a peace process be advanced under conditions of severe state repression? Is there a risk that the AKP will exploit the process for its own electoral interests? And does participating in the talks mean politically aligning oneself with the government?


“These are all legitimate questions. As a party, we raise them with the same clarity as you do. The concerns and objections of the Alevi community must be taken seriously and discussed openly, Hatimoğulları stated. In this context, she also criticized the political instrumentalization of ongoing investigations and the unequal treatment of alleged financial crimes. “While opposition figures and smaller businesses are being targeted with considerable severity, the names of politically influential individuals allegedly implicated in the major investment fund scandal remain undisclosed.”


“If these were names from the opposition, wouldn’t they have published them on every front page long ago? But now they won’t even reveal the names. Why? Because the matter reaches into their own ranks. Despite the contradictions between the peace process and government policy, the democratic opposition must not abandon the struggle for a political solution.”

author: Sheila Kalunga and Willy Mutunga
title: The Children We Do Not See: Infants and Toddlers Behind Bars
content:
There is a silent population inside Kenya’s correctional facilities that rarely enters public debate, penal policy discourse, or the national imagination. They appear in no crime statistics, are absent from sentencing records, and have committed no legal infraction. Yet they wake up behind locked steel doors, live within barbed perimeter walls, and spend their most formative developmental years in state custody.


These are the infants and toddlers—children under the age of four—who reside with their incarcerated mothers under Section 30(4) of the Prisons Act. Historically, their presence has been framed as an administrative concession, a humanitarian allowance, or a compassionate exception to preserve maternal attachment. But examined through the joint prisms of neuroscience and transformative constitutionalism, their situation is neither benign nor humane. It represents an unconstitutional paradox: the de facto penal detention of innocent citizens by association.


Our observations inside Kitui Women’s Prison—undertaken through the Early Play & Healing Initiative of the Early Years Development Centre (EYDC) under the Alpha New Beginnings Foundation—have brought this reality into sharp focus. Combining the perspectives of early childhood neuropsychology and constitutional jurisprudence, we have witnessed how babies grow, adapt, and regress within an institutional environment structurally hostile to human flourishing.


We have watched infants learn to crawl on cold, abrasive cement. We have seen toddlers take their first tentative steps along narrow, echoey cell corridors under the armed watch of uniformed correctional officers. We have listened to mothers whisper lullabies through stifled tears, attempting to soothe distressed infants while suffocating under their own unprocessed trauma.


These scenes do not fit within Kenya’s stated narrative of justice, humane rehabilitation, or constitutional protection. They are an indictment of an unthinking penal architecture that demands urgent legal interrogation and systemic repair.


The constitutional paradox: Guarantees on paper, violations in concrete


Kenya’s penal framework operates in open defiance of the 2010 Constitution. Section 30(4) of the Prisons Act—a colonial relic enacted long before modern human rights jurisprudence—permits a child to remain with an incarcerated mother until the age of four. While ostensibly conceived to prevent abrupt separation, the statute is silent on developmental standards, psychosocial care, environmental adequacy, or the child’s autonomous civil liberties.


The supreme law of the republic permits no such legal blind spot. Under Article 2(4) of the Constitution of Kenya 2010, any law, customary practice, or institutional conduct inconsistent with the constitution is void to the extent of the inconsistency.


Article 53 is categorical: Every child has the right to basic nutrition, shelter, and healthcare (Art. 53(1)(c)); Every child has the right to be protected from abuse, neglect, inhuman treatment, and punishment (Art. 53(1)(d)); Every child has the right not to be detained, except as a measure of last resort, and when detained, to be held for the shortest appropriate period of time, separate from adults, and in conditions that take account of their sex and age (Art. 53(1)(f)); A child’s best interests are of paramount importance in every matter concerning the child (Art. 53(2)).


These guarantees are reinforced by Section 8 of the Children Act 2022, which secures every child’s right to a nurturing, safe, and stimulating environment.


Constitutional rights do not terminate at the prison gates. They do not dissolve because a parent has been convicted or remanded. Yet in practice, infants residing in Kenyan prisons are subjected to structural, daily breaches of Article 53. They are detained not as a measure of last resort, but as collateral consequence; they are held in adult penal wards; and they inhabit environments devoid of the sensory and psychosocial resources necessary for early childhood survival.


Subjecting an infant to an ecosystem of containment, sensory deprivation, and institutional stress amounts to cruel, inhuman, and degrading treatment under Article 25(a) and Article 29. The state recognizes these children as rights-bearing citizens in theory, yet reduces them to legal non-entities—appendages to their mothers’ punishment—in execution.

ARREST FOR ATTEMPTED STREET THEATRE by Camilla Power

On Mayday morning, I’m wondering whether to head to Clerkenwell on the day when pagan, anarchist and socialist hope springs eternal. If I step onto the Green, I am liable to arrest under bail conditions imposed after 25 hours detention in Lewisham Police Station from around 6 pm on the eve of the royal wedding.

What did I do to be banished from the sacred Mayday space? Nothing…yet. I was picked up in one of last week’s preemptive raids during what’s become known in ‘activist’ circles as the Great Royal Wedding Purge. The police have begun to arrest people whom they suspect of thinking of doing something.

These arrests have been written about in terms of democratic rights to free speech. From my perspective, it’s about the human right to ritual participation. My work as an anthropologist combines Darwinian and Durkheimian models on the evolution of ritual as the necessary condition for language. Performative deeds precede and provide the necessary scaffolding for speech. In activist mode, I put theory to empirical test, helping create ritual street theatre to move into and around politically contested spaces, at ritually charged ‘cracks’ in time, establishing symbolic presence. As part of a motley crew known as the Government of the Dead, I’ve worn silly costumes, devised ways to hang and decapitate effigies, spilt fake body fluids, committed cannibalism, cast spells, bodypainted, sung and danced badly.

On the eve of the wedding, several cars and a van load of police – maybe twenty odd officers of the law – swooped on a south London street corner to round up a theatrical troupe. Suddenly I was in the midst of the most extraordinary street theatre yet; what’s so exciting is you never know who is going to turn up and take part. The police were the ones in costume, apart from the detective and shifty undercover surveillance; we were distinctly underdressed. We’d been moving theatrical props – some quite heavy. And the police knew the drill of the choreography, stringing themselves into a line between us and the suburban street, backing us steadily against the London brick walls behind. Slyly, they ringed around a white van which they suspected we were walking towards. We just waited expectantly to be auditioned while the detective in the suit flashed his badge and pointed to some of us, denying others – ‘no, he’s alright’ – as if he were casting us for roles. The only one who happened to be wearing some fancy dress got picked on; as did my close friend and colleague Chris Knight, a Professor of anthropology – best known for his top hat, dark glasses and vampire blood Baron Samedi look – but now in a motheaten jumper. By a stroke of fortune, a Channel 4 documentary team and an independent filmmaker were on hand to film the whole episode. A friend pointed out later, more police officers were needed to arrest us than for the Krays!

I was under suspicion of conspiring to cause a public nuisance. But what had I done? No ritual had yet been …

author: Brian Hioe
title: China Steps Up Transnational Repression Ahead of Elections
content:
CHINA HAS STEPPED up efforts to intimidate Taiwan ahead of elections in November. This has occurred with the usual combination of domestic threats and military exercises. Nevertheless, one can point to a discernible effort to project power over Taiwan.

In particular, China released high-resolution satellite images of Taiwan, as well as a propaganda poster, on the anniversary of the handover of Taiwan from Japanese to ROC control.

The satellite imagery was designed to convey a sense of having already penetrated Taiwan, such that it can observe Taiwan easily from without–and to contribute to the sense that the Chinese military could take Taiwan at any time. To this extent, as with any display of Chinese military hardware, this would also be signalling between the two militaries, with the Chinese government showing its capacities to the ROC military as a means of intimidation.

One can perceive attacks that have occurred in Taiwan in recent memory as similarly aimed at projecting power. News broke earlier this month of the indictment of five men over a plot to hit stand-up comic Huang Yi-hao with a car, in retribution for a comedy show in which Huang mocked Chinese president Xi Jinping.

The five men slammed into Huang with a car, injuring his pelvis, after being ordered to hurt Huang enough to hospitalize him. Subsequently, they acted as though the incident was an accident and assisted Huang with an insurance claim. Huang was not injured as heavily as those who ordered the attack wished, who were to pay the attackers 450,000 NT for successfully hospitalizing Huang.

News of the plot to attack Huang follows suit from the indictment of two men over a May attack on a comedy club where Huang was performing, during which the comedy club had a mixture of feces and paint thrown at its entrance. A 35-year-old man surnamed Kuo was reportedly paid 50,000 NT by a 33-year-old man surnamed Liu to carry out the attack.

Earlier this year, political commentator Akio Yaita was attacked in a Taichung hotel where he was giving a speech. The attacker had flown in for the attack from Hong Kong, and subsequently attempted to flee abroad.

It is to be seen if other potential attacks take place ahead of elections. The uptick in such violence, conducted as a means of transnational repression by China, may be intended to influence elections and also convey the message that China already observes Taiwan closely and will retaliate against criticism. Nevertheless, such efforts at intimidation may not cow Taiwan, but instead have the effect of pushing Taiwan further away.

author: By Niko Georgiades, Unicorn Riot
title: Minneapolis March Against Police Brutality Connects Local, State and Federal Violence
content:
Minneapolis, MN — For the 31st annual National Day of Protest Against Police Brutality on Oct. 22, activists drew the connection to the violence perpetrated by local, state, and federal law enforcement as they marched from the memorial site of

Alex Pretti

 to

Renée Good

‘s memorial and ended at

George Floyd Square

.


Organizing the march for the twenty-sixth straight year was

Communities United Against Police Brutality

 (

CUAPB

). “We want to draw the lines, make the connections, help people understand that it does not matter whether that brutality is by a local law enforcement, a county law enforcement, a state police, or the federal law enforcement. It doesn’t matter when somebody loses their lives to police brutality, misconduct, and abuse of authority. We will always be out here demanding justice. That will never change,” said Michelle Gross, the president of CUAPB.


Before the march started from Alex Pretti’s memorial at 26th St. and Nicollet Ave.,

Brass Solidarity band

 got the crowd moving and singing along to their resistance songs. In attendance for the action were several impacted families and friends of families with stolen lives, including, but not limited to,

Tekle Sundberg

 (Minneapolis Police),

Paul Castaway

 (Denver Police) and

Kobe Heisler

 (Brooklyn Center Police).


Toshira Garraway, whose fiancé

Justin Teigen was found dead in a recycling center

 after an interaction with the St. Paul Police in 2009, spoke at the rally and reminded the crowd that before the deadly Operation Metro Surge, Minnesota police have been deadly.


“Let’s think about the brutality and the evil and the corruption that we were facing right here in Minnesota by our local law enforcement before the Ice agents even showed up,” said Garraway, “and then the ICE agents showed us up and brutalized us even more.”


After marching to Good’s memorial on 33rd St. and Portland Ave., activist Jae Yates noted that Good’s “identity was erased repeatedly after she was killed. Nobody wanted to talk about the fact that this is also violence against the queer community,” they said, “that this is violence against a queer mom who moved here specifically for the safety that she thought that she would find in Minneapolis.”


“This is what we mean when we say all of these struggles are connected. Because if you can murder a white queer woman in the street. What do you think is happening to Black and brown people? If you can kill a Native woman [

Allison Lussier

], not investigate her death, and then face zero consequences within your department? What do you think is happening to the rest of your neighbors?”


Jae Yates


Also at Good’s memorial, Jaylani Hussein, the Executive Director of the Minnesota Chapter of the Council on American-Islamic Relations (

CAIR-MN

) reminded the crowd of the collective power that the Twin Cities community showed to push out the federal occupation.


Hussein noted that it was Minneapolis neighbors looking out for their neighbors like Renée Good “who stood on the streets with their whistles and with their phones,” that got Greg Bovino, the former “commander at large” of the Border Patrol and Kristi Noem, the former Homeland Security Secretary, fired. He implored Minnesotans never forget what happened and to continue to make strides toward justice.


The march ended at George Floyd Square where the community met at independent photojournalist

KingDemetrius Pendleton

‘s

Listen 2 Us Studio

 on 37th St. and Chicago Ave for refreshments and rides back to the march’s starting point.

author: Kodao Productions
title: The risks journalists face (3)
content:
Filipino journalists have actually been walking on eggshells since 2016, when then President Rodrigo Duterte said newsmen are as vulnerable to physical attacks as any other citizen of the republic, especially when journalists purportedly abuse press freedom and engage in hit jobs and deny the subjects of their commentary the right to reply.


Duterte’s law thus justifies, not due process of law, not the protection of journalists, but the right of armed reply to abusive reporters and columnists, commentators and editors. Journalists are responsible for what they write, whether right or wrong, or whether or not their reporting is beyond reproach or not. Yet, the context of Duterte’s law is not the protection of the aggrieved but the sanctification of vengeance. Certainly, the people of Davao City knew what happened to Jun Pala, once pals to Duterte but broke with him over what the latter reported was a graft-ridden waste disposal deal.


Pala was killed in 2003 by a team that was recruited by Duterte and his henchmen, according to a very long affidavit executed by former police officer Arturo Lascañas, a confessed member of the Duterte Death Squad (DDS) who revealed the many murders perpetrated in Davao City, including the massacre of entire families, the disappearance of young men who figured in a fistfight with a Duterte relative, the killings of petty criminals and the summary execution of perceived political enemies. Lascañas’ disclosures hewed closely to the pieces of information that the late broadcaster Waldy Carbonell had gathered when he was sent to Davao City by former National Press Club of the Philippines (NPC) president Tony Antonio to investigate Pala’s murder in 2003.


Pala, who was once elected Davao City councilor, was not only critical of the DDS killings under the baton of Duterte; he likewise slammed graft-ridden projects in the city, like the P1-million daily budget for waste disposal. Carbonell said experts estimated that only P200,000 was needed for trash collection and disposal daily. When Carbonell sought to interview Duterte, the mayor flew into a rage and said he will slap the broadcaster, shoot him dead and bury him vertically. Carbonell told Davao City journalists he will also slap Duterte, who was shorter than him as he stood at 6’ 3. An indignant Duterte challenged Carbonell to a duel and the broadcaster obliged him.


Coming in from Gen. Santos City, where he served as councilor before martial law was declared, Carbonell toted his reliable pistol and motored to City Hall at the appointed time, only to be told, after 30 minutes of waiting, that the brave Duterte flew to Taiwan so his possible appointment with the Angel of Death had to be cancelled. By not being at the appointed time and place, Duterte failed to prove that he can do a repeat of the duel between Alexander Hamilton and Aaron Burr. It was some kind of *skedaddle that left a bad taste in the mouth of a gallant adversary.


However, Atty. Manases “Mans” Carpio is not Digong and he is far removed from the antics of his father-in-law even as his maneuvers leading to the filing of a cyberlibel against tabloid columnist Philip Lustre Jr. are classic schemes to use legal ploys to ensure that the complainant will not have a chance to a mandatory preliminary investigation to hasten the trial. Failing to get Lustre’s side was a deliberate move that favors Carpio. How the prosecutors and the police did not get the real address of Lustre is a mystery.


It was strange that the judge who issued the arrest warrant, Judge Retrina Espe Fuentes of Regional Trial Court (RTC) Branch 10, did not bother to see the accused or question the prosecutors if the respondent were informed that he was being charged criminally for violating Sec. (4C) 4 of the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012, also known as Republic Act No. 10175. This is elementary but then a different kind of law must hold sway in the Duterte fiefdom, particularly among the Davao City prosecutors, who have taken to heart the lessons about railroading cases, fabricating evidence and pressuring litigants to settle in an unfair and unjust manner. Some may call this shared legal psychosis. Fuentes was the same judge who issued the arrest warrant for Davao Death Squad (DDS) whistleblower Arturo Lascañas in 2017 after he turned his back on Rodrigo Duterte. Lascañas tagged Duterte as the architect of the “tokhang” murders. Eventually, Lascañas fled the country and revealed everything he knew …

author: EDRi
title: EDRi-gram, 29 October 2026
content:
What has the EDRi network been up to over the past few weeks? Find out the latest digital rights news in our regular newsletter. In this edition: Celebrating end-to-end encryption, and the digital justice community in Europe and beyond

We’re still riding the high from October milestones showcasing the strength of our community. We had the pleasure of greeting many of you in person and online for #PrivacyCamp26 two weeks ago to discuss the origins of technology and how to pivot from conversations around “sovereignty” to meaningful, community-led self-determination. If you weren’t able to make it but you’re curious about the conversations, you can rewatch the livestream of some of the panel discussions.

Then, on October 21, we celebrated Global Encryption Day, highlighting end-to-end encryption as a crucial foundation to our right to safe and secure communication online and to life as we know it. Thanks to our members and partners, our message of protecting encryption was visible across several European capitals – from the metro trains of Prague to key landmarks in Berlin, Paris and Dublin with mobile “encryption trucks”. We also worked with European Sex Workers Alliance and Féministes contre le cyberharcèlement to raise awareness on the importance of safe and secure communications for sex workers as well as womens’ rights. You can read more about the action in this edition, and stay tuned for more updates coming soon on our social platforms.

Yet another win for digital rights this month came with the news of Norway’s data protection authority imposing a fine of 92 million Norwegian crowns (roughly EUR 8.8 million) on Microsoft’s adtech unit Xandr for unlawfully sharing ​Grindr users’ sensitive data with thousands of advertisers.

While we’re bolstered from the wins and community spirit, there’s a lot more to resist and much work to be done. We are still reeling from the EU governments’ final position on the Digital Omnibus on Data, which amongst other unsavoury things, will to allow companies to use our data to develop or use their AI systems if it serves a ‘legitimate interest’ – without us knowing or accepting. This is a blank cheque for tech corporations to indulge in outrageous data grabs and exploit potentially sensitive information about us.

Earlier this week, the European Commission also announced a revamp of Frontex, EU’s border agency, that is set to double its budget and expand its role in deportations and surveillance. Not only will this turn Frontex into EU’s ICE equivalent, the new Regulation also wants to allow Frontex to be able to monitor social media for information that may forecast people’s movements at EU borders. Let alone leading with solidarity and care, the EU seems intent on violating people’s freedom to move and to express themselves. Keep your eyes out for an analysis of the new proposal from the Protect Not Surveil coalition.

author: Franck Dick Rosete
title: Cyberlibel complaints vs journalists strengthen calls to decriminalize libel
content:
The criminal sanction for Philippine libel laws is “excessive” and is in violation of the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR) to which the Philippines is a signatory.

Libel complaints were recently filed against journalists and media company executives. For a journalists’ group, these validate the previous calls to decriminalize libel.

The GMA chapter of the National Union of Journalists of the Philippines (NUJP) stressed that libel laws silence journalism. “[C]riminalizing speech only undermines the public’s fundamental right to know,” the chapter said in a statement.

Davao City 1st District Rep. Paolo Duterte filed libel and cyberlibel complaints against GMA executives and broadcast journalists which stemmed from the network’s report about alleged cash deliveries to the Dutertes claimed by dismissed police officer Rodulfo Gracioso Jr.

Duterte filed the complaint before the Davao City Prosecutor’s Office on October 23, more than two weeks after his sister, Vice President Sara Duterte, made a joke about filing a multimillion-peso libel case against GMA Network. Her remarks happened during a press conference on October 6 while reading her affidavit which answers Gracioso’s claims.

Among the respondents were GMA executives Felipe Gozon and Gilberto Duavit, as well as journalists Mel Tiangco, Vicki Morales, Emil Sumangil, Darlene Cay, Marvin Parado, Joel San Luis, and other unidentified individuals.

In a statement released on October 23, the TV network said that they have not yet received the complaints.

Gracioso and National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) director Melvin Matibag were also named as respondents.

Meanwhile, veteran journalist Philip Lustre Jr. was arrested on October 24 over a cyberlibel complaint reportedly filed by Mans Carpio, Sara’s husband. He was unaware of the complaint, according to his legal counsel. He was released on bail on the same day.

NUJP has been campaigning for the decriminalization of libel, echoing the views of the United Nations (UN) Human Rights Committee that the criminal sanction for Philippine libel laws is “excessive” and is in violation of the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR) to which the Philippines is a signatory.

Right(s) Up: Why journalists and advocates push for decriminalization of libel

On September 18, NUJP released its policy review on libel laws, stating that the high court has already identified the problem of these laws but reform requires legislation. The review, to name a few, cited Justice Marvic Leonen’s opinion in Disini, Jr. v. Secretary of Justice which stated that libel was unconstitutional as penal sanctions impose “an invidious chilling effect.”

It added that removing jail time alone, as proposed by some legislators, is not decriminalization because of limitations of a fine-only regime, saying that if the accused cannot pay, subsidiary imprisonment may follow.

The review cited the data obtained from the Office of Cybercrime of the Department of Justice (DOJ), indicating that 3,770 cyberlibel cases had been filed, as of May 2022, since the enactment of the Cybercrime Prevention Act. More than 2,500 cases remained pending in courts and before the prosecution level. There were already 12 convictions.

In the 2023 study by NUJP, 61.5% of the libel cases against 50 journalists from 2021 to 2023 were filed by politicians.

ML Party-list Rep. Leila de Lima said that filing a libel suit against journalists and media workers for doing their job sends a “chilling message” to other members of the press. Parties being accused can just respond to the allegations, she wrote in a Facebook post.

Under the Journalist’s Code of Ethics approved by media groups, journalists shall recognize the duty to air the other side and the duty to correct substantive errors promptly.

“Contrary to allegations of malice or unverified reporting, the report went through standard, multi-layered editorial and legal verification procedures,” the NUJP GMA Chapter said. “The team conducted due diligence—verifying information through official sources, law enforcement documents, and background checks—and obtained proper clearance from network leadership and legal counsel before airing the story.”

In the subject report, the reporter, Cay, and anchor Tiangco mentioned that they were trying to get the comments of the people implicated by Gracioso, including the Dutertes, but they did not receive a response when the report was aired …

title: La bande à « Balance ton Claude »
content:
Nous avons déjà longuement abordé les ressorts de l'« affaire Thélyson Orélien » dans nos pages (nous renvoyons, entre autres, à

cet excellent texte de Jean Claude Noel

). L'enquête qui suit porte sur ses délateurs, la bande à « Balance ton Claude » du nom du compte X à l'origine de la polémique. On y découvre que l'affaire Thélyson Orélien, est un double écran de fumée qui masque une convergence d'intérêts, financiers, idéologiques et géopolitiques, entre l'industrie de l'IA, les libertariens de la Silicon Valley, les christo-fascistes de l'administration Trump, et leurs imitateurs bien-de-chez-nous.


« Démarche complètement apolitique », « lanceur d'alerte », anonymat nécessaire pour éviter les attaques

ad hominem

… Toutes ces auto-justifications offertes par la bande à « Balance ton Claude », qui est derrière la polémique Thélyson Orélien, servent à ripoliner une opération idéologique, menée par un groupe de jeunes « libéraux-conservateurs » (doux euphémisme), très actifs dans l'espace médiatique, depuis les colonnes du Figaro, et les fabriques à propagande du projet Périclès. En outre, ces alarmes hypocrites s'inscrivent dans les récits

IApocalyptiques

 déployés par l'industrie pour faire gonfler investissements publics et privés. Une bulle profitant surtout aux nouveaux technoligarques, qui sont prêts à jeter la démocratie et l'humanité entière dans le chaudron de la valorisation et de la domination sans partage.


Les problèmes posés par la rédaction

I

A

ssistée

cachent une autre forme d'imposture : les allégations de neutralité politique répétées par la bande à « Balance ton Claude ». Une fine équipe, composée de cinq membres, d'après le premier accusateur anonyme sorti du bois

 [

1

]

, et qui n'a pas eu droit à la même attention que Thélyson Orélien.


«

Notre démarche était complètement apolitique

 [

2

]


 »

, déclarait ainsi Samuel Fitoussi dans

Le Point

, après avoir tombé le masque. Pourtant, le profil de nos Claudettes risque d'affoler votre détecteur à

bullshit

. Pas besoin du logiciel Pangram, vous allez voir, pour confondre ces immenses tartufes, présentés comme des «

lanceurs d'alerte

ayant

 l'amour de la vérité chevillé au coeur

et dénonçant les impostures intellectuelles

 [

3

]

 ».


Samuel Fitoussi


Commençons par vous donner une idée de l'honnêteté intellectuelle de M. Fitoussi. Quelques heures après avoir lancé la polémique sur le livre de Thélyson Orélien depuis le compte X « Balance ton Claude » (encore anonyme à ce moment-là), le chroniqueur du

Figaro

 intervient sur Radio J, où il déclare : «

comme aujourd'hui, le RN n'est pas un parti particulièrement violent ou antisémite ou quoi que ce soit, [renvoyer dos à dos les extrêmes] c'est en fait banaliser la dangerosité de cette gauche pro-Hamas...

 »


La journaliste lui fait alors remarquer que l'extrême-droite est quand même «

très proche de l'AfD, un parti néo-nazi

 ». Réponse de Samuel Fitoussi : «

J'ai beaucoup de critiques à l'égard de ces partis. Pour le RN, par exemple, je les trouve étatistes, socialistes, relativement incompétents

 […]

mais je pense qu'il faut reconnaître que les choses ont évolué, que le RN n'est plus le RN d'il y a 30 ans, et c'est même plus le RN d'il y a dix ans, qui voulait sortir de l'Union européenne, et c'est plus le RN antisémite

 [

4

]

 ».

L

'amour de la vérité chevillé au cœur

, on vous dit.


Par ailleurs, l'intérêt de M. Fitoussi pour les implications de l'IA générative n'est pas pure curiosité, étant donné qu'il travaille pour le fonds d'investissement FRST CAPITAL, spécialisé dans l'industrie naissante du

machine learning

(un des domaines informatiques que l'on trouve derrière la formule générique « IA », et dont les avancées ont notamment permis le développement des « grands modèles de langage » – ou

LLM

 – comme le célèbre ChatGPT).


Incidemment, FRST CAPITAL est une ancienne filiale d'OTIUM CAPITAL, la holding de Pierre-Edouard Stérin, milliardaire christo-libertarien qui utilise ses gains pour financer un projet de conquête politique par l'extrême-droite, baptisé « Périclès » (pour Patriotes, Enracinés, Résistants, Identitaires, Chrétiens, Libéraux, Européens, Souverainistes), et doté d'un budget de 150 millions d'euros

 [

5

]

.


Cerise sur le gâteau : FIRST CAPITAL n'investit pas seulement dans les « laboratoires d'IA », mais également dans la fabrique d'opinion, en produisant des sondages douteux sur la popularité d'Elon Musk ou …

title: Terminal Kadıköy’ün reklam ekranı hack’lendi: “Bu bina kent suçudur”
content:
İstanbul'un Kadıköy Söğütlüçeşme’deki Terminal Kadıköy’de bulunan bir reklam ekranı, “BU BİNA KENT SUÇUDUR” yazısıyla hack’lendi. Kent hakkı savunucuları, deprem toplanma alanı ve yeşil alanın alışveriş merkezine (AVM) dönüştürülmesine tepki göstererek kentlerin her alanının kâr maksimizasyonuna göre planlandığını vurguladı.


ETHA’daki habere göre, Söğütlüçeşme Tren İstasyonu’nun viyadük altındaki alanında kurulan Terminal Kadıköy, Nisan 2025’ten bu yana işletiliyor. Açıldığı günden bu yana onlarca dükkânın faaliyet gösterdiği alan, yeni bir tüketim merkezine dönüştü.


Kent hakkı savunucuları, ekoloji örgütleri ve Kadıköylüler, projeye karşı yıllardır itirazlarını sürdürüyor. Haydarpaşa Dayanışması, projeyi “soylulaştırma merkezi” olarak nitelendirerek “Kamusal alanlar ticarileşiyor, bu bir kent suçudur” açıklamasını yapmıştı.


Savunucular, AVM’ye dönüştürülen alanın geçmişte sokakta yaşayan hayvanların kent sakinleri tarafından beslendiği geniş bir yeşil alan olduğunu belirtiyor. Bölgenin yıllarca “izbe bir alan, güvensiz bir yer” olarak tanımlandığını aktaran kent hakkı savunucuları, bu söylemle projeye toplumsal rıza oluşturulmaya çalışıldığını ifade ediyor.


500’den fazla ağaç kesildi


Proje kapsamında bölgede 500’den fazla ağaç kesildi. Kent hakkı savunucuları, Söğütlüçeşme’deki alanın deprem toplanma alanı niteliği taşıdığını ve projenin bu işlevi fiilen ortadan kaldırdığını belirtiyor.


Savunucular, “Hem bir deprem toplanma alanı hem kentsel bir yeşil alanın tümü, bir avuç AVM’ye kurban edildi” diyerek kamusal alanın sermayeye peşkeş çekilmesine tepki göstermişti.


Çevre, Şehircilik ve İklim Değişikliği Bakanlığı ise proje için “ÇED Gerekli Değildir” kararı vermişti.


Terminal Kadıköy sonrası Kadıköy’de artan yoğunluk ve trafik baskısı


14 Nisan 2026

title: Siber Güvenlik Başkanlığı'ndan kritik güvenlik uyarısı
content:
Siber Güvenlik Başkanlığı, dünya genelinde yaygın olarak kullanılan PHP yazılım altyapısında kritik güvenlik açıkları tespit edildiğini belirterek şu açıklamayı yaptı “Dünya genelinde yaygın olarak kullanılan PHP yazılım altyapısında kritik güvenlik açıkları tespit edilmiştir.

Başkanlığımız, söz konusu zafiyetlerin oluşturabileceği risklerin erken tespiti ve olası etkilerinin sınırlandırılması amacıyla ulusal ölçekte güvenlik taramalarını başlatmış, ilgili kurum ve kuruluşlara acil güvenlik bildirimlerini iletmiştir.

Kamu kurumlarımızın, kritik altyapı işletmecilerimizin ve özel sektör kuruluşlarımızın sistemlerini gözden geçirerek gerekli güvenlik güncellemelerini ivedilikle uygulamaları önem taşımaktadır.

Dijital altyapılarımızın güvenliği ve kritik hizmetlerin sürekliliği için ulusal düzeyde koordinasyon ve önleyici güvenlik çalışmalarımız sürmektedir.”

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Agenda2029
title: Sabotage gegen Rheinmetall – Niemals Kriegstüchtig!
content:
In Kassel soll das größte Panzerwerk Europas gebaut werden. Wir stellen uns dagegen, zur Rüstungshauptstadt für die kommenden Kriege zu werden. Deshalb haben wir in der Nacht die Baustelle des Logistikzentrums von Rheinmetall in Kassel-Calden sabotiert und mehrere Bagger und Radlager angezündet.


Zeitenwende in Nordhessen


Wer in Nordhessen lebt, spürt was Zeitenwende heißt. Tag für Tag überschlagen sich die Nachrichten von Rüstungsinvestitionen. Fast kein Abend vergeht ohne Panzer in unseren Straßen zu sehen, die in die Kriegsgebiete der Welt exportiert werden. Kaum ein Kommunalpolitiker, mittelständisches Unternehmen oder Forschungsstandort der nicht hofft, etwas von den Milliarden der Zeitenwende abzubekommen.


Wir haben uns dafür entschieden, dabei nicht länger zuzuschauen und ein zentrales Projekt der Aufrüstungskampagne angegriffen: den Defence Hub Nordhessen von Rheinmetall.


Der Defence Hub Nordhessen umfasst den Ausbau des Panzerwerks in Kassel sowie den Bau eines Logistikzentrums auf 30.000 Quadratmetern und eines militärischen Drohnenzentrums am Kassel-Airport. Mit 260 Millionen Euro von Rheinmetall und über 20 Millionen Euro vom Land Hessen soll das Projekt bis Ende 2027 hochgezogen werden.


Für das Pressespektakel zum Auftakt verkündete Rheinmetall Chef Armin Papperger stolz: Kassel wird zukünftig das größte Panzerwerk Europas und „eine neue Drehscheibe“ der Rüstungsindustrie sein. Boris Rhein ergänzte: Der kriselnde Flughafen Kassel-Calden wird „künftig noch stärker als militärische Drehscheibe, für Trainingsflüge der Bundeswehr sowie zur Erforschung und Erprobung neuer Drohnen-Technologie“ dienen.


Während jeden Monat Millionen an Steuergeldern in einen leeren Flughafen versenkt werden, von dem nur die Privatjets von Superreichen starten, soll das Aufrüstungsprogramm nun die Rettung sein: Drohnen, Bundeswehrflüge und Logistik ersetzen die Passagiere und Urlaubsgäste, die partout nicht kommen wollen.


Mit Staatsgeldern in die Krise


Was in Kassel-Calden passiert, ist ein Sinnbild für die Zeitenwende in Deutschland: Der Staat tritt als Auftraggeber auf und versucht mit Milliarden an Rüstungsinvestitionen die schwächelnde Wirtschaft anzukurbeln. Deutschland tritt die Flucht nach vorne an. Wenn die Autoproduktion auf dem Weltmarkt nicht mehr konkurrenzfähig ist, dann immerhin der Leopard-Panzer und vielleicht auch bald wieder das deutsche Heer.


In einer Zeit, die weltweit von imperialistischen Konflikten und Kriegen geprägt ist, will die Bundesrepublik ihre Krise durch militärische Aufrüstung lösen und zukünftig ohne die USA an der Spitze Europas stehen können. Was uns als notwendige Investitionen in die Verteidigungsfähigkeit verkauft wird, ist die Option, die eigenen Interessen wie Zugang zu Ressourcen und Handelsrouten mit militärischen Mitteln außerhalb Deutschlands durchsetzen zu können. Der Bau von eigenen Langstreckenwaffen oder die Befugnisse der Geheimdienste zur Sabotage im Ausland sind offensive Fähigkeiten. Es ist die Möglichkeit, künftig weiter die Konfrontation mit dem russischen Regime um die Vormachtstellung in Osteuropa eingehen zu können.


Von der Drehscheibe …


Wir wissen aus allen Konflikten der Großmächte, dass am Ende die einfachen Menschen, die Frauen und die Jugendlichen am meisten unter den Folgen des Krieges leiden werden. Nicht Armin Papperger und Boris Rhein oder deren Kinder sollen im Schützengraben von der Drohne zerfetzt werden, sondern wir. Wenn wir den Kriegsvorbereitungen nicht international entgegen treten, haben wir bald keine Perspektive für unser Leben mehr.


Je mehr Geld in die Rüstungsprojekte fließt und je weiter der Umbau ziviler Wirtschaft zur Kriegsindustrie voranschreitet, desto größer wird auch hier die wechselseitige Abhängigkeit und die Verflechtung zwischen Rüstungskonzernen und den staatlichen Auftraggebern werden. Gleichzeitig gehen die Panzer, die am Ende von Rheinmetall und Co. durch Staatsgelder produziert werden, nicht wieder produktiv in den Wirtschaftskreislauf ein. Die Aufrüstung wird die Krise der letzten Jahre nicht lösen, sondern höchstens verschieben.


Wenn in ein paar Jahren die Hallen voll mit Panzern und Sprengköpfen sind, werden die Probleme der deutschen Schwerindustrie und der mittelständischen Zulieferer nicht gelöst sein. Für Kassel bedeutet das: Geht die staatliche Nachfrage nach Kriegswaffen in ein paar Jahren wieder zurück, wird auch die davon abhängige Industrie zusammenbrechen und zahlreiche Menschen ihre Arbeit …

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: Nobel Peace Laureate Navi Pillay on ICC, Gaza, Rape as War Crime, Her South African Roots & Mandela
content:
We speak with the acclaimed South African human rights lawyer and international jurist Navi Pillay, who was awarded this year’s Nobel Peace Prize. Pillay has been the United Nations high commissioner for human rights and a judge at both the International Criminal Court and at an international tribunal investigating the 1994 genocide in Rwanda. Most recently, she led the U.N. Independent International Commission of Inquiry that concluded Israel had committed genocide in Gaza. Hours after Pillay was announced as winner of the Nobel Prize, the United States imposed sweeping new sanctions against the International Criminal Court.


“It’s extremely shocking to me, totally unacceptable, that the United States administration can today impose sanctions against the International Criminal Court,” says Pillay, speaking to

Democracy Now!

 from The Hague.


Navi Pillay is now 85 years old. She was born into an Indian Tamil family in apartheid South Africa in 1941. The first woman to start a law practice in Natal, South Africa, in 1967, Pillay began her legal career defending anti-apartheid activists including Nelson Mandela, exposing torture, and helping establish key rights for prisoners on Robben Island. Mandela, as president, later appointed Pillay to the High Court of South Africa, making her the first woman of color on that bench.

author: Unknown
title: Putin'den Avrupa'ya savaş uyarısı: “Kazanan olmayacak”
content:
Rusya Devlet Başkanı Vladimir Putin, Avrupa ile olası bir savaşın sonuçlarının yıkıcı olacağını belirterek böyle bir çatışmada kazanan tarafın olmayacağını söyledi. Moskova’da düzenlenen Rusya-Afrika Zirvesi’nin ardından Afrika Birliği Dönem Başkanı ve Burundi Devlet Başkanı Evariste Ndayishimiye ile ortak basın toplantısı düzenleyen Putin, Avrupa ülkelerinin 2030’a kadar Rusya ile savaşa hazırlanma yönündeki açıklamalarını değerlendirdi.

Putin, “Biz her şeyden önce hazırız ancak Avrupa ile herhangi bir savaş istemiyoruz. Eğer isteyen varsa hazırlansın” dedi. Batılı ülkelerin Rusya’ya stratejik yenilgi yaşatma hedeflerine ulaşamadığını savunan Putin, bu hedefin 2030’a kadar gerçekleştirilmesinin de mümkün olmadığını ileri sürdü.

Avrupa ile olası bir savaşın sonuçlarına ilişkin konuşan Putin, “Eğer işler çok ileri giderse hiçbir kazanan olmayacak. Bunu kimse unutmasın” ifadelerini kullandı.

Rusya’nın Birinci ve İkinci Dünya Savaşlarından ders çıkardığını söyleyen Putin, benzer çatışmaların yeniden yaşanmaması için çaba gösterdiklerini belirtti.

Putin, Finlandiya Cumhurbaşkanı Alexander Stubb ve Norveç Başbakanı Jonas Gahr Store ile yaptığı telefon görüşmesine de değindi. İki liderin Moskova ile doğrudan temas kurmasını olumlu değerlendiren Putin, Avrupa ülkeleriyle ilişkilerin yeniden kurulmasına yönelik adımları desteklediklerini söyledi.

Putin, Baltık Denizi’ndeki deniz ulaşımına yönelik kısıtlamaların da yeni gerilimlere yol açabileceği uyarısında bulundu. Rusya’nın bölgede seyrüseferin engellenmesini istemediğini belirten Putin, iletişim ve ulaşımın kısıtlanmasının Basra Körfezi ve Hürmüz Boğazı’ndaki duruma benzer bir tablo yaratabileceğini ifade etti.

Rusya’nın herhangi bir meydan okumaya karşılık vereceğini söyleyen Putin, buna karşın Baltık Denizi’nde gerilim istemediklerini kaydetti.

author: labor4pal
title: European dockers to strike against war (Socialist Worker-UK)
content:
Workers are ‘calling for an end to war, austerity and to threats to trade union freedoms’

Dockers strike comes as revolts spread across Europe (Photo: sicobas.lavoratoriautorganizzati.9/Facebook)

Ports across the Mediterranean will shut down this Friday as workers at over 100 in 17 countries go on strike.

For years, military cargo used to ravage Palestine has gone through civilian ports across the world.

These workers are uniting their demands over pay and conditions with the fightback against war and genocide.

Giorgos Gogos, president of the Dockworkers’ Union of Piraeus Port Authority in Greece, spoke to Socialist Worker about the action.

He said, “We have called a global day of action against the militarisation of ports and war. We are calling for an end to austerity and to threats to trade unions’ freedoms.

“Across the world, armed conflicts are increasing instability and insecurity,” he said. “People are bleeding for the profits of imperialists and capitalists.

“Plans for militarisation like the European Union’s ReArm Europe project affect all European ports, states, societies and citizens,” he said.

“There is international dialogue between dockers in the European Dockworkers Council and many others.

“Dockworkers have a tradition of international cooperation. We have struggled and won together many times.”

The strike comes as revolts are spreading across Europe. In Italy a general strike has been called for the same day.

Giorgos said, “We think that every struggle from below has to link with others and in unity for social rights and trade union rights.

“Many social struggles are spreading with shared demands. Our action is following the young people and students in France, Albania, Belgium, Spain.

“We want to connect with them because we face similar problems. People are fed up with decisions from elites.

“Our militant answer to these attacks is going to be more effective if they are coordinated across Europe.

“We are asking British workers to support us practically and participate in the struggle for peace and prosperity. We are demanding welfare not warfare.”

30 October, International day of action in support of dock and port workers. Go to stopwar.org.uk

author: Antimilitaristisches Aktionsnetzwerk (a2n)
title: „War Resisters Welcome!“ Mitmachen bei Adbusting-Aktion?
content:
Am 10. Dezember ist der Internationale Tag der Menschenrechte. Dieses Datum wollen wir nutzen, um in vielen Städten mit selbst gebastelten Plakaten für Asyl für Kriegsdienstverweiger*innen zu protestieren. Dazu haben wir mit Farbe und Papier selber Plakate erstellt. Diese sind grün wie Notausgangsschilder. Sie haben auch die typische weiße Tür, den Pfeil und das menschliche Piktogramm. Doch das Piktogramm hat einen Stahlhelm und ein Gewehr vor dem Notausgang fallen gelassen. Dazu steht auf dem Poster weiß auf Grün der Slogan „War Resisters Welcome!“ Wie Du mitmachen kannst, erfährst Du hier:


Asyl für Kriegsdienstverweigerer*innen


Ohne Soldat*innen können Diktaturen keine Kriege führen. Deswegen ist Asyl für Kriegsdienstverweiger*innen und Deserteur*innen so wichtig. Aber entgegen vollmundiger Ankündigungen will die Bundesregierung diese Leute aus Russland und Belarus lieber schnell wieder los sein. Nur etwas weniger als 100 russische Deserteur*innen, Kriegsdienstverweiger*innen und vor der Einberufung Geflüchtete hat die Bundesregierung bisher anerkannt!


Aufmerksamkeit schaffen mit Adbusting


Adbusting, also das Kapern von Werbevitrinen, ist eine sehr gute Möglichkeit, um einem politischem Thema Raum in der Öffentlichkeit zu verschaffen. Und das ist nicht einmal verboten: Die Staatsanwaltschaft Berlin findet, dass das Öffnen und Hineinhängen eigener Poster nicht strafbar sei. Wir wollen mit selbst gebastelten Postern in Werbevitrinen im öffentlichen Raum Asyl für Kriegsdienstverweiger*innen fordern.


Mitmachen?


Du und deine Gruppe wollen gerne mitmachen, habt aber noch keine Erfahrung mit Adbusting? Keine Bange, dann könnt ihr das bei uns lernen! Denn wir haben das Skillshare „Bundeswehr-Werbung busten!“ vorbereitet. Es findet in Berlin vom Freitag, den 4. bis Sonntag, den 6. Dezember statt. Das genaue Programm findet ihr hier:


https://antimil-aktionsnetzwerk.site36.net/2026/10/27/skillshare-bundeswehr-werbung-busten-berlin-4-6-12-2026/


Schon Erfahrung?


Ihr habt schon Erfahrung mit Adbusting? Super, schreibt uns an antimil_aktionsnetzwerk@riseup.net Dann können wir gemeinsam Absprachen treffen, wie die Poster zu euch kommen. Bitte sendet uns nach der Aktion schicke Bilder der Poster in den gekaperten Werbevitrinen in eurer Stadt zu. Macht die Fotos bitte in einem horizontalen Format. Bitte fotografiert die Bilder so, dass man die Slogans lesen kann. Und bitte gerne vor einem Gebäude oder einer Straßenszene, die symbolisch für eure Stadt ist. Bitte überlegt auch, ob ihr nicht an unserem Skillshare „Bundeswehr-Werbung busten“!“ in Berlin vom Freitag, den 4. Dezember bis Sonntag, den 6. Dezember teilnehmen möchtet. Eure Erfahrung und euer Wissen ist sicher wertvoll! Das genaue Programm findet ihr hier:


https://antimil-aktionsnetzwerk.site36.net/2026/10/27/skillshare-bundeswehr-werbung-busten-berlin-4-6-12-2026/


Repression?


Doch, Adbusting gibt Ärger. Es hat sich in den letzten zehn Jahren dank wehrhafter Soli-Arbeit zwar einiges getan. Damals beschäfftigte sich das Terrorabwehrzentrum GETZ vier Mal mit Adbusting, der Bundesverfassungsschutz warnte in seinem jährlichen Bericht für 2018 vor Adbusting als Gefahr für die Republik und die Berliner Cops traten 2017 und 2018 verzweifelt allem und jedem, den sie mit Adbusting in Verbindung bringen konnten, die Tür ein. Das hat sich geändert: Das Bundesverfassungsgericht erklärte 2023 Hausdurchsuchungen wegen Adbusting für illegal. In Berlin werden Verfahren wegen Adbusting seit 2020 eingestellt, wenn beim Aufhängen eigener selbst produzierter Plakate nichts geklaut oder kaputt gemacht wurde. Das Ordnungsamt Tübingen versuchte es 2025 erfolglos mit der Behauptung einer Ordnungswidrigkeit. In Schwerin gab es 2026 sogar einen Freispruch.


Oldenburg?


Doch In Oldenburg ging die Staatsanwaltschaft gerade mit einer Hausdurchsuchung gegen selbst gedruckte Adbustings vor. Auf Urteile aus Karlsruhe scheißen sei dort „übliches Vorgehen“, sagt die Staatsanwaltschaft.


Guten Chancen


Wir denken, dass man angesichts der juristischen Lage gute Chancen hat, auch in Oldenburg aus Ärger wieder rauszukommen, wenn wir uns anschließend gemeinsam kollektiv angemessen gegen Repression wehren. Aber klar: Erfolgreicher Protest führt im demokratischen Rechtstaat erstmal zu Repression und viel Arbeit; das muss jedem klar sein, der/die sich auf diese Weise politisch engagiert. Auch deswegen haben wir beim Skillshare „Bundeswehr-Werbung busten“!“ einen Schwerpunkt zu …

author: webadmin
title: No Land, No Hunting
content:
Thank you to West Midlands Hunt Saboteurs for this guest article.


On Thursday 8th October, West Midlands Hunt Sabs (WMHS) held a protest outside The Bower House in Shipston on Stour. The restaurant is owned by Andrew Stephen Bower Knight, who continually allows, not only the Warwickshire Hunt to illegally hunt foxes on his land at Compton Scorpion, but the North Cotswold Hunt too.


The protest caused quite a stir amongst the pro-hunt community prompting the British Hound Sports Association (BHSA) to publish a social media post stating

“Rural businesses are under attack by urban saboteurs.”


Visitors to The Bower House in Shipston on Stour were made aware that business owner, Andrew Stephen Bower Knight, enables illegal fox hunting.


The campaign against the Warwickshire Hunt is one that spans back years and is steeped in controversy, including the fact that Warwickshire Police entered into a “secret deal” with the hunt when they withdrew the Community Protection Notice that they had been issued.


WMHS have always highlighted the importance of holding landowners to account, something which featured heavily in the campaign against the now defunct Atherstone Hunt. The Hunting Act stipulates that should a landowner allow the hunting of a wild mammal with dogs on their land then they are breaking the law.


Demonstrations took place outside businesses that supported the now defunct Atherstone Hunt.

© West Midlands Hunt Sabs


Section 3.1 of the Hunting Act 2004 states;

“A person commits an offence if he knowingly permits land which belongs to him to be entered or used in the course of the commission of an offence under Section 1.”

Section 1 of the Hunting Act states;

“A person commits an offence if he hunts a wild mammal with a dog.”


“Trail” hunting does not exist, a fact which was openly discussed during a 2020

webinar

 held by the then Hunting Office, now the BHSA. It was the hunting community who coined the term “smokescreen” to describe “trail” hunting, as they discussed ways that hunts could continue to break the law. Now they are acting the victim, especially when landowners are reminded of their part in this pantomime.


WMHS work alongside other anti-hunt groups such as Locals Against the Warwickshire Hunt and Warwickshire Hunt Watch to use a varied approach to their campaigning. One of which is writing to landowners to remind them of their responsibilities and to inform them of what the Warwickshire Hunt are capable of.


As well as detailing the contents of the Hunting Act, the letters remind landowners that only last year, Ben Halsall of the Warwickshire Hunt was convicted under the Hunting Act after a fox was killed. The letter also states that the presiding judge at the trial made a statement that there was

“no evidence at all of any trail being laid.”


In 2023 this fox was killed by the Warwickshire Hunt, on land owned by Marcus Dill of Idlicote House Estate. Hunt member Ben Field was found guilty; however, no charges were brought against Marcus.


The letter goes on to say that

“The new huntsman, Jack Weedon has previously been caught on camera blocking an active badger sett in a Site of Special Scientific Interest and has recently been cautioned under a Section 4a Public Order offence.”


The protest held on 8th October took place during a book signing event by Dame Prue Leith. The aim; to make people aware of the fact that the business, through its owner, is linked to illegal fox hunting. However, the pro-hunt community have tried to claim that by protesting, sabs are putting people’s livelihoods at risk, rather than focusing on the fact that the only person putting any livelihood at risk is Andrew, by continuing to break the law and enable an illegal fox hunt.


If people choose to not use an establishment or support a business because they facilitate fox hunting, that’s their prerogative.


The Warwickshire Hunt have already lost a lot of land, some of which is through landowners rescinding their permission due to public outcry. In October 2025 Warwickshire Christmas Tree Farm very publicly withdrew permission for the hunt to use their land, stating that due to the public’s disgust at their affiliation with the Warwickshire Hunt they were left with no choice.


Warwickshire Christmas Tree Farm publicly withdrew permission for the Warwickshire Hunt to use their land.

author: L214
title: Enquête abattoir Cooperl
content:
L214 publie une enquête sur l’étourdissement des cochons au CO₂ dans l’un des plus gros abattoirs de France : l’abattoir Cooperl de Montfort-sur-Meu, en Ille-et-Vilaine (Bretagne).

Les images, commentées par l'écrivaine Marie Darrieussecq, montrent la cruauté de cette méthode d'étourdissement dont les instances scientifiques ont établi qu’elle est source de peur, de détresse et de souffrance.

Plus de trente vétérinaires signent un appel publié ce jour pour demander l’interdiction du gazage au CO₂ des cochons. L214 se joint à cette demande et entame un recours contre l’État pour faire interdire cette pratique. L’enseigne de supermarchés Carrefour fait fabriquer par son partenaire Cooperl ses produits à base de viande de porc sous ses marques distributeurs, notamment sa marque Filière Qualité Carrefour. L’association demande à Carrefour de refuser le gazage des cochons et de signer le Plant Protein Pact.

Le musicien Moby apporte son soutien et appelle à signer la pétition.

Chaque heure d’abattage, plus de 800 cochons sont gazés au CO₂ à l’abattoir Cooperl de Montfort-sur-Meu, en Bretagne. Plongés dans une fosse à haute concentration en CO₂, les cochons ont la sensation de se noyer : ils hurlent, paniquent, cherchent désespérément à fuir. Il leur faut entre 21 et 60 secondes pour perdre conscience…

Ce n’est ni instantané, ni sans souffrance. Les instances scientifiques européenne (EFSA) et britannique (AWC) l’affirment depuis 20 ans : cette méthode provoque douleur, peur et détresse respiratoire. Le Royaume-Uni envisage même d’y renoncer, et plus de trente vétérinaires demandent son interdiction.

Pourtant, l’abattoir Cooperl de Montfort-sur-Meu a investi en 2024 environ 5 millions d'euros dans cet équipement qui permet d’abattre un nombre gigantesque d’animaux, de conquérir de nouveaux marchés, d’augmenter les cadences et la productivité. L’enseigne Carrefour fait fabriquer par son partenaire Cooperl des produits à base de cochons gazés sous ses marques, dont la Filière Qualité Carrefour, tout en se disant « pionnier sur le bien-être animal »…

À l’État français : interdire le gazage au CO₂ des cochons ;

À Carrefour : ne plus s’approvisionner en produits issus de cochons gazés et participer à un changement collectif en s'engageant dans le Plant Protein Pact, pour prendre part à une réduction de moitié du nombre d’animaux tués d’ici 2030.

Plus nous serons nombreux et nombreuses, plus il sera difficile pour les responsables de fermer les yeux. Signez et partagez : les cochons ne peuvent pas parler pour eux-mêmes, mais nous, oui.
