author: Unknown
title: Elisée Reclus - The Vivisection of China
content:
Author

: Elisée Reclus

Title

: The Vivisection of China

Date

: 1898

Notes

: From the September 1898 issue of The Atlantic

Source

: Retrieved on October 22, 2026 from an archived copy of https://www.theatlantic.com/magazine/archive/1898/09/the-vivisection-of-china/636369/


 THE great events which are creating such an excitement in the West Indies over the last shreds of the ancient colonial empire of Spain will undoubtedly have consequences of extreme importance, and become, in the fullest sense of the term, a part of history. But, however intense their interest, and however marked the change which they are certain to occasion in the equilibrium of the world, they remain altogether inferior in real significance to the revolutions which are taking place in the Far East.


 War of some sort between America and Spain on the subject of Cuba had long been unavoidable. No less than a century ago, — at the time when France lost her plantations in San Domingo, and the republic of Hayti was born, — it was easy to foresee the rupture of the ties which had bound to the Spain of Cortez and Pizarro the insular fragments of the great hemisphere appropriated by Pope Alexander VI. The various colonies were sure to break away, one by one, from their metropolitan stepmother, set up for themselves, and live their own life. Cuba and Porto Rico, sucked into the whirlpool of war, are but accomplishing their “manifest destiny,” and fulfilling the prophecies repeatedly uttered by the historians of the last generation but one.


 The progress of events in the eastern portion of the Asian continent had by no means been so fully anticipated. One might certainly have ventured to predict that there, also, populations long crushed by civil and military oppression would one day lay claim to the rights of free men; but it could never have been foreseen under what amazingly dramatic conditions the claim would be asserted. Our ancestors, at the beginning of the nineteenth century, would never have harbored, in their wildest dreams, the fantastic notion that Japan, the empire of the Rising Sun, would spontaneously transform itself into a “European power;” European, at least, if not in language, history, and traditions, in the complete recasting of its administration, institutions, customs, and theories, in its devotion to science, and in its entire and unreserved acceptance of a policy based on observation and experience.


 This is the great event of the century, — one which casts into the shade all the other occurrences of an epoch which has nevertheless been rich in memorable events. And it will be no solitary

avatar;

 there are unmistakable signs that other transformations of the same character are about to take place in the vast empire of China, and in all those countries where inhabitants of different race, yellow, red, or black, are brought into close contact with the men of our own Aryano - Greco - Latin civilization. So vanishes that oft-repeated assertion of the ethnologists, that

race

 is a final and irreducible fact, and that no possible progress in the perception of scientific or moral truths can ever prevail against it. It is from this point of view that the recent history of the Far East presents phenomena to which it behooves us to devote our most serious attention.


 There are those, of course, who tell us that all these events are illusory; that the prodigious changes which have taken place in the Japanese world are a lying phantasmagoria and a vain show; that the national mind and character have undergone no real modification; and that the Japanese are sure to escape, sooner or later, from the sphere of European attraction. We hear them compared to savages, who, having learned in the schools of London or Paris the customs of civilization, make haste, as soon as they get back to their forests and savannas, to cast aside their conventional garments, and array themselves in the toggery consecrated by ancestral instinct and hereditary custom.


 Such assertions appear to us to rest on a complete misconception of indisputable facts. The Japanese have most certainly entered into that realm of civilization on which Bacon and Darwin have set their seal; for if imperial caprice and the spread of bourgeois fashions have power to alter the external aspect of a nation, such influences can have but little effect on its underlying moral sense, its religious beliefs, its educational theories, and the essential principle of its …

author: Benji
title: Töten im Takt – Die grausamste Maschine bei Tönnies
content:
Töten im Takt – Die grausamste Maschine bei Tönnies

Tiere leiden vor dem Schlachten Höllenqualen bei CO₂-Betäubung

ARIWA veröffentlicht jetzt erstmals umfangreiche Aufnahmen aus einem Schlachthof von Tönnies. Schlachthöfe gehören zu den schwierigsten Herausforderungen für Undercover-Aufnahmen, da sie extrem gut gesichert sind. Die Betreiber setzen alles daran, dass das, was dort geschieht, nicht an die Öffentlichkeit gelangt.


19.10.2026, Deutschland


 NDR berichtet mit Videomaterial von ARIWA.


Er ist Deutschlands größter Schlachtkonzern und gilt als eines der mächtigsten Unternehmen der europäischen Fleischindustrie: Tönnies. Als Marktführer produziert er 30 Prozent des gesamten deutschen Schweinefleischs. Allein 2023 meldete der Konzern einen Jahresumsatz von über 7 Milliarden Euro. Dafür tötet Tönnies jedes Jahr 16 Millionen


Schweine. 


Das uns vorliegende Material zeigt, wie Mitarbeiter*innen die Tiere beim Zutrieb schlagen und sie unter automatischen Toren eingeklemmt werden. Es zeigt den grausamen Erstickungskampf in der CO₂-Anlage mit Tieren, die in Gondeln vor Angst schreien und versuchen zu fliehen. Und es zeigt zahlreiche Verstöße gegen die gesetzlichen Vorschriften vor und während der Schlachtung.


Von der Ankunft bis zum Tod:

Erste Undercover-Aufnahmen aus Tönnies Schlachthof


Das vorliegende Material dokumentiert erstmals unabhängig den gesamten Ablauf der Schlachtung von der Ankunft der Tiere im Schlachthof bis zur Tötung. Die Aufnahmen zeigen, wie leidvoll die letzten Stunden im Leben der Tiere sind. Das liegt auch an einer Maschine im Schlachthof, die grausamer nicht sein könnte: Die sogenannte CO₂-Betäubungsanlage.


Die Betäubung vor dem Schlachten ist gesetzlich vorgeschrieben. Die Tiere sollen so vor Schmerzen und Stress geschützt werden. Auch zur Betäubung selbst gibt es eindeutige Vorgaben: Paragraf 12 der Tierschutz-Schlachtverordnung legt fest, dass Tiere “schnell und unter Vermeidung von Schmerzen oder Leiden in einen (…) Zustand der Wahrnehmungs- und Empfindungslosigkeit” versetzt werden müssen. Der Betäubungsvorgang darf also keine Schmerzen oder Leid auslösen und muss bis zum Tod des Tieres anhalten. Doch die Aufnahmen zeigen eindeutig, dass die Betäubung mit CO₂ gegen diese Vorschrift verstößt!


Ankunft im Schlachthof


Am frühen Morgen kommen die ersten LKWs auf dem Schlachthof an. An den aufgenommenen Tagen werden mindestens fünftausend Schweine pro Tag hier angeliefert und getötet. Tönnies verfügt über ein riesiges Netz von Zulieferbetrieben in ganz Deutschland.


Nach ihrer Ankunft werden die Tiere in enge Wartebuchten gebracht. Hier läuft sanfte Musik, sie soll die Tiere entspannen. Es wirkt makaber. Neunzig Minuten lang sollen sich die vom Transport und Ausladen gestressten Schweine hier beruhigen, dabei ist zu erkennen, wie ängstlich sie sind.


Doch das wahre Grauen kommt erst noch. Nach anderthalb Stunden öffnet sich ein Tor. Ein Mitarbeiter beginnt, die Tiere in einen Treibgang zu scheuchen. Dabei kommt Gewalt zum Einsatz: Wenn die Schweine panisch versuchen zu fliehen, schlägt der Mitarbeiter mit der Treibstange zu, auch ins Gesicht. Die Schweine werden nach und nach in Sechsergruppen aufgeteilt. Als nächstes geht es für sie in die Betäubungsanlage.


Per Gondel in den Erstickungskampf


Die Schweine sind jetzt in einem engen Abteil, aus dem es kein Zurück gibt. Ein Mitarbeiter treibt die Gruppen nacheinander in die Gondelkäfige, mit denen es in wenigen Augenblicken gut 9 Meter nach unten in eine mit CO₂ gefüllte Grube geht. Manche Tiere werden von den schweren hydraulischen Trenngittern eingeklemmt und können sich nicht alleine befreien. Sie schreien vor Schmerz.


Sobald die erste Gruppe von Schweinen in ihre Gondel getrieben wurde, schließt sich der Käfig aus dicken Metallstangen. Kurze Zeit später setzt sich die Gondel in Bewegung. Die versteckte Kamera fährt mit. Innerhalb weniger Sekunden reagieren viele Schweine mit Panik. Viele schreien, schnappen nach Luft, werfen sich gegen die Gitterstäbe und steigen aufeinander. Die Fluchtversuche können so heftig sein, dass manche Tiere sich verletzen und Blutspuren an der Anlage zurücklassen.


Je tiefer die Tiere in den Schacht fahren, desto heftiger werden ihre Fluchtversuche. Die CO₂-Konzentration beträgt nach wenigen Metern schon 80 Prozent. Zeitgleich wird oben die nächste Gruppe in die Gondeln getrieben. Sie können die Angstschreie ihrer Artgenossen aus den Gondeln unter ihnen hören.

author: Brian Hioe
title: Animal Rights Advocates Call for Referendum on Snare Traps
content:
ANIMAL RIGHTS ADVOCATES are currently campaigning for a referendum to be held on the use of wild boar snares.

In particular, animal rights advocates have long criticized wild boar snares as overly cruel. Such traps use spring-loaded mechanisms to tighten around animals’ limbs when triggered.

Nevertheless, such traps have also been criticized for ensnaring other species, as they do not distinguish. Endangered species such as Formosan black bears and leopard cats had also been killed by such traps, as have cats and dogs, sometimes resulting in their losing limbs if they survive.

Though claims had been made that Indigenous hunters used such traps as part of traditional hunting rights, animal rights groups have generally cited that this was rarely the case, in that Indigenous hunters generally do not use such traps. By contrast, such animal rights advocates state that Indigenous hunters more commonly use traps made from wood, bamboo and vines, and other natural materials. In the past, the Central Election Commission turned down calls for a referendum on the use of wild boar snares on the basis that the referendum was unclear as to whether it pertained to traps used by Indigenous hunters.

Otherwise, such traps are sometimes used by farmers as a means of preventing damage to their crops. Animal rights advocates have called on the government to provide electric fencing, protective netting, or other means for farmers to protect their livestock and crops.

The proposals called for by animal rights advocates are relevant to the use, display, and sale of wild boar snares, as well as their import and export. It is thought that China is a major source of some of the wild boar snares used in Taiwan.

It is unclear as to whether the Central Election Commission will approve the referendum currently called for by animal rights advocates. At the same time, without a major political party endorsing it as an issue, such a referendum is unlikely to gain traction. It is to be seen if either the DPP or KMT, or perhaps even both parties, throw their weight behind the proposal.

One notes that there have been cases of political bipartisanship between both major parties on the issue of animal rights in past years, as seen with politicians of both parties supporting enshrining animal rights in the constitution. Even so, such politicians ultimately did not prove serious about such promises outside of election campaigning, as a result of which neither the KMT nor DPP acted on claims in past election cycles that animal rights would see constitutional protection.

author: Sophie Lemcke
title: So ist es, als weibliches Rind in der Milchindustrie zu leben
content:
Die Milchindustrie ist ein grausamer Kreislauf des Leids und endet mit einem gewaltvollen Tod.


Wie fühlt es sich an, in dieses System hineingeboren zu werden, ohne die Möglichkeit, dem zu entkommen?


Der einzige Grund, weshalb die Industrie dich „produziert“ hat: Auch du sollst Kinder gebären, immer wieder, damit du Milch produzierst. Milch, die dann von Menschen, statt von deinem Kalb konsumiert werden kann.


Du wirst fixiert, während jemand das Besamungsgerät in deine Vagina sowie seinen Arm in deinen Anus einführt. Wenn die Zwangsbefruchtung nicht beim ersten Mal zur Trächtigkeit führt – was oft der Fall ist –, wird dieser Vorgang mehrfach wiederholt.


Neun Monate – wie bei uns Menschen – wächst dein Kalb in dir heran. Du spürst eine Verbindung, merkst, wie es sich bewegt und immer größer wird. Je schwerer du selbst wirst, umso stärker werden deine Gelenkprobleme. Die rutschigen und harten Spaltenböden, auf denen du fast dein ganzes Leben verbringst, führen oft zu Verletzungen.


Dann bringst du dein Kalb zur Welt. Um dich herum riecht es extrem nach Kot und Ammoniak, von den Ausscheidungen der Tiere.


Endlich ist es da, noch ganz nass und schwach. Du leckst ihm über das Fell, um es zu wärmen. Es sucht deine Nähe und will an deinem Euter die für ihn so wichtige Erstmilch trinken. Sie stärkt sein noch schwaches Immunsystem und gibt ihm Kraft. Doch dann kommen die Arbeiter*innen.


Sie zerren dein noch ganz wackelig stehendes Kalb weg von dir. Es ruft nach dir. Du versuchst, bei ihm zu bleiben, aber du hast keine Chance. Die Menschen haben es weggebracht – du wirst es wahrscheinlich nie wiedersehen und nach nur zwei Monaten direkt wieder gewaltvoll befruchtet.


Du wirst nach der Geburt monatelang mehrmals täglich in den Melkstand getrieben – und die meiste Zeit davon bist du bereits wieder schwanger. Dein Körper muss gleichzeitig ein neues Kalb versorgen, das in dir heranwächst, und täglich über 22 Liter Milch produzieren. Dein Euter und deine Zitzen schmerzen. Aufgrund der extremen Überzüchtung produzierst du viermal so viel Milch, wie du es natürlicherweise für dein Kind tun würdest.


Die Prozeduren und Haltungsbedingungen zehren stark an deinem Körper. Dein Euter ist entzündet und schmerzt bei jeder Berührung. Andere Tiere humpeln, weil ihnen jeder Schritt wehtut. Viele sind schwach und ausgelaugt.


Wenn du nicht schon vorher stirbst oder getötet wirst, weil dein Körper nicht mehr kann, dann wirst du voraussichtlich nach nur fünf Jahren getötet – obwohl du unter natürlichen Bedingungen 25 Jahre alt werden könntest.


Dann kommt der Tag, an dem du als nicht mehr profitabel giltst. Du wirst aus dem Stall getrieben – das erste Mal nach Jahren verlässt du ihn, aber das ist kein Grund zur Freude.


Zusammen mit anderen erschöpften „ausgedienten Milchkühen“ wirst du auf einen Transporter verladen. Du hast Mühe, über die Rampe zu gehen. Deine Gelenke schmerzen vom jahrelangen Stehen auf Spaltenböden. Im engen Transporter stehst du dicht an dicht mit den anderen Tieren, der Lkw wackelt. Manche fallen hin und werden versehentlich getreten. Eure Fahrt in den Schlachthof dauert mehrere Stunden, ohne Wasser, ohne Nahrung, ohne Pause.


Angekommen erwartet dich ein brutaler Tod. Überall riecht es nach Blut, du bekommst Panik, aber es gibt keinen Ausweg. Dann ein Bolzenschuss in deinen Kopf. Wenn die Betäubung korrekt durchgeführt wurde und wirkt, brichst du zusammen. Wenn nicht, kann es sein, dass du bei Bewusstsein und unter extremen Schmerzen erlebst, wie dir deine Kehle aufgeschnitten wird und du verblutest.


Es ist unvorstellbar, was Mutterrinder in der Milchindustrie erleiden müssen.


Der wahre Preis von Milch


Ein Ermittler von Animal Equality hat mehrere Monate undercover in einem deutschen Milchgewinnungsbetrieb gearbeitet und den Alltag der Tiere dokumentiert. Was unsere Undercover-Recherche zeigt, ist der wahre Preis von Milch: Ausbeutung, Gewalt, Schmerz, Leid und Tod.


Auf unserer Webseite erfährst du mehr und kannst die Stellungnahme des Betriebs nachlesen:


Zur Undercover-Recherche


Unterstütze dieses grausame System nicht!


Entscheide dich konsequent für pflanzliche Lebensmittel. Im Supermarkt findest du zahlreiche Alternativen zu Milch, wie:


Hafermilch – mild, cremig, perfekt für Kaffee und Müsli (oft die günstigste Option!)


Sojamilch – proteinreich, ideal zum Kochen und Backen


Mandelmilch – leicht nussig, besonders lecker in Smoothies


Reismilch – süßlich und gut verträglich …

author: PETA-Team
title: Tierpark Neumünster: PETA kritisiert halbherzige Neuausrichtung mit heimischen Wildtieren
content:
Update vom 29. Oktober 2026


Künftig weniger

 „

exotische Tiere

”

im Tierpark Neumünster


Laut Medienberichten will der Tierpark Neumünster in Zukunft vor allem heimische Wildtiere zur Schau stellen. Viele der dort gehaltenen „exotischen“ Tiere, darunter der 26-jährige Eisbär Vitus, sollen künftig andernorts untergebracht werden.


Wir von PETA Deutschland begrüßen die geplante Abgabe exotischer Tiere als Schritt in die richtige Richtung, da wir die schlechten Haltungsbedingungen im Tierpark seit Jahren kritisieren. Damit die Tiere eine Chance auf ein besseres Leben haben, muss bei der Vermittlung der Tiere sichergestellt werden, dass sie nicht in ungeeignete Privathaltungen oder andere fragwürdige Einrichtungen gelangen.


Allerdings sollten auch heimische Wildtiere wie Elche, Wisente und Luchse nicht in Gefangenschaft leben müssen – selbst weitläufige Waldgehege können ihren komplexen Bedürfnissen nicht gerecht werden.


Wir fordern deshalb, dass der Tierpark künftig ausschließlich als Auffangstation für beschlagnahmte und aus schlechter Haltung gerettete Tiere dient.


Update vom 13. Juli 2026


Eisbärin Larissa ist eingeschläfert worden


Die Eisbärin Larissa wurde am 10. Juli 2026 im Tierpark Neumünster getötet, da sich ihr gesundheitlicher Zustand altersbedingt verschlechtert hat. Mit 36 Jahren galt sie laut dem Tierpark als die älteste Eisbärin der Welt. Larissa zeigte, wie viele Eisbären in Zoos, deutliche Verhaltensstörungen. Wir von PETA Deutschland hatten bereits 2022 ein Video veröffentlicht, in dem zu sehen ist, wie sie über längere Zeit immer wieder dieselben wenigen Meter am Beckenrand auf und ab lief.


Aufgrund ihrer traurigen Lebensgeschichte fordern wir erneut ein Ende der Eisbärenhaltung in Zoos und setzen uns mit einer Petition an das Bundeslandwirtschaftsministerium dafür ein, die Zucht der Tiere auslaufen zu lassen.


Originalbeitrag vom 22. Juni 2023


Video: Erschreckendes Tierleid im Tierpark Neumünster


Seit Jahren erhalten wir bei PETA Deutschland regelmäßig Hinweise von Whistleblower:innen auf Tierleid im Tierpark Neumünster. Im April 2023 dokumentierten wir daraufhin selbst vor Ort schlechte Haltungsbedingungen und

Verhaltensstörungen

 bei mehreren Tieren im

Zoo

, die nach unserer Einschätzung auf seelisches Leid hinweisen. Wir haben daher Strafanzeige gegen den Tierpark erstattet.


Verhaltensgestört: Eisbären laufen immer hin und her


In einem Video ist zu sehen, wie die

Eisbärin

 Larissa am Beckenrand immer wieder ziellos wenige Meter auf und ab läuft. Auch ihr Partner Vitus schwimmt die immer gleichen kleinen Kreise. Larissa und Vitus sind beide seit April 2017 in dem winzigen, heruntergekommenen Gehege in Neumünster eingesperrt. Die Verhaltensstörungen der beiden Eisbären sind seit Jahren bekannt und wurden uns seit 2018 wiederholt gemeldet, teilweise auch mit Videomaterial.


„Das Eisbärenpaar zeigt sehr auffällige Verhaltensstörungen. Einer läuft hin und her […] und der andere schwimmt im Pool in einem kleinen Radius im Kreis stundenlang.“

Whistleblower-Meldung vom Juli 2022


„ […] wir haben heute den Tierpark in Neumünster besucht und sind nachhaltig schockiert, unter welchen Bedingungen die Tiere dort gehalten werden. Die Eisbären […] laufen in einem sehr kleinen Gehege immer wieder verstört denselben Weg und wirken höchst apathisch. Das Gehege ist verwildert, verschmutzt und das Wasser im Schwimmbecken der Tiere ist so grün, dass man nicht hine[i]n sehen kann.“

Whistleblower-Meldung vom August 2018


Das Eisbären-Gehege ist beengt und heruntergekommen.


Die ausgeprägten Verhaltensstörungen der Eisbären werden heruntergespielt und „besondere Gerüche“ und ein angeblicher „Hormonüberschuss“ dafür verantwortlich gemacht.


Namhafte Fachleute sind überzeugt, dass Eisbären in Gefangenschaft nicht artgerecht gehalten werden können, da die Diskrepanz zwischen den Bedingungen in ihrem natürlichen Lebensraum und denen im Zoo zu groß ist. [1, 2] Obwohl die Folgen der viel zu kleinen Gehege in Zoos bekannt sind, werden die Tiere weiterhin in diese Leid verursachende Umgebung hineingezüchtet. In freier Natur wandern Eisbären jedes Jahr Hunderte bis Tausende Kilometer. Können sie sich nicht artgemäß bewegen, entwickeln sie auffällige Verhaltensstereotypien, die sich in sich ständig wiederholenden Bewegungsabläufen zeigen. Schon mehrfach veröffentlichte PETA

Videomaterial

, das schwere Zwangsstörungen bei den Tieren belegt.

title: QUORN HUNT TRAINING HOUNDS TO KILL: WRITE TO YOUR MP
content:
The Hunt Saboteurs Association is asking our supporters to contact their MPs following the release of horrific drone footage involving the Quorn Hunt in Leicestershire.


Members of the Quorn Hunt use the fox’s body to encourage hounds to tear it apart.

Image: Northants Hunt Saboteurs


On Friday 16 October 2026, Northants Hunt Saboteurs filmed an incident near Kirby Bellars in which a fox was killed by hounds during a Quorn Hunt cubbing meet.


Hounds converge on the fox as hunt staff look on. Image:

Northants Hunt Saboteurs


The footage shows hounds seizing and tearing at the fox while hunt staff intervene to repeatedly encourage the hounds to attack. A hunting horn can be seen being blown over the hounds to reinforce the association between the horn call and the kill!


Take action: Contact your MP


Don’t let this disturbing footage go unnoticed.


Write to your MP, ask them to watch the video and to support robust legislation to strengthen the Hunting Act. 


Template letter below:


Organised Hunts hunting as usual – Famous Quorn Hunt filmed killing a fox


Dear [MP]


The 1st November will see the official start of the foxhunting season, but hunts have been out since August training their hounds to hunt and kill. This is called autumn hunting by them and cub hunting by the rest of us. 


This is illustrated by the film we obtained taken from a drone showing the Quorn Hunt killing a fox. This is ‘trail hunting’ in its bloody reality, and it happened just a few days ago, on the eve of the BHSA’s National Trail Hunting Day.


The full video can be viewed here:

https://www.huntsabs.org.uk/smokescreen-saturday-exposed/


Cub hunting is not some isolated activity. It is the preparation for the hunting season ahead. Throughout the autumn, young hounds are taught what to chase, what to kill and how to respond to the huntsman’s commands. What they learn – or fail to learn – during these crucial weeks sets the tone for the entire season.


This is what makes the Quorn Hunt footage so damning. It shows hounds being deliberately encouraged to seize and tear at a fox, with hunt staff repeatedly intervening to reinforce that behaviour.


As the British Hound Sports Association (BHSA) and the Countryside Alliance prepared to showcase so-called ‘trail hunting’ on National Trail Hunting Day – aka Smokescreen Saturday – the Quorn Hunt provided a horrifying glimpse of the reality behind the myth of trail laying.


The BHSA and defenders of so-called trail hunting want the public to believe the same hounds will spend the season following scent trails. Yet here they are, being trained on foxes, and of course, killing to the delight of the hunters.


The footage strikes at the very heart of the trail hunting smokescreen.


We need parliament to finish the consultation and push through a real hunting ban in the next parliament term as promised in the manifesto.


Regards


[Name]


[Address]


Find contact details for your MP here


The post

QUORN HUNT TRAINING HOUNDS TO KILL: WRITE TO YOUR MP

 appeared first on

Hunt Saboteurs Association

title: Resistance against solar power plant project in Kulp on day 91
content:
Resistance against the planned solar power plant project.in the village of Cixsê, in the Kulp district of Amed (Diyarbakır), has continued for three months. For 91 days, residents have maintained a vigil in protest against the project, which threatens grazing lands, water sources, and agricultural livelihoods. An investigation by the Union of Chambers of Turkish Engineers and Architects (TMMOB) has now confirmed significant shortcomings in the environmental impact assessment. The organization is calling for the immediate cancellation of the project.


Representatives of the TMMOB Coordination Council in Amed presented their findings during a protest in Cixsê. The findings are based on a site inspection conducted on October 14, during which experts examined both the proposed construction site and the information contained in the environmental impact assessment documentation.


Grazing lands and water sources at risk


According to Filiz Kaçar, a member of TMMOB’s Energy and Ecology Commission, approximately 30 hectares of land within and around the project area are used as grazing grounds for livestock. The installation of solar panels, fencing of the site, and construction of access roads would fragment continuous grazing areas and significantly restrict their use. The commission is particularly concerned about the potential impact on local water resources. The affected area contains a pond and several streams that are important for supplying water to livestock. The planned construction work could damage these natural resources.


Cixsê is also an important center for silkworm breeding and cocoon production. Alongside livestock farming and crop cultivation, this sector forms a vital foundation of local livelihoods. According to the experts, habitats of migratory birds such as cranes, storks, and swallows would also be affected.


Significant shortcomings in the environmental impact assessment


According to Kaçar, TMMOB’s investigation found that key ecological and economic factors had been inadequately addressed in the project documentation. These include existing bodies of water, the traditional use of grazing lands, biodiversity, natural hazards, and the planned energy storage systems. The organization does not fundamentally oppose the expansion of renewable energy, but rather its implementation at the expense of local residents and their livelihoods. “The transition to renewable energy is necessary. But an energy transition that ignores nature and life is not sustainable. The solar project planned in Cixsê must be stopped immediately,” Kaçar stated.


Fatoş Nujen Ayhan of the TMMOB Coordination Council also criticized the economic interests behind the project: “Cixsê’s energy resources must be used and managed by the local population itself. We cannot allow corporations to exploit our resources and then sell the energy generated from them back to the people at high prices.”


Incorrect photographs previously discovered in environmental report


The new findings have intensified the dispute over the approval of the project. As early as September, it emerged that the environmental impact assessment report contained photographs that had not been taken in the proposed project area. The Amed Bar Association and the Association of Lawyers for Freedom (ÖHD) subsequently filed a criminal complaint against officials of the environmental consultancy Global ÇED and the construction company VBZ İnşaat. However, the public prosecutor’s office in Kulp found insufficient grounds for suspicion of document forgery and closed the investigation. The lawyers appealed the decision. Separately, the decision approving the environmental impact assessment is the subject of administrative court proceedings.


“Our land belongs to us”


The DEM Party also supports the villagers’ resistance. Berivan Turan, a member of the party’s provincial executive board in Amed, warned of the long-term social and ecological consequences during the protest. She stated that the loss of agricultural land and natural resources could exacerbate unemployment, poverty, and migration. “The people do not want a solar power plant on this grazing land. They have been expressing their opposition for months,” Turan said. She placed the resistance in Cixsê within the broader context of local struggles against the economic exploitation of natural resources in Kurdistan, citing the vigil in Arzoxlî as an example.


“We do not want to lose our cemeteries, our culture …

title: Villagers Barred from Public Hearing on Rs 10,000-Crore Steel Project in Raghunathpur, Purulia; Allege Police Repression
content:
Accusing the administration of staging a secretive, stage-managed public hearing for Shakambhari Ispat and Power Ltd in Purulia, villagers blocked a state highway, raising concerns over air pollution, water scarcity, and loss of farmland and the health of communities already living amid polluting industries.


 


Raghunathpur, October 28, 2026:

Residents of several villages in Raghunathpur sub-division of West Bengal’s Purulia district blocked the Raghunathpur–Santaldihi State Highway on Wednesday in protest against the public hearing for a proposed Rs 10,000-crore steel and power complex of Shakambhari Ispat and Power Ltd. The villagers accuse the administration of keeping them out of the hearing, held at the office of the Sub-Divisional Officer (SDO) of Raghunathpur, by deploying a large police force, barricading the approach and locking the main gate, while a handful of people allegedly handpicked by the company were allowed inside, so that what they describe as a farcical hearing could be staged to manufacture public consent for the project.


A large police force, barricaded the approach and locked the main gate of the SDO office


The hearing, scheduled for noon, has revived long-standing fears in a region that is already heavily industrialised, where communities have for years been living with the consequences of industrial pollution and now worry about further threats to their water, their agricultural land and their health.


 


In an emergency press release issued the same day, the

Forum for Opposition to Pollution and Protection of Life and Nature

 said that villagers from Durmut, Hurra, Nildi, Manipur, Kewabathan, Joradi, Jharukhamar and Layekdi had reached the SDO’s office before 11 am to exercise what they described as their constitutional right to take part in a hearing that would decide the future of their lives and livelihoods, only to find police barricades and a locked gate standing between them and the proceedings.


Villagers sit on road in protest against the sham public hearing


A hearing without notice or translation


 


The forum further alleged that the hearing had been organised without adequate public notice. According to its statement, there were no announcements by loudspeaker, no traditional forms of public announcement and no posters in the affected villages during the mandatory 30-day notice period. It also alleged that residents of the predominantly Adivasi villages were not given the relevant project documents in Bengali, or in Santali in the Ol Chiki script, leaving those most affected without any meaningful means of understanding what was being proposed.


 


These allegations go to the heart of the process. Under the Environment Impact Assessment Notification, 2006, the public hearing is the principal stage at which people likely to be affected by a project can place their concerns on record before environmental clearance is considered; the notification requires at least 30 days’ notice and the availability of a summary of the draft EIA report in the local language. A hearing from which the affected public is physically excluded, the forum argues, cannot be regarded as a hearing at all, and it has demanded that the proceedings be cancelled and the project’s environmental impact assessment (EIA) report be rejected.


 


Industrial expansion beside homes, schools and forests


 


The proposed complex is to comprise a steel plant with a stated capacity of 2.73 million tonnes, a ferro-alloy unit of 0.54 million tonnes per annum, a cement plant of 2 million tonnes per annum and a 484-megawatt power plant.


 


According to the press release, the facility would sit immediately adjacent to Hurra village, with Kewabathan reportedly 140 metres from the project boundary, Nildi 380 metres, Durmut 400 metres and Manipur 420 metres. Hurra Primary School is said to lie roughly 150–160 metres from the site and Nildi High School about 410–430 metres away, while seven protected forest areas are located between 200 metres and 1.7 kilometres from the proposed project.


 


The forum warned that the plant would add to the cumulative pollution burden of an area already ringed by major polluting industries. It identified five large red-category industrial units within a 10-kilometre radius of Durmut mouza:


 


Shakambhari Ispat and Power, Nakshit Iron and Steel, Odisha Alloy Steel/Odisha Metallics, the Damodar Valley Corporation’s Raghunathpur Thermal Power Station and Shyam Steel …

2.1. The Anarchistic Nature of Buddhism

2.2. Socio-Cultural Critique Emerging from Zen and Anarchism

What can esoteric knowledge and spiritual practices from the East teach us about the deep psychological roots of domination and hierarchy? In what ways have ancient Buddhist sages acted as anarchist exemplars and deep ecologists long before these traditions began in the West? How might these anarchistic spiritual traditions inform our approaches to work in education, expand our notions of community, help us navigate ecological collapse, and contribute to our efforts to sustain living systems and rekindle our connection to the myriad sentient inhabitants of the places we live beyond the reaches of capital and the State? This paper will examine the anti-doctrine doctrine of Zen Buddhism as a concrete and embodied system of thought and practice for seeing through the delusions of the ego and the psychological and cultural conditioning these delusions engender. What will also be acknowledged is the general lack of attention this spiritual tradition has given to the capitalistic, authoritarian, and anti-ecological systems that tap into and flow from these delusions. It will be argued that these experiential approaches to overcoming the tyranny of the ego have significant implications for loosening the grip of hierarchical thinking, capitalist hyper-consumption, centralized systems of obedience and command, and human destruction of the biosphere.

“The mercy of the West has been social revolution; the mercy of the East has been individual insight into the basic self/void. We need both.”

—Gary Snyder, Buddhism and the coming revolution, 1969.

title: „Freiheit gibt es in Amerika nicht ohne Kampf“
content:
Michael Koch: Danke, dass du dir Zeit für dieses Interview nimmst. Viele Menschen aus ganz Deutschland und von überall schicken dir die allerbesten Geburtstagsgrüße. Es gibt viele Menschen, die die Forderung nach deiner Freiheit unterstützt haben. Jetzt fragen sie uns oft, wie deine Situation ist, seit du aus dem Gefängnis raus bist, aber unter Hausarrest stehst. Seit unserem letzten Interview haben sich die Dinge entwickelt, es scheint Auflagen zu geben, von denen wir vorher nichts wussten. Wie ist die Situation jetzt?

Leonard Peltier: Ich möchte allen noch einmal danken für eure Unterstützung und euren Einsatz, mich aus dem Gefängnis zu befreien. Ich bin euch für eure Arbeit in Europa sehr dankbar, aber auch für die Unterstützung durch meine People. Die Indigenen haben eine Geschichte, in der sie jede Form von Grausamkeit erlitten haben, die die Menschheit kennt. Sie haben Millionen Tote erlitten, Folter und alle Gräueltaten, die die Welt kennt. Man hat versucht, uns auszulöschen, aber wir sind immer noch hier und werden weiterhin hier sein – auch wenn der Krieg gegen uns weitergeht. Ich genieße es, nicht mehr in einer Gefängniszelle zu sitzen, sondern in meinem eigenen Zuhause zu sein. Solche Dinge haben mir die Menschen ermöglicht – die Regierung hat mir das nicht gegeben. Die Regierung bezahlt meine Rechnungen nicht. Sie bezahlt weder meine Strom- noch meine Wasserrechnung, kauft mir weder Essen noch Benzin, um zu Arztterminen zu fahren. Ich bin darauf angewiesen, dass Menschen auf der ganzen Welt mir weiterhin helfen, auch in diesen Bereichen. Aber trotzdem ist es so viel besser, hier zu Hause zu sein als in einer Gefängniszelle. Zu Hause kann ich Gesellschaft genießen, eine gute, warme Mahlzeit meiner Wahl, so viel Liebe und Freundlichkeit von allen Menschen auf der Welt erfahren, die mich unterstützen. Mir geht es viel besser, aber ich stehe immer noch unter harten Auflagen. Ich kann nicht zum Arzt gehen, und es wird sogar noch schlimmer. Selbst wenn ich einen Termin bei einem Arzt außerhalb des Reservats oder in Reservaten mache, muss ich vorher eine Genehmigung einholen. Bisher wurde mir die Genehmigung in 99 Prozent der Fälle verweigert. Ich bekomme also nicht einmal die medizinische Versorgung, die ein Häftling im Gefängnis bekommt. Aber ich halte durch. Ich habe nicht aufgegeben und werde für den Rest meines Lebens Widerstand leisten.

Michael: Gibt es neue Entwicklungen? Gibt es Leute, die juristisch daran arbeiten, die Auflagen deines Hausarrests zu lockern oder aufzuheben?

Leonard: In den letzten Wochen habe ich ein Rechtsteam aus Anwält*innen und Unterstützer*innen organisiert, die nun wieder in großer Zahl zurückkommen. Wir werden Rechtsmittel bei den Gerichten einlegen, denn was sie tun, verstößt gegen die Verfassung der Vereinigten Staaten – und gegen die Anordnung der Vereinten Nationen. Die Vereinten Nationen haben meine Freilassung gefordert und gesagt, dass ich für die Fehlverurteilung entschädigt werden soll. Aber nein … Wir werden Klage einreichen und eine Anhörung darüber verlangen, was mit mir gemacht wird.

Michael: Wenn wir über die Auflagen sprechen – das sind ja Einschränkungen bei deiner medizinischen Versorgung, sodass du nicht die Behandlung bekommst, die du brauchst, weil du nicht einfach zum Arzt gehen kannst, sondern erst um Erlaubnis fragen musst. Wie ist dein Gesundheitszustand im Moment?

Leonard: Ich habe seit fast 30 Jahren Diabetes und konnte sie unter Kontrolle halten. Aber seit ich vor zwanzig Monaten herausgekommen bin, hat sie sich verschlechtert. Ich habe grauen Star am rechten Auge bekommen. Am linken Auge wurde meine Netzhaut geschädigt. Ich hatte vor etwa 15 Jahren im Gefängnis einen Schlaganfall, und die Fachärzte dort sagten der Gefängnisleitung: „Bringen Sie ihn jetzt zu uns, dann können wir das beheben.“ Sie haben mich nicht einmal untersuchen lassen, mein linkes Auge nicht untersuchen lassen. Ihr alle auf der ganzen Welt habt uns unterstützt – wir mussten uns an die Vereinten Nationen wenden, um zu fordern, dass ich untersucht werde. Aber das geschah erst ein Jahr später, und da war es zu spät, man konnte nichts mehr machen. Seit ich draußen bin, hatte ich grauen Star am rechten Auge, sie haben ihn operiert, und ich habe 80 Prozent meiner Sehkraft verloren. Das ist der Zustand meiner Augen. Außerdem habe ich noch Probleme mit den Schultern und den Knien. Aber alles andere ist, soweit wir wissen, noch in Ordnung. Letzte Woche musste ich allerdings für eine …

title: EL GOBIERNO DE SANTA FE QUIERE CAMBIAR EL DESTINO DE 19 PARTIDAS Y LOS PUEBLOS ORIGINARIOS EXIGIMOS EXPLICACIONES!
content:
¡NO SE PUEDE PROTEGER LA NATURALEZA DESPOJANDO A LOS PUEBLOS ORIGINARIOS DE SUS DERECHOS TERRITORIALES!


 


EXIGIMOS EXPLICACIONES AL GOBIERNO DE PULLARO Y AL IPAS POR LA DESAFECTACIÓN DE 19 PARTIDAS DE TIERRAS DESTINADAS A LA RESTITUCIÓN INDÍGENA.


A raíz de la publicación realizada por el diario El Litoral, donde se informa que el proyecto de creación del Parque Provincial Jaaukanigás contempla la desafectación de 19 partidas inmobiliarias comprendidas en la Ley Provincial N.º 12.086, desde Fuerza Ancestral Indígena de Santa Fe expresamos nuestra profunda preocupación y exigimos explicaciones urgentes al Poder Ejecutivo Provincial y al Instituto Provincial de Aborígenes Santafesinos (IPAS).


 


Lo que se está poniendo en discusión es de enorme gravedad: tierras que estaban contempladas dentro de un régimen legal destinado a la restitución territorial de comunidades indígenas serían retiradas de ese marco para incorporarlas al sistema de áreas naturales protegidas.


 


Según lo publicado, la justificación sería que no existen solicitudes de restitución ni permisos vigentes sobre esos inmuebles y que, por lo tanto, estarían técnicamente disponibles.


 


¿Desde cuándo la falta de un expediente administrativo significa que un territorio deja de tener historia, identidad y derechos ancestrales?


 


Nos preguntamos quién realizó los relevamientos, qué comunidades fueron consultadas y bajo qué criterios se determinó que esas tierras pueden dejar de estar comprendidas en la Ley 12.086.


 


También exigimos saber cuál fue la intervención concreta del IPAS. ¿El organismo acompañó esta decisión? ¿Emitió algún dictamen? ¿Consultó a las comunidades? ¿Defendió los derechos territoriales de los pueblos que tiene la responsabilidad institucional de representar?


 


No alcanza con mencionar que las comunidades Qom y Moqoit participarán de un futuro Plan de Manejo. La participación en la administración de un área protegida no reemplaza el reconocimiento de los derechos territoriales ni la obligación del Estado de garantizar la restitución de tierras.


 


Queremos ser claros: no estamos en contra de la protección ambiental de Jaaukanigás. Estamos en contra de que, bajo el argumento de la conservación, se debiliten herramientas legales destinadas a garantizar derechos indígenas.


 


El Convenio 169 de la OIT y el artículo 75 inciso 17 de la Constitución Nacional no son declaraciones decorativas. Son obligaciones que el Estado debe respetar.


 


La provincia no puede hablar de reconocimiento de la preexistencia indígena mientras toma decisiones que pueden comprometer el futuro territorial de nuestros pueblos.


 


Por eso exigimos explicaciones públicas, acceso al expediente completo, los informes técnicos que fundamentan la desafectación y la intervención institucional del IPAS.


 


Asimismo, solicitamos que se suspenda el avance de la desafectación de las 19 partidas hasta que se esclarezca esta situación y se garantice la consulta previa, libre e informada a las comunidades involucradas.


 


¡LOS TERRITORIOS INDÍGENAS NO SON TIERRAS VACANTES, NI TIERRAS DISPONIBLES PARA QUE EL ESTADO CAMBIE SU DESTINO POR DECISIÓN ADMINISTRATIVA!


 


No vamos a aceptar que se construya una política de conservación ambiental a costa de poner en riesgo los derechos territoriales conquistados por nuestros pueblos.

author: Nahuel Lag
title: Aparicio exonerada en el INTA: “Vamos a ir a la justicia para que revise lo absurdo e irregular de todo el procedimiento”
content:
Por Nahuel Lag 


El Consejo Directivo del INTA, presidido por Nicolás Bronzovich —miembro de la Asociación Argentina de Productores en Siembra Directa (Aapresid) y de la Sociedad Rural de Balcarce—, exoneró a la investigadora Virginia Aparicio, la mayor especialista de la institución en estudios sobre el impacto de los agrotóxicos. Lo hizo a través de la Resolución 366, en la que le adjudica cuatro faltas administrativas graves a Ley de Empleo Público durante la coordinación del

proyecto Sprint

 —con el que se documentó la presencia de plaguicidas en muestras ambientales, vegetales, animales y humanas—. La resolución deja a Aparicio fuera de su cargo en el INTA-Balcarce, a pesar de reconocer que la investigadora realizó sus tareas, no obtuvo beneficios económicos ni contaba con antecedentes disciplinarios. 


“Virginia está fuerte”, asegura su abogado Mario Bolla en diálogo con Tierra Viva, y explica que se agotará la vía administrativa y luego se irá por vía judicial para revertir los cargos contra la investigadora que “se caen por su propio peso”. “Si se reconocían los resultados del proyecto Sprint no había que prohibir necesariamente el uso del glifosato, lo que se pretendía estudiar era ver cómo incide en contacto con otras sustancias como la Atrazina, que en Argentina se continúa utilizando pero está prohibida en Europa, Uruguay y Brasil”, señala Bolla sobre los intereses detrás de la persecución y ejemplifica: “Bayer compró a Monsanto por 66 mil millones de dólares, como para dimensionar la plata que hay detrás de todo esto”.  "Los pequeños agricultores podrían ir hacia un cambio de modelo agropecuario, pero detrás de esto están los intereses de los pooles de siembra que quieran más rendimiento y más uso de agroquímicos", concluye.  


En las próximas semanas, mientras se canaliza un recurso administrativo de reconsideración,  Aparicio continuará yendo a ocupar su oficina en el INTA-Balcarce, donde, como

contó Tierra Viva, es sometida a un proceso de aislamiento por parte de las autoridades

 desde inicios de 2025, cuando comenzó el proceso administrativo de exoneración. La resolución 366 será recurrida ante el propio Consejo Directivo del INTA, que deberá ratificar su decisión y elevarla para la firma del secretario de Agricultura, Sergio Iraeta. 


Iraeta se define como “empresario” del agro y tiene una silla en el consejo que ya votó la exoneración, representada por María Inés Amuchástegui. También tienen su lugar allí las organizaciones de la Mesa de Enlace y las facultades de Agronomía y Veterinaria. 


Si Iraeta ratifica la exoneración a pesar de los repudios sindicales, académicos y populares, el paso siguiente para la investigadora y su defensor será ir vía judicial con un pedido. “Vamos a ir a la justicia federal para que un juez revise lo absurdo e irregular de todo el procedimiento, lo arbitrario de los argumentos, y solicitaremos la nulidad de lo actuado por vía administrativa y una cautelar para que la restituyan en su cargo”, señala Bolla. 


La exoneración —la más grave de todas las sanciones administrativas—, dejaría a Aparicio no solo fuera de su cargo en el INTA sino también de su carrera como investigadora del Conicet y de cargos en universidades públicas nacionales. Solo podría ejercer cargos privados o provinciales. 


La resolución del INTA contra Aparicio 


La

resolución 366 del Consejo Directivo del INTA

 tiene 29 páginas en las que realiza un largo recorrido desde el inicio del proceso administrativo iniciado contra Aparicio en 2023, durante el gobierno de Alberto Fernández. En aquel momento, el entonces presidente del INTA Mario Garmendia y la vicepresidenta Nacira Múñoz decidieron la salida de la Argentina del proyecto Sprint. El financiamiento del Programa de Investigación e Innovación Horizonte 2020 de la Unión Europea, la coordinación de la Universidad de Wageningen y el convenio para desarrollar una evaluación integrada de los riesgos de los productos fitosanitarios para los ecosistemas, las plantas, los animales y las personas habían sido aprobados por el INTA en 2020. 


Sin embargo, tres años después, el argumento oficial para abandonar el proyecto fue que el INTA no tenía dentro de sus competencias realizar estudios sobre humanos. El argumento fue rechazado por la coordinación del proyecto Sprint, debido a la firma del convenio que contempló todos aquellos parámetros. author: Joseph Lee
title: For Indigenous peoples in Brazil, the election results offer a reprieve — not a resolution
content:
Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s reelection as president of Brazil gave Indigenous communities a measure of relief after a campaign in which his opponent, Flávio Bolsonaro, promised to halt recognition of new Indigenous territories and push for more mining and development.


“For Indigenous Peoples, the reelection of Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva is more than a victory, and it is bigger than Brazil,” said Edson Krenak, who is Indigenous Krenak. “It is not about victory; it is about the possibility to dream and to fight without fear of death.”


But Sunday’s runoff election strengthened Bolsonaro’s movement in Congress, where his Liberal Party won the largest number of seats in both houses and the broader right gained a Senate majority. Leaders warn that this could open their territories to mining, weaken environmental protections, and roll back land rights, making it much harder for Lula to advance his Indigenous and environmental agendas.


Climate Observatory, a nonprofit coalition of 172 organizations, says

70 percent of the incoming lawmakers

 oppose the climate and environmental agenda, according to The Associated Press.


The stakes were especially high for Indigenous peoples because Bolsonaro campaigned on policies aligned with those of his father Jair Bolsonaro, whose presidency from 2019 to 2023 saw an increase in mining, land grabs,

deforestation

, and

attacks on their rights

. Amazon deforestation reached a record in 2022, and Indigenous leaders say their communities endured unchecked violence from illegal mining operations during the elder Bolsonaro’s time in office.


His son finished more than 2 million votes ahead of Lula in the first election earlier this month, but neither candidate secured the 50 percent required to win outright. That result sparked fear in Indigenous communities and environmental advocates, who warned that

the future of the Amazon was at stake

. Lula came back to win Sunday’s runoff by roughly 4.4 million votes, securing a fourth, nonconsecutive term as president.


In an interview between the two rounds of voting, Toya Manchineri, the general coordinator of the Coordination of Indigenous Organizations of the Brazilian Amazon, or COIAB, said Indigenous peoples across the rainforest were deeply concerned about the possibility of a Bolsonaro win. Much of the last three years of Lula’s administration were spent undoing the damage the Bolsonaro administration caused, Manchineri said.


Manchineri said Lula’s term has largely been a period of rebuilding as Indigenous peoples gained greater roles in decision making. “We were only beginning to see the resources returning,” he said.


In 2023, the administration established the Ministry of Indigenous Peoples and appointed Sônia Guajajara to lead it. Lula also revitalized the federal Indigenous affairs agency FUNAI after Bolsonaro had used it to support agribusiness, despite Indigenous resistance. The government also announced just before the election that Amazon

deforestation had fallen to its lowest level

 since recordkeeping began in 1988, according to the AP.


Still, Indigenous leaders say the progress made under Lula has not resolved deeper conflicts over land, development, and decision-making.


“Lula’s victory prevents a president who promised to halt Indigenous land demarcation from taking office, but our territories are far from safe,” Alessandra Korap Munduruku, coordinator of the Munduruku Pariri Indigenous Association,

said in a statement

. “We have demanded that Lula’s government respect our decisions and listen to Indigenous Peoples before advancing projects that affect our rivers and forests. Congress has become more dangerous for us, and we must remain organized. Our struggle does not end with an election’s outcome.” 


For Indigenous organizations, Lula’s victory is cause for hope, but they must now work with a Congress dominated by lawmakers who have already voted in favor of easing environmental protections and against Indigenous land claims. Given that dynamic, Krenak expressed concern about the difficulty Lula may face advancing his agenda. “The costs of negotiating with the Congress and senate will be very high, if ever successful,” he said.


The election also came amid years of Indigenous voters struggling to access the polls. Earlier this month, a court denied a request for transportation assistance filed by Indigenous peoples in the Javari Valley in northern Brazil. Other efforts were more successful: Court …

author: Petala Ironcloud
title: Data Center Near Yellowstone River Would Cause “Irreparable Harm,” Activist Says
content:
The Northern Cheyenne Tribal Council voted to ban data centers, but the Apsáalooke have yet to take a position.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

The Northern Cheyenne Tribal Council voted unanimously this October to ban data centers on tribal land in Montana. The ban follows a decision in August by the Fort Peck Tribes to bar officials from projects involving data center developers.

But Montana’s Tribes are now split. Next door to the Northern Cheyenne, the Apsáalooke, or Crow Tribe, has not taken an official position and remains open to hearing proposals from companies, according to Shane Doyle, an Apsáalooke tribal member and The Nature Conservancy’s Indigenous right relations director. Doyle grew up on the Crow Reservation and has consistently advocated for reciprocity with the land, rendering him a voice in the dissent, whether he intends to be or not.

The stakes are highest in Crow country. In the small city of Hardin, at the Crow Indian Reservation’s northern edge, a former cryptocurrency mine is being actively converted into an AI data center. About 14 miles northwest of the reservation, Texas-based Quantica Infrastructure plans to build its Big Sky campus on nearly eight square miles of ranchland near the town of Broadview, north of Billings, Montana’s most populous city. As it’s currently planned, the data center would rank among the largest data centers in the world. The Yellowstone River Valley is “the heart of the Crow Nation,” Doyle said.

Krystal Two Bulls, who is Oglala Lakota and Northern Cheyenne, has been tracking these data centers closely. As the executive director of Honor the Earth, a nonprofit tracking data centers on or near reservation lands, she takes an extensive view of history and geography when it comes to tribal land and AI developments.

“Broadview is still a traditional territory of the Northern Cheyenne and also the Crow,” she told Truthout. “It may not technically be on the reservation, but it definitely is still going to have an impact on the land and the people around it.”

The divide over data centers comes as developers eye Montana for its land, water, and power, and as Tribes test how far their sovereignty can actually reach. Bans like the Northern Cheyenne’s are enforceable on tribal land, said Matthew Fletcher, a University of Michigan Law professor and member of the Grand Traverse Band of Ottawa and Chippewa Indians. But tribal bans on off-reservation data centers that affect reservation waters are “unlikely to be enforceable,” Fletcher said, unless a tribe can show a very significant threat to its waters, enterprises, or citizens’ health.

Quantica has asked Northwestern Energy for more than 7,000 megawatts. The utility currently serves about 750 average megawatts, said Anne Hedges, executive director of the Montana Environmental Information Center. “We’ve never imagined something this massive,” she told Truthout. The company’s plan includes about 1,700 megawatts of gas generation, which alone would be more than the gas generated by all Montana’s existing gas plants combined.

The gas would affect more than just the rural Broadview community. A retired Billings pulmonologist modeled the air-quality impact of 1,700 megawatts using EPA tools, Hedges said, and found fine-particulate pollution spreading to communities east of the site, including the Crow, Northern Cheyenne, and Fort Peck reservations. “It’d be a disaster,” she said.

The Northern Cheyenne resolution, which passed by a vote of 8-0, covers all land on the reservation, says Melissa Lonebear, a Northern Cheyenne citizen and tribal council member. It quashes any extant or future data center discussions on their territory. (None are currently active.) “We have fought historically to preserve our land,” says Lonebear. “We have fought against coal development, coal bed methane, all these things.”

The Northern Cheyenne own nearly all of the land within their reservation, which makes the Tribe a target for developers looking for large, contiguous sites, Lonebear said. She added that the governor had remarked in a closed meeting with tribal leaders that big corporations were looking for land. “I almost felt like we would be targeted,” she said.

Fort Peck’s ban bars the tribal government, individuals, and entities from discussing proposals to build data centers on the tribe’s reservation. The tribe passed the ban after three companies …

author: daniel
title: Ableistisches journalistisches Versagen
content: Dieser wurde aber weitgehend totgeschwiegen. Es gab kaum Presseberichte. Selbst über die Besetzung eines Bundesministeriums berichtete einzig die Frankfurter Rundschau. Journalist*innen schreiben lieber über Einzelschicksale. Mitleid-erweckende Berichte generieren online Klicks und gefallen Leser*innen. Die Berichte bleiben oberflächlich und die systemischen und politischen Hintergründe werden nicht beleuchtet. Betroffene als Objekte einer bequemen Berichtserstattung. Sobald Betroffene als Akteur*innen auftreten und das System, das sie behindert, anprangern, werden sie unsichtbar gemacht. Die Redaktionen stehen offenbar zu dieser ableistischen Linie. Der Lüneburger Behindertenbeirat kritisierte die Nicht-Berichtserstattung der Landeszeitung (LZ) über eine Kundgebung am europäischen Protesttag für die Gleichstellung von Menschen mit Behinderung. Die Redaktion antwortete am 22. Mai 2026 wie folgt: „Anm. d. Red.: Am Protesttag selbst hat die LZ tatsächlich nicht berichtet. Wir stellen hingegen regelmäßig Schicksale von Menschen mit Einschränkungen in den Mittelpunkt von Geschichten – unabhängig von Protest- oder Gedenktagen. So haben wir beispielsweise am 9. Mai von der 16-jährigen Lotti berichtet, die trotz Unterstützungsbedarf ihren Traumberuf lernen will.“ Selbst die verwendete Sprache ist hier ableistisch. Das Wort „Behinderung“ wird gemieden, obwohl dies kein Schimpfwort ist, sondern eine neutrale Eigenschaft. Das ist ein journalistisches Versagen. Die Graswurzelrevolution wird dagegen über die Proteste und ihre Hintergründe ausführlich in der GWR 514 berichten. Seid auf den Schwerpunkt der Dezemberausgabe gespannt!

author: Chandra Bozelko
title: I’m Done With Mental Health Providers
content:
B

ack in the early 2000s, my parents had me involuntarily hospitalized several times. I got the whole psychiatric smorgasbord: strapped to a gurney when I was perfectly able to walk, injected with medications against my will,

spoken slowly and loudly to

 like I was incapacitated. I got the works, except for one hallmark experience of forcible treatment: I was never restrained because I didn’t do anything to endanger anyone. When people ask me why I didn’t kick or punch the nurse administering the shots, I don’t have a good answer. I’m just not good at violence.


The psychiatrists are, though. They never physically struck me — with all the damage they inflicted, they didn’t need to — but I saw one esteemed Yale shrink throw a red-haired woman onto a couch.


Because I criticized the system and I wouldn’t agree to debilitating regimens of medications, I was labeled as having no insight into my own illness. That’s worse than any diagnosis they can muster. To them, I was so ill that even the most severe psychiatric interventions would never help me. One famed Columbia doctor told my parents to abandon me, like leave me stranded there in New York, because I was terminally mentally ill.


He was just one example of psychiatry’s total divorce from the healing arts. One NYU psychiatrist left a message on my parents’ voicemail calling them “pieces of excrement” because they supposedly hadn’t paid his bill, only to call three minutes later to say in a pleasant lilt: “Never mind, I found the check.” Or the Fifth Avenue psychiatrist who wore women’s eyeglass frames (but not in that accidental and ironic way George Costanza did on Seinfeld) and told me I should become a firefighter because I had muscular thighs.


Cross-legged, I sat in front of Barnes and Noble’s psychology rack and picked out books by prominent critics of modern psychiatry whose titles told my story: Peter Breggin’s

Your Drug May Be Your Problem

, and

Antipsychiatry: Quackery Squared, The Manufacture of Madness

, and

Psychiatric Slavery

 by Thomas Szasz.


The books confirmed what I had surmised. We’ve buried trauma with diagnostic codes. We’ve medicalized feeling too much or not enough. We’ve pathologized normal responses to abnormal situations. I refused to see any practitioner who worked within these constructs because they’re contrived, and designed to accomplish several goals that don’t include my health.


I refused, that is, until a jury convicted me of several crimes after a trial that has become a minor legend in the history of criminal justice in Connecticut, and I couldn’t stop crying. I went to a psychiatrist who wore a “Four More for Gore in 2004” political button on his jacket. It was 2007.


He wrote a prescription for Wellbutrin, a pill I had never been prescribed so its novelty intrigued me and goaded me into swallowing it. It didn’t make me less depressed; it gave me tiny seizures. But I did stop crying, and it put my ulcerative colitis into remission, an unexpected bonus.


I continued to take it throughout over six years in prison, meeting every six weeks with a psychiatrist who struggled with English, so conversation was a challenge and abuse either constant or impossible — the language barrier never let me know. When I left, a condition of the four years of probation awaiting me was that I had to get “mental health treatment as required.”


I dutifully surrendered myself to the Midwestern Connecticut Council on Alcoholism. I didn’t have a substance abuse disorder; MCCA treats low-income people, and I had nothing when I came home.


”I’m not doing group therapy or 12-step stuff. So I guess whatever you’re going to have to do to send me back [to prison], get it started now,” I told the intake worker. I was willing to do more time to avoid the psychiatric industrial complex.


Once they realized I was serious, they were floored, but they accommodated me, and found me individual therapists who made me skittish but at least I would only disappoint one person and not an entire room with my contrariness.


First was Cheryl. I really liked her but she was disciplined by the state for going furniture shopping with a client. I couldn’t tell from the licensing order if the furniture was meant for an abode that they would share, which would be a whole different kind of misconduct.


Then it was Rona, who was unproblematic. She winced every time she handed over a urine cup because she knew there was no risk of the sample coming back ‘dirty’ …

author: Sarah Hughes
title: Members Alarmed by End-Run around Democracy at Buffalo Health Care Local
content:
Things had been tense for some time inside the leadership of Communications Workers (CWA) Local 1168, a 4,800-member health care union based near Buffalo, New York. Still, it was a high-functioning local with a busy calendar of events, stewards handling grievances, organizers pursuing leads, and leaders organizing at work.


So it was a surprise to members in June when their parent union, CWA, put the local into trusteeship, at the request of the local’s president and seven of the nineteen executive board members.


Trusteeship meant the union’s bylaws and elected leaders were suspended, and most of its work temporarily ground to a halt. The appointed Director of Organizing and Mobilizing Mary Nowocien and elected Vice President Patrick Weisansal II found themselves locked out of their group chats, email, and union hall, and facing an internal union prosecution.


A staffer of CWA District 1, Erin Spaulding, was assigned as trustee—tasked with maintaining the functioning of the local, setting up and overseeing judicial processes for the charges against officers, and making a plan to return the union to local control.


Nowocien and Weisansal saw the sudden trusteeship as an escalation of a long-running conflict and a deliberate undermining of the upcoming union elections. Weisansal had just announced his intention to run against incumbent President Cori Gambini.


Now the elections are on hold until the trials are over, whenever that is. And lately, the employer has been taking advantage of the turmoil in the union.


While the allegations are serious, members are concerned that the trusteeship was a nuclear option for an internal financial matter and that it has torn apart relationships at the local, weakened opposition to management’s schemes and denied democratic processes to an active, engaged union membership.


ALLEGED TIMECARD ISSUES


The trusteeship filing lists the cause as “serious allegations of financial misconduct” from officers and “dueling charges” between leaders.


Gambini and Executive Vice President Robert Andruszko had accused Nowocien and Weisansal of defrauding the local of thousands of dollars, by getting paid by both the union and their employer for the same hours worked, and by falsifying records. These issues came to light during a timecard audit in the fall of 2025 by their employer, Kaleida Health.


Nowocien and Weisansal acknowledged there were significant errors on old timecards and paychecks, but said it was the product of the employer’s faulty timekeeping and payroll system, and human error. The majority of other officers also had issues, they pointed out, but only some were being singled out for discipline by the local and the employer.


Spaulding, the trustee, interviewed all the suspended officers and allowed the majority to return to their paid positions—with the exception of Nowocien, Weisansal, and three others not facing any charges: the Communications and Political Directors and one of the Area Vice Presidents. Also fired were two longtime staff organizers, on the grounds that there was no work for them to do, according to one, Ann Converso, who had recently helped organize a new unit of substance use disorder counselors and was gearing up for their first contract fight.


Many current leaders on both sides of this schism were part of a reform caucus in Local 1168, the Caucus of Rank-and-File Healthcare Employees (CORHE), which dissolved when they won their positions in 2020.


Since winning, Gambini and a few others have butted heads with Weisansal, Nowocien, and others over how to tackle problems. The latter camp frequently organized their facility—Buffalo General Hospital, the union’s largest unit—to push back against management’s changes and violations. Gambini and leaders aligned with her argued that that wasn’t the right approach—that they had to pick their fights and not overextend the membership, according to Weisansal.


One Buffalo General steward, who asked to not be named, said members were appalled that the trustee had removed elected officers. “If our employer treated one of our members in a similar fashion,” the steward said, “union leadership would rally around them and fight to return them to their position!”


Spaulding wrote in a public FAQ posted on the local’s social media that the temporary administration “is not intended to be punitive or find guilt against any individual in the Local. It is intended to stabilize the Local while issues are …

author: Tam Saavedra
title: WEI and UN Women Co-Launches Guide for Disability-Inclusive
content:
Across Asia and the Pacific, 350 million women and girls with disabilities navigate conflict, crisis, and climate instability. While they are frontline peacebuilders, community leaders, and human rights defenders, they remain systematically excluded from formal peace and security decision-making.

To break down these barriers, Women Enabled International (WEI) and the UN Women Regional Office for Asia and the Pacific have officially launched a landmark publication today: the Guidance Note on Disability-Inclusive National Action Plans on Women, Peace and Security in Asia and the Pacific. Released ahead of the annual UN Security Council high-level debate in New York, this first-of-its-kind guide provides a practical, policy-oriented blueprint for governments, policymakers, and civil society.

Read the full Guidance Note on Disability-Inclusive NAPs on WPS in Asia and the Pacific

Historically, women with disabilities in peace policies have been viewed narrowly as victims or passive recipients of protection. Co-drafted through consultations with 26 women and gender-diverse people with disabilities, in collaboration with Women Enabled International and the UN Women Regional Office for Asia and the Pacific, this guide directly challenges that narrative. It grounds its framework in a human rights model of disability and the core movement principle: “Nothing about us without us”.

As WEI Executive Director Maryangel García-Ramos Guadiana stated during the launch:

“The true value of this Guidance Note is that it exists, not as a siloed document, but as a means to ensure we, as feminist disabled change-makers, are not left out of the agenda, but we are the ones who get to set the agenda.”

UN Women Regional Director for Asia and the Pacific, Christine Arab, added:

“National Action Plans on WPS that include everyone lead to peace that lasts.”

The publication was shaped by participatory research, drawing on focus groups and surveys with 26 grassroots leaders with diverse disabilities across the region. It addresses critical ground-level hurdles—including digital exclusion, inaccessible evacuation infrastructure, and ableism in mainstream spaces—ensuring that the voices of women, girls and gender-diverse people with disabilities form the foundation of the guidance.

The publication urges stakeholders to align National Action Plans (NAPs) with international standards—including the CRPD, CEDAW, and UN Security Council Resolution 2475—across all four WPS pillars:

Participation: Reserve seats for organizations of persons with disabilities (OPDs)—especially women-led OPDs—on NAP steering committees with full accessibility support.

Participation: Reserve seats for organizations of persons with disabilities (OPDs)—especially women-led OPDs—on NAP steering committees with full accessibility support.

Prevention: Recognize women and gender-diverse people with disabilities as active peacebuilders and integrate intersectional early-warning indicators.

Prevention: Recognize women and gender-diverse people with disabilities as active peacebuilders and integrate intersectional early-warning indicators.

Protection: Address unique forms of violence (such as caregiver abuse or institutionalization) and guarantee accessible shelters and evacuation procedures.

Protection: Address unique forms of violence (such as caregiver abuse or institutionalization) and guarantee accessible shelters and evacuation procedures.

Relief & Recovery: Ensure transitional justice mechanisms, reparations, and post-conflict upskilling actively include women with disabilities.

Relief & Recovery: Ensure transitional justice mechanisms, reparations, and post-conflict upskilling actively include women with disabilities.

The guide also features a practical Disability-Inclusive WPS NAP Checklist to help stakeholders evaluate progress at every stage of policy implementation.

This Guidance Note was made possible with the generous support of the Government of the Republic of Korea (through the Ministry of Gender Equality and Family) as part of the project “Promoting Leadership of Future Generation Peacebuilders and Change-makers in Asia and the Pacific”, and of the Australian Government under the Regional Framework Towards Peaceful, Inclusive Societies (2023–2027).

author: Sara Luterman
title: Nursing Home Residents Have a Right to Vote — Despite What Trump CMS Agency Says
content:
The Nursing Home Reform Act of 1987 requires facilities to support their residents in exercising their rights.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

Cindy Napolitan and her daughter Melissa have multiple sclerosis, a degenerative condition in which the immune system attacks the brain, spinal cord and nerves. They have lived together at a nursing home in Mesquite, Texas, for nine years. In previous elections, Cindy and Melissa Napolitan voted by mail, but this year they took an unusual step: They voted in person. They worried their mail-in ballots — and even their in-person votes — may not be counted.

“I’ve never worried like this before. I’ve never worried that I don’t have the proper ID. I’ve never worried that somebody is going to intimidate me. Will I encounter somebody that’s going to threaten me or make me feel less than? So yeah, I’m very worried, and I shouldn’t be,” Cindy Napolitan said. “I shouldn’t have to be worried about stuff like that. This is the 19th Amendment. I’m allowed to vote.”

Nursing home residents are guaranteed the right to vote. Around two-thirds of all nursing home residents in the United States are women, making aging and long-term care gendered issues.

There is no data on how many nursing home residents exercise that right. Cindy, 70, and Melissa Napolitan, 48, at least, feel like they’ve had good experiences with voting at their facility. Cindy Napolitan, in particular, has worked with the activities coordinator to organize rides to the polls for her, her daughter and other interested residents.

“We are scheduled to go on the first day of early voting. So in case there are any issues that we come across, we still have time to rectify the situation and be allowed to vote,” Cindy Napolitan said.

Cindy and Melissa Napolitan are more concerned this year than in previous years about government interference and voter suppression. Their fears are not unfounded: Experts and advocates for the rights of nursing home residents, older adults and people with disabilities are worried too.

In July, the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services rescinded previous guidance affirming that nursing home residents have the right to vote.

“The memo does not alter the underlying law. Nursing homes are governed by the Nursing Home Reform Act of 1987 and its implementing regulations,” said Nina Kohn, a professor at Syracuse University and expert on elder law. “That law still requires facilities to support their residents in exercising their rights as Americans.”

The memo also emphasized voter fraud in nursing homes, specifically around mail-in ballots. For years, President Trump has disparaged mail-in ballots, insisting without evidence that fraudulent votes by mail had a role in his loss during the 2020 presidential election. His comments have led to some states restricting who can use a mail-in ballot and in what contexts.

According to experts, including Kohn, there is no evidence that voter fraud is a serious or widespread problem in nursing homes. Instead, Kohn is concerned about the chilling effect that it may have on residents’ rights.

“The language in the memo itself is intimidating, and it may understandably make staff think that they could face criminal prosecution or be in some other form of legal trouble if they help residents vote,” Kohn said.

Cindy and Melissa Napolitan do everything together — and on Monday, they voted together. They are also roommates at the facility; most people living in nursing homes are assigned roommates who are strangers.

“Unlike other people that have roommates that don’t get along, I’m very lucky and fortunate that I have somebody that loves me and I love her,” Cindy Napolitan said.

This is the second time Cindy and Melissa Napolitan have voted in person since entering a nursing home. The first time was during the 2024 presidential election.

“I’ve been checking my status weekly to make sure that I haven’t been dropped off the voter rolls, making sure my daughter and I don’t have some sort of issue that says that we can’t vote,” Cindy Napolitan said.

People living in nursing homes and other long-term care facilities face specific barriers. Some residents may need assistance filling out their ballots because they lack the movement or dexterity to hold a pen or press buttons on a computer screen. People with dexterity or coordination issues may also be unable to produce the same signature twice …
