title: ‘Citizens’ health’ session at Egypt Forum 2026 boasts spending success with no mention of declining hospital bed numbers
content:
On Tuesday, the second day of Egypt Forum 2026, Health Minister Khaled Abdel Ghaffar described the political leadership’s support for the healthcare sector as unprecedented.


Speaking at the “citizen’s health”

session

 of Egypt Forum 2026, he said the approach dated back to the beginning of President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi’s presidency in 2014, when, he

said,

 Egypt faced a massive “disease burden,” with a lack of data and years of inadequate budget allocations that had failed to meet developmental ambitions for the system, particularly as population growth accelerated.


The minister said the state’s development plan had delivered gains in the sector, citing 16 presidential initiatives that had benefited 95 million citizens at a cost of LE44 billion. 


Abdel Ghaffar stressed that success in healthcare should not be measured by spending levels, but by the results citizens ultimately experience.


Mada Masr looked into some of those results, drawing from government

data

 published by the Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS).


One clear result over the time period is the notable decline in the number of beds in public hospitals between 2013 and 2024, with a drop from around 98,291 to 84,225. 


Over the same period, the number of beds in private hospitals rose from 26,009 to 36,014. 


Still, the combined total of beds in public and private hospitals fell from 124,300 in 2013 to 120,239 in 2024.


While Abdel Ghaffar portrayed inadequate budget allocations as a problem of the past, the state

has consistently fallen short

 of the constitutionally mandated minimum for healthcare spending.

 Article 18 of the Constitution requires the state to allocate at least three percent of gross national product to public healthcare starting in FY 2016/17 and gradually increase spending over time. The state has not met this threshold since the Constitution was adopted in 2014. Since then, healthcare spending has not exceeded 1.7 percent of GNP in most years.


The government allocated 1.51 percent of GNP to healthcare in the current fiscal year’s budget, half the constitutional minimum. 


Meanwhile, the government has

introduced

 a different method for calculating budget allocations that allows it to claim it is meeting the minimum spending threshold.

 


Rather than using its previous classification, which was based on the Health Ministry’s expenditure, the government now uses a “broader and more comprehensive” definition. Under this new definition, healthcare expenditure also encompasses spending by a number of off-budget economic authorities and companies as well as “any other entities providing healthcare services, such as police and military hospitals, Al-Azhar hospitals, the comprehensive health insurance system and its associated programs,” a Finance Ministry source previously told Mada Masr. Without publicly available data on these entities’ healthcare spending, it is impossible to verify whether they bring total annual healthcare spending to the constitutionally mandated minimum.


The same expansion of what constitutes annual “health spending” also allows the government to include the budgetary allocation for these entities’ debt repayments as investment in the sector, according to the same source.


The president

confessed

 three years ago that the state is not meeting the constitutional requirements, saying in a public address that “the required numbers aren’t available, folks.”

 His comment came days after the government’s assertion that it was meeting the required spending levels.


Aside from its commentary on expenditure, the government’s Egypt Forum 2026 also highlighted the Universal Health Insurance System, one of the leading presidential health initiatives.


Egypt’s Healthcare Authority head, Ahmed al-Sobky,

described

 the system as a comprehensive reform of Egypt’s healthcare sector, capping an “enormous leap forward” under Sisi, following earlier historic transformations under King Fouad I and former President Gamal Abdel Nasser.


Shortly before the forum, the government began promoting the second phase of the Universal Health Insurance System, launching a pilot phase in Minya Governorate. 


The first phase launch in the governorates of Port Said, Ismailia, Suez, South Sinai, Luxor and Aswan began in 2018 and was

completed

 in 2025.

title: Ulus: Healthcare must be free and accessible to all
content:
Structural problems in public hospitals and shortcomings in healthcare services are making it increasingly difficult for citizens to access medical care. People struggling to secure appointments through the Central Physician Appointment System (MHRS) sometimes have to wait at least 15 days just to submit an appointment request. Patients who eventually manage to obtain appointments after considerable effort must then try to explain their health problems within limited consultation times due to overcrowding in hospitals.


Difficulties in securing appointments and restrictions on consultation times are further deepening problems concerning the quality and accessibility of healthcare services.


Mehmet Nuri Ulus, Co-Chair of the Diyarbakır (Amed) Branch of the Health and Social Service Workers’ Union (SES), spoke to ANF about the problems facing public hospitals.


‘Healthcare is not being transformed, it is going backwards’


Ulus recalled that the Justice and Development Party (AKP) government has introduced healthcare reform and transformation programmes since 2002. He said that the policies implemented in recent years have caused serious problems in healthcare services and continued: “The AKP government has announced numerous programmes under the names of healthcare reform and healthcare transformation. However, particularly over the past 10 to 15 years, what has been called healthcare transformation has, from our perspective, meant collapse and regression. We have experienced both the COVID-19 pandemic and the earthquake during this period. These major crises showed us just how inadequate the healthcare system was in responding to the problems that arose.


The healthcare system should have been prepared for these crises and should have had the capacity to meet society's healthcare needs. Healthcare is a service that must be provided within the framework of the social welfare state. Everyone must be able to receive healthcare services equally, accessibly and in their mother tongue.


However, in recent years, we have seen healthcare services increasingly turn into a system in which those who have money can access care more easily. The proliferation of private hospitals is one aspect of this. Another is the emergence of an approach in which even public hospitals link faster access to certain tests, radiological examinations, medical reports and surgical procedures to payment. This undermines the principle that healthcare services should be equal for everyone.”


‘Physical queues have been replaced by virtual queues’


Ulus addressed the appointment crisis in the healthcare system, pointing out that the queues once seen outside hospitals now continue through the Central Physician Appointment System. He said appointment systems should make healthcare more accessible, but many citizens are currently unable to secure appointments.


Ulus said: “The AKP government used to say that people had to go to hospitals early in the morning and wait in queues to see a doctor. Today, physical queues have been replaced by virtual queues. Instead of waiting for hours outside hospitals, people now try to book appointments on their phones or online. However, when you access the system, you cannot find an available appointment. The queues have therefore not disappeared; they have simply changed form. Citizens now find themselves waiting in front of digital systems to access healthcare.


People face serious difficulties securing appointments, particularly in departments such as ear, nose and throat, ophthalmology and dermatology. Citizens who cannot obtain appointments are then forced to turn to private hospitals. However, considering the economic crisis, the struggle to make ends meet and the housing problems in Turkey, not everyone has the financial means to seek treatment at private hospitals.


As a result, the inability to access healthcare has become another dimension of economic hardship. Healthcare should be free and accessible, yet citizens are forced to stretch their financial resources to obtain the medical care they need.”


‘The budget is not allocated to preventive healthcare services’


Ulus said that the problems facing the healthcare system are not limited to difficulties in securing appointments. He drew attention to the following issues: “When we look at the Ministry of Health's budget and healthcare policies, we see that preventive healthcare services are consistently pushed into the background. title: Söke Ekmek ve Gül açıklaması: Her çocuğa okullarda bir öğün ücretsiz, sağlıklı yemek istiyoruz
content:
Aydın - Söke'de Belediye Meydanı’nda Söke Ekmek ve Gül "Bir Öğün Ücretsiz Sağlıklı Yemek Güvenli Okul Güvenli Ulaşım İstiyoruz” diyerek basın açıklaması yaptı.

Söke Ekmek ve Gül’ün çağrısıyla yapılan açıklamaya veliler, Söke Kadın Dayanışma Derneği ve Söke Emek ve Demokrasi Güçleri de destek verdi. "Bir öğün ücretsiz sağlıklı yemek güvenli okul güvenli ulaşım istiyoruz” pankartının açıldığı basın açıklamasıni Söke Ekmek ve Gül adına öğrenci velisi Huri Abrinç okudu.

Çocukların okullarda bir öğün ücretsiz, sağlıklı ve dengeli yemek yiyebilmesi için yıllardır ülkenin dört bir yanında ve Söke’de aralıksız mücadele ettiklerini belirten Abrinç; “Söke Ekmek ve Gül olarak imza kampanyaları düzenledik, stantlar açtık, çocukların beslenme hakkını kararlılıkla savunduk. 2022 yılında Ekmek ve Gül tarafından başlatılan, 2023’te Kocaeli Ekmek ve Gül Kadın Dayanışma Derneği’nin çalışmalarıyla büyüyen, Esenyalı Kadın Dayanışma Derneği üyesi bir kadının hukuki mücadelesine kadar uzanan bu talep; bugün Türkiye’nin her köşesindeki kadınların, velilerin, öğretmenlerin ve eğitim emekçilerinin ortak talebidir. Toplanan binlerce imza, yapılan basın açıklamaları ve dayanışma ağları bu ihtiyacın ne kadar hayati, acil ve vazgeçilmez olduğunu defalarca kanıtlamıştır.

Çünkü biliyoruz ki derinleşen ekonomik kriz ortamında çocukların okula aç gittiği, ailelerin beslenme çantalarını doldurmakta zorlandığı, temel gıda ürünlerinin dahi lüks hâline geldiği bir ülkede; sağlıklı beslenme bir lütuf veya yardım değil, en temel insan hakkıdır. Çocuklar açken eğitimde fırsat eşitliğinden ya da nitelikli bir eğitimden söz edilemez” dedi.

Yürütülen bu haklı mücadeleler ve yükselen kamuoyu baskısı sonucunda Millî Eğitim Bakanlığının 5-19 Ekim tarihleri arasında ücretsiz okul yemeğine ilişkin velilerin görüşlerini almak amacıyla bir anket süreci yürüttüğünü hatırlatan Abrinç: “Yıllardır dile getirilen bu yakıcı ihtiyacı anlamak için çocukların açlığının bu kadar derinleşmesini bekleyen Bakanlığa soruyoruz: Velilerin ve kadınların sesi neden bugüne kadar duyulmadı” sorusunu sordu.

Bakanlığın adım atması önemli olsa da, yürütülen anketin kapsamı, erişilebilirliği ve yöntemi ciddi soru işaretleri doğurduğunu vurgulayan Abrinç anketle ilgili eksiklikleri sıraladı:

İnternet üzerinden yürütülen ankete pek çok veli eşit biçimde katılamamıştır. Veliler ankete ulaşmaya çalıştıklarında "yetkiniz yok" uyarılarıyla, sistemde yaşanan teknik sorunlarla karşılaşmış; internet ve telefon imkânı bulunmayan ya da dijital araçları kullanmakta zorlanan aileler süreçten tamamen izole edilmiştir. Ayrıca anket hakkında velilere yeterli bilgilendirme yapılmamıştır.

Edindiğimiz bilgilere göre ilkokul öğrencileri anket kapsamı dışında tutulmuş, süreç yalnızca ortaokul ve lise düzeyine sıkıştırılmıştır. Oysa en temel gelişim çağındaki ilkokul ve okul öncesi çocukların beslenme hakkı nasıl göz ardı edilebilir?

Servis imkânlarının kaldırılması veya kısıtlanmasıyla mağdur edilen taşımalı eğitim kapsamındaki aileler, bu anket hakkında da yeterince bilgilendirilmemiştir. Çocukların ulaşım ve beslenme ihtiyaçları birlikte değerlendirilmelidir.”

“İnternete erişemeyen, yetki engeline takılan ya da anket kapsamına alınmayan çocukların sağlıklı beslenmeye ihtiyacı yok mu? Çocukların en temel hakkı, teknik aksaklıklarla dolu bir anketin sonucuna ya da hangi eğitim kademesinde olduğuna indirgenebilir mi?” sorularını soran Abrinç, “Bir ankete katılamamış olmak, ücretsiz yemek ihtiyacının olmadığı anlamına gelmez! Çocukların açlığı anket sorularıyla giderilemez; beslenme sorumluluğu yalnızca ailelerin ve kadınların omuzlarına yıkılamaz” ifadelerini kullandı

Mıllî Eğitim Bakanlığına ve yetkililere çağrı yapan Abrinç şu talepleri sıraladı

Eşit ve Koşulsuz Hak: Okul öncesinden liseye kadar, kamu okullarındaki tüm öğrencilere ayrım yapılmaksızın her gün bir öğün ücretsiz, sağlıklı ve dengeli yemek derhal sağlanmalıdır.

Anket Sonucu Beklenmemelidir: Ücretsiz okul yemeği bir anketin sonucuna bağlanmadan, bütçe bahanelerinin arkasına sığınmadan kalıcı bir kamu hizmeti olarak uygulamaya konulmalıdır.

Şeffaflık ve Hesap Verilebilirlik: Yapılan anketin kaç veliye ulaştığı, hangi kademeleri kapsadığı ve sonuçların nasıl değerlendirildiği kamuoyuyla açık ve şeffaf bir şekilde paylaşılmalıdır.

Erişilebilir Katılım Yöntemleri: Dijital araçları kullanamayan veya erişim sorunu yaşayan veliler için yüz yüze görüşmeler, basılı formlar ve okullar aracılığıyla katılım kanalları oluşturulmalıdır.

author: Tam Saavedra
title: ¡Las Directrices de la CDPD de la ONU sobre Interseccionalidad están aquí!
content:
Read in English


Las Directrices de la CDPD de la ONU sobre Interseccionalidad acaban de cambiar las reglas del juego para los derechos de las personas con discapacidad: Esto es lo que necesitas saber

 


¡Grandes noticias para las mujeres con discapacidad y para todas las personas defensoras, aliadas y organizaciones feministas y con discapacidad en todo el mundo!

 


Durante su 35º Período de Sesiones en agosto de 2026, el

Comité de las Naciones Unidas sobre los Derechos de las Personas con Discapacidad

 (CDPD de la ONU)

 adoptó oficialmente las

Directrices sobre la Identificación y Abordaje de la Discriminación Interseccional Contra las Niñas, Adolescentes, Mujeres y Mujeres Mayores con Discapacidad

.

 


Este hito representa un paso gigante para los derechos de las personas con discapacidad. Por primera vez, los Estados Partes cuentan con orientación explícita y accionable para respaldar sus obligaciones en la intersección entre género y discapacidad.

 


Lee las Directrices oficiales de la CDPD de la ONU aquí

 


¿Qué son las Directrices de la CDPD sobre Discriminación Interseccional?

 


Las Directrices constituyen un marco internacional autorizado, desarrollado por la CDPD de la ONU, para ayudar a los Estados a prevenir, supervisar y abordar de mejor manera la discriminación interseccional.

 


A lo largo de años de procesos de revisión de países por parte de la CDPD de la ONU, el Comité identificó una brecha persistente y crítica:

los derechos humanos específicos de las mujeres con discapacidad y la discriminación interseccional y compleja que experimentan, rara vez son comprendidas o abordadas por los gobiernos.

 


Al celebrar el 20º aniversario de la CDPD de la ONU

, e

stas Directrices fueron emitidas para cerrar esa brecha, garantizando que la convención se aplique a favor de

todas

las mujeres y niñas con discapacidad, y las personas de género diverso con discapacidad a lo largo de sus vidas.

 


¿Por qué estas Directrices cambian las reglas del juego?

 


Los documentos internacionales rara vez se centran de forma explícita en las experiencias de vida y los derechos de las mujeres con discapacidad. Estas Directrices nombran y explican las barreras sistémicas que las mujeres y personas de género diverso con discapacidad enfrentan a diario en todo el mundo, incluyendo:

 


Salud y Derechos Sexuales y Reproductivos (SDSR):

 Abordar y prevenir la esterilización forzada, la anticoncepción forzada, la falta de atención médica accesible, las restricciones al aborto y la falta de atención perinatal, menstrual y menopáusica.

 


Violencia de Género y Basada en la Discapacidad:

 Exponer la violencia institucional, el abuso digital/en línea y la falta generalizada de servicios de apoyo para las víctimas.

 


Reconocimiento de las labores de cuidado:

 Validar a las mujeres con discapacidad como cuidadoras activas y madres, en lugar de tratarlas únicamente como receptoras de cuidados.

 


Exclusión económica y educativa:

 Destacar las barreras en el mercado laboral y la exclusión de la educación durante la pubertad.

 


Respuesta a crisis y cambio climático:

 Combatir la exclusión agravada durante desastres ambientales, emergencias climáticas y esfuerzos de ayuda humanitaria.

 


Por nombrar sólo algunas.

 


7 avances clave en el enfoque de las Directrices

 


Lo que hace que este documento sea un instrumento transformador único es su enfoque estructural y progresista:

 


Inclusión explícita de la diversidad de género:

 Las Directrices abarcan explícitamente los derechos de las personas transgénero, intersexuales, no binarias y de otras diversidades de género con discapacidad, y solicitan una interpretación inclusiva de la diversidad de género de todas las obligaciones descritas.

 


Reconocimiento de las raíces históricas:

 El Comité aborda explícitamente el legado y los impactos continuos del colonialismo y la esclavización, estableciendo que los Estados que se benefician de estos sistemas históricos tienen la responsabilidad particular de reparar sus efectos actuales.

 


Un catálogo abierto de diversidad:

 El texto reconoce que las mujeres con discapacidad pertenecen a comunidades multimarginalizadas —incluidos grupos indígenas, afrodescendientes/negros, dalit, adivasi, refugiados, solicitantes de asilo, minorías religiosas, pastoriles o personas que viven en asentamientos informales, entre otros— dejando espacio para todas las identidades interseccionales.

“Just as we arm our hands to strengthen our blows, we must also fortify our minds. Our imagination, nourished by memories of resistance that has come before, bolstered by a precise projectuality, sharpened by critical thinking and corrosive insight, proves to be an arsenal of choice. […] Obviously there is no shortage of military and political campaigns against existing powers to inspire those who don’t concern themselves with ethical and practical coherence, dismissed as an excess of purism, but there is also no scarcity of revolts against the long conquest of domination over life. And while the tension towards freedom transcends all “isms,” for anarchists, the two-fold challenge is to both grasp the particularities of our contexts with realism and draw on historical experiences that resonate with our uncompromising ideals.” –History Drowned in Lethe

There was a world in which I was tempted to be charitable to the author of “Good Night Eurocentric Pride“. The article in Tinderbox #9 which it is criticizing certainly had a limitation. On the one hand, it calls us towards a profoundly difficult task: to separate ourselves from the heavy legacy of organized confusion in which revolt has been conflated with its enemies. As “History Drowned in Lethe” astutely analyzes, this confusion was an industry perpetuated by the commissars of the Soviet Union’s departments of propaganda and the ethically and intellectually bankrupt armchair academics who penned various marxist cultural theories that continue to go in and out of fashion. The article suggests, instead and against all this, a project of permanent research, interwoven with all other avenues of struggle, to recover the memory of the rebellions which, wherever and whenever they erupted, left the political charades and armed party cliches behind. On the other hand, the references of “History Drowned in Lethe” itself were thin, and centered — out of a well warranted but perhaps naive enthusiasm — on the intransigent italian anarchist minority in the United States in the early part of the 20th century. There is certainly an incoherence here. Many, many, realities of struggle have contained an incalculable libertarian and informal fringe whether they have taken on the name of anarchism or not, and the article says little to demonstrate in practice how to go about making these inquiries that it argues are completely necessary. In opting for a single example furnished to us in a widely distributed book, Plain Words, the article contravenes the effort which it (rightly) invites all of us to begin making.

But contrary to how the response portrays “History Drowned in Lethe”, at no point does it make the argument that anarchists should not seek to contribute to non-anarchist struggles, whether anti-colonial or otherwise. It’s clear that the text is instead arguing, in light of a widespread tendency to romanticize authoritarian points of reference, that this romanticization doesn’t serve us. To address this obstacle, it proposes making a greater effort …

author: 张皓翔
title: The Dislocation of Vendémiaire—A Commentary on the European Movement Centered on France from September to October 2026
content: From September to October 2026, a movement centered on France provided us with an excellent window for observing the communist cause in the 21st century and also triggered widespread public discussion. Previously, in the form of four separate commentary articles, we published them successively on the libcom platform, unfolding one by one as the movement progressed. These four pieces are not independent theoretical expositions; rather, they develop within the whole theoretical system represented by The Shackles of the Elements, Dance a Dance of Roses on the Land of Rhodes, and The Contemporary Dimensional Ascension of Capital. Now we have found the opportunity to combine them into one volume and add some notes. This is also the first time we have taken theory out of the study and put it to trial on the real field of movement.

title: Эррико Малатеста - Наконец-то! Что такое "диктатура пролетариата"
content:
Автор

: Эррико Малатеста

Название

: Наконец-то! Что такое "диктатура пролетариата"

Дата

: 28 сентября 1920

Источник

: Umanità Nova, год 1-й, №187


НАКОНЕЦ-ТО!

Что такое "диктатура пролетариата"


 Наконец-то появился тот, кто говорит ясно!


 До сих пор, когда мы говорили, что то, что социалисты называют

диктатурой пролетариата

, на самом деле есть не что иное, как диктатура некоторых людей, которые с поддержкой партии становятся над пролетариатом и навязывают себя ему, нас за это называли чуть ли не клеветниками.


 Вопреки всякой вероятности и всем установленным фактам утверждалось, что в России разрешена та квадратура круга, которой было бы правительство, действительно представляющее интересы и волю управляемых.


 Соответственно, Москва стала Меккой пролетариата: оттуда исходил свет, а вместе со светом – и категорические приказы относительно идей, которых должны придерживаться, и линии поведения, которой должны держаться те, кто с разрешения вышестоящих хотел называть себя коммунистами.


 Вследствие этого изумительного открытия, сделанного в России, – правительства, созданного по образу народа и для блага народа (или пролетариата, как угодно называть), – всё, что приходило из России, казалось обладающим чудотворной силой; и достаточно было назвать по-русски

советом

 любое собрание или комитет, чтобы он был возведён в верховный фактор революции.


 Но вот очарование разрушено.


 На этот раз не мы раскрываем секрет: мы, анархисты, злоязычные и непочтительные по убеждению. На этот раз это официальная газета Итальянской социалистической партии, до сих пор наиболее авторитетный орган московского слова.


 Это

Avanti!

 от 20-го числа текущего месяца, которая говорит:


 «....

В России при советском режиме Партия действительно направляет всю политику Государства, и вся общественная деятельность как отдельных лиц, так и коллективов подчинена решениям Партии, так что

 В САМОМ ДЕЛЕ ДИКТАТУРА ПРОЛЕТАРИАТА ЕСТЬ ДИКТАТУРА ПАРТИИ И, СЛЕДОВАТЕЛЬНО, САМОГО ЦЕНТРАЛЬНОГО КОМИТЕТА».


 Итак, теперь мы знаем, чего нам следует ожидать: диктатуры Руководящего органа Социалистической партии, или диктатуры нарождающейся Коммунистической партии, или даже диктатуры Д'Арагона и компании!


 Но руководители Социалистической партии, претендующие ввести Диктатуру, должны понять, что это, по крайней мере в Италии, невозможно: невозможно, потому что есть мы, анархисты и синдикалисты.


 Если бы мы находились в том же соотношении сил с социалистами, в каком, возможно, оказались наши товарищи в России, дело было бы простым: диктаторы избавились бы от нас средствами, дорогими всем диктатурам, – виселицами и тюрьмами, – и шли бы вперёд, пока не были бы свергнуты революцией или реакцией.


 Но мы уже сила, с которой необходимо считаться, и мы быстро развиваемся, чему благоприятствуют обстоятельства и то, что

Avanti!

 называет

необузданным темпераментом трудящихся масс

. И мы твёрдо решили не подчиняться.


 Не то чтобы мы верили, что массы всегда правы и что мы хотим всегда следовать за массами в их изменчивых настроениях. У нас есть программа, идеал, который мы хотим привести к победе, и поэтому мы отличаемся от массы, – мы люди определенного направления. Мы хотим воздействовать на массу, подталкивать её по пути, который считаем лучшим; но поскольку наша цель – освобождение, а не господство, мы хотим приучать массы к свободной инициативе и свободному действию.


 Мы верим, что свобода учит свободе и солидарности, и поэтому питаем отвращение к любому авторитарному устройству – как в обществе в целом, так и в любой отдельной партии или объединении.


 Социалисты хотели бы подготовить народ к свободе посредством власти.


 Но если бы, по предположению, которое мы отвергаем, было верно, что для торжества революции и устройства нового общества необходимо сосредоточить в немногих руках государственную власть, если бы было верно, что кто-то обязательно должен командовать, – тогда, пусть социалисты хорошенько поймут, – командовать хотели бы мы и не подчинились бы, разве что силой, командованию того, кто, по нашему мнению, заблуждается.


 Следствием чего было бы то, что революция, совершённая по авторитарным меркам и с диктаторскими целями, неизбежно привела бы в Италии к войне между одними революционерами и другими.


 Этого не хотели бы мы; этого не должны хотеть социалисты.


 Поэтому, оставив в стороне теории и судя о вещах реалистично, социалистам следовало бы отказаться от всяких диктаторских притязаний и принять либертарную …

¿QUÉ es el patriotismo? ¿Es el amor por el lugar donde uno nació, el lugar de los recuerdos y las esperanzas de la infancia, de los sueños y las aspiraciones? ¿Es el lugar donde, con ingenuidad infantil, contemplábamos las nubes fugaces y nos preguntábamos por qué nosotros tampoco podíamos correr tan rápido? ¿El lugar donde contábamos los miles de millones de estrellas centelleantes, aterrorizados ante la idea de que cada una de ellas fuera «un ojo» que traspasara lo más profundo de nuestras pequeñas almas? ¿Es el lugar donde escuchábamos el canto de los pájaros y anhelábamos tener alas para volar, como ellos, hacia tierras lejanas? ¿O el lugar donde nos sentábamos a los pies de nuestra madre, embelesados por maravillosos relatos de grandes hazañas y conquistas? En resumen, ¿es el amor por ese lugar, donde cada pulgada representa recuerdos queridos y preciosos de una infancia feliz, alegre y juguetona?

Si eso fuera patriotismo, pocos hombres estadounidenses de hoy en día podrían considerarse patriotas, ya que el lugar de juego se ha convertido en fábrica, molino y mina, mientras que los sonidos ensordecedores de la maquinaria han sustituido a la música de los pájaros. Tampoco podemos ya escuchar las historias de grandes hazañas, pues las que cuentan hoy nuestras madres no son más que historias de dolor, lágrimas y aflicción.

¿Qué es, entonces, el patriotismo? «El patriotismo, señor, es el último recurso de los sinvergüenzas», dijo el Dr. Johnson. León Tolstói, el mayor antipatriota de nuestro tiempo, define el patriotismo como el principio que justifica la formación de asesinos en masa; un oficio que requiere mejor equipamiento para el ejercicio del asesinato que para la fabricación de artículos de primera necesidad como zapatos, ropa y viviendas; un oficio que garantiza mejores beneficios y mayor gloria que el del trabajador medio.

Gustave Hervé [1], otro gran antipatriota, califica acertadamente el patriotismo de superstición —una mucho más perjudicial, brutal e inhumana que la religión—. La superstición de la religión tuvo su origen en la incapacidad del hombre para explicar los fenómenos naturales. Es decir, cuando el hombre primitivo oía un trueno o veía un relámpago, no podía dar una explicación a ninguno de ellos y, por lo tanto, concluía que detrás de ellos debía de haber una fuerza mayor que él mismo. Del mismo modo, veía una fuerza sobrenatural en la lluvia y en los diversos cambios que se producen en la naturaleza. El patriotismo, por el contrario, es una superstición creada artificialmente y mantenida a través de una red de mentiras y falsedades; una superstición que despoja al hombre de su autoestima y dignidad, y aumenta su arrogancia y vanidad.

De hecho, la vanidad, la arrogancia y el egoísmo son los elementos esenciales del patriotismo. Permítanme ilustrarlo. El patriotismo parte de la base de que nuestro planeta está dividido en pequeños rincones, cada uno rodeado por una verja de hierro. Quienes han tenido la suerte de nacer en un rincón concreto se consideran mejores, más nobles, más grandiosos y más inteligentes que los seres vivos que habitan en cualquier otro rincón. Por lo tanto, es deber de todo aquel que vive en ese rincón elegido luchar, matar y morir en el intento de imponer su superioridad sobre todos los demás.

Los habitantes …

I den ungsocialistiska pressen hade så tidigt som år 1907 agitation förts för syndikalismen. I majnumret år 1910 av den fackliga tidningen Bageriarbetaren gjorde bagarnas förtroendeman, Anders Sjöstedt, som var redaktör för nämnda tidning, ett försök att hindra syndikalismens spridning bland bagarna, vilka i stort antal gripits av den syndikalistiska agitationen. Då skrev undertecknad ett genmäle mot den mäktiga förbundschefens angrepp under rubriken: **.."Man säger... Genmäle på artikeln i majnumret."*

"Man säger, att bagarna skola vara med då det gäller att upplösa förbunden och bilda Lokala Samorganisationer", inledde vår förtroendeman Anders Sjöstedt, och tillade sedan: "Tack för erbjudandet, men skall man då behandla bagarna på samma sätt som man vill göra nu, tycker vi synd om bagarna." På detta sätt vill jag svara att aggressiva kommer arbetsgivarna alltid att vara oavsett vilken organisationsform arbetarna har, tills dess de får så kraftigt mothugg så de lugnar sina rovdjurskänslor. Och då behövs det sannerligen syndikalistiskt försvarskraft. Därför kan inte en förtroendeman, om än med stor vilja, uträtta något ensamt - utan en vaken, handlingsfull och slagkraftig organisation.

Lusten att krossa arbetarnas organisationer har icke saknats av de privata arbetsgivarna - ej ens från styrelser och föreståndare för kooperativa bagerier i södra Sverge. Närmare angivet Skåne. Där har till och med öppna strider utbrutit.

Alla arbetsgivare vill ha utgifterna så små som möjligt. Men inkomsterna så stora som möjligt. Detta får ju främst arbetarna, producenterna, lida för.

Vidare hade Sjöstedt skrivit: "Lyssna på styrelserna för 'Föreningsbagerierna' och och för en del kooperativa bagerier vilka diskutera om bagarna på ett utmanande sätt, när det gäller deras avtal."

För min del tyckte jag att bagarna icke skulle bry sig om vad dessa konservativa styrelsemedlemmar pladdrar om. Och är det någon underhandling de ej vill bry sig om och önskar de icke vara med om någon överenskommelse som vi vet att de kan gå med på, behöver vi icke kompromissa och springa och berusa dessa herrar i all evighet, och tigga om rätt till mänsklig existens. Vi ha förmåga att slå till! Vi äro de starka! Gör slut på fegheten! Det är vi som är producenter!

Därför behöva att omändra organisationerna till kampduglighet och smidig anpassningsförmåga efter de förhållanden som kan uppstå. Vad de Lokala Samorganisationerna angår så äro de mest praktiska, och kan med heder avlösa de gamla tungrodda byråkratiska fackföreningarna, som äro i majoritet i detta land.

Att inte organisationsfrågan är ett aktuellt spörsmål just nu, bland bagarna, är en lögn av stort mått. Den är aktuell och skall bliva det ännu mer när tiden är mogen. Trots vad Sjöstedt skriver! Och hans ångest som så tydligt märks!

Allt sedan de reformistiska organisationernas början har i regel "förts de korslagda armarnas strid", som de gamla ledana är så förtjusta i - till borgardömets fromma!

Detta har visat sig odugligt. Vi har ju bagerier, som är bojkottade ända sedan den tid som "Svenska Bageri- och Konditoriarbetareförbundet" startades. Och det var inte i går!

Vi har exempel på detta i Göteborg och i Uddevalla, ja lite varstans i detta land.

Det skulle taga allt för stort utrymme i anspråk att räkna upp alla. Och när uppgörelse kommer att träffas vet ingen! Och ingen gör något för att ändring skall ske. Ingen delar ut så mycket som en bojkottslapp för att upplysa allmänheten om förhållandet, att konflikt råder. Därför behövs det pigga organisationer i vilka medlemmarna äro socialistiskt skolade och nyktra. Då kan vi marschera framåt och vinna något, trots det att arbetsgivarna göra allt för att slå ned vår frammarsch. Detta få ingen glömma!

Man skriver så ofta och påstår att folk är så egoistiska, att de ej vill betala avgifterna till föreningarna …

Halloween is nearly here and the ghouls are coming out to haunt us. In Rotorua they are taking the form of Harry and Meghan Windsor. These two visitors and their entourage are about to descend upon us. Who are they? They are pretty masks covering ugly political zombies. In any genuinely progressive and democratic society, these parasites would have no social influence or special place worthy of anybody’s attentions because the institution of hereditary monarchy they represent, wouldn’t exist.

Hereditary monarchy is unfair and elitist. We are expected to defer to someone simply because of their birth. The people in those positions aren’t the most intelligent in society, the hardest working or the most talented in any way. The order of succession in a monarchy specifies a person who will become head of state, regardless of qualifications. You are born into it and that’s the only way you can get there. Hard work or real talent and abilities won’t make you a Prince or Queen. As the teenage philosopher Lorde astutely put it “We will never be royals”.

In some cases it isn’t really clear what they do have going for them. In fact it’s just that their ancestors managed to wrestle power for themselves and made others accept them in that role through control of the military and ideological tools such as religion. Then they spread their influence across the globe, robbing and plundering along the way. Only due to sustained resistance from indigenous people in the colonies (Ireland, India, Aotearoa etc) and ordinary people in the ‘motherland’ have we reached the stage where the monarchy is more of a figurehead than an absolute power. While appearing outwardly strong, this form of rule does not make for a society that is at ease with itself. By maintaining a privileged royal family, society is diminished because it encourages a sense of dependency in people. Instead we should have confidence in ourselves as ordinary working people.

Since it is no longer absolute in its powers, the monarchy has been scrambling to justify its continued existence and there is an entire media industry and various other apologists helping them do this. The result has been a number of arguments that don’t really stack up.

For example, that the monarchy is good for tourism. The visit by Charles Windsor and his wife Camilla to Aotearoa in 2015 cost the tax payer $1.4 million (Stuff NZ 5/5/16). Not a small amount and you have to wonder… why can’t they pay for it themselves, the way the rest of us have to pay for our own holidays? One justification offered for that visit and the upcoming one by Harry Windsor is that they are worthwhile for the tourism spinoffs. Though it’s hard to show whether that has been the case and even if it was, is that really a good enough reason for having them? In the case of Britain itself, research from VisitBritain (the national tourist agency) indicates that people go there to see all sorts of other attractions rather than for example, Windsor Castle, which is way down the list of sites people go …

author: Archipelago Anarchist Archive
title: Pengarsipan Anarkis: Kritik & Kritik-Diri #1
content:
Belum selesai menghadapi permasalahan ekonomi yang bagai melempar api setitik ke padang ilalang itu, muncul permasalahan baru yang kini menghantui pengarsipan anarkis, permasalahan yang lebih halus dan bahkan tidak dipermasalahkan karena tidak tampak bermasalah di permukaan.

Kata-kata yang dicetak dan diterbitkan (atau bahkan yang tidak diterbitkan sekalipun), seperti buku, pamflet, leaflet, zine mendapat tempat yang signifikan di kalangan anarkis. Karena media tersebut terbukti mampu menyimpan berbagai pengalaman dan pemikiran banyak individu, yang bahkan dalam kasus tertentu, jika terdapat intervensi terhadap media cetak tersebut, eksistensinya akan tetap bertahan—untuk tidak menyebut abadi—lebih lama dari umur para individu yang mengalami pengalaman dan yang mencetuskan pemikiran tersebut. Dan individu-individu yang secara lengkap menyimpan kata-kata yang dicetak serta diterbitkan itu pun kemudian akan mendapatkan suatu manfaat, seperti dapat memiliki akses untuk melihat kembali “praktik untuk mencapai emansipasi” (gerakan dan perjuangan) yang terdahulu.

Itulah mengapa, menurut Baker (2023) ketika meneliti budaya tandingan—atau proses perubahan evolusioner—anarkis Spanyol, banyak perpustakaan anarkis dibangun untuk menyediakan akses terhadap koleksi lengkap kata-kata tercetak yang telah lama tidak diterbitkan kembali. Sayangnya, sejarah pertumbuhan budaya tandingan atau proses perubahan evolusioner anarkis ini tidak terjadi secara mulus atau bahkan macet di Indonesia. Karena Indonesia mengalami periode otoritarianisme—dalam artian paling kerasnya—yang berkepanjangan. Para anarkis tahun 1920-an habis dibuang ke Digul pasca pemberontakan 1926; sedangkan para individu berkecenderungan (anarkis-)sindikalis yang muncul pada tahun 1940-an disingkirkan secara paksa oleh rezim Orde Lama Karno dari pabrik-pabrik yang mereka swa-kelola dan disingkirkan secara perlahan dari arena pemikiran/intelektual oleh PKI; dan menjadi sama sekali tidak terlacak eksisensinya pasca genosida 1965 dan naiknya rezim Orde Bau Harto ke tampuk kekuasaan (Bima, 2018).

Walaupun, periode otoritarianisme berkepanjangan tersebut tidak khas dialami oleh para anarkis di Indonesia saja. Periode otoritarianisme keras yang berkepanjangan, yakni rezim Komunis Gheorghe Gheorghiu-Dej (1948-1965/17 tahun) dan Nicolae Ceaușescu, menjadikan para anarkis di Rumania dan di Indonesia memiliki—tanpa menafikan perbedaan dampak dari pasca-komunis di Rumania dan pasca-kolonial serta pasca-otoriter-militer di Indonesia yang menciptakan perbedaan yang kompleks—kesamaan dalam hal sejarah perkembangan budaya anarkis mereka. Karena ketika rezim komunis naik ke tampuk kekuasaan para anarkis disingkirkan mulai dari ditekan pergerakannya sampai dibunuh, dan sebagian yang hidup harus pergi mengasingkan diri ke luar negeri atau tetap di Rumania tetapi memilih untuk mengambil sikap tiarap total (Anarhiva, 2021). Situasi ini akhirnya, menurut Tataran (2026), membuat para anarkis yang bermunculan di Rumania pada masa-masa keruntuhan rezim komunis pada 1989 atau setelahnya, yang mayoritas bergerak di skena anarko-punk, hanya memiliki pengetahuan yang secuil atau bahkan tidak memiliki sama sekali pengetahuan tentang para anarkis yang eksis sebelum mereka, sehingga secara otomatis mereka tidak memiliki pengalaman kolektif yang dapat dijadikan rujukan ketika mereka menjalankan praktik anarkis/anti-otoritarian.

Sejalan dengan Adrian Tataran, Ucok (2026) dalam diskusi buku Unfinished Nation yang diselenggarakan di Perpustakaan Bunga di Tembok pun mengatakan hal yang nyaris sama. Menurutnya, sebelum buku Perang yang Tidak Akan Kita Menangkan karya Bima Satria Putra terbit—jauh setelah reformasi—pada tahun 2018, para anarkis yang bermunculan—dan sama seperti di Rumania, yang banyak pula bergerak di skena anarko-punk—saat masa-masa kejatuhan Harto beserta rezim Orde Baunya dan masa setelahnya tidak memiliki pengetahuan tentang gerakan anarkis terdahulu, sehingga sempat terbersit dalam pemikiran mereka kalau diri mereka adalah anarkis generasi pertama di Indonesia. Alhasil, tanpa pengalaman dan memori kolektif yang diwariskan dari para anarkis terdahulu, para anarkis yang hadir kemudian tersebut harus mulai membangun dari awal; berbanding terbalik dengan otoritarianisme yang walaupun dikatakan runtuh, mereka sudah memiliki birokrasi, struktur, militer, yang telah dibangun selama berdekade dan mapan serta siap diwariskan, sehingga bukan hal yang sulit untuk kembali ke tampuk kekuasaan …

title: Рикардо Флорес Магон - Революция
content:
Автор

: Рикардо Флорес Магон

Название

: Революция

Дата

: 19 ноября 1910

Источник

: Regeneración


 Вот-вот упадёт вполне созревший плод внутреннего мятежа; плод горький для всех, кто возгордился положением, которое приносит почести, богатства и награды тем, кто основывает свои наслаждения на страдании и рабстве человечества; но плод сладкий и отрадный для всех, кто так или иначе ощутил на своём достоинстве копыта тех зверей, которые в одну ночь, длившуюся тридцать четыре года, крали, насиловали, убивали, обманывали, предавали, скрывая свои преступления под покровом закона и уклоняясь от кары под сенью официальной власти.


 Кто боится Революции? Те же самые, кто её вызвал; те, кто своим гнётом или своей эксплуатацией народных масс довёл до того, что отчаяние овладело жертвами их подлостей; те, кто несправедливостью и грабежом возмутил совесть и заставил бледнеть от негодования честных людей земли.


 Революция вот-вот разразится. Мы, столько лет следившие за всеми событиями общественной и политической жизни мексиканского народа, не можем обманываться. Симптомы грозного катаклизма не оставляют места сомнению в том, что нечто вот-вот возникнет и нечто вот-вот рухнет, что нечто воспрянет и нечто вот-вот падёт. Наконец, после тридцати четырёх лет позора, поднимет голову мексиканский народ, и наконец, после этой долгой ночи, обратится в развалины чёрное здание, чья тяжесть нас душила.


 Сейчас уместно снова сказать то, что мы говорили так часто: нужно сделать так, чтобы это движение, вызванное отчаянием, не стало слепым движением того, кто делает усилие, чтобы сбросить с себя вес огромной ноши, – движением, в котором инстинкт почти полностью господствует над разумом. Мы, либертарии, должны позаботиться о том, чтобы это движение приняло направление, которое указывает Наука. Если этого не сделать, поднимающаяся Революция послужит лишь тому, чтобы заменить одного Президента другим Президентом, или, что то же самое, одного хозяина другим хозяином. Мы должны помнить, что нужно, чтобы у народа был хлеб, было жильё, была земля для обработки; мы должны помнить, что никакое Правительство, сколь бы честным оно ни было, не может декретировать отмену нищеты. Именно сам народ, именно голодные, именно обездоленные должны отменить нищету, в первую очередь вступив во владение землёй, которая по естественному праву не может быть прибрана к рукам несколькими, но является собственностью всякого человеческого существа. Невозможно предсказать, до какого предела дойдёт дело восстановления прав в грядущей Революции; но если мы, борцы доброй воли, несём намерение продвинуться по этому пути как можно дальше; если, берясь за винчестер, мы идём решительно не к возвышению очередного хозяина, но к восстановлению прав пролетариата; если мы несём на поле вооружённой борьбы стремление завоевать экономическую свободу, которая есть основа всех свобод, которая есть условие, без которого нет никакой свободы; если мы несём это намерение, мы направим грядущее народное движение по пути, достойному этой эпохи; но если из желания легко победить; если из стремления поскорее закончить борьбу мы уберём из наших устремлений тот радикализм, который делает их несовместимыми с устремлениями чисто буржуазных и консервативных партий, тогда мы совершим дело разбойников и убийц, ибо пролитая кровь послужит лишь тому, чтобы придать больше силы буржуазии, то есть касте, владеющей богатством, которая после победы снова наденет цепь на пролетариат, чьей кровью, чьей жертвой, чьим мученичеством она завоевала власть.


 Итак, необходимо, пролетарии; необходимо, обездоленные, чтобы вы не обманывались. Консервативные и буржуазные партии говорят вам о свободе, о справедливости, о законе, о честном правительстве и говорят вам, что, если народ сменит людей, стоящих у Власти, на других, у вас будет свобода, будет справедливость, будет закон, будет честное правительство. Не давайте себя обмануть. Вам нужно, чтобы вам обеспечили довольство ваших семей и хлеб насущный; довольство семей не сможет дать вам никакое Правительство. Это вы сами должны завоевать эти блага, с самого начала вступив во владение землёй, которая есть первоисточник богатства, а землю не сможет дать вам никакое Правительство, – поймите это хорошо! – потому что закон защищает

право

 тех, кто удерживает богатство; вы должны взять её сами, вопреки закону, вопреки Правительству, вопреки мнимому праву собственности; вы должны взять её во имя естественной справедливости, во имя права, которое имеет всякое …

title: Anonymous - Devil’s Night Against Landlords
content:
Author

: Anonymous

Title

: Devil’s Night Against Landlords

Date

: November 17, 2023

Source

: Retrieved on Oct 29 2026 from https://mtlcounterinfo.org/devils-night-against-landlords/


 Devil’s night is

traditionally

 a time of mischief and subversive activity, striking fear into the forces of order. On this night, the weekend before Halloween, we took the form of mischievous creatures and decided to haunt the Upper Westmount mansion of the real estate boss Stephen Shiller. Stephen is one half of Shiller Lavy, and his son Brandon Shiller runs Hillpark Capital. These firms are responsible for renovicting and pricing out many tenants in the Montreal area in the past decade, putting hundreds of people out on the street.


 The action was simple, any trickster could do it: we inserted a garden hose left outside into the mail slot of the front door and turned on the water, before disappearing into the night.


 We summon others in the fight against Bill 31 to join the incantations of anti-landlord discourse with nocturnal rituals of anti-landlord action.


 While we targeted Stephen Shiller for being an especially horrific landlord, we recognize authority must be washed away wherever it appears.


 — some anarchist ghouls


 La nuit du démon est

traditionnellement

 un moment de malice et d’activité subversive, saisissant de peur l’ordre des choses et leurs protecteur·ices. Cette nuit là, durant la fin de semaine précédant Halloween, nous avons pris la forme de créatures maléfiques et avons décidé de hanter le manoir du haut Westmount appartenant au patron de l’immobilier Stephen Shiller. Stephen représente la moitié de la compagnie Shiller Lavy et son fils Brandon Shiller dirige Hillpark Capital. Ces firmes sont responsables de la rénoviction et de l’augmentation abusive des loyers pour de nombreux·ses locataires à Montréal ces dernières années, mettant à la rue des centaines de personnes.


 L’action était simple, n’importe quel petit fourbe pourrait le faire : nous avons inséré un boyau d’arrosage laissé dehors dans la fente à courrier de la porte avant puis allumé l’eau, avant de disparaître dans la nuit.


 Nous invoquons d’autres dans la lutte contre le projet de loi 31 à joindre les incantations des paroles anti-proprios à des rituels nocturnes d’actions contre elleux.


 Bien que nous ayons visé Stephen Shiller pour être un proprio particulièrement horrifiant, nous reconnaissons que l’autorité doit être lavée à grande eau partout où elle apparaît.


Des goules anarchistes

author: 张皓翔
title: The Dislocation of Vendémiaire (II): The Illusion of National Economics and the Polarization of Political Economy【葡月的错位（二）国民经济学的幻象与政治经济学的极化】【A commentary on the French riots between September and October】
content: This essay, titled The Dislocation of Vendémiaire, explores the theoretical and practical contradictions within contemporary capitalist society, using the socio-political unrest in France as a backdrop. Grounded in Marxist philosophy and dialectics, the author critically examines the illusion of national economics and the polarization of political economy. By distinguishing between "national economics" (which obscures exploitation through material comfort) and "political economy" (which reveals the deep alienation of social relations), the text argues that modern digital capitalism has stripped workers of their "wealth of real relations" (现实关系的财富). The essay articulates a fundamental shift from the "first struggle" (economic demands for wages and welfare) to the "second struggle" (reclaiming the autonomy of labor production and resisting the reduction of human beings to mere production factors). Ultimately, it posits that the recent French protests represent a historical "dislocation"—an attempt at the second struggle without the necessary political foundation of the first.

Мак-Кинли, глава североамериканской олигархии, орудие и защитник крупных капиталистов, предатель кубинцев и филиппинцев, человек, санкционировавший расправу над бастующими в Хэзлтоне, пытки шахтёров Айдахо и тысячу гнусностей, ежедневно совершаемых против рабочих в «образцовой республике», тот, кто воплощал милитаристскую, завоевательную, империалистическую политику, в которую ринулась американская буржуазия, пал жертвой револьвера анархиста.

О чём вы хотите, чтобы мы скорбели, если не о судьбе, уготованной великодушному человеку, который – уместно или неуместно, с хорошей или плохой тактикой – принёс себя в жертву делу равенства и свободы?

Повторим это и в данном случае, как и во всех аналогичных: поскольку мы находимся в обществе волков, где насилие окружает нас и разит со всех сторон, мы, продолжая спокойно бороться за то, чтобы прекратилась эта ужасная необходимость отвечать на насилие насилием, – хотя и желая, чтобы скорее наступил день, когда антагонизмы интересов и страстей между людьми можно будет разрешать человеческими и цивилизованными средствами, – бережём свои слёзы и свои цветы для других жертв, а не для этих людей, которые, становясь во главе эксплуататорских и угнетательских классов, берут на себя ответственность и идут на риск, связанный с их положением.

И всё же нашлись анархисты, которые сочли полезным и прекрасным оскорблять угнетённого, который восстаёт, не имея ни слова осуждения для угнетателя, понёсшего кару за преступления, которые он совершил или позволил совершить!

Это извращение, это нездоровое желание получить одобрение противников, или же неосмотрительная ловкость, которая хотела бы завоевать свободу пропаганды своих идей, добровольно отказываясь от права выражать истинное и глубокое чувство души, – более того, искажая это чувство, притворяясь не тем, что есть?

Я делаю это с сожалением, но не могу не выразить боль и возмущение, которые вызвали во мне и во всех товарищах, каких мне довелось видеть в эти дни, необдуманные слова, посвящённые Agitazione покушению в Буффало.

Чолгош – несознательный человек! Но знают ли они его? Его поступок – обычное преступление, не имеющее ни одного из признаков, необходимых для того, чтобы подобный акт мог считаться политическим!

Полагаю, что ни один государственный обвинитель – королевский или республиканский – не осмелился бы утверждать нечто подобное. В самом деле, есть ли хоть какой-нибудь повод судить о Чолгоше как о человеке, движимом личными интересами или личной злобой? Разве не ясно, что он действовал по мотивам общественного порядка и намеревался – с основанием или без основания, но, несомненно, искренне и самоотверженно – принести себя в жертву ради дела? И разве не эти элементы придают факту наиболее яркий характер политико-социального покушения?

Впрочем, неправильно говорить о преступлении в подобных случаях. Кодекс это делает, но кодекс создан против нас, против угнетённых, и не может служить критерием для наших суждений.

Эти факты – акты войны; и если война есть преступление, то она преступление для тех, кто в ней стоит на стороне несправедливости и угнетения. Преступниками могут быть, являются английские захватчики Трансвааля; ими не являются буры, когда защищают свою свободу, даже если защита была бы безнадёжной.

Поступок Чолгоша (могла бы ответить Agitazione) нисколько не продвинул дело пролетариата и революции: Вместо Мак-Кинли придет Рузвельт, такой же, как и он, и всё останется как прежде, разве что положение анархистов станет немного труднее. И, возможно, Agitazione была бы права; более того, в американской среде, насколько я её знаю, мне это кажется вероятным.

Это значит, что на войне есть ходы удачные и ошибочные, есть бойцы осмотрительные и есть те, кто …

author: Jesse Staniforth
title: ‘We take care of each other’: Voices from Montreal’s Cabot Square
content:
In Montreal’s Cabot Square, where homeless Indigenous people have gathered for decades, news that a member of the city’s police services (SPVM) had been suspended for urinating on homeless Montrealers was greeted largely without shock.


Regular visitors, as well as outreach workers from the various organizations serving unhoused populations in the west of downtown, describe relations between homeless people and police in and around Cabot Square as marked by distrust and fear.


People APTN News spoke with in Cabot Square over the last two weeks reported accumulating tickets, amounting to hundreds of dollars in fines, for fare evasion on the city’s transit system or jaywalking on Ste. Catherine Street. People who drink alcohol in the Square also said they’d received tickets for open containers.

Few make any attempt to pay the tickets. For them, getting another ticket is simply a fact of life in Cabot Square, though one that may give police a reason to eventually arrest them.


Cabot Square


Measuring one block by one block, Cabot Square is the only significant piece of greenspace in the western end of downtown Montreal. Located on Ste. Catherine St. at the corner of Atwater Ave., the Square is directly across from the former Montreal Forum.

 


For decades, the space has attracted homeless Indigenous people, thanks in part to a years-long provincial policy of housing Inuit from Nunavik, flown south for medical care, in the nearby YMCA. 


Though medical patients from Nunavik have been sent to the Ullivik residence in Montreal’s western suburbs since 2016, Cabot Square maintains a community of unhoused people with a strong Indigenous presence.

 


During the golden years of Montreal hockey, crowds used to gather in Cabot Square ahead of the Montreal Canadiens’ many victory parades. The 1955 Rocket Richard Riot kicked off there when enraged French supporters of Canadiens’ great Maurice (Rocket) Richard gathered to protest his suspension by an Anglophone NHL president, which they believed to be ethnically motivated.

 


Northeast view of Cabot Square from the corner of Ste. Catherine and Lambert-Closse. The former Montreal Forum is on the right, just out of frame. Photo: Jesse Staniforth/APTN


Since the Forum closed in 1996, a

city document about revitalizing the neighbourhood

 notes that “The disappearance of this important generator of traffic caused a marked deterioration of rue Sainte Catherine Ouest.” 


In practice, this has meant Cabot Square has largely been the domain of unhoused people.

 


In 2013, the city redeveloped the Square, but by that point the homeless population was so stable that developers expected they would return. Designers maintained benches and low walls that denizens of the Square routinely sleep on, and the city renovated the small building known as the “Round House” that has become a café and office for outreach workers working with the square’s unhoused occupants.

 


A small geography

 


A mediator from the Cabot Square Project, an initiative started in 2014 by the Native Women’s Shelter of Montreal in collaboration with the local borough and the YMCA Homelessness Assistance Program, told APTN the Square tends to separate along linguistic and ethnic lines. In the eastern part of the park, there are more white people and more francophones.

 


In the west of the Square, near the Round House, mostly Indigenous people gather, mixing with Black people, all speaking English. The seating space around the statue of Giovanni Caboto (John Cabot) in the centre of the park is shared by everyone, while the alley due east of the Square is where people go to smoke crack.

 


On rainy days, Cabot Square empties, as regular visitors head to the Resilience day centre a few blocks down the hill on Atwater Ave., as well as nearby libraries and shopping centres. 


They used to go into the Metro, Montreal’s transit system, particularly the entrance to the Atwater Metro station adjacent to the Round House in the west end of the park. But in November 2024, Montreal’s public transit authority the Société de transport de Montréal (STM) sealed access to the station from the Square. 

 


The west side of Cabot Square, featuring the Round House (renovated in 2013) on the right, which has a small café and outreach office. On the left is the sealed entrance to Atwater Metro station, bearing the notice (in French), “Access closed to improve security at your station.” Photo: Jesse Staniforth/APTN News …

author: Lilli Akpaleeapik
title: Professional women hockey players to lead training camp in Iqaluit
content:
A team of professional women hockey players is coming to Iqaluit this weekend to lead a hockey camp for girls.


The Nunavut Ukpiit Hockey Association has brought in three players from the Toronto Sceptres, who compete in the Professional Women’s Hockey League, to take part in strength and conditioning courses led by Sceptres training coach Kate Germain, according to an update on the association’s Facebook page.


Events are scheduled to start Friday at 4:30 p.m. and continue through Sunday. Girls registered with the Iqaluit Amateur Hockey Association are invited to take part.


Regularly scheduled events hosted at Arctic Winter Games Arena, such as public skating and other practices, have been cancelled to allow for the hockey camp programming.


According to the association’s website, the goal of this camp is to empower women’s hockey players across the territory, both in hockey and in life.

author: Cierra Bettens
title: InFocus: What’s at stake for Indigenous Peoples in the U.S. as midterm elections draw near?
content:
On Tuesday, U.S. voters will cast their ballots in the country’s midterm elections. The elections come halfway through a president’s four year term.

A record-breaking number of Indigenous candidates–at least 355–are running in this year’s race.

This week on InFocus, Pawnee/Ponca lawyer Brett Chapman tells us about the candidates he’s following and how Native Americans are feeling the impact of Trump’s second term.

A recent study by the Brookings Institution reported that the Trump administration slashed $469 million in grants and contracts to tribal communities.

“I think a big problem with the administration, the second go around, is that because of the focus by them on DEI [Diversity, Equity and Inclusion], things of that nature, they have really tried to reduce Native American issues to [being] race-based,” Chapman said.

“What defines being Native American in the United States is not being a member of a race. It’s political sovereignty in the history of over 500 tribes having treaties with the government, and they’re having their own governments. And so you’re having a government-to-government relationship.

“You’re really seeing a weakening of that when it should be stronger.”

Covering elections is nothing new for Mark Trahant, a founding editor of Indian Country Today, now called ICT. The Shoshone-Bannock journalist has been in the industry for over 50 years.

However, with the Trump administration’s threats to press freedom, it’s a slightly different terrain.

“One thing I’ve been writing a lot about is how do we plan for life after Trump and start to build institutions again? And I think media is a big part of that,” Trahant said on InFocus.

“One that I would advocate for…is starting to think about government funding of media. You look at, particularly in Indian Country, how much people have to do with so little resources. Whereas, in other countries in the world, they have a steady stream of revenue that allows them to expand, and report, and do things that you would normally do in a media environment that’s healthy.”

Listen to this week’s episode for a closer look at how the U.S. midterm outcomes could impact Indigenous communities.

Cierra is the host and co-producer of the of the weekly APTN News InFocus podcast. She joined APTN in 2024 as a reporter-correspondent in Winnipeg after working in campus and city news. She’s currently completing her Master of Arts in Media Studies at Concordia University in Montréal. Cierra has mixed settler and Red River Métis roots and is a member of the Manitoba Métis Federation.

author: Dominique Gené - Local Journalism Initiative Reporter
title: Kuujjuaq Greenhouse gets $1M in federal funding
content:
The Kuujjuaq Greenhouse has $1 million in federal funding to expand local food production and processing in the community.


Indigenous Services Minister Mandy Gull-Masty and Crown-Indigenous Relations Minister Rebecca Alty toured the greenhouse Friday morning as part of a funding announcement from Canada Economic Development for Quebec Regions. It’s a federal program that gives financial support to small and medium-size businesses and non-profit organizations.


The money will go toward the construction of a new service building connected to the existing greenhouses that were built in 1999 and 2012, said Roxane Archambault, a member of the four-person volunteer committee managing the Kuujjuaq Greenhouse. The project is operated by the municipality.


The new building will include an insulated space to help extend the gardening season, washrooms and improved facilities to provide more comfortable working conditions, Archambault said. The committee also hopes to integrate a seedling container into the new building.


It will also support the greenhouse’s food-processing activities, preservation equipment and workshops on growing fresh food.


The Kuujjuaq Greenhouse’s gardening season has wrapped up for the year, with community members expected to return to their plots when the season reopens in late May or early June. (Photo by Dominique Gené)


“We’re really glad to get this funding. We were not sure what we would do without it,” Archambault said in an interview in French.


The project is expected to be completed by fall 2027, she said.


The Kuujjuaq Greenhouse currently has 46 gardening plots available to community members, Archambault said. Inuit beneficiaries and residents who have lived in Kuujjuaq for at least 10 years automatically qualify for a plot.


After Inuit and longtime residents get their plots, anyone else can apply for a plot, after living at least one year in the community.


The remaining plots are awarded by lottery if necessary. Organizations also automatically qualify.


Alongside individual plots, there are community plots with fresh produce, such as lettuce, spinach and herbs available to residents.


This gardening season has officially ended and is expected to resume in late May or early June next year.


Gull-Masty congratulated the greenhouse committee on the project and said she hoped to return for another visit in the summer.

author: Unknown
title: Iranian security bodies block medical leave for Kurdish political prisoner
content:
Iranian security bodies have blocked medical leave and access to adequate treatment for Fahim Ebadi, a Kurdish political prisoner in Orumiyeh Central Prison who suffers from diabetes, high blood pressure and high blood fat levels, the Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN) has reported.


Iranian forces arrested Ebadi, who is from Orumiyeh and is serving a 45-month sentence, in the city around two years ago.


After several weeks of interrogation at the Ministry of Intelligence’s detention facility, he was transferred to Orumiyeh Central Prison, where he has remained since.


After several months in detention, a branch of the Islamic Revolutionary Court of Orumiyeh sentenced him to 60 months in prison on charges of “membership of opposition groups” in connection with membership of the Kurdistan Workers’ Party (PKK).


His sentence was subsequently reduced to 45 months after he waived his right to appeal and requested a sentence reduction.

author: Unknown
title: Concern for at Least 14 Kurdish prisoners facing death sentences in Iran
content:
30 October has been declared International Day of Political Prisoners. A review of published human rights reports identifies at least 14 Kurdish political prisoners and protesters facing death sentences in Iran.


This list brings together reported cases and includes both initial court rulings and sentences upheld on appeal. Pakhshan Azizi, Hatem Ozdemir, Yousef Ahmadi, Pezhman Touberehrizi, Arman Marefati, Mohammad Faraji, Raouf Sheikh-Maroufi and Mohsen Eslamkhah are eight of these prisoners.


Earlier human rights reports warned that they could face execution. The reports described unfair and secretive proceedings, torture, pressure to obtain forced confessions, and violations of their right to defend themselves.


Hatem Ozdemir is a Kurdish citizen of Turkey imprisoned in Iran. Khosrow Mohammadnia, Masoud Toushmalani, Sirwan Shabani, Borzou Rezaei and Omran Amani are five others on the list. They were sentenced to death in connection with the January 2026 protests. The sentences against the first three were reported on 1 October, and Rezaei’s on 6 October. On 29 October, it was reported that 21-year-old Omran Amani had been formally informed of his death sentence at Great Tehran Penitentiary.


Varisheh Moradi, a Kurdish political activist and member of the East Kurdistan Free Women’s Society, is also among the 14. On 14 October, Branch 15 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court sentenced her to death for a second time. The Supreme Court had overturned her earlier sentence because of an incomplete investigation and problems with the trial process. Her lawyers say the court repeated the death sentence without addressing those problems.


The cases are at different stages of the legal process. The Supreme Court has previously upheld the death sentences against Pakhshan Azizi, Hatem Ozdemir and Yousef Ahmadi. One of Ahmadi’s two death sentences was changed to financial compensation and imprisonment. However, his other death sentence, on a charge of “armed rebellion,” remains in place.


This year’s International Day of Political Prisoners places a strong emphasis on keeping prisoners’ names in public view and supporting their families.


In a joint statement, the 30 October Coalition called for sustained international attention and the immediate, unconditional release of people imprisoned for exercising their basic rights. It also stressed the need to hold those responsible for abuses accountable.

author: Unknown
title: Human rights violations against Kurds continue in Iran
content:
The Iranian regime’s practices of detention, imprisonment and punishment targeting Kurds continue. According to information reported by the Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN), a request for medical leave by Fehîm Ebadî, a Kurdish prisoner with diabetes held in Urmia Central Prison, has been rejected, preventing him from accessing medical treatment.


Ebadî was detained by Iranian regime forces in Urmia two years ago. He was sentenced to five years in prison on the allegation of being a “member of the Kurdistan Workers’ Party (PKK).” His sentence was subsequently reduced to 45 months.


Detained without a warrant


Mohammad Reza, who lives in the Malekshahi region of Ilam Province, was detained by Iranian regime forces and taken to an undisclosed location. According to KHRN, Mohammad Reza was detained at his family home in the early hours of the morning on 29 October, without the authorities presenting an arrest warrant. No information has yet emerged regarding the grounds for his detention.


Kurdish cultural activist arrested


Metîn Feremerzpûr, a Kurdish cultural activist and doctoral student in philosophy at the University of Tabriz, was also detained by regime forces on allegations of “propaganda against the state” and taken to Mahabad Prison. According to KHRN, Feremerzpûr was detained on 8 July at Şêx Şaltut Park in Mahabad. After being released, he was summoned to give another statement and was detained again when he appeared.


Prison sentences handed down to two Kurdish political prisoners


KHRN also reported that prison sentences have been handed down to Kurdish political prisoners Mîlad Nasirîran and Afşîn Ezîzî, who were transferred to Urmia Central Prison. Nasirîran was sentenced to 11 months in prison, while Ezîzî received a three-year prison sentence. Mîlad Nasirîran was reportedly detained by Iranian regime forces in Ilam Province three months ago and transferred to Urmia Central Prison a few days ago.

author: Nehaa Bimal
title: Arviat singer-songwriter finds inspiration on the land
content:
For Coral Harbour-based musician Jocelyn Malla, a $9,000 songwriting prize means more than recognition for her music.


“It really helps a lot day to day, living in a very expensive community, along with my children and grandchildren,” Malla said in an interview Thursday.


Malla

won first place

 in the Government of Nunavut’s 2026 Qilaut Inuktut songwriting contest with her song

Tukisivunga

, earning the $8,000 grand prize. She also placed fifth with

Kamatsiaqta

, winning her an additional $1,000.


She previously

took the grand prize

 in 2022,

 and placed fourth and seventh in 2025 in the same competition. 


Tukisivunga

, meaning “I understand,” was inspired by Malla’s experiences spending time on the land with her family from a young age.


“This song really represents who I am, where my ancestors came from and the creation of everything, which is so spectacular,” said Malla. “Going through this song made me realize how much I must appreciate life itself and my surroundings.”


Malla initially considered skipping this year’s competition but said she changed her mind after learning its theme,

Avatiliriniq

, which is focused on respect and care for the land, animals and environment.


She began writing during her summer break this year, starting with a guitar melody before the lyrics came together. She submitted her songs

July 1 and later travelled to Iqaluit to record both entries at Aakuluk Studio this month.


Malla’s interest in music began when she was about eight or nine years old, she said. Growing up in a Christian household in Arviat, she learned from her father, who was also a musician.


She started with keyboard and piano before joining a Christian band as a teenager.


“The passion for music is in me. I really love it and I love sharing my Inuit culture, especially my language. I speak my mother tongue most of the time, and I love to share that,” Malla said.


Her love of music is also shared with students at the Sakku School in Coral Harbour where Malla teaches music and art.


Her classes are currently learning basic guitar chords on the ukulele.


“I try to promote my language but today, [the students] mostly speak English, but I try to speak Inuktitut and it’s kind of hard, encouraging them to speak their language, ” Malla said.


She released her debut solo album,

My Irnik & My Panik

, in October 2024. A second album has been approved, and she hopes to begin recording next year with producer Chris Coleman, who owns Nuvu Music and Sound, a recording studio in Iqaluit.


Malla said the Qilaut competition has given her an opportunity to reflect on her own experiences as an Inuk woman through songwriting.


“Through music, you learn a lot. You pick up words and memorize them, which is really useful. You get the sense of, ‘Yeah, that’s us Inuit. That’s me as an Inuk,’” she said.

We speak with Forensic Architecture’s Eyal Weizman about his new book, Ungrounding: The Architecture of Genocide, a meticulous investigation into Israel’s genocide in Gaza, the physical destruction of the territory and its impact on the Palestinian people.

Forensic Architecture was founded in 2010 as an interdisciplinary research group focused on investigating state violence and human rights violations. Since 2023, Forensic Architecture has focused on producing evidence for South Africa’s genocide case against Israel at the International Court of Justice.

Weizman says “ungrounding” is “a kind of destruction that we have not seen anywhere else,” with Israeli bulldozers “terraforming” the landscape to erase all traces of Palestinian life. With thousands of bodies still unrecovered from under destroyed buildings, Israel’s flattening, extraction and reshaping of the rubble in Gaza is a continuation of its crimes, says Weizman.

“Israel is actively and against court order, against the order of the ICJ, destroying the evidence of the genocide that it has perpetrated,” he says.

AMY GOODMAN: Israel is continuing to commit genocide in Gaza long past the so-called ceasefire agreement. That’s according to a new report out this week from the U.N. Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory. The report also accuses Israeli forces of committing crimes against humanity in the West Bank, including extermination, torture and rape.

The Israeli Mission in Geneva said the latest report was part of a “misinformation campaign to demonize the State of Israel” and to, quote, “destroy the Jewish state,” unquote.

The United Nations-commissioned experts said Israel was, quote, “continuing to commit genocidal acts with the genocidal intent to destroy, in whole or in part, the Palestinians in Gaza,” unquote. They found Israeli forces continued using heavy munitions, drones, quadcopters, artillery and sniper fire in densely populated areas during the ceasefire. They also found that the so-called Yellow Line, which was presented as a temporary ceasefire demarcation, is increasingly encroaching into Gaza and becoming a de facto border.

Well, the organization Forensic Architecture, which has been mapping Israel’s military conduct in Gaza since October 2023, details exactly how Israel has used the Yellow Line to expand its territorial control of Gaza. Here’s a clip from the project titled “A Cartography of Genocide.”

NARRATOR: When the ceasefire came into effect, most of the area Israel had depopulated remained under its control. This constituted 54% of Gaza, marked by the Yellow Line. The Yellow Line is meant to mark phase one of Israel’s withdrawal from Gaza. Instead, Israel is using the line to expand its control.

Along the Yellow Line, Israel has placed concrete yellow blocks, signaling areas Palestinians cannot approach. We have mapped the position of more than 100 yellow blocks. Most have been placed well beyond the agreed withdrawal line. Over time, Israel is moving these blocks further into the area where Palestinians are concentrated. With every expansion, the military destroys another neighborhood, preventing Palestinian return.

Israel also imposed an additional boundary, which it called the Orange Line. In some places, this line encroaches more than one kilometer beyond the Yellow Line.

At the same time, Israel has entrenched its military presence. Around every 1.8 kilometers along the Yellow Line, it has built a fortified military base. We have documented 34 active bases. Many bases, like this one in Bani Suheila, have been constructed on the ruins of Palestinian homes.

Israel has also demolished and compacted nearby buildings which remained standing. Building by building, Gaza’s landscape is being permanently reconfigured. This picture shows the neighborhood before it was erased.
