title: Grad Students Strike at Harvard, University With $68 Billion Endowment
content:
“None of us here, despite attending the wealthiest university in the entire world, make a living wage.”

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

Harvard graduate student workers walked off the job on Tuesday in their second strike of 2026 — and other Harvard workers are set to follow with additional strikes in the coming weeks, as union activity heats up on campuses in the Boston area.

The Harvard Graduate Students Union-United Auto Workers Local 5118 (HGSU), which represents over 4,000 student workers, began their strike at midnight on Tuesday. The strike comes five months after the union ended a six-week strike in the spring, which ended without a contract.

The union’s demands are “safe work, fair pay, and the right to stay”— meaning stronger grievance processes and the right to third-party arbitration in sexual harassment and discrimination cases; pay equity and wages on par with those for student workers at MIT and Brown University; and protections for non-citizen and disabled workers.

Sarah Johns, a member of HGSU’s bargaining committee, told Truthout that the union called off their first strike this year in May after some progress in contract negotiations with the university. But despite bargaining over the summer, “we were really disappointed in the lack of momentum from Harvard,” she said. As a result, “our membership voted that it was necessary to escalate this fight in order to get a contract.”

In a letter published on Tuesday, HGSU President Denish Jaswal wrote that Harvard had “refused to meaningfully engage” with the union and offered a “regressive contract worse than our last, stripping away millions in previously negotiated benefit funds” and removing protected classes from the contract, while also resorting to “anti-labor tactics.”

“Our benefits have been completely gutted,” Johns told Truthout. “Harvard has cut over $3 million from our benefits funds that we had access to in our last contract. We also no longer have access to health care, dental, vision, and they also cut our parental benefits by 50 percent.”

Harvard grad student workers currently only have access to “emergency funds,” which do not cover costs for people with disabilities and chronic conditions, she said. Though HGSU had brought over a dozen student workers to a negotiating session to testify on the importance of these benefits, Harvard refused to budge on the issue, she added.

A day after HGSU’s last contract expired on June 30, 2025, Harvard “carved out” over 900 student workers from the union, claiming that those covered by stipends could not be considered employees eligible for union protection, weakening the union’s ranks.

In a video taken after the strike’s launch, Jaswal said: “None of us here, despite attending the wealthiest university in the entire world, make a living wage. Right now, I make $26,000, in fact, which qualifies me for SNAP benefits in the state of Massachusetts. Harvard’s offer was to bring me to $29,000 by the year 2029, which still qualifies me for SNAP benefits.”

Harvard has also maintained that they will not bargain on harassment or discrimination policies. The union has asked for third-party grievances and additional protections to be written into their contracts — issues that have been core to the union’s fight since it began organizing in 2018, and which have recently come under the national spotlight with the Cornell rape case.

One in five student workers at Harvard reports experiencing harassment or discrimination while at Harvard, Johns explained. “We have found that many of our students are reluctant to come to Harvard and interact with Title IX processes because they just don’t trust the university and they don’t trust Title IX procedures.”

“We know from notable news stories that Harvard has an interest in not finding itself guilty,” Johns went on, regarding the university’s control over grievance processes. “There are a couple departments that had a number of high profile professors with allegations against them, and Harvard has taken no action against those professors.”

The union is also asking for protections for its non-citizen students, including a policy barring Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents from entering campus without a judicial warrant. While this is Harvard’s current policy, the union is asking for it to be codified into their contract.

author: rimsha syed
title: Houston Activists Are Working to Disrupt the Flow of Weapons to Israel
content:
Organizers and workers around the world are highlighting the invisible complicity of logistics companies in genocide.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

On October 30, port workers in over 100 locations across the world stood in principled resistance to Israel’s ongoing genocide through an international strike meant to constrict the arms trade and physically halt munitions destined to be used in Palestine. From coast to coast, linking arms in the struggle against maritime transport has been a historic strategy to intervene in the material transport of weapons, ammunition, and military equipment, through coordinated direct action by the working class.

Three years into Israel’s livestreamed genocide, actions of international magnitude underscore the immediate and collective need to stop the flow of artillery into Gaza. Following the repeated demands of the Palestinian General Federation of Trade Unions to “urgently halt the arms trade with Israel” and “take action against complicit companies involved in implementing Israel’s brutal and illegal siege,” several grassroots arms embargo campaigns in port cities across the United States — including New York City, Oakland, and Houston — have been mobilizing alongside dockworkers, transportation crews, and unions.

In New York, the “Break the Chain” campaign is fighting to halt explosives and F-35 bomber components from reaching Gaza through the JFK Airport. In Oakland, the People’s Arms Embargo gathered hundreds outside FedEx’s massive Air Freight Center in East Oakland to protest the company’s complicity in shipping arms to Israel. Last year, the Palestinian Youth Movement shared a report stating that in 2025, at least 280 military cargo shipments, including parts for one of the world’s most lethal fighter jets, reached Gaza via Oakland’s airport. Now, the Houston arms embargo campaign is calling on Texans to join their week of action to confront logistics executives complicit in unfathomable violence and destruction at the 2026 Houston International Maritime Conference.

In the sweltering September Houston heat, at a cafe with “ICE not welcome” signs plastered on every door and window, arms embargo organizers hosted a teach-in about the city’s port — a key transportation hub for the global weapons supply chain. Elsewhere in the cafe, others hand-crafted banners with calls that read “A Future Without Genocide, A Port for the People” as a response to the conference’s slogan “Lessons from the Past, Strategies for the Future.”

The fifth annual maritime conference, hosted from November 2-5, presents a unique opportunity to directly confront executives from logistics companies responsible for supplying the Israeli military with weapons. Roshni Ahmed, a member of the outreach working group, said that the arms embargo demands aren’t new: “Many people in the past three years have felt a deep sense of hopelessness and heartbreak watching the genocide unfold.” In May 2024, the Palestinian Youth Movement launched the #MaskOffMaersk campaign, in which Houston has played a critical role through a myriad of ongoing organizing strategies.

“Through coordinated pressure, boycotts, and refusal to handle military cargo, the world can make these genocidal supply chains politically untenable.”

“Arms embargo campaigns, such as this one in Houston, give people a very tangible way to stop the genocide by cutting off the very weapons that are used to kill Palestinians,” said Ahmed. The movement against the blood-soaked military industrial complex in Houston centers on Lockheed Martin’s massive aeronautics production plant in nearby Fort Worth, where the F-35 fighter jet is assembled from components transported on Maersk container ships before being flown directly to the Nevatim Airbase and used to bomb the besieged population in Palestine. “From 2020 to 2025, Houston’s port processed 85 percent of all Israeli shipments of F-35 fighter jet parts,” said Ahmed, noting how logistics companies like Maersk directly facilitate U.S. and Israeli wars.

Logistics companies like Maersk “are integral to the arms pipeline sustaining Israel’s genocidal assault in Gaza and its brutal military occupation of the West Bank,” said Dr. Jake Alimahomed-Wilson, a professor of sociology at California State University. author: daniel
title: Der rechte Durchmarsch kann gestoppt werden
content:
die Graswurzelrevolution setzt seit 1972 auf die emanzipatorischen sozialen Bewegungen. Die letzten Wochen haben gezeigt, dass diese Bewegungen, allen Rückschlägen zum Trotz, weltweit den gesellschaftlichen Wandel hin zu einer besseren Gesellschaft vorantreiben. Wer hätte gedacht, dass die studentische Bewegung in Serbien den seit neun Jahren regierenden Autokratie- und Putin-Fan Aleksandar Vučić hinwegfegen würde? Diese Protestbewegung erreichte bei der Wahl am 25. Oktober mit einer eigenen Liste die absolute Mehrheit: 52 Prozent der abgegebenen Stimmen. Bei der Wahl in Brasilien wurde der rechtsextremistische Kandidat Bolsonaro junior massiv vom Trump-Regime, den Techmilliardären Musk und Zuckerberg und ihren Propagandamaschinen X, Facebook, instagram, Whatsapp und Co. unterstützt. Trotzdem gewann am 25. Oktober der von großen Teilen der emanzipatorischen Bewegungen des Landes unterstützte Sozialist Lula die Wahl im größten Land Lateinamerikas. Eine gute Nachricht für den Amazonas und die Überlebenschancen zukünftiger Generationen. Als Anarchist bin ich grundsätzlich kein Freund von Regierungen. Aber ich weiß, dass es einen Unterschied macht, ob es eine linke Regierung gibt, die die Verfeuerung des Regenwalds eindämmt oder eine faschistische Lügenbaron-Mafia, die die Lebensgrundlagen der Menschheit und alles, wofür wir kämpfen, für einen profitorientierten, menschenfeindlichen Turbokapitalismus zerstört. Auf dem Weg zu einer solidarischen, gewaltfreien und herrschaftslosen Gesellschaft, können wir nicht zulassen, dass soziale Errungenschaften getilgt und Menschenrechte mit Füßen getreten werden. Die Ereignisse in Serbien und Brasilien zeigen, dass der rechte Durchmarsch gestoppt werden kann, wenn die antifaschistischen Menschen sich unterhaken. Alle Despoten werden fallen, wenn wir sie vom Pferd ziehen. Seit Wochen sind in Europa Hunderttausende auf der Straße, um sich gegen die Sozialkahlschlagspolitik zu wehren, mit der die Regierungen ihre massive militärische Aufrüstung finanzieren. An den überwiegend gewaltfreien Massenprotesten in Frankreich (siehe Artikel auf Seite 3) beteiligten sich allein am 24. Oktober über 500.000 Schüler*innen und Student*innen, der Polizeigewalt und Hetze von rechten Politiker*innen und Medien zum Trotz. Wunderbar! Mit der GWR 512 konnten wir ein bisschen zur Mobilisierung für die Konzertkundgebung „UNZWINGBAR – Kein Bock auf Krieg und Wehrpflicht“ in Berlin beitragen. Am 2. Oktober zeigten über 20.000 überwiegend junge Menschen vor dem Brandenburger Tor, dass der Antimilitarismus lebt. Zusammen mit Musiker*innen u.a. von Dritte Wahl und K.I.Z. setzten sie ein Ausrufezeichen gegen Aufrüstung und Militarisierung.

Die GWR ist ein Sprachrohr u.a. des Antimilitarismus. Auch diese Ausgabe hat wieder einen antimilitaristischen Schwerpunkt (S. 1, 8-11, 18). Wie erfolgreich eine soziale Bewegung auch hierzulande sein kann, das hat die Anti-Atomkraft-Bewegung gezeigt. Nach jahrzehntelangem Kampf wurden am 15. April 2023 mit Lingen 2, Isar 2 und Neckarwestheim endlich die letzten von 37 AKWs des Landes stillgelegt. Der Atomausstieg ist aber auch in Deutschland noch nicht verwirklicht. Das zeigen der deutsch-französische Atomdeal mit dem Putin-Konzern Rosatom (siehe GWR 512) und der Betrieb der Urananreicherungsanlage (UAA) in Gronau (S. 1, 19). In dieser GWR geht es auch um Repression gegen soziale Bewegungsaktivist*innen in der Türkei (S. 6), in Griechenland (S. 4), in Ungarn (S. 7) und in den USA (S. 5). Wie sehr eine mediale Hetzkampagne ins Leere laufen kann, zeigt die seit dem Wahlsieg der Linken in Berlin andauernde Schmutzkampagne von CDU/CSU und AfD gegen die Rote Hilfe (S. 7). Die Mitgliederzahl der linken Hilfsorganisation geht seitdem durch die Decke. Da möchte ich Heinrich Mann zitieren, der 1913 mit „Der Untertan“ eines der wichtigsten Bücher des 20. Jahrhunderts geschrieben und 1926 klar gestellt hat: „Die Rote Hilfe ist vor allem ein zivilisatorisches Werk, sie wirkt der uns bedrohenden Barbarei entgegen.“ Wir brauchen einen langen Atem und Utopien, die uns Kraft spenden „für den Kampf ums Paradies“ (Ton Steine Scherben). Dazu empfehle ich Euch die Beiträge unter der Rubrik „Jetzt oder nie – Utopie“ (S. 13 f.), die Texte über die Anarchistinnen Erna Paul (S. 16) und Kati Horna (S. 17). Außerdem die Film- und Buchrezensionen, die ihr im „Feuilleton“ (S. 20 ff.) findet. Anarchie und Glück, Bernd Drücke (GWR-Red.)

author: Sharon Zhang
title: Starlink Reportedly Tried to Upsell Ukraine on New Plan After Throttling Service
content:
Ukraine is highly dependent on Starlink connectivity as the company has a relative monopoly in the industry.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

After Elon Musk ordered his company SpaceX to throttle Ukraine’s satellite internet service amid disagreements over its military operations earlier this month, the company suggested that Ukraine’s government upgrade its plan to avoid service interruptions, new reporting finds.

The upsell was reported in The Atlantic, which found that SpaceX, which operates Starlink, advised that Ukraine switch to a more expensive plan to avoid service interruptions when asked about the outage.

“If anything can yet restrain Musk from abandoning Ukraine, it may be his own financial interests,” The Atlantic reported this week. “Earlier this month, when U.S. military officials asked SpaceX about the outages in Ukraine, the company advised switching to an upgraded contract to restore Ukraine’s access, U.S. officials told us.”

The incident came just four months after SpaceX’s IPO this June. Reports have suggested that Starlink has already made hundreds of millions of dollars providing Ukraine and its military with internet service since the start of Russia’s invasion.

Early in the war, Musk supposedly “donated” thousands of Starlink satellite kits to the country, making much of Ukraine dependent on the service that holds a relative monopoly over satellite network systems and Ukraine’s ability to conduct critical military operations, such as drone piloting.

The New York Times reported in 2023 that the company is charging $2,500 per terminal per month, with over 42,000 Starlink terminals in use across the country. The co-founder of the Ukraine Defense Fund, which has helped secure Starlink access for the Ukrainian military, told The Atlantic that he estimates there are now over 250,000 Starlink terminals in use across the war zone.

Musk’s capping of service was met with outrage earlier this month, sparking panic within both the Ukrainian and U.S. governments as a large swath of the country’s military was effectively out of service. On Saturday, Musk admitted that he was behind the decision and accused the military of violating Skylink’s terms of service, which Ukraine has denied.

“Were Starlink to be turned off, the Ukrainian front line would collapse immediately. This is NOT a threat, it is simply a statement of fact,” Musk said. “That said, I have nothing but UTTER CONTEMPT for the virtue-signaling evil warmongers who push for endless slaughter and offer no realistic solution to the conflict. May you burn in hell.”

Musk’s seeming turn on Ukraine comes as the Trump administration is increasingly embracing Russia and cutting funding to Ukraine.

The incident has shined a spotlight on Musk’s vast ability to control world events and swing the favor of an entire war toward one side if he so chooses — an enormous amount of power left to one man who represents nothing but his own whims and profits.

Despite this, the Pentagon’s inspector general is effectively refusing to investigate Musk’s interruptions to the service, it told Congress this week.

Critics have already raised concerns about the enormous control that Starlink has over space in low orbit, while its services are the only option in many places that otherwise lack connectivity. Starlink has already faced scrutiny for monopolizing internet services in rural areas of the U.S., and then raising prices dramatically after getting communities hooked.

author: CMI Argentina
title: “No vendan el Estatuto”: el gremio de prensa reclamó al Senado que trate en comisión los proyectos para proteger el periodismo
content:
Sindicatos de prensa de todo el país, representantes de las carreras de comunicación y organizaciones de la sociedad civil se movilizaron este jueves 29 al Congreso de la Nación para reclamar que traten los diversos proyectos legislativos para actualizar o prorrogar el Estatuto del Periodista Profesional (Ley 12.908), cuya derogación fue establecida por la regresiva Reforma Laboral del gobierno nacional de ultraderecha a partir del 1 de enero de 2027.


“Senadores, diputados: NO VENDAN EL ESTATUTO DEL PERIODISTA, la libertad de expresión y el derecho a la información”, pidieron dirigentes gremiales, periodistas y trabajadores y trabajadoras de prensa en la bandera que desplegaron en la puerta del Congreso Nacional. La acción de visibilización fue impulsada por el Sindicato de Prensa de Buenos Aires (SiPreBa) y la Federación Argentina de Trabajadores de Prensa (FATPREN).


Presentamos una solicitud formal a su presidenta, @carmenAlvarezR , y al resto de los legisladores para exigir que cumplan su compromiso y traten los proyectos de actualización y prórroga del Estatuto.


No vamos a permitir que el silencio parlamentario y los intereses de las empresas de medios destruyan nuestros derechos ante un contexto de ataques a la prensa y grave precarización laboral.


#SiPreBA2026


— SiPreBA – Sindicato de Prensa de Buenos Aires (@sipreba)

October 30, 2026


En el marco de la protesta, se presentó una solicitud formal dirigida a la senadora Carmen Álvarez Rivero, presidenta de la Comisión de Trabajo y Previsión Social del Senado, y a los legisladores que la integran. El documento exige la inmediata convocatoria a reunión de comisión para evitar que la inacción parlamentaria decante en un vacío legal, que termine exponiendo al periodismo en una situación de vulnerabilidad mayor a las presiones políticas, económicas y judiciales.


La nota convoca a todos los miembros de la comisión a tratar los proyectos, pero puntualmente a los legisladores que se comprometieron a discutir una actualización de la Ley 12.908 en el marco de la prórroga, como los senadores Carolina Losada, Eduardo Vischi, Sonia Rojas Decut, José Carambia, Flavia Gabriela Royón y Carolina Moises, entre otros.


“Desde la sanción de la reforma laboral, la Comisión de Legislación del Trabajo del Senado no se volvió a reunir ni una sola vez. Las y los senadores que muchas veces hablan de la regulación laboral no están haciendo su laburo”, sostuvo Agustín Lecchi, secretario general de SiPreBA.


“En un contexto de gran ataque a la libertad de expresión, donde el Presidente de la Nación dice que nos quiere quemar en la hoguera, los empresarios de medios aprovechan la política laboral de este gobierno para derogar una ley que nos protege y resguarda la libertad de expresión”, agregó Lecchi.


 NI UN DÍA SIN ESTATUTO DEL PERIODISTA


Mariano Recalde @marianorecalde , senador de Unión por la Patria, realizó un pedido de preferencia para que se trate de manera urgente los proyectos para sostener la vigencia y actualización del Estatuto del Periodista Profesional.


Exigimos a la senadora @carmenAlvarezR que sesione la Comisión de Trabajo y Previsión. Denunciamos que desde la Reforma Laboral no se juntó ni una sola vez, bloqueando cualquier tipo de debate democrático.


— SiPreBA – Sindicato de Prensa de Buenos Aires (@sipreba)

October 30, 2026


Durante el acto expresaron su apoyo los senadores Mariano Recalde, Marcelo Lewandowski, Jimena López, Ana Inés Marks y María Teresa González, junto al diputado Esteban Paulon y el legislador porteño Gabriel Solano.


Los senadores no están haciendo su trabajo y tienen que tratar el Estatuto del Periodista.


Nuestro secretario general, @AguLecchi estuvo en @radioconvos899 en el programa de @aleberco donde comentó que desde la sanción de la reforma laboral, la Comisión de Legislación del Trabajo del Senado no se volvió a reunir ni una sola vez y convocó mañana a las 12 frente al Senado para exigir a la comisión laboral que trate el proyecto de actualización del Estatuto del Periodista Profesional y del Personal Administrativo presentado en junio pasado.


Convocamos junto a muchos sindicatos de prensa del país nucleados en la @PrensaFATPREN , la @FIP_AL , @aRGra_ , @Fadeccos , @REDCOMargentina , el @CELS_Argentina , @comuUBA , @PeriodistasdArg

author: Neesha Powell
title: North Carolina Movement Urges Voters to Reject Corporate Tax Breaks
content:
Organizers say the ballot amendments won’t benefit working-class people, but rather corporations and the ultra-wealthy.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

The affordability crisis is hitting people hard across the country, but it’s especially acute in North Carolina. For the sixth year in a row, North Carolina holds the distinction of being the worst state in the nation for workers based on its wage policies, worker protections, and rights to organize, according to Oxfam. Nearly half of renters in the state are struggling to afford their homes, while nearly a third of households are cost-burdened (spending over 30 percent of their income on housing).

North Carolina voters’ eyes may light up when they see two proposed constitutional amendments on their November ballots: one to cap the state personal and corporate income tax rates at 3.5 percent, down from a cap of seven percent, and another to limit how much local governments can levy in property taxes. On their face, they appear as if they might bring much-needed tax relief to North Carolina’s working class.

The amendments are deceptively framed as being beneficial to working people and homeowners, reading as if they would lower individual taxes when there’s no indication that they will, according to Todd Warren, statewide campaign strategist at Down Home North Carolina, a member-led organization that endorsed a “no” vote. Instead, Warren said, the measures would be a giveaway to corporations and wealthy individuals by limiting how much they pay toward the public good — and a “scam” for voters.

Since the passage of the two Republican-sponsored bills that placed the amendments on the ballot this past May, Down Home NC and over 20 other groups have come together as the NC Vote Against coalition to defeat them, as well as to oppose a third amendment that would enshrine voter identification requirements in the state constitution.

Each organization has its own expertise and its own tactics, but a common message: The amendments will not benefit working-class people, but rather corporations and the ultra-wealthy. Each group is playing its part in collecting a total of 100,000 pledges from North Carolinians who commit to voting against the amendments.

Down Home NC joined together with another coalition member, the Carolina Federation, to launch the Fund the Future campaign, deploying nearly 200 paid canvassers.

Jenn Frye, co–director of the Carolina Federation, spent part of this weekend canvassing at the poll at a Durham, North Carolina library, where she convinced an older couple to vote “no” on the amendments. After a member-led endorsement process that included political education on the amendments, a leadership summit and a vote at a statewide membership meeting, the Carolina Federation decided they wanted to deeply engage in the amendment fight. “We see more and more people in North Carolina who agree that corporations and the wealthiest individuals aren’t contributing what they owe when day in and day out, North Carolinians are working really hard,” Frye said. “We pay our taxes, and we contribute what we owe.”

Down Home NC and the Carolina Federation were founded in 2017 and 2018, respectively, in the wake of President Trump first taking office and Republicans winning control of both North Carolina’s state legislature and governorship in 2013 (for the first time since Reconstruction). The groups share a long-term goal of loosening corporate power’s grip on the state legislature and supplanting it with people power.

The Fund the Future campaign campaign is knocking doors, talking to voters at the polls, getting resolutions against the amendments passed by local governments and school boards, and placing signs in small businesses and in yards, among other tactics. So far, the Carolina Federation’s canvassers have knocked on over 600,000 doors across six counties, collecting over 33,000 pledges, while Down Home NC’s canvassers had knocked 500,000 doors across 20 counties and collected about 8,000 pledges.

“Whatever the outcome of this amendment fight, Federation’s members plan to launch a statewide campaign next year with other organizations like Down Home and Siembra to demand that the legislature pass fair tax policies that make corporations and the wealthiest individuals pay what they owe our communities in taxes,” Frye said. “That may be a multi-year fight. It is one our members feel is worth …

author: Marina Amaral
title: É o momento de aprofundar a democracia e agir pelo país que queremos
content:
Quer receber os textos desta coluna em primeira mão no seu e-mail? Assine a Newsletter da Pública, enviada sempre às sextas-feiras, 8h. Para receber as próximas edições,

inscreva-se aqui

.


Não sei se todos vocês sabem, mas a

Pública

tem um podcast sobre a emergência climática que chama “

Bom Dia, Fim do Mundo

”. Somos três em volta da mesa — o escritor Ricardo Terto, a jornalista Isabel Seta e eu — dirigidos por Sofia Amaral, nossa coordenadora de audiovisual, e com uma coluna em áudio de uma economista do NoVe — Novas Vozes Econômicas, um grupo que busca abrir e qualificar o debate sobre o tema na imprensa.


Conversamos durante 30 minutos, todas as semanas, com realismo e bom humor, sobre os fatos relevantes para o futuro do país e do mundo, em momento em que a própria existência da humanidade depende da possibilidade de criar uma nova maneira de viver. Como disse o sociólogo Miguel Lago na Piauí: “o clima tornou-se a condição a partir da qual todas as demais questões devem ser pensadas”.


Por isso a gravação do último episódio foi tão emocionante. Depois de alertas e denúncias durante toda a campanha,

celebramos a democracia, o diálogo, o debate e o engajamento público

 que decolaram na reta final da campanha e afastaram a extrema direita do poder. Comemoramos o resgate de nossa identidade e soberania, ameaçadas por gente que ostenta a bandeira — e o míssil — dos Estados Unidos e de Israel em manifestação de rua.


Não há como engajar os governos e as sociedades para cumprir uma tarefa global, a luta pela emergência climática, sem respeito à autodeterminação dos povos e à soberania das nações, sem espaço para o diálogo e o debate, atravancados pela guerra, pela miséria, por governos autoritários, e atravessados por pensamentos mórbidos de quem considera o fim do mundo inevitável (o que está por trás do negacionismo propositalmente fomentado por aqueles que pensam estar acima do sofrimento global).


Por isso, o mundo comemorou a vitória brasileira contra a extrema direita, forjada por gente que aprendeu a força que detém valores como a vida, a liberdade, a fraternidade, a luta para que todos vivam melhor. Sem ingenuidade, mas com sinceridade, fé no diálogo, e na capacidade de persuasão ancorada em fatos e inspirada por afetos.


Das redes às ruas, as lições do Exército de Lula são agora armas para resistir, junto com o governo democraticamente eleito pelo povo de um país soberano, mas também para ir além, exigindo transparência e urgência em ações e decisões e cobrando a abertura de canais para a participação política. Não há como imaginar possibilidades e agir na direção da mudança, sem entender o significado, a forma e a intensidade que tomou a mobilização eleitoral que levou à vitória da democracia em condições inéditas.


A imagem de Lula com a Constituição de 1988 nas mãos, cercado da multidão com o verde-amarelo da nação e o vermelho da resistência, é para mim um símbolo dessas eleições, e um guia para a construção coletiva desse futuro. Começando pelo presente, com ações eficazes para cumprir o que está determinado na Constituição Cidadã, o que tem sido tarefa sobretudo de organizações e movimentos sociais, indígenas, negros, pessoas trans e mulheres que frequentemente são alvo da violação de direitos fundamentais.


O “povo da luta” pode contar agora também com a mobilização de todos que se aliaram pela democracia, pela soberania e pela defesa das conquistas sociais nas eleições e forçar a implementação dos princípios e garantias determinados pela Constituição, incluindo o direito à informação e à participação política, para construir um futuro mais justo e inovador.


Neste

episódio

 do Bom Dia, Fim do Mundo, em que também falamos dos desafios internos e externos que temos pela frente, lembramos de um artigo da Constituição, pouco utilizado, que traz grandes possibilidades para os que desejam uma nova forma de governar, como disse o presidente Lula no discurso da vitória.


“A soberania popular será exercida pelo sufrágio universal e pelo voto direto e secreto, com valor igual para todos, e, nos termos da lei, mediante: I- plebiscito, II – referendo; III – iniciativa popular”, enuncia o artigo 14. Até hoje tivemos um único plebiscito (em 1993, para decidir sobre sistema e forma de governo) e um referendo (em 2005, para decidir se a comercialização de armas continuaria a ser permitida).


O terceiro instrumento, a iniciativa popular, é ainda menos lembrado, embora crucial para o …

author: Liza Gross
title: Utilities, Developers, and Tech Companies Spend Millions to Pass Proposition 45
content:
The ballot measure would rewrite California’s foundational environmental law to fast-track major projects.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

Political action committees funded by technology companies, the state’s major utilities and other corporate interests have spent nearly twice as much to pass a ballot measure that would greenlight major development projects with minimal environmental or public review as public interest and labor groups have spent opposing it.

Developers and other corporate interests aim to streamline the California Environmental Quality Act, or CEQA, which requires public agencies to identify, disclose and mitigate a development project’s negative impacts on a wide range of environmental resources, including wildlife, air and water quality and tribal cultural resources.

Proposition 45 shifts who determines the scope of environmental review from public agencies and communities to project developers by rewriting the state’s foundational environmental law to fast-track major projects.

Supporters of Prop 45, sponsored by the California Chamber of Commerce, have spent more than $56 million to pass the measure, the most recent state records show. Opponents, led by a coalition of more than 550 labor, health and environmental organizations, have spent close to $30 million to defeat what they say will give polluters a free pass.

“Prop 45 will modernize the approval process for essential projects by establishing clear, enforceable timelines for agency decisions and court challenges,” the chamber said in promotional materials, “while keeping environmental protections intact and preserving worker protections, tribal protections and local control.”

Critics say Prop 45 will gut the state’s primary vehicle for allowing people to learn about plans for polluting developments in their neighborhoods and propose alternatives.

“It undermines basically every stage of that process,” said Woody Little, the spokesperson for No on Prop 45.

Little and his allies say the 41-page ballot measure was written by corporations who have paid to get their special interests on the ballot to create loopholes that favor polluting industries like recently regulated data centers while limiting the input of communities and local tribes.

Critics of CEQA, signed in 1970 by then-Gov. Ronald Reagan, blame the law for hobbling home construction and driving housing and cost of living increases in California, which are among the highest in the nation.

Prop 45 will lower housing and utility costs by reducing “endless” bureaucratic delays and protect taxpayers by reducing waste and cost overruns, Yes on Prop 45 materials argue.

Yet there is no requirement in the measure to reduce housing costs or utility bills. And the nonpartisan Legislative Analyst’s Office estimates that Prop 45 could leave state and local governments paying $100 million or more a year, partly to cover fast-tracked projects’ environmental impacts.

“The housing issue is a smokescreen for all these other polluting projects,” said Little.

California passed laws last year that significantly streamlined CEQA by exempting urban and mixed-use housing construction from its provisions as well as certain infrastructure and clean energy projects.

None of the grassroots groups that promote “yes in my backyard,” or YIMBY, policies to build more housing and public transit in urban and suburban areas support Prop 45, Little said. Most are neutral, he said, while others oppose it.

Expanding housing beyond already developed areas means building new freeways, water connections and other expensive infrastructure that taxpayers ultimately pay for, Little said. And these projects often encroach on the wildland-urban interface, raising wildfire risk just as climate change is making fires more destructive.

At a time when California is already seeing the catastrophic costs of climate-fueled fires, Little said, the state should be requiring more environmental review around developments to assess and mitigate risk, not less.

Prop 45 covers nine types of “essential” projects, among them housing, water systems, clean energy (including carbon capture and storage), transportation, wildfire risk reduction and broadband internet access. All related and “ancillary” infrastructure is also covered.

Whether “ancillary” includes data centers, which typically require broadband infrastructure, has been a major point of contention …

author: Dulce Amor Rodriguez
title: 9 years later, parents still seek answers over son’s killing amid ‘drug war’
content:
Nanette Castillo, mother of a drug war victim, expresses her sentiment during a protest at the University of the Philippines Diliman on February 27, 2026, in conjunction with the last day of Rodrigo Duterte's confirmation of charges hearing before the International Criminal Court. Photo by Dominic Gutoman/Bulatlat

Nine years later, the family still has no definitive answers about who killed their son, why the gunmen targeted him, and whether authorities thoroughly investigated the shooting.

Trigger warning: details of violence and death

Nine years after their son was killed in former president Rodrigo Duterte’s drug war, Nanette and Bong Castillo stepped forward to the Truth Commission’s fifth Public Truth-Telling Session on October 23 to recount what they believe happened to Aldrin Castillo and seek answers on his death.

They believe that the case of their son may have been a case of mistaken-identity, while the police and medical records reviewed by forensic pathologist Raquel Fortun exposed significant gaps in the original documentation of Aldrin’s death.

Aldrin was 32 when gunmen shot him in Tondo, Manila, on October 2, 2017. He was visiting his sister to help repair her air conditioner.

His parents believe the gunmen were looking for another man and killed Aldrin because they mistook him for their intended target.

Nine years later, the family still has no definitive answers about who killed their son, why the gunmen targeted him, and whether authorities thoroughly investigated the shooting.

Nanette came to the Truth Commission determined to tell people who Aldrin was beyond the circumstances of his death.

“I want everyone to know how good Aldrin was as a son,” she said in Filipino.

Aldrin was her firstborn, whom she remembered as affectionate, hardworking, and attentive to the needs of others.

In elementary school, he was recognized for keeping himself neat and clean, and he ranked first in his class in Grade 4.

Nanette recalled that he would ask her to share food with friends who had nothing to eat, even when their own family had little money.

When Aldrin began earning, he gave his mother part of his salary and made sure they ate together before she went home.

Bong also brought his son to catering jobs so he could learn to work and earn money.

Aldrin later learned welding through his partner’s family and dreamed of working abroad to give his parents a better life.

Nanette remembered his promise to take her to Saudi Arabia and build her a house when he found work there.

“Gagawin kitang doña,” (I will make you rich.) Aldrin would tell her.

For Nanette, the promise represented a future her son wanted to build for their family, a future cut short when he was killed.

On October 2, 2017, Aldrin visited his sister in Tondo to help repair her air conditioner.

Nanette hesitated before allowing him to leave because she had heard reports of killings in the area. She thought the checkpoints and the election gun ban in effect at the time might help keep him safe.

She gave him money for transportation and watched him leave.

Bong was away in Quezon City for work when the family learned that Aldrin had been shot.

According to the police incident report presented by Fortun, Aldrin was with friends in Tondo when armed men arrived on motorcycles and shot him before fleeing.

Nanette recalled reaching the scene and finding her son lying motionless on the street, his eyes open.

She called for a doctor and an ambulance, still hoping someone could save him.

She held his hand and pressed her ear against his chest, trying to feel a pulse or hear a heartbeat.

“Umaasa ako. Umaasa ako. Umaasa ako,” she recalled, repeating how she kept hoping that her son might still be alive.

Nanette also recounted how police officers initially prevented her from approaching Aldrin, saying she might disturb the crime scene. She pleaded to stay beside him, promising not to move anything.

The shock of that night has remained with her.

She still remembers the ordinary details of life with Aldrin, including the meals he loved and the way he would come home and ask what they would eat.

Those memories now coexist with the questions that followed his death.

During the session, Nanette recalled hearing that the gunmen had been looking for someone wearing a white sleeveless shirt. It was her nephew who mentioned this detail.

Bong also recounted that a man later approached him and said he was the person the gunmen had been looking …

author: Shan Kenshin Ecaldre
title: SC ruling exposes pork barrel system
content:
Photo by Supreme Court of the Philippines

A significant part of the ruling concerned the Strengthening Assistance for Government Infrastructure and Social Programs (SAGIP).

The Supreme Court’s (SC) declaration that the 2024 and 2025 national budgets were unconstitutional has renewed calls to hold Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and other government officials accountable for the flood control corruption scandal. This also exposes how budget insertions and discretionary funds enabled the questionable use of billions of pesos in public money.

In its October 7 ruling on Lagman v. Congress (G.R. No. 271059), the high court struck down budgetary additions that exceeded the spending ceiling submitted by the President. It also permanently prohibited the release mechanisms for certain Unprogrammed Appropriations (UA) under the 2026 national budget.

For progressive lawmakers, the decision affirms long-standing warnings that the pork barrel system persisted despite earlier Supreme Court (SC) rulings restricting discretionary and lump-sum appropriations.

“The party’s over,” said ACT Teachers Partylist Rep. Antonio Tinio, deputy minority leader, in his October 21 discussion of the ruling.

Tinio said that the decision exposed how Congress and Malacañang used budgetary mechanisms to expand allocations beyond the limits set by the executive’s proposed budget, creating opportunities for patronage and corruption.

The court ruled that the national budget ceiling covers both programmed and unprogrammed appropriations. Congress cannot increase their combined total beyond the amount submitted by the President.

In the 2024 budget, lawmakers added P449.5 billion ($7.02 Billion) to unprogrammed appropriations. In 2025, they added P17.99 billion ($208.83 Million) to the Department of Public Works and Highways’ (DPWH) Special Road Fund. The court declared these additions unconstitutional and, consequently, the respective General Appropriations Acts.

The ruling also found that certain release conditions for unprogrammed appropriations in the 2026 budget violated constitutional requirements. The provisions allowed the executive to determine which projects would receive funding without clear standards for prioritization.

A significant part of the ruling concerned the Strengthening Assistance for Government Infrastructure and Social Programs (SAGIP), which the court declared unconstitutional as a prohibited lump-sum appropriation.

According to Tinio, P200 billion ($3.12 Billion) was released through SAGIP in 2024. Of this amount, P155.9 billion ($2.43 Billion) went to the DPWH during the final quarter of the year, including P85.8 billion ($1.34 Billion) for flood control projects.

The court described SAGIP as a covert repository for lump-sum allocations for DPWH infrastructure projects, including flood control.

The arrangement allowed the executive to determine the projects and amounts to be funded after Congress passed the budget, undermining legislative oversight over public spending.

The court also cited economist Solita Monsod’s observation that discretionary DPWH allocations had become a new form of pork barrel, reportedly accompanied by a six-percent “parking fee.”

The ruling criticized congressional amendments that reduced funding for strategic development projects while increasing allocations for infrastructure and assistance programs that could be used for political patronage.

Among the projects affected by cuts in the 2024 budget were the North-South Commuter Railway which faced a P53.93 billion ($841.87 Million) shortfall, and the Metro Manila Subway which faced a P52.63 billion ($821.57 Million) shortfall.

The court said that Congress created artificial fiscal space by reducing funding for development programs and redirecting allocations to other budget items, including DPWH infrastructure and assistance programs under the Department of Health, Department of Social Welfare and Development, and Department of Labor and Employment.

According to Makabayan, these findings highlight how budget decisions can deprive essential public services of funding while expanding discretionary spending that lacks sufficient transparency.

For the Bagong Alyansang Makabayan (Bayan), the ruling vindicated progressive lawmakers who opposed the 2024 and 2025 national budgets, warning that the flood control scandal demonstrated the consequences of allowing pork barrel allocations to persist.

author: Unknown
title: DEM Party delegation meets with prisoners: Rights violations continue in Aegean region
content:
A DEM Party delegation which included MPs Nevroz Uysal Aslan, Burcugül Çubuk, İbrahim Akın, Vezir Parlak, and Onur Düşünmez, met with prisoners held at Buca and Aliağa Şakran prisons between 26 and 29 October.


Speaking outside Şakran Prison, lawyer and MP Nevroz Uysal Aslan said prisoners’ access to social activities was being restricted, problems were occurring during conditional release procedures, and petitions were being left unanswered.


Aslan noted that some women prisoners at Şakran were being prevented from using the shared exercise yard, that the imposition of identity requirements continued, and that some detainees were being denied access to their rights to sports, outdoor exercise, and social activities.


She also stated that sick prisoners were facing obstacles in accessing healthcare, while letters, books, and publications in Kurdish were being delayed or withheld.


Referring also to the Peace and Democratic Society Process, Nevroz Uysal Aslan said political prisoners held in prisons should be released to pave the way for democratic politics and enable legal steps to be taken.


The delegation’s prison visits are expected to continue at Bodrum S-Type Prison.

author: Unknown
title: Kobanê students: Our language is our existence
content:
Students in Kobanê protested against the Syrian Ministry of Education's decision to limit Kurdish-language education to three lessons. The students said that Kurdish was a fundamental part of their identity and existence and expressed their desire to continue receiving education in their mother tongue. 


We want to continue receiving education in our mother tongue


Eleventh-grade student Rehef Feysel Sedûn told ANF that they were not opposed to any language and that every people had the right to receive education in their mother tongue. Rehef Feysel Sedûn said, "I am the daughter of Martyr Abu Layla, and I have been receiving education in my own language for 11 years. We want to continue receiving education in our mother tongue. We already have Arabic and English lessons as well."


 


Rehef Feysel Sedûn pointed out that millions of Kurds had the right to receive education in their own language, stressing that mother-tongue education was a fundamental right of every people.


Rehef Feysel Sedûn, who wants to become a lawyer, said, "As Kurds, we also have the right to receive education in our mother tongue. I want to become a lawyer, and my dream was to do so in my own language. I want to fulfil my dreams in my mother tongue and defend my people in my own language."


‘I want to live my future in my own language’


Eighth-grade student Hêlîn Cuma Eto also said that they were not opposed to any language but wanted to receive education in Kurdish. Hêlîn Cuma Eto, who has been studying in Kurdish for eight years, said: "We are not against any language. But we want to receive education in Kurdish, our mother tongue. We have worked very hard, and the education I have received for eight years has been in Kurdish. I want to live my future in my own language as well. Our language is our existence, and we will keep our language alive to the very end."


‘I will continue receiving education in Kurdish’


A student named Jiyan also expressed her desire to continue studying using the Kurdish alphabet, saying, "My mother and father are also Kurdish. I will receive education in Kurdish, and I am continuing my studies."


Another student, Cana, who performed the song Bi xeml û rewş e, said that Kurdish was their mother tongue and that they should therefore receive education in it. Cana, who wants to become a doctor, said, "Our language is Kurdish. That is why we need to receive education in Kurdish. I want to become a doctor, and I want to pursue this goal through education in my own language."


The students emphasised that they wanted to continue building the futures they had envisioned through Kurdish-language education in their mother tongue and called for the protection of their right to mother-tongue education.

title: Over 600 international personalities appeal to Council of Europe to act on Right to Hope for Öcalan
content:
International efforts to secure the implementation of the Right to Hope for Abdullah Öcalan, and to enable him to participate in the Peace and Democratic Society Process under free conditions, have entered a new phase.


As part of the international campaign “Freedom for Abdullah Öcalan, a Political Solution to the Kurdish Question,” a letter has been sent to the Presidency of the Committee of Ministers of the Council of Europe (CoE). According to information provided by the campaign organisers, the letter was prepared with the support of 620 signatories from 29 countries around the world.


The letter, sent ahead of the Council of Europe's Committee of Ministers' human rights meeting, scheduled to take place from 1 to 3 December 2026, calls for the implementation of the 2014 ruling by the European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR) concerning Öcalan.


According to information shared by the campaign organisers, the new letter has received the support of 58 elected representatives. The signing initiative also includes individuals affiliated with 30 political parties, 90 civil society organisations and 16 trade unions.


Politicians, academics, lawyers, trade unionists, representatives of women's organisations and human rights advocates from Austria, Germany, Italy, France, Belgium, Denmark, Norway, Sweden, Switzerland, Spain, Canada, the United States and other countries have signed the letter.


Among the signatories are 2022 Nobel Prize in Physics laureate Anton Zeilinger, philosopher Slavoj Žižek, Member of the European Parliament Özlem Alev Demirel, Nicola Fratoianni and Maurizio Acerbo from Italy, Bjørnar Moxnes from Norway, Carlo Sommaruga from Switzerland, Kadir Kasırga from Sweden, and Mertxe Aizpurua, a representative of EH Bildu from the Basque Country.


The list also includes numerous former and current members of parliament, municipal councillors, lawyers, academics, trade union representatives and representatives of organisations engaged in solidarity work with Kurdish institutions.


The letter, addressed to the Presidency of the Committee of Ministers, is as follows: 


"On behalf of the international campaign “Freedom for Öcalan, Political Solution to the Kurdish Question,” we call on the Committee of Ministers of the Council of Europe to ensure Turkey’s implementation of the “Right to Hope” in accordance with the European Court of Human Rights’ judgments in Öcalan v. Turkey (No. 2) and the related Gurban Group of cases. The international campaign started on the 9th of October 2024 with participation of undersigned social movements, trade unions, Nobel Laureates, lawyers, academics, youth, women’s organisations, NGOs, elected officials, and others in its third anniversary renews its demands for the release of Mr. Abdullah Öcalan for the success of the peace process. 


This is a decisive moment to support Turkey in fulfilling its obligations as a Council of Europe member state and advancing the ongoing Peace and Democratic Society process initiated by Mr. Abdullah Öcalan. Implementing the Right to Hope is the essential legal step toward ending the regime of extreme isolation imposed on Mr. Öcalan for the past 27 years and enabling him, as the principal negotiator, to participate effectively in the peace process.


The December 2026 meeting of the Ministers’ Deputies presents a crucial opportunity for the Committee of Ministers to reaffirm its commitment to the rule of law, democracy, and human rights through concrete action. A strong decision supporting implementation of the Right to Hope would help Turkey in breaking out of its current deadlock on such fundamental issues, while demonstrating international support for a peaceful and democratic resolution of the Kurdish question.


Mr. Öcalan’s Call for Peace and Democratic Society, announced on 27 February 2025, has had significant impact in Turkey and the wider region. It has contributed to reducing violence and renewed hope for democratic dialogue and peaceful coexistence after decades of conflict. However, for these hope to materialise significant changes domestically and the support of the international community are needed more than ever. 


Despite recent legislative developments, Mr. Öcalan remains imprisoned under conditions that severely restrict his fundamental rights and communication with the outside world. While some legal reforms have been introduced, they fall short of genuine democratisation and do not implement the ECtHR’s judgments …

title: Journalist Mavioğlu: Corruption in Turkey has become institutionalised plunder - Part Two
content:
Journalist Ertuğrul Mavioğlu spoke to ANF about how corruption has developed into a systematic structure over the years, the mechanisms through which public resources are transferred to capital and how this system is sustained through impunity.


Part one of this interview can be read

here

. 


‘Football is not just football’


Mavioğlu discussed the controversies surrounding financial scandals, allegations of stock market manipulation, and match-fixing and betting investigations in Turkish football, saying that football could not be considered independently of the relationship between capital and politics.


Mavioğlu recalled the scandal publicly known as the “Fatih Terim fund”, arguing that the enormous sums of money circulating in football and the betting system had created an environment vulnerable to inadequate oversight.


Mavioğlu continued: “The most recent example was the scandal known as the Fatih Terim fund. A bank manager was imprisoned, and the scandal, which briefly occupied public attention, was eventually forgotten. Nothing clean can emerge from an environment where transfer fees worth millions of dollars are being discussed and the country's major capital owners dominate football clubs. And indeed, nothing clean does emerge.


Match-fixing is the most widespread example because football is also connected to the lottery and betting system. Wherever there is match-fixing, there is inevitably the mafia. And wherever the mafia operates, the conditions for violence, drugs and every kind of wrongdoing are already present.


This is why football is not just football. In Turkey, as elsewhere in the world, football is an industry in which all kinds of illegal activities are widespread and overlooked, yet it remains indispensable to the system. That is because football serves to manipulate the consciousness of millions of supporters.”


Mavioğlu cited historical examples of football being used by political authorities to influence society, drawing attention to the periods of António de Oliveira Salazar in Portugal and Francisco Franco in Spain: “People will remember the three-F formula associated with Portugal's fascist dictator Salazar and Spain's fascist dictator Franco. Salazar found a way to sustain his system through Football, Fado and Fatima, while Franco relied on Football, Fado and Fiesta. The only difference was that Salazar lulled the people through Fatima, meaning religion, while Franco used festivals and entertainment.


Perhaps that is precisely why Franco is said to have remarked, referring to stadiums, ‘I had three cradles built, each holding 50,000 people.’ When we consider all this alongside the fact that both Salazar and Franco remained in power for 36 years, we can better understand how the three-F formula invoked by these dictators provided a powerful source of support for fascism.


If we adapt this formula to Turkey, we should not overlook the possibility that the current government could continue making our lives miserable for at least another 11 years. Joking aside, Marx said, ‘Religion is the opium of the people.’ We cannot underestimate the significance of packed stadiums, alongside the government's firm reliance on religious arguments, just like Salazar. Perhaps this makes it easier to understand why football is not simply a game involving three referees and 22 players running around a pitch.”


‘Public tenders have become a means of transferring wealth to big capital’


Mavioğlu argued that corruption in public procurement had become normalised over time and that the allegations emerging today represented only a small part of a much wider system.


He drew particular attention to the growing use of the negotiated procurement procedure under Article 21(b) of the Public Procurement Law, arguing that a method intended for exceptional circumstances had become routine practice.


Mavioğlu said: “The most widely used method in public procurement is the negotiated procedure under Article 21(b) of Law No. 4734. In fact, the law requires extraordinary circumstances for this procedure to be used. In other words, negotiated procurement is subject to conditions such as natural disasters, epidemics, threats to life and property, sudden and unexpected events, security considerations and technical construction requirements.


However, particularly under AKP rule, open tendering has become the exception, while negotiated procurement has almost become the rule. This is because, under the …

author: Publicación Abierta
title: ¿De Sudamérica en disputa a Sudamérica en remate?: el reto de Lula
content:
¿De Sudamérica

en disputa

 a Sudamérica

en remate

?:

el reto de Lula


Por Rafael Bautista S.


 


 


 


“

Ahora somos un Imperio y cuando actuamos


creamos nuestra propia realidad.


Y mientras ustedes estudian esa realidad, juiciosamente,


como ustedes quieren, nosotros actuamos nuevamente


y creamos otras realidades, nuevas,


    que ustedes pueden estudiar igualmente,


y así suceden las cosas.


Nosotros somos los actores de la historia.


Y ustedes, todos ustedes,


sólo pueden estudiar lo que nosotros hacemos

”

[1]

.


 


La supuesta disposición política entre izquierda y derecha es ya un tópico que precisa una redefinición o sustitución conceptual, porque ya no expresa aquellas perspectivas dicotómicas que perfilaban proyectos distintos y que se excluían mutuamente. La crisis civilizatoria ha puesto también en crisis este esquema topográfico de la política mundial. Aun siendo todavía su uso relativamente útil en su contexto nacional, es en la política exterior –o sea, el tuétano mismo de la política– que su decadencia nos arrastra a los mismos esquemas que ya no sirven como

herramientas hermeneúticas

 adecuadas de la crisis global. La geopolítica destaca ahora una contradicción más urgente a resolver (en un mundo acechado por un rapto que se manifiesta al modo de un reseteo global sin precedentes): la lucha por un mundo en el que quepan todos, se expresa mejor en la disputa entre

soberanistas

 y

globalistas

.


El “progresismo” que ha vaciado, en muchos casos, la radicalidad de la izquierda histórica, es lo que ha domesticado la

crítica

 al poder (como superación y liberación) en una mera disputa por él. Por eso fracasan, porque siguen en el

paradigma globalista

 que financia a los demócratas gringos, a la izquierda mundial y al activismo funcional a la ideología liberal. Todos actúan como meros portavoces de agendas que se piensan a sus espaldas, usando demandas hasta populares que legitiman sus apuestas, una vez que éstas se implementan nacional, regional y mundialmente.


Es en los fondos de inversión donde se cotizan –y están decidiendo– el destino y el futuro de la humanidad, donde se generan las plataformas de los guiones supuestamente críticos que adoptan (con fuerte respaldo económico), el activismo antisistémico y los ideólogos incrustados en el campo popular para impedir su constitución en

bloque histórico

–

político

 (reduciendo la lucha a corporativismos ideológicos); como lo admitió hace poco Larry Fink, CEO de BlackRock.


En ese contexto, la política ya se halla privatizada, siendo los lobbies congresales el conducto mediante el cual se controla y diseña las políticas estatales. Esto ha conducido al escenario

postdemocrático

 que ya sufrimos (el propio concepto de democracia precisa una resemantización que desencubra su errática demarcación basada en los prejuicios de la narrativa imperial). Ya no escoge la sociedad y menos el pueblo, sino las agencias de inteligencia, los softwares, los algoritmos y la IA.


Sudamérica es la nueva arena de disputa financiera. Si de tercera guerra hablamos, ya estamos metidos en ella y se trata de la guerra del dólar contra toda soberanía monetaria (la destrucción masiva ya no se expresa tanto en el espectáculo militar sino en el proceso de degradación humana, sometida al desprecio y la indiferencia por la vida ajena, enmarcada por la incertidumbre y el abandono total de esperanza en un mundo inclemente). El rapto de la economía mundial significa la preservación de toda la institucionalidad global dólar-céntrica (en manos de los fondos de inversión), siendo, esta disputa sobre los recursos estratégicos y los corredores de suministros, la única garantía de restauración de Occidente (de sus principios y valores, o sea, sus negocios). Si el fascismo actual se ampara en la doctrina “Don-roe”, la “izquierda progre” cree que los demócratas son diferentes y que puede negociar con los financiados por Soros y otro tipo de capitales. Pero todo ello no es más que meterse en el banquete, pero para ser devorado. Aun así, las ilusiones “progres” siguen siendo seducidas a seguir por la misma vía que le condujo el fracaso. ¿Es mejor Soros que mal acompañado?


Por eso el triunfo de Lula, si desea volcar nuestra suerte regional y decidir lo que ya propuso el comandante Chávez (y nadie le entendió), deberá acabar con la subordinación al dólar y hacer de la región la plataforma estratégico-disuasiva del BRICS+. Generando las condiciones para que …

title: Elecciones en EE UU: el programa de los DS refleja exactamente lo que necesita y quiere una amplia mayoría de los estadounidenses
content:
Abdul El-Sayed, candidato demócrata al Senado por Michigan. Foto: Jeff Kowalsky/AFP/Getty Images


¿Son los Demócratas Socialistas (DS) “la amenaza más grande que ha enfrentado EE UU desde que fue fundada”?


Mario Hernandez


Desde 2016, cuando Bernie Sanders perdió las primarias contra Bill Clinton, el Partido Demócrata vive atormentado por el argumento de la “elegibilidad” que le ha llevado a optar siempre por los candidatos moderados con la idea de que los situados más a la izquierda podían asustar a algunos votantes. Desde entonces, para muchos progresistas ese argumento solo ha servido para preservar el inmovilismo y perder las elecciones frente a los candidatos republicanos disruptivos como Trump. Lo cierto es que los demócratas tradicionales perdieron las elecciones presidenciales de 2016 y 2024. Y las fallidas campañas presidenciales de Sanders en 2016 y 2020 sentaron las bases para el reciente levantamiento, que comenzó el año pasado con la elección de Zohran Mamdani, el popular alcalde socialista demócrata de Nueva York. Desde entonces, los votantes de las primarias demócratas han elegido a más candidatos comprometidos con la defensa firme de los valores progresistas.


La campaña de El-Sayed


La campaña en Michigan enfrentó a El-Sayed, un político carismático de 41 años, de religión musulmana y médico de salud pública, respaldado por el senador Bernie Sanders, contra la representante Haley Stevens, que contaba con el apoyo de gran parte del establishment demócrata. Los videos de la campaña de El-Sayed lo muestran como una persona ingeniosa y jovial. En 2007, fue el mejor alumno de su promoción en la Universidad de Michigan y por ese motivo leyó el discurso de fin de curso en presencia del Presidente Clinton. Haley Steevens recibió en su campaña más de 30 millones de dólares provenientes de donantes pro israelíes, pero El-Sayed tuvo la habilidad de utilizar en su contra ese apoyo financiero. El Comité de Asuntos Públicos Estadounidense-israelí (AIPAC) acusó a El-Sayed de adoptar una “retórica extremista”, de impulsar “falsas acusaciones de genocidio” y de apoyar la suspensión de la ayuda a Israel. Efectivamente, El-Sayed ha calificado la actuación del gobierno israelí en Gaza como un “genocidio” y ha afirmado que Estados Unidos no debería financiar militarmente esas acciones. Por ese motivo ha pedido poner fin a la ayuda militar incondicional de Estados Unidos a Israel, argumentando que la asistencia exterior debería estar sujeta al respeto de los Derechos Humanos y que los recursos deberían priorizar necesidades internas de Estados Unidos.


El-Sayed ha insistido en que criticar al gobierno de Israel no es antisemita y ha condenado el antisemitismo de forma explícita, afirmando que combatir el antisemitismo y la islamofobia son obligaciones morales igualmente importantes. Cuando CNN le preguntó a El-Sayed en julio si se podía ser sionista y progresista a la vez, respondió que “toda definición de un Estado (supremacista) judío termina por articular valores antiliberales, absolutamente todas”.


Los fondos oscuros


En Estados Unidos, la financiación de los partidos políticos y de las campañas electorales depende casi por completo de fondos privados. Se basa en donaciones individuales —limitadas por la ley a determinado importe—, aportaciones ilimitadas de los propios candidatos y grandes sumas canalizadas a través de comités y organizaciones sin límite de gasto amparadas por la libertad de expresión. Según el Tribunal Supremo, en la decisión adoptada en 2010 en el fallo Citizens United, limitar el gasto electoral vulnera la Primera Enmienda de la Constitución, lo que ha permitido el flujo ilimitado de fondos corporativos. Los Comités de Acción Política (PAC) son organizaciones que reúnen dinero de ciudadanos para entregarlo a las campañas, pero están sujetos a restricciones de cantidad. Sin embargo, los súper-PACs (Comités de Acción Política Superiores) recaudan fondos ilimitados de personas ricas, empresas y corporaciones. Si bien no pueden coordinarse de forma directa con la campaña del candidato, pueden gastar millones en anuncios independientes para apoyarlo. Se supone que los súper-PACs deben operar independientemente de los candidatos y partidos políticos, pero esta independencia está definida por reglas débiles que casi nunca se cumplen, de modo que terminan formando parte del aparato de campaña de cada partido. A los súper-PACs deben sumarse las organizaciones sin fines de lucro (dark money) …

title: Escándalo: INTA exoneró a la científica de Balcarce que detectó glifosato en las personas
content:
Escándalo: INTA exoneró a la científica de Balcarce que detectó glifosato en las personas


https://www.newsdigitales.com/nota/348472/escandalo-inta-exonero-a-la-cientifica-de-balcarce-que-detecto-glifosato-en-las-personas/


26/10/2026

 | Se trata de Virginia Aparicio, quien estuvo a cargo del estudio interrumpido por el gobierno de Milei.


INTA exoneró a la científica de Balcarce Virginia Aparicio (Foro Radio Gabal).


 


Sergio Di Pino


El Instituto Nacional de Tecnología Agropecuaria (

INTA

) resolvió exonerar a 

Virginia Aparicio

, la investigadora de la Estación Experimental Agropecuaria 

Balcarce

 que coordinó en Argentina el proyecto internacional

 SPRINT

, un estudio internacional que detectó 

glifosato

 en la orina del 84% de las personas analizadas.


La sanción es la más grave prevista en el régimen disciplinario del empleo público y supone su expulsión del organismo y la imposibilidad de ejercer en la función pública.


En el mismo expediente, otros dos funcionarios recibieron suspensiones temporales, mientras que varios agentes quedaron exentos de responsabilidad por el alcance de sus funciones o por no haberse acreditado una participación disciplinariamente relevante.


La resolución contra la destacada ingeniera agrónoma e investigadora lleva la firma del presidente del organismo, 

Nicolás Bronzovich

, y pone fin al sumario administrativo que se abrió contra la científica por presuntas irregularidades en la ejecución de la investigación.


La decisión llega después de que el 

INTA

 retirara a la Argentina del proyecto en 2023, durante la administración de 

Javier Milei

, y suspendiera la presentación pública de los resultados.


La investigación internacional buscaba medir la presencia de residuos de plaguicidas en personas, animales y el ambiente, en un contexto de creciente preocupación por la exposición a productos utilizados en la actividad agropecuaria.


La investigadora tiene 20 días para solicitar la reconsideración de la medida. Si ese planteo no prospera, su estrategia es recurrir a la Justicia y pedir un amparo,

 según indicaron fuentes gremiales a 

NewsDigitales.


La sanción máxima y el contraste con otros funcionarios


La resolución del Consejo Directivo del INTA, identificada como 

RESOL-2026-366-APN-CD#INTA 

y fechada el 26 de octubre, dispuso la 

exoneración

 de Aparicio por 

presuntas irregularidades 

que el organismo atribuye a su actuación como investigadora principal y coordinadora local del proyecto.


El expediente también concluyó con sanciones para otros dos integrantes del organismo. 

Facundo Quiroz,

 director de la Estación Experimental de Balcarce, recibió una suspensión de 15 días, mientras que 

Eduardo De Gerónimo

 fue sancionado con 25 días de suspensión.


En el caso de Quiroz, el INTA cuestionó que hubiera firmado un protocolo sin verificar adecuadamente su encuadre normativo y que demorara en elevar formalmente información sobre el envío de muestras al exterior y la participación de terceros. El organismo consideró como atenuante que no se hubiera acreditado una intención de ocultamiento.


A De Gerónimo, en tanto, le atribuyó inconsistencias en la documentación presentada para obtener permisos, la falta de comunicación de cambios en el circuito de análisis de las muestras y omisiones vinculadas con el acceso de terceros a información identificable de los participantes.


Otros agentes fueron eximidos de responsabilidad por distintas razones, entre ellas el carácter subordinado de sus tareas o la falta de una relación causal entre su intervención y las irregularidades investigadas.


Qué cuestionó el INTA sobre el estudio liderado por Aparicio


El organismo fundamentó la sanción en una serie de presuntas faltas administrativas vinculadas con la organización y ejecución de SPRINT. Entre ellas, señaló que la investigación habría excedido las autorizaciones institucionales, que se enviaron muestras biológicas a laboratorios extranjeros sin la aprobación correspondiente y que se modificó el comité de ética que intervenía en el proyecto.


También cuestionó el manejo de los consentimientos informados, la comunicación de resultados individuales y la participación de personas que habrían tenido acceso a datos identificables de los voluntarios sin contar con la autorización necesaria.

 presunta falta de declaración de un conflicto de intereses

Perseguir y censurar a la ciencia: el INTA echa y exonera a su mayor investigadora en agrotóxicos


septiembre 24, 2026


https://agenciatierraviva.com.ar/perseguir-y-censurar-a-la-ciencia-el-inta-echa-y-exonera-a-su-mayor-investigadora-en-agrotoxicos/


Sección: 

Agronegocio

 | 

Selecciones


Es el hecho más grave de persecución en el INTA desde la vuelta a la democracia. El Instituto está a un paso de echar a Virginia Aparicio, la mayor investigadora en agrotóxicos de la institución. En un proceso plagado de irregularidades y animosidad que lleva tres años, la condenan por haber confirmado los impactos del modelo de agronegocio en las personas y el ambiente. Aparicio lideró un proyecto internacional que encontró plaguicidas en la población, suelos y agua. Entrevista con la investigadora.


Foto: INTA


Por Darío Aranda


El INTA tiene un largo historial de persecuciones, censuras, precarización y maltrato laboral, pero dio un paso extremo y está a punto de cometer 

el hecho más grave desde la vuelta a la democracia: el despido y exoneración de Virginia Aparicio

, la mayor investigadora de agrotóxicos en la institución. ¿El motivo? Haber realizado su trabajo: 

analizó y confirmó los efectos terribles del modelo de agronegocio

 en la salud de la población y en el ambiente. La exoneración implica que nunca más podrá ser contratada por el Estado.


Los responsables directos de la censura y persecución: las autoridades del INTA, funcionarios de dos gobiernos, aliados de la Mesa de Enlace, Aapresid y de las empresas de transgénicos y agrotóxicos.


Pruebas contundentes


Con 22 años de carrera dentro del Instituto Nacional de Tecnología Agropecuaria (INTA), Aparicio tiene larga experiencia en la detección de agrotóxicos en el ambiente. Cuenta con publicaciones científicas, participó de libros y 

fue perito en causas judiciales sobre pueblos fumigados

. Siempre cumplió un rol científico-técnico y no silenció los resultados, aunque sabía que eran incómodos para el 

INTA, reconocida institución al servicio del agronegocio.


Pero el quiebre fue un 

proyecto internacional llamado Sprint

 (“Transición Sostenible de Protección Vegetal”), realizado durante cinco años por académicos de once países y que 

detalló el grave impacto del modelo agroindustrial

. Los países con población estudiada fueron Argentina, Francia, España, Portugal, Italia, Países Bajos, Suiza, Dinamarca, República Checa, Croacia y Eslovenia.


Aprobado por los distintos eslabones burocráticos y jefes del INTA, Aparicio participó del proyecto que incluía análisis de 73 personas de la provincia de Buenos Aires, tanto del ámbito rural como urbano.


Los resultados de Argentina fueron lapidarios, como contaron 

Cecilia Gárgan

o

 y 

Anabel Pomar en Tierra Viva

:


Todas las personas testeadas tenían glifosato en su cuerpo

.


Los

 

suelos y el agua bonaerense tienen una concentración de agrotóxicos

 más alta que en los países Europeos.


Se confirmo presencia abrumadora de 

glifosato, 2-4D, atrazina, clorpirifos, fipronil,

 

imidacloprid y cipermetrina, entre otros.


El total de participantes argentinos (73) presentó un rango

 

de 6 a 13 plaguicidas en orina, de 2 a 10 plaguicidas en sangre y hasta 18 plaguicidas en materia fecal.


Agua superficial se encontraron entre 10 a 28 plaguicidas.


Los resultados finales fueron presentados en Bélgica en una 

conferencia pública

.


Los resultados de 

Argentina lo ubican como el país con mayor cantidad de peligrosos plaguicidas

 

como el glifosato y el clorpirifos

.


Y, lejos de tomar medidas para proteger a la población, en Argentina sobrevino la censura.


El Instituto Nacional de Tecnología Agropecuaria 

abandonó la investigación en 2023

 mediante la Resolución 2023-399-APN-INTA, sin comunicar jamás los hallazgos de agrotóxicos en las personas y en el ambiente.


Los responsables directos: 

Mariano Garmendia

 y 

Nacira

 

Belén Muñoz

, presidente y vice del INTA en ese momento, y el entonces director nacional 

Carlos Parera

. El INTA prohibió que se hable del tema. Y apuntó las “culpas” a la reconocida y experimentada científica Virginia Aparicio, del INTA Balcarce.

 

Insólito: Garmendia y Muñoz participan de sindicatos (el primero en Ate, la segunda en Apinta), que tienen como regla principal defender a los trabajadores.


Era el año 2023. Gobernaba el peronismo de Alberto Fernández.

title: Kurdish businessman arrested in Belgium
content:
Businessman Muhsin Talay, who sought refuge in Belgium, has been arrested in Brussels on the basis of an Interpol notice issued at Turkey’s request. Talay, who was acquitted in a murder trial before a court in Amed (Turkish: Diyarbakır), is now in custody. His asylum proceedings in Belgium are still pending. His family warns of possible extradition to Turkey and calls on the Belgian authorities to grant him protection.


Murder accusation despite court acquittal


The arrest is linked to the murder of Murat Baycan, who was killed under unclear circumstances in Amed in 2005. Baycan is alleged to have worked as an informant and agent for the Turkish intelligence service (MIT). Muhsin Talay was accused of involvement in the killing but was acquitted in the subsequent proceedings before the 4th High Criminal Court in Amed.


According to his family, Talay continues to be linked to the murder despite his acquittal. The allegations are reportedly based on a report by the Turkish intelligence service (MIT), even though the evidence presented during the trial was discredited. The family accuses the Turkish authorities of seeking to prosecute and sentence Talay again on this basis.


Talay was reportedly subjected to repeated pressure from MIT during the court proceedings. Fearing mistreatment and renewed prosecution, he eventually left Turkey and applied for asylum in Belgium. While his application was still under review, he was arrested in Brussels on the basis of an Interpol notice.


Family calls for protection against extradition


According to the family, other relatives are also unable to return to Turkey. Two of Talay’s uncles are likewise living in Europe as asylum seekers or refugees and consider themselves unable to return. The family appeals to the Belgian authorities not to extradite Muhsin Talay to Turkey and to grant his asylum application. They fear that he could face mistreatment and renewed penalty if returned.


They are also calling on the Kurdish public, democratic organizations, and human rights groups to support Talay and mobilize public pressure against his possible extradition.
