author: EDRi
title: Draconian access block orders in Turkey
content:
Court orders to block access to X accounts in Turkey reached an unprecedented number in September 2026. In this blog, EDRi-member Alternatif Bilisim detail the crackdown on civil rights defenders and independent media in the country, and call on public authorities to reconsider block orders and protect fundamental rights.

By Alternatif Bilisim (guest author) · October 29, 2026

Court orders to block access to X accounts in Turkey reached an unprecedented number in September 2026, followed by the closure of T24, an independent news website. According to data from the EngelliWeb project of the Freedom of Expression Association (İFÖD), X blocked at least 1,270 accounts. In comparison, a total of 995 accounts were blocked in the entire year of 2025. In fact, the website of EngelliWeb, which tracks and documents online censorship in Turkey, was also blocked on 1 October 2026. Authoritarian measures and alarming levels of censorship in the country are increasingly eroding freedom of expression.

The common factor in all decisions related to access block orders is Article 8/A of Law No. 5651. This article allows the right of life, the safety of life and property of the persons, the protection of national security and public order, the prevention of crime or the protection of the internet contents or the prevention of access to the internet content. Several restrictions on access blocks in September cited grounds such as national security or protection of public order under 8/A.

Article 8/A was introduced by the government as an arrangement that was supposed to be implemented in exceptional cases, but its use has been gradually expanding. The use of this article is also being combined with the new provisions on family values under the so-called “My Family is Safe” investigations, which have led to a brutal crackdown on LGBTQ+ and HIV advocacy groups in Turkey.

EDRi-member Alternatif Bilisim condemns this act by the Turkish authorities and the complicity of X on the shadow bans. Turkey is increasingly witnessing an ideological surge on critical opinion and its clear consequences for the journalism landscape as well as digital spaces at large.

According to Engelliweb, in September 2026, many different accounts – from LGBTQ+ organisations and activists to journalists, academics to economists, from women’s organisations to individual users – were impacted by the access blocks. A few examples of note are the accounts of Evrensel, a socialist newspaper; Amnesty International Turkey; Academics for Peace; and the Media and Law Studies Association.

In the second half of September, social media posts on capital markets have also a key focus of blocks due to alleged cause of fear and panic in the society. A major capital-markets scandal in Turkey involved widespread market manipulation by asset managers who allegedly inflated fund values using worthless “junk stocks,” leading to the liquidation of 131 funds and affecting about 455,000 investors. Authorities arrested over 114 people and froze assets as part of the investigation into fraud and criminal organization charges.

A more recent disproportionate measure has been the closure of a prominent independent news website T24 and its social media accounts after the justice ministry reported that they had published 118 items during the previous year which the court classified as “LGBTQ propaganda”. The X accounts of Independent News Network Bianet, as well as several of its reporters have also been banned due to court orders citing national security and protection of public order.

Court decisions on access to an account does not mean that the account will automatically become invisible in X from Turkey. The decision must also be implemented by the platform. X did not implement all the decisions. According to the IFÖD’s findings, 1,139 of the at least 1,270 accounts (around 90 percent) that were blocked in September were made invisible from Turkey by X. According to X’s official policy, the company can only block access to certain content or accounts in the respective country when it receives a valid and appropriate legal request from an competent authority. The account is not closed globally in this case. Co-founder of EngelliWeb, Yaman Akdeniz, argues that platforms have become more harmonious with the demands of the authorities in Turkey, especially after March 19, 2025, following the arrest of Istanbul mayor and presidential candidate of the main opposition party (CHP), Ekrem …

author: EDRi
title: Surveillance in times of insecurity: a wicked and stupid strategy
content:
Sweden has been grappling with crime-related challenges in the past years. The difficulty to address violent crimes in cities notably has triggered extensive legislative reforms to increase surveillance and repression, including that of children. Tougher criminal penalties, widespread videosurveillance, mass electronic monitoring and government hacking are just a few examples illustrating the Swedish government’s attempt to counter public safety threats.

Sweden has been grappling with crime-related challenges in the past years. The difficulty to address violent crimes in cities notably has triggered extensive legislative reforms to increase surveillance and repression, including that of children. Tougher criminal penalties, widespread video surveillance, mass electronic monitoring and government hacking are just a few examples illustrating the Swedish government’s attempt to counter public safety threats.

However, this approach is not only misguided, as no evidence of its effectiveness exists, but also harmful to the fundamental right to personal integrity and thus to Swedish democracy. Furthermore, its impacts disproportionately fall on communities already marginalised and overpoliced.

Personal integrity is a key principle firmly embedded in the Swedish constitution. Between 2004 and 2017, the Swedish government tasked several inquiry committees to assess the impacts of new technologies on democracy and privacy, which led to important constitutional amendments reinforcing protections. And for very good reasons. The right to privacy ensures the respect and protection of people’s self-determination and their freedom of expression, assembly and association, the exercise of which is a sine qua non for democratic societies.

Privacy is neither a luxury nor a niche concern to the most computer-savvy. Examples of data breach, abuse and exploitation show how people lose power when their data, communications, movements, and associations are captured, monitored and exploited. In the digital age, nobody has “nothing to hide”.

In 2020 the New York Times revealed that the US company Clearview AI had amassed a database of billions of photos of people’s faces by scraping them from social media without their knowledge or consent, in order to provide a facial recognition tool to police forces. Clearview’s tool was used by hundreds of law enforcement agencies across the world, including in Sweden where the Data Protection Authority had to intervene to stop and sanction the unlawful processing of people’s sensitive biometric data. Whether you chose for your face to appear online or not, it is crucial for your right to privacy and for a flourishing and open Internet where you can freely express yourself that no private company steals your photos and shares all that information with the police for no valid reason.

For some categories of the population, privacy is even a lifeline. In 2023, a mother and her daughter were convicted for allegedly carrying out an illegal abortion in the US after Facebook transferred their private conversation on Messenger to the police. This case example underlines the importance of minimising the amount of user data internet companies should be able to access and store, especially in a context of increasing restrictions imposed on reproductive rights in many countries. Services offering access to safe abortion rely on secure and private communication channels, such as encrypted platforms, to protect themselves and their patients against multiple threats.

Privacy enables autonomy, dissent, and democratic participation. It acts as a shield when activists, journalists and even ordinary people get criminalised. If privacy goes down, all rights start falling like dominoes. Protecting our collective and personal boundaries today preserves freedom tomorrow.

Surveillance measures to tackle insecurity are doomed to fail. They are usually sold by politicians as quick technological fixes to complex societal issues. Yet, they are never backed up by robust evidence to prove their efficiency.

The presumption that videosurveillance cameras in public spaces help investigations or contribute to reducing crime rates has long been debunked by research studies. In 2016, the Court of Justice of the European Union (CJEU) declared the Swedish regime of mass retention of telecommunications data illegal under European Union (EU) law because the Court found no objective evidence supporting the fact that putting everyone …

author: Semhal Meles Zenawi
title: Ethiopia: Elections, Constitutional Change, and Genocidal Violence
content:
In November 2020, a war erupted in the Ethiopian region of Tigray. Six hundred thousand to a million civilian lives are estimated to have been lost. Amongst the many war crimes and crimes against humanity committed during the two-year war was genocide against Tigrayans. Abiy Ahmed has on several occasions insisted that the catalyst for war was his intolerance for voluntary disassociation and the exercise of the right to vote. 


The National Electoral Board of Ethiopia (NEBE) postponed the 2020 election several times, but the final “indefinite” postponement under the cover of COVID-19 breached the constitutionally set term limit. Then NEBE chair Birtukan Mideksa’s claim that COVID-19 introduced public health imperatives that overrode those of democracy was unconvincing given the government’s non-enforcement of other measures such as lockdowns or even social distancing, and its farcical claim of having developed a “homegrown” cure. 


Following a public outcry over the “corona-clouded power grab”, four prescriptive options for a “constitutional route to postponement” were presented to a curated array of government-aligned opposition by the then minister of justice, now minister of foreign affairs, Gedion Timothewos. The exercise was met with derision, even by its hand-selected participants. An equally performative constitutional “tribunal” was held, but that too failed to foster agreement over the legality of the postponement and the legitimacy of the government following the expiration of its term. 


Having catalysed constitutional chaos, Mideksa set about facilitating Ahmed’s bypassing of various laws and bylaws to dissolve the Ethiopian People’s Revolutionary Democratic Front (EPRDF) and establish the Prosperity Party (PP). Beyond legal and procedural controversies, the move to reconstitute the EPRDF drew criticism for its intent. Abiy’s desire to dissolve the EPRDF and

“Medemer”

 (amalgamate) its constituent and affiliated parts was viewed by many as an initial step towards constitutional remaking and a reversal of multinational federalism.


The dissolution of the EPRDF ended the “reformist” coalition known as Team Lemma that propelled Abiy Ahmed to its chairmanship and Ethiopia’s prime ministership. In August 2020, Lemma Megersa, after whom Team Lemma was named, was removed from the Prosperity Party and as Minister of Defence for opposing the EPRDF’s amalgamation. The PP’s establishment was so ad hoc that it remains unclear if Megersa had actually joined the PP before he was booted out.


The relationship between the erstwhile allies came under strain as early as 2019 and was indicative of a wider rift between Abiy Ahmed and his Oromo base over the meaning of “reform” and its alignment with the demands of the protests that spurred Team Lemma’s rise. Ahmed positioned himself as an Oromo populist championing the cause of the Oromo farmer and, more broadly, seeking the “proper implementation of federalism”. Once in power, he started to appeal to a form of “pan-Ethiopian” nationalism which hoped to homogenize national identity and recentralize Ethiopia’s governing structures. Many in Ahmed’s Oromo base viewed the turn as a betrayal of the cause. Even before Megersa’s political downfall, suspicions over Ahmed’s intentions ignited a still-raging conflict with the Oromo Liberation Army. 


For a time, Abiy managed to force together the antagonistic nationalisms by offering a shared enemy – Tigrayan supremacy. Once considered the champion of the “national question”, the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) was recast as the primary impediment to its “proper implementation”, while maintaining its long-held position as the primary impediment to the return of a unitary institutional setup. “Tigrinya speakers” became “daytime hyenas” on whom the country’s many political and social crises could be scapegoated. 


The TPLF opposed the postponement of the election and refused to recognize the federal government once its constitutionally set term was over. Unfortunately, the TPLF did not lodge an official challenge to the postponement through its seats in both chambers of parliament. Instead, it retreated into Tigray to shore up its base and made plans to hold a regional election within constitutionally set limits.


Both the dissolution of the EPRDF and the postponement of the elections drew widespread criticism from divergent opposition groups. Still, the TPLF’s concerns were dismissed as the mere disgruntlements of …

author: Lionel Bopage
title: Green Left Radio: Nationalism and class struggle in Sri Lanka
content:
Lionel Bopage joined Green Left Radio on October 23 to discuss his new book, Roots of a Crisis: Nationalism, Class Struggle and the National Question of Sri Lanka.

The book offers a critical examination from within the Marxist tradition of how a serious revolutionary analysis of Sri Lanka’s national question was formulated, where it succeeded and where it failed. This includes support for Tamil liberation.

Bopage argues that socialists need to take a strong stand defending minority rights “even if it costs them votes” among majority communities.

Listen to the full episode at 3CR.

author: Diane de Vignemont
title: ‘If we burn, you burn with us’: France’s youth ignite a massive revolt
content:
While media fixated on the violence in Paris, French high school students achieved something rare and important on October 17–18: sectors that usually fight alone marched together in massive protests that are seeing repercussions around Europe.

Truthdig's Diane de Vignemont spoke to high school students, educators and others at the protest in Paris about their demands and how the movement is evolving.

“Make sure you tell the Americans that trash cans aren’t the only things burning in France,” 16-year-old Ewen told Truthdig as protesters gathered on the Place de la République on Saturday [October 17]. Tear gas canisters had been falling into the growing crowd for about an hour, and the teen struggled to make himself heard with his mask.

“Our future is burning, too,” Ewen added. Due to the repression and arrests by police, most protesters asked that only their first names be used.

In rapid succession, he listed everything he’d come to protest against: his rat-infested high school, the violent police repression of the student movement, but also the lack of hospital beds across the country, the cost of living, the saturated job market and the quickly-forgotten fires that ravaged France this summer. During the country’s hottest summer on record this year, some 250,000 acres of forest burned.

Grabbing his three friends, Ewen then posed for a photo, holding up a sign that read: “If we burn, you burn with us!”

“It’s a Hunger Games reference,” Ewen explained, as though I were decidedly too ancient to get it on my own. “It means that we’re not just fighting for ourselves, but for you, too.”

Marine Champetier de Ribes, who teaches literature at a school in a Paris suburb, told Truthdig that she felt France’s youth had awakened something in the rest of society. “Us adults had collectively fallen into torpor,” she said. “They shook us out of it and reminded us all that we’re right to be angry.”

That torpor lifted in plain sight on October 17. Between 550,000 and 800,000 people marched across the country. Though much of the national and international coverage focused on the violence that marred the margins of Saturday’s protests, the lesson was elsewhere: In less than a month, the high schoolers’ movement managed to pull a tired, resigned country back into the streets. Students were joined by teachers, parents, doctors, nurses, lawyers, pensioners, Yellow Vests, farmers and firefighters in perhaps the most intersectional movement France has seen in decades.

Champetier de Ribes, 34, told Truthdig that she and her colleagues across the education sector had been organising for years, but had been slowly losing steam. “No one was listening to us,” she lamented.

In her school alone, she cited “cockroach-infested walls, clogged toilets, rat droppings in the microwaves and boiling classrooms that have yet to cool down after this summer’s heat waves.” Champetier de Ribes said she has also been forced to fit 38 students into her 215-square-foot classroom, which never has enough chairs and desks: “I’ve had to insist that at least three of them be absent every week so I can teach the rest,” she said.

Champetier de Ribes said teachers had become disillusioned. “We’d quite forgotten how to be angry, until, that is, our students began leading by example,” she said.

Starting on September 17, high schoolers across the country began barricading their schools to demand better material conditions and equal education opportunities. The movement began in the Paris suburb of Créteil and it spread fast: By October 1, the Interior Ministry reported that more than 1000 of France’s 3700 high schools had been affected, more than 200 of them blockaded.

The students’ demands are more specific than their critics let on: a 10 billion-euro investment plan for schools, and an end to Parcoursup, the national platform that manages university admissions, which is often compared to a “social sorting machine” and criticised for its lack of transparency.

They’re also asking for more teachers, Last year, students across France lost some 20 million hours worth of lessons because absent teachers were not replaced. The education shortfalls are a result of President Emmanuel Macron’s neoliberal approach to public education funding while simultaneously increasing defense spending.

author: Unknown
title: Zeynep Karayılan: Peace process cannot be one-sided
content:
Discussions continue over establishing a legal framework for disarmament and the return of members of the Kurdish Freedom Movement as part of the Peace and Democratic Society Process, launched with the aim of achieving a democratic solution to the Kurdish question. Two years into the process, the National Security Council (MGK) has yet to issue the decision required to implement the framework law passed by parliament on 10 August with the support of 467 MPs.


The law, published in the Official Gazette on 16 August, requires security agencies to verify that disarmament has taken place, with their findings subsequently confirmed by an MGK decision before the mechanism established under the law can be activated. The absence of concrete steps towards implementation, despite parliament beginning its new legislative year and the MGK holding a meeting, has drawn criticism.


Zeynep Karayılan, Co-Chair of the Diyarbakır (Amed) Branch of the Association of Lawyers for Freedom (ÖHD), spoke to ANF about the legal dimensions of the process, the shortcomings of the framework law, expectations for democratisation and the steps that need to be taken.


 


‘Implementation of the law requires an MGK decision’


Zeynep Karayılan said the implementation of the law had been made conditional on assessments by security institutions and an MGK decision, reflecting the continued treatment of the Kurdish question through the framework of security policies.


Karayılan said: “For the mechanism established under this law to become operational, the security forces must first determine that the organisation has laid down its arms. This must then be confirmed by a decision of the National Security Council and published in the Official Gazette. In other words, the verification and confirmation mechanism must first be activated before the provisions of this law can take effect.


We have repeatedly said that this law is deeply inadequate, that numerous problems will arise in its implementation and that, far from resolving the Kurdish question, it once again places security-oriented policies at its core. Nevertheless, despite all its shortcomings, we, Abdullah Öcalan and the Kurdish Freedom Movement have regarded this law as a starting point.”


‘The Kurdish side takes historic steps, but the government lacks transparency’


Karayılan said negotiations aimed at resolving the Kurdish question were particularly important after a century of policies of denial and destruction and 50 years of conflict. She added that the emergence of a basis for dialogue carried historical significance, particularly in light of the policies pursued over the past decade.


Karayılan said the Kurdish Freedom Movement had taken and implemented significant decisions as part of the process, while the government had failed to take corresponding concrete and transparent steps.


Karayılan said: “Following the Collapse Plan implemented over the past 10 years, sitting down at the negotiating table is extremely important, as is demonstrating the political will to pursue a solution. Mr. Öcalan is undoubtedly the principal architect of this process. The Kurdish Freedom Movement has also supported the process and, from the very beginning, made and implemented a series of historic decisions. Just recently, it issued a unilateral statement announcing the evacuation of camps near the Turkish border. In doing so, it once again demonstrated its determination to pave the way for the process.


However, looking at the other side of the negotiating table, we see from the government's statements that the process is still being approached primarily through security and disarmament. Although two months have passed since the law was adopted, there has been no official explanation of how the verification and confirmation mechanism is being implemented. Councils convene and meetings take place, but no official information is provided about their content. The government is not conducting the process transparently.”


‘Toxic language and uncertainty undermine public trust’


Karayılan said uncertainty surrounding the progress of the process and the language used in the media were weakening public confidence in peace. She said the Kurdish question could not be treated solely as a matter of disarmament or ending the conflict.


Karayılan said: “The media uses extremely toxic and hostile language. Both this language and the current uncertainty and prolonged period of waiting are undermining public …

author: Kodao Productions
title: Makabayan urges recall of House approved 2027 budget to correct ‘unconstitutional insertions’
content:
Makabayan urges recall of House approved 2027 budget to correct ‘unconstitutional insertions’


The Makabayan Coalition of progressive legislators suggests the recall of the House-approved 2027 proposed budget in order for flagged entries to be corrected before bicameral discussions.


ACT Teachers Party Rep. Antonio Tinio said such a move would give the House of Representatives (HOR) the chance to align the entire budget with the recent Philippine Supreme Court ruling that some budgetary practices in the last three years were “unconstitutional.”


“It is important for the House to accept the correctness of the decision, rather than adopting Malacañang’s stance that the Court committed ‘judicial overreach,’” Tinio said.


Tinio added provisions that need correction pertain to unprogrammed appropriations, insertions for thousands of questionable infrastructure projects in the guise of institutional amendments, as wells as lump sum allocations such as the so-called local government support fund.


He said the practice of project insertions and lump sump allocations are what fuels corruption in the Philippine government.


Road projects in the ocean?


Tinio’s statements came as the group People’s Budget Coalition (PBC) flagged farm-to-market road (FMR) and infrastructure insertions in the proposed P7.2-trillion 2027 Philippine national budget that have geographic coordinates plotted in the open sea and international/foreign locations.


A P23 million (Dh1.3 million) FMR project designated for the landlocked province of Nueva Ecija, but its coordinates plot out in the Pacific Ocean near the Philippine Rise.


A P30 million (Dh1.7 million) FMR project intended for Cebu Province, but its listed coordinates map far south into the Celebes Sea near Indonesia.


A P55 million (Dh3.15 million) proposed FMR project for Quezon Province, but its coordinates place it in the ocean near Brunei.


The Coalition also discovered at least two proposed projects whose coordinates turn out to be in faraway Africa.


A building project worth P7 Million (Dh 401,334) in Misamis Oriental but its listed coordinates originally pointed to the Sahara in Algeria or South Sudan in the proposed budget submitted by the office of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. This has been corrected in the HOR version.


Road Project in Negros Occidental but with coordinates pointing to Nigeria, which remained uncorrected in the House-approved version.


Honest mistake or deliberate acts?


HOR leaders meanwhile dismissed the revelations as mere “typographical errors” during the compilation of extensive budget amendments.


While acknowledging that coordinates provided in the budget are “misplaced,” HOR Deputy Speaker Ronaldo Puno and Committee on Appropriations Senior Vice Chairperson Albert Garcia stated that the items were results of honest mistakes.


Garcia asked the Coalition to provide a specific itemized list of the questioned projects so the chamber can review and correct them before the final enactment of the P7.2 trillion proposed budget.


But Puno went on attack mode, calling the PBC “ignorant” of the budget process. “I hope they get serious with their attacks, because it just betrays ignorance like that,” he quipped. He stated that the House does not create the budget but merely reviews proposals submitted by executive agencies.


PBC however dismissed HOR’s denials, revealing that nearly 7,000 House-inserted infrastructure and farm-to-market road projects worth around P190 billion — including 355 farm-to-market roads worth nearly P6 billion — also lacked proper project attachments or featured wrong coordinates.


Vigilance, not ignorance


PBC likewise clapped back at Puno, saying it is deeply disappointed by the HOR leader’s remarks dismissing corruption watchdogs as ignorant.


“We are more than 5,000 volunteers, alongside members of various civil society organizations, carefully scrutinizing the national budget as it passes through Congress. We analyze the figures, examine the details, question questionable allocations, and demand accountability for every peso of taxpayers’ money,” PBC convenor Kenneth Abante said.


Abante said they are not ignorant but citizens exercising their right and responsibility to hold those in power accountable.


“Public funds are not personal money, political favors, or resources to be manipulated for private gain. They are the hard-earned contributions of the Filipino people, entrusted to the government to serve the …

author: Unknown
title: ABD'den müttefiklerine İran uyarısı: Seçim sonrası saldırı gündemde
content:
ABD yönetimi, Orta Doğu’daki müttefiklerini İran’a yönelik yeni askeri saldırı olasılığına ve Tahran’ın verebileceği karşılığa karşı hazırlıklı olmaları konusunda uyardı. Associated Press’in (AP) haberine göre Washington, yeni saldırıların 3 Kasım’da yapılacak ABD ara seçimlerinin ardından gündeme gelebileceğini bölge ülkelerine iletti.

Konuyla ilgili bilgi sahibi iki ABD’li diplomat, Başkan Donald Trump’ın İran’a yeniden saldırı düzenlenmesi konusunda henüz nihai kararını vermediğini belirtti. İsimlerinin açıklanmasını istemeyen diplomatlara göre ABD, olası saldırıların birkaç gün sürebileceği uyarısında bulundu.

Washington’ın müttefiklerinden, İran’ın misilleme kapsamında enerji tesislerini ve diğer kritik altyapıyı hedef alabileceği ihtimaline karşı önlem almalarını istediği aktarıldı. Trump’ın saldırı tehditleri ve ABD’nin bölge ülkelerine yaptığı uyarılar, Orta Doğu’da çatışmaların yeniden genişleme riski taşıdığı yönündeki endişeleri artırdı.

ABD’nin saldırı ihtimaline ilişkin uyarıları, bölgedeki askeri hareketliliğin arttığı bir dönemde geldi. Pentagon, eylül ayının sonunda uçak gemisi USS Theodore Roosevelt ile deniz piyadelerini taşıyan amfibi çıkarma gemilerini San Diego’dan Basra Körfezi’ne sevk etti. AP’nin aktardığına göre sevkiyat yaklaşık 9 bin askeri kapsıyor.

ABD’li bir yetkili, bu sevkiyatın ardından bölgede 20 binden fazla denizci ve deniz piyadesi ile yüzlerce hava aracının konuşlandırılabileceğini belirtmişti. ABD Donanması, nisan ayında 2003’ten bu yana ilk kez Orta Doğu’da aynı anda üç uçak gemisi bulundurmuştu.

Wall Street Journal da daha önce Körfez ülkelerinin İran’la olası bir askeri tırmanışa karşı hazırlıklı olmaları konusunda bilgilendirildiğini bildirmişti.

ABD’nin bölgedeki askeri varlığını artırması, Trump yönetiminin diplomatik seçenekleri tamamen dışlamadığı açıklamalarına karşın yeni bir saldırı olasılığını gündemde tutuyor.

İran’la savaşın ekonomik sonuçları, ABD’deki ara seçimler öncesinde Cumhuriyetçi adaylar üzerindeki baskıyı artırıyor. Saldırılar ve bölgedeki çatışmalar nedeniyle yükselen akaryakıt fiyatları, taşımacılıktan sanayiye kadar birçok alanda maliyetleri artırdı.

Trump, son haftalarda Cumhuriyetçi adayların seçim kampanyalarına ağırlık verirken İran’a yönelik yeni adımlar konusunda net bir takvim açıklamadı.

AP’nin haberinde, ABD’nin İran’a karşı yürüttüğü savaşın maliyetinin de arttığına dikkat çekildi. Pentagon’un Kongre’ye sunduğu son tahmine göre savaşın ABD bütçesine maliyeti 47,1 milyar dolara ulaştı.

İran Dışişleri Bakanı Abbas Arakçi, çarşamba günü yaptığı açıklamada Tahran’ın diplomasiye şans vermeyi sürdürdüğünü bildirdi. Arakçi, İran’ın daha önce sunduğu ve ateşkese dönüş için temel alınmasını istediği öneri üzerindeki görüşmelerin arabulucular aracılığıyla sürdüğünü belirtti.

Birleşik Arap Emirlikleri Dışişleri Bakanlığı da taraflara gerilimin düşürülmesi ve siyasi çözüm yollarının izlenmesi çağrısında bulundu.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Publicación Abierta
title: Continúan las movilizaciones en Albania
content:
Continúan las movilizaciones en Albania


Mario Hernandez


 


La policía disparó gas lacrimógeno y utilizó cañones de agua para hacer retroceder a los manifestantes el martes 20 de octubre, en el octavo día consecutivo de violentas protestas antigubernamentales en la capital albanesa, Tirana, marcadas por la tensión y sin visos de que vaya a cesar.


 


Estudiantes de secundaria y universitarios, se suman a los franceses e italianos, que exigen matrículas más bajas y una mayor inversión estatal en educación, al mismo tiempo que un mayor combate a la corrupción que le acaba de dar el triunfo en las legislativas a la Lista Estudiantil en Serbia.


Desde hace días, los manifestantes han arrojado piedras, bengalas, bombas incendiarias y fuegos artificiales contra la policía, que ha utilizado palos, cañones de agua y gas lacrimógeno para repeler a los descontentos.


Las calles del centro de Tirana han vuelto a estar tomadas por manifestantes, en su mayoría jóvenes, que demandan también la salida del Gobierno que encabeza Edi Rama.


Rama, en un intento de apertura hacia las demandas de los estudiantes, ha sacado siete sillas con tapicería roja a la escalinata junto a la sede de su oficina, cerca del bulevar donde tienen lugar las protestas, con un cartel en el que se leía ‘diálogo’ sobre el asiento.


La acción no ha sido bien acogida por los manifestantes que, horas después, han tomado las sillas y las han roto frente a la oficina en una nueva señal de falta de sintonía entre el primer ministro y la calle.


Por su parte, los sindicatos estudiantiles hacen fuerza junto a los profesores prometiendo seguir en las plazas y vías públicas “todos los días”.


Asimismo, un balance ofrecido por las autoridades albanesas tras los primeros siete días de movilizaciones, con altercados graves como la quema de la sede del Tribunal Supremo, ha arrojado que 310 personas resultaron heridas, en su mayoría agentes de Policía, 191, además de 88 manifestantes y 31 personas transeúntes.


“Entre los casos más graves se encuentran las lesiones que han requerido intervención quirúrgica. Hasta el momento, se han realizado un total de tres intervenciones quirúrgicas”, han explicado las autoridades sanitarias en informaciones recogidas por la cadena pública

RTSH

.


En el frente judicial, un Juzgado de Primera Instancia de Tirana ha ordenado medidas cautelares contra once de los detenidos en los altercados de estos días, del más del centenar de personas arrestadas en este contexto. A estas personas se les ha aplicado medidas como presentarse ante la policía judicial o prohibición de acercarse a 100 metros de instituciones públicas.


Por su parte, el martes 20 el presidente del país, Bajram Begaj, se ha reunido con representantes del cuerpo diplomático en Tirana y con los ex presidentes del país, Bamir Topi y Rexhep Meidani, para valorar la situación en medio de las protestas estudiantiles.


También, han acudido a la cita el embajador de Estados Unidos, Eric Wendt, el embajador de la Unión Europea, Moreira de Sousa y el embajador de Alemania, Karl Bergner, entre otros diplomáticos.


El fin de semana anterior, la legación estadounidense criticó “la violencia, los disturbios, el daño físico a otros y la destrucción de propiedades” en el marco de las protestas, pidiendo a todos los ciudadanos ejercer su derecho a la protesta “de manera pacífica”.


 


“Guerra híbrida”


 


El primer ministro albanés, Edi Rama, afirmó que la causa de las violentas protestas antigubernamentales que agitan la capital Tirana es una “guerra híbrida”.


El movimiento comenzó hace meses con manifestaciones mayoritariamente pacíficas contra un proyecto turístico vinculado a la familia del presidente estadounidense, Donald Trump, que generó indignación por las acusaciones de corrupción y la falta de transparencia del gobierno.


Sin embargo, el martes 13 comenzaron protestas estudiantiles para pedir mejoras en las condiciones en las universidades y denunciar la corrupción y también exigir la dimisión de Rama.


Esta movilización estuvo marcada por enfrentamientos diarios entre manifestantes, muchos de ellos encapuchados, y la policía. Alrededor de 300 personas fueron heridas, más de la mitad de ellas policías, según las autoridades.


El primer ministro Rama se reunió una semana después con los directores de las escuelas secundarias y culpó a una “guerra híbrida” de los disturbios y reiteró sus acusaciones de que hay injerencia extranjera detrás de ellos.

author: Brian Hioe
title: What Explains the Rise of Puma Shen as a DPP Candidate in Taipei?
content:
THE METEORIC RISE of Puma Shen as the DPP’s Taipei mayoral candidate has made what was previously perceived as a relatively slow election into an unpredictable and exciting one. It is generally expected that Shen, whether or not he wins the Taipei mayorship, could be the best-performing DPP Taipei mayoral candidate since Chen Shui-bian in 1992–Chen, of course, later became president.

Shen being sent to run in Taipei was originally perceived as his being sent there as a sacrificial candidate. After all, Shen was previously mainly known for tough stances on China, as the founder of the Doublethink Lab, which researches Chinese disinformation, and of the Kuma Academy, Taiwan’s best-known civil defense organization. It would be expected that he would struggle in historically pan-Blue Taipei. Running Shen, then, would be to field a younger and untested candidate for Taipei, whereas running another post-Sunflower politician, such as Enoch Wu, who had previously contested Taipei mayor Chiang Wan-an unsuccessfully, would have been seen as putting little effort into the race. Shen, as a party list legislator, had never had to run an electoral campaign before.

As Shen has related in interviews, however, as it turns out, the public was little aware of him. This allowed Shen to radically reinvent his image, so as to appeal to Taipei voters. And Shen has doubled down on a focus on good governance.

In particular, while Taipei mayor Chiang Wan-an was previously seen as one of the KMT’s stronger candidates, he has suffered in recent times. Chiang became embroiled in a number of controversies, ranging from a police raid on a gay bar, his abrupt proposal to relocate Songshan Airport, and his son’s placement in a scholarship program for travel to the US.

Chiang was already known for poor public speaking skills, including being unable to relate details of policy and having to rely on aides, but Shen has managed to distinguish himself by seemingly effortlessly being able to respond to questioning and having a deep recall of facts without needing to consult materials or aides. Shen has put forward detailed and intricate policy proposals, with his campaign crafting an image for Shen as a policy wonk.

Shen, then, has been remarkably popular–especially among young people. One notes that Shen was already popular among young people, as one saw during the 2024 Bluebird Movement–one of the reasons why young people mobilized so quickly was because Shen was among the legislators injured during scuffles in the series of events that triggered the movement.

If young people were already fond of Shen, this could be attributed not only to his strong stance on China, but also to his relatable public image–Shen was prone to late-night posts about his sometimes negative feelings on work. One could scarcely imagine Chiang doing the same. This may be another contributing factor to his success at present–his ability to connect to voters on an emotional level, whereas Chiang instead comes off as a nepotistic elite who is remote from everyday concerns.

One can perhaps compare the rise of Shen and the “Ocean Current” phenomenon to the rise of Zohran Mamdani as New York mayor. But if Mamdani campaigned on the basis of promises to act against socioeconomic inequality, Shen has doubled down simply on good governance, based on a strong command of policy, with innovative policy proposals–that this is the political message that has resonated with the public, rather than one of socioeconomic inequality even at a time of widening social inequality, perhaps speaks to the lack of class consciousness in Taiwanese society.

Regardless of whether Shen wins or not–in many ways, despite his missteps, the race is still Chiang Wan-an’s to lose–Shen’s political future is assured. As with Hung Sun-han, another post-Sunflower politician who became a DPP party list candidate, the DPP will likely keep Shen in circulation in government positions so as to keep him in the public eye. Likewise, Chiang Wan-an’s chances of running for president in 2028 may have receded, given how his poor defense against Shen has revealed many political weaknesses, with Chiang gesturing toward backing Lu Shiow-yen as a presidential candidate.

author: Andrés
title: Villa Soldati: caravana por la salud comunitaria y contra la violencia y la falta de recursos
content:
Bajo la consigna «Nos cuidamos entre todes», trabajadores de la salud, organizaciones comunitarias y vecinos recorrerán este jueves 29 de octubre las calles de Villa Soldati. La iniciativa busca visibilizar las situaciones de violencia que atraviesan el barrio, y las dificultades de acceso a la salud pública. Desde el CeSAC 24 advierten sobre la falta de recursos para garantizar tratamientos méd

icos.


Por Mario Canaviri para ANRed.


Trabajadores de la salud, organizaciones comunitarias y vecinos de Villa Soldati realizarán este jueves 29 de octubre desde las 8.00 una caravana bajo la consigna «Nos cuidamos entre todes». La movilización partirá del Centro de Salud y Acción Comunitaria (CeSAC) 24 y finalizará en la posta sanitaria Las Gemelas, ubicada en Portela 2500.


La convocatoria surge de la organización colectiva frente a las situaciones de violencia que afectan a los barrios populares del sur porteño y las dificultades que atraviesan los equipos sanitarios para garantizar el acceso a la salud.


«La iniciativa siempre es la misma, es decir, juntarnos en comunidad y poder visibilizar las problemáticas, en este caso, de violencia. La violencia que vivimos nosotros la semana pasada la vive el barrio en forma permanente», explicó a ANRed Marcela Corin, directora del CeSAC 24.


La profesional recordó que estas acciones tienen antecedentes en el territorio. Hace aproximadamente dos años y medio, trabajadores y referentes comunitarios realizaron una caravana bajo la consigna «Paz para Soldati», frente a episodios de violencia armada en el barrio.


La salud pública frente a las problemáticas del territorio


Corin señaló que entre las situaciones más complejas que enfrenta el equipo sanitario se encuentran el consumo problemático de sustancias, la violencia de género, el maltrato, el abuso sexual infantil y la tuberculosis.


A estas problemáticas se suman las dificultades para garantizar medicamentos y el acceso a especialidades médicas.


Según precisó, el CeSAC 24 recibió en octubre un presupuesto de 25 millones de pesos para farmacia y otorga alrededor de 100 turnos diarios de dispensa de medicamentos. La directora sostuvo que, de acuerdo con un relevamiento realizado por el equipo, necesitarían aproximadamente el doble de recursos para cubrir la demanda.


«Se genera un cuello de botella y un problema muy grave con los pacientes con enfermedades crónicas o enfermedades psiquiátricas que necesitan medicación sí o sí», advirtió la profesional de la salud pública.


La organización comunitaria como respuesta


Frente a las situaciones de violencia, Corin cuestionó que las respuestas se limiten a colocar efectivos policiales en los establecimientos de salud y planteó la necesidad de construir políticas de seguridad que involucren a distintos sectores de la comunidad.


La caravana contará con la participación de trabajadores, referentes barriales y vecinos de Fátima, Carrillo, Piletones, Los Pinos y 26 de Junio, entre otros sectores de Villa Soldati.


La convocatoria está abierta a toda la comunidad y busca fortalecer la organización territorial frente a problemáticas que atraviesan la vida cotidiana de los barrios populares.


El recorrido comenzará a las 8.00 en el CeSAC 24, y finalizará en la posta de salud

Las Gemelas

, en Portela 2500.

author: cnt.es
title: 3 de noviembre. Resolución de dudas sobre el derecho a huelga
content:
La asesoría laboral de CNT Ciudad Real ofrecerá una sesión práctica el martes 3 de noviembre para informar sobre el ejercicio del derecho a huelga y resolver las dudas más habituales de la plantilla.


¿Podemos hacer huelga? ¿Qué ocurre si la empresa nos dice que no tenemos derecho? ¿Qué pasa si trabajamos como falsos autónomos?


Ante una convocatoria de huelga, es habitual que surjan dudas sobre nuestros derechos y las posibles consecuencias de secundarla. La desinformación y las presiones empresariales pueden generar incertidumbre entre las personas trabajadoras y dificultar su participación.


Por eso,

CNT Ciudad Real organiza una sesión de resolución de dudas sobre el derecho a huelga

, a cargo de su asesoría laboral. El encuentro servirá para abordar situaciones concretas, aclarar cuestiones legales y ofrecer herramientas prácticas para conocer y defender nuestros derechos.

Mussolini continues to tower above and parliament crawls at his feet more than ever.

Full powers have been granted with the care of servants who compete with each other in degradation. Mussolini had said, “give them to me or I’ll take them”, and no one had the dignity to answer, take them from us, but don’t force us to play the part in a comedy of the bosses, when we are servants and are pleased to be so.

The socialists themselves have not understood that they cannot remain with dignity in an assembly that functions under the terror of the baton, or of dissolution, and where opposition can only be a farce.

Dictatorship triumphs: a dictatorship of adventurers without scruples or ideals, which came to power and remains there due to the disorientation of the proletarian masses and the anxious avarice of the bourgeois class in search of a saviour. But everyone feels that the situation is such that it cannot last, and the most enlightened conservatives, while paying due homage to the masters of the hour and revealing with every word the fear that dominates them, demand the restoration of the “liberal state”, that is, a return to constitutional deception.

The method by which Mussolini came to power does not allow deception, and this is what torments the innocent souls of the conservatives.

Mussolini, if he manages to consolidate his power, will do no more and no less than any other minister would: he will serve the interests of the privileged class, and will charge for his services. But he won’t make anyone believe that he arrived in government by the will of the people. His tyranny is too recent for him to be able to hide its origin: perhaps for this reason his murky conscience advises him to appeal to God!

We do not want to deal with the new government’s plans and intentions, whether new or old, sincere or otherwise. It’s always the same habitual rehashing of old lies, the old attempt to repair a collapsing house with a coat of paint.

For us, the only important change is this: we were enemies of government because government is no more than the armed defender of all social injustices, the creator of new injustices, the enemy of freedom, the material obstacle along the path of civilization. And we were enemies of fascism because it is a movement intended to defend bourgeois privileges, to impede the ascent of the proletariat, to choke out any aspiration towards a society more just and free; and it used brutal, ferocious and vile means to achieve its goals.

Now government and fascism have become the same thing, and are made up of the same personnel: there is therefore no longer the possibility of hesitation as there was when those two forces of oppression seemed to oppose each other.

Simplified situation: so much the better. So much the better if this can serve to reunite all the forces of progress in the struggle against triumphant barbarism.

author: Ian Angus
title: Ecosocialist Bookshelf II — October 2026
content:
Climate and Capitalism editor Ian Angus presents five new books on the affordability crisis, petrochemicals, punishing polluters, forever chemicals and the costs of climate change.

Grand Theft Capital: What Workers Should Know About the Affordability Crisis By Fred Magdoff and John Bellamy Foster Monthly Review Press Workers’ current conditions are the result of a deliberate, long-term effort by the corporate rich to increase their own wealth, largely by extracting it from workers’ pockets. Successive generations of young workers have been confronting difficult and precarious employment conditions. What workers face is nothing less than a class war waged from above; the only solution is an equally determined class war from below.

Petrochemical Planet: Multiscalar Battles of Industrial Transformation By Alice Mah Duke University Press Mah juxtaposes the petrochemical industry’s destructive corporate worldviews with environmental justice struggles in the United States, China and Europe. She argues that amid intensifying public pressures, a profound planetary industrial transformation is underway that is challenging the reigning age of plastics and fossil fuels.

Rivers On Fire And Corporate Liars: The Monitoring and Sanctioning of U.S. Water Pollution Crimes By Joshua Ozymy and Melissa Jarrell Ozymy Rutgers University Press How has the United States government prosecuted environment crimes over four decades? Have the prosecutions actually deterred crime? This analysis provides a comprehensive empirical examination of how the criminal enforcement of water pollution has evolved over time and how criminals were sanctioned.

Inescapable: Facing Up to Forever Chemicals By Marina Schauffler John Hopkins University Press Invisible and nearly indestructible, per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) have seeped into everyone’s blood and permeated the natural world. Schauffler shows how individuals and communities have been affected and offers a roadmap for tackling this chemical Hydra.

Slow Burn: The Hidden Costs of a Warming World By R Jisung Park Princeton University Press Drawing on a wealth of new data and cutting-edge economics, Park shows how climate change headlines often miss some of the most important costs. By investigating how climate change interacts with social and economic institutions, he shows how climate change already affects everyone and may act as an amplifier of inequality.

[Reprinted from Climate and Capitalism. Inclusion of a book does not imply endorsement.]

author: anred
title: La carta que la maestra Nancy Godoy escribió dos meses antes de que la mataran y el Estado no atendió
content:
La docente Nancy Godoy denunció por escrito el abandono de la Escuela 626 de Corrientes, donde faltaban condiciones básicas para enseñar y el director titular no asistía desde hacía años, según los testimonios que reunió. Dos meses después, Nancy fue asesinada. ¿Por qué nadie fue a corroborar y hacer algo con lo que estaba pasando? Y ¿cómo pudo funcionar una escuela pública en medio de una estancia privada, con un acceso tan difícil que la maestra debía recorrer kilómetros a caballo para llegar?Las preguntas inevitables: si el Concejo de Educación de Corrientes recibió una carta que describía semejante nivel de abandono, ¿por qué no hizo algo para verificar las condiciones de la escuela y ponerla en condiciones? ¿Se podría haber evitado el femicidio de Nancy Godoy?. Por Manuela Wilhelm (ANRed)


La carta tiene fecha del 15 de agosto de 2026. Nancy Ester Godoy, de 52 años, acababa de asumir como directora suplente de la Escuela Primaria Común N.º 626, ubicada en el paraje El Malezal, en la zona rural de Esquina, Corrientes. Lo que dejó asentado de su puño y letra no era un reclamo menor: describió un

establecimiento escolar totalmente abandonado

, sin agua, con baños inutilizables, techos deteriorados y rastros de roedores y murciélagos. También dejó constancia de que el docente titular llevaba años sin asistir regularmente a dar clases.


El documento, firmado por la docente y acompañado por las firmas de padres y vecinos, expuso una situación que requería una intervención urgente. Sin embargo, la muerte de Nancy abre una pregunta que va más allá del femicidio: ¿Qué respuesta del Estado recibió esa denuncia y qué medidas concretas se tomaron entre la presentación de la carta y el crimen?


Una escuela abandonada, sin agua y con murciélagos en el techo


Nancy describió con precisión lo que encontró al llegar a la institución, que tenía una matrícula de ocho alumnos. El edificio estaba sucio, deteriorado y, según su relato, llevaba tanto tiempo sin actividad regular que necesitó dos días de limpieza para dejarlo en condiciones mínimas de uso.


«La parte edilicia totalmente abandonada», escribió al comienzo del documento. Los baños: llenos de tierra. Las paredes del frente: rajaduras. El techo: a punto de caerse. Los ventanales estaban rotos y la humedad había deteriorado el interior del edificio. Desde el techo caían tierra y suciedad acumulada por la presencia de

ratas y murciélagos, cuyo olor, señaló, hacía insoportable permanecer en el lugar

.


Como maestra rural, Nancy cubría el cargo de directora suplente pero abarcaba una multiplicidad de tareas: docente, portera y cocinera. La falta de agua agravaba las condiciones al punto de que para limpiar la caca de los pisos, Nancy tuvo que conseguir de un vecino o de una laguna. 


Los pupitres estaban cubiertos de mugre, numerosos libros se habían mojado y no había muebles adecuados para guardarlos. Ni siquiera el lugar donde se colocaba la bandera estaba en condiciones: el mástil había sido reemplazado por un hierro alto y la tela estaba tan sucia que no se distinguían sus colores.


La docente también advirtió que no había registros ni documentación correspondiente a 2024, 2025 o 2026. Solo encontró libros antiguos.


La situación era tan precaria que Nancy no pudo quedarse a dormir en la escuela

. En la misma carta dejó constancia de que

tuvo que alojarse durante tres noches consecutivas en la casa de


María Rosa Leguizamón

, una mujer que luego quedó involucrada en la investigación por el crimen.


No se trataba solamente de las condiciones en las que debía trabajar una docente. Ocho alumnos dependían de una institución pública que, de acuerdo con lo que ella documentó, no reunía las condiciones básicas para garantizar la educación.


 Las advertencias que quedaron bajo la responsabilidad del sistema educativo


En su presentación, Nancy también dejó asentado que los padres y vecinos le habían manifestado que el docente a cargo llevaba entre dos y tres años sin concurrir a dar clases con regularidad. Según consignó, cuando recibió las llaves, le dijeron que hacía un mes que no iba.


La denuncia contra el director titular y el reclamo por la falta de supervisión escolar aparecen entre los antecedentes que se investigan en el caso.


La docente había asumido un cargo interino mientras el director titular se encontraba de licencia. Sus denuncias apuntaban a un problema institucional que, por su naturaleza, debía ser revisado por las autoridades educativas …

author: Kari Thompson
title: The First-Ever California State Workers’ Strike
content:
State workers went on a one-day unfair labor practice strike across California October 21, with picket lines in Sacramento, San Francisco, Los Angeles, and other cities. They're demanding better pay, affordable health care coverage, and flexibility to work from home.


This was the first strike in the history of SEIU Local 1000, which represents about 100,000 government employees, ranging from accountants to custodians to nurses at state offices, hospitals, and prisons.


They have been working without a contract since July 1. Some 5,000 employees were

excluded

 from striking.


Governor Gavin Newsom’s “return-to-office” mandate went into effect this past summer. It requires workers to be in the office four days per week—even though workers report there isn’t enough space for all of them.


Workers argue the return-to-work policy compounds the lack of pay increases. Being forced back into the office is “more than just a pay cut,” said Jonah Paul, who works for the Employment Development Department in Sacramento. ”It’s a huge reduction in quality of life.


“Telework is a stopgap for a lot of problems our society is not willing to address,” Paul said: “the cost of childcare, and insane commutes. Telework becomes a catch-all solution for a grueling life.”


ZERO RAISE


Last year, Local 1000 agreed to a pay freeze to help the state meet a budget shortfall. This summer, however, workers were supposed to see raises. But they got zilch.


The union is asking for a 20 percent raise over three years to catch up, especially given increased state revenue over the past two years.


Though Local 1000 and the state have met several times to negotiate a new contract, the union says CalHR, the bargaining representative for the state, has not been negotiating in good faith. It filed unfair labor practice charges with the state Public Employment Relations Board against CalHR for delaying negotiations and failing to respond to proposals.


“When I first started working for the state 10 years ago, for the most part CalHR would throw us a bone,” said steward Giovanni Martinez, a state worker in Sacramento. “This is the worst bargaining cycle I’ve witnessed. They don’t want to budge on a lot of stuff. Newsom takes us for granted, and the people he’s appointed in CalHR are the same way.”


Under previous leadership, the union

kicked in $1 million

 to help Newsom fight a recall campaign in 2021. Members question why a governor they supported doesn’t have their backs now.


STRIKE SCHOOLS


Members of Local 1000 have been organizing over the past few months to increase membership numbers. Activists have been approaching nonmembers at their own worksites to ask them personally to join the union, and calling others on the phone.


Stewards did their best to increase communications across the membership, though they were hampered by limited updates from the official Bargaining Unit Negotiating Committee.


Paul said that three years ago, the local offered “strike schools” to members, but these were more about discouraging members from planning for a strike. This time, he said, strike schools emphasized that the decision to strike was one for members to make, building membership numbers along with enthusiasm for walking out together.


In a strike authorization vote held from September 9 to October 7, 96 percent voted “yes” to walk out.


On the final day of the vote, the union held informational pickets to encourage participation in the vote. One picket happened to be next door to a building where Newsom was giving a speech.


With just a half-hour’s notice, stewards and other union leaders managed to get members together to cover every entrance of the building and make enough noise that Newsom had to comment on it during his event.


Despite this pressure from members, there was no last-minute deal to avert the strike, as happened 10 years ago under Governor Jerry Brown.


“For a lot of folks this is their first strike—this is mine,” Martinez said. ”We didn’t want to walk off the job—we have a good relationship with our supervisors—but we had no choice.”


WORLD’S FOURTH-LARGEST ECONOMY


Strike participation appeared strong, with thousands of workers joining rallies and marches in cities across the state. Striking workers in the state’s capitol shut down multiple blocks with a march from CalHR headquarters to the capitol building.


“I was up on the truck with our president and a few other folks, leading people to different rally …

author: Ellen Ormesher
title: Interactive Archive Shares Secrets of Shell’s Early Climate Research
content:
Campaigners backing attempts to sue Shell over a typhoon in the Philippines have launched an online archive showing that the British oil major knew that burning fossil fuels could harm the climate as early as the 1960s.

ExposeShell.com features documents including a 1966 memo Shell commissioned from British scientist James Lovelock and the ‘Greenhouse Effect’, a confidential 1988 report predicting that human-caused warming could trigger “dramatic” changes in sea level, ocean currents, weather and precipitation — “larger than any that have occurred over the last 12,000 years.” [Read these and other documents in the DeSmog series #ShellKnew]

The interactive site went live as Shell announced the latest figures showing that oil majors are enjoying bumper profits as the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran pushes oil prices higher. Shell said its adjusted third-quarter earnings had doubled to £10.8 billion in comparison to the same period last year.

“We don’t need any more reports to us that this big oily industry has been creating disaster,” Robin Wells, director of Fossil Free London, one of the groups behind the website, said in a statement. “Shell researched the reality but tore up the truth and locked it in the dark. Now, we are all facing the disastrous consequences.”

Fossil Free London protesters took to the streets outside Shell’s head office in London on Thursday, dressed in 1960s-style suits and holding banners that read “Shell Knew.”

ExposeShell.com is also backed by The Odette Case, a campaign group supporting more than 100 survivors of Typhoon Rai — known in the Philippines as Typhoon Odette — who began seeking damages from Shell last December in a first-of-its-kind case in the UK courts.

The typhoon tore through the Philippines in December, 2021, killing 400 people, injuring more than 1,000, and forcing almost 3.2 million people from their homes.

The survivors argue that Shell should be held liable for its historic contribution to the greenhouse gas emissions fuelling extreme weather events and its support for climate science denial via its past membership of industry groups such as the Global Climate Coalition — despite its early knowledge of the risks posed by burning its products.

Filed by UK law firm Hausfeld, the case draws on recent advances in attribution science that enable scientists to assess the degree to which climate change has contributed to an extreme weather event. Through Shell’s contribution of more than 2.5 percent of historical global greenhouse gas emissions, the suit alleges that Shell contributed to both the likelihood and severity of Typhoon Rai. It is the first civil claim to link the climate impacts of an oil and gas company’s activities with death, personal injury, and damage to property that has already occurred in the Global South.

Shell has dismissed the lawsuit as “baseless” and said that it had no “unique knowledge about climate change.”

(This story was updated at 12:44 GMT on October 29, 2026 to include Shell’s third-quarter earnings)

author: Amanda Audi
title: Críticas do público fazem imprensa dar nome a golpismo de Bolsonaro, aponta Fabiana Moraes
content:
Assim que foi divulgada a carta golpista na qual o candidato derrotado Flávio Bolsonaro se autoproclamou “presidente” do Brasil,

muitos jornais brasileiros divulgaram a fala como se fosse mais uma notícia, em tom declaratório, sem evidenciar seu teor golpista.


“Em carta divulgada por aliados, Flávio Bolsonaro se diz presidente eleito do Brasil após chegar aos EUA fugido”, noticiou a Folha de S.Paulo. “Nos EUA, Flávio se autodeclara ‘verdadeiro presidente eleito’ e agradece a Trump e a Milei”, manchetou o Estadão. Outros veículos também fizeram títulos similares.


Depois de alguns minutos no ar, a maioria dos portais corrigiu o tom. “Flávio Bolsonaro se diz presidente eleito do Brasil em carta golpista divulgada por aliados”

, reformulou a Folha. O Estadão também mudou: “Após fuga, Flávio se autodeclara ‘presidente eleito em carta golpista e agradece a Trump e a Milei”. Mais tarde, o próprio candidato derrotado postou uma nova carta, na qual se chama “líder do Brasil”.


Duas versões da mesma “carta” golpista apresentada por Flávio Bolsonaro no dia de hoje


A

Agência Pública

 conversou com Fabiana Moraes, professora e pesquisadora do Núcleo de Design e Comunicação da Universidade Federal de Pernambuco (UFPE), para quem a mudança de postura dos grandes veículos nesta ocasião pode ter sido fruto de um maior “letramento midiático” do público depois das últimas eleições, que atua de forma mais crítica ao trabalho da imprensa.


Jornalismo investigativo é antídoto contra a desinformação. Ajude a garantir informação acessível e gratuita para mais pessoas. Faça um Pix para

contato@apublica.org

 ou doe em

apoie.apublica.org

.


A professora, que pesquisa a objetividade jornalística — isto é, a crença de que o jornalismo consegue ser isento de ideologias e vieses — relembra como a mídia foi alvo de muitas críticas nesta cobertura eleitoral. “Flávio almoçar com a Globo antes da entrevista no Jornal Nacional foi um escândalo”, disse, sobre a

reunião

 do ex-senador com executivos da emissora no dia em que seria sabatinado. “Acho que essas eleições ensinaram para uma população maior algumas questões que geralmente ficariam meio uma conversa entre jornalistas.”


A pesquisadora aponta que parte dos veículos que, em um primeiro momento, normalizaram o discurso golpista “queriam Flávio presidente, ou sempre tiveram uma enorme antipatia por Lula”.

 “Eu não diria que há uma nova postura [deles], mas uma correção nesse caso específico porque rapidamente as pessoas questionaram as manchetes.”


A pesquisadora relembra que ficou evidente que os

algoritmos

 das redes sociais não são puramente técnicos e, por isso, podem ser questionados. Do mesmo modo, o jornalismo também não é puramente técnico, no entendimento de Moraes. “Acho que há uma questão de mostrar para onde a imprensa estava indo”, aponta, citando como exemplo as relações da imprensa com o ex-banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro, que atuava quase como um ‘editor-chefe’ de algumas redações. A

Pública


mostrou

 a interferência editorial de Vorcaro no alto escalão do grupo Globo.


Moraes também aponta que, nessas eleições, ficou mais claro o peso do jornalismo independente, além do peso de estratégias diferentes da cobertura tradicional, como o uso de humor, ficção e de influenciadores digitais.


Um dos livros de Moraes é “A pauta é uma arma de combate”, em que trata sobre como os jornalistas definem o que vai ser ou não notícia, muitas vezes reproduzindo preconceitos e hierarquias de gênero, classe social e raça.


Moraes acredita que essa eleição será importante para “riscar o chão com a faca” para pactuar novas posturas.

 “Por exemplo, que precisamos promover de fato o jornalismo independente e financiá-lo. Porque é isso: Lula se torna presidente em uma eleição mais do que histórica, e, no dia seguinte, os jornais estão falando sobre a Bolsa de Valores – algo que sempre acontece –, mas minimizam o tamanho dessa vitória. Quando você olha para a imprensa internacional no dia seguinte, a cobertura e o peso que se dá a essa vitória do Lula são bem diferentes”, afirma.


“A imprensa vai continuar seguindo suas apostas, como a Globo com Flávio – apostas mesmo, né? Mas acho que há uma coisa boa, que é o reconhecimento do jornalismo que olha para a democracia não como negócio, mas como um ambiente necessário para respirar.”

title: Ephéméride des luttes : 29 octobre
content:
Le 29 octobre de l'éphéméride des luttes résonne des noms de Luca, Leon, Sergio, Rocco et de toutes celles et ceux qui ont lutté dans le passé, pour que la mémoire de leurs luttes ne soient pas ensevelies sous la poussière du présent.


1390 :

 Premier procès en sorcellerie à Paris, lors duquel Jeanne de Brigue est condamnée au bûcher.


1901 :

 Aux USA, l'anarchiste Leon Czolgosz est exécuté sur la chaise électrique pour avoir assassiné le président des Etats-Unis William McKinley le

6 septembre

.


1916 :

 A Montevideo en Uruguay, parution du premier numéro de '

El Hombre

', hebdomadaire anarchiste de combat.


1947 :

 A Milan, la Volante Rossa attaque un siège du nouveau parti fasciste, le MSI, reconstitué un an à peine après la 'chute' du fascisme.


1952 :

 La conférence de presse de Charlie Chaplin est perturbée par l'Internationale Lettriste.


1964 :

 En Bolivie, c'est le premier des trois jours de grève générale décrétés par la Centrale Ouvrière Bolivienne. L'armée mènera une répression féroce et sanglante et finit par renverser le président et à s'emparer du pouvoir.


1972 :

 Des militants du groupe palestinien Septembre Noir détournent un avion de ligne ouest-allemand et obtienne la libération de trois autres de leurs militants.


1974 :

 A Florence, au cours du braquage d'une banque, deux militants des Nuclei Armati Proletari (NAP), Luca Mantini et Sergio Romeo, sont tués après un échange de coups de feu avec la police, et deux autres (Pasquale Abatangelo et Pietro Sofia) sont arrêtés après avoir été blessés au cours de la fusillade.


1975 :

 A Rome, le groupe 'Lutte Armée pour le Communisme' tire plusieurs coups de feu sur un rassemblement fasciste, tuant l'un d'entre eux.


1977 :

 - A Cagliari en Sardaigne, des molotov sont lancés sur un répétiteur téléphonique.


 A Turin, le jeune militant autonome Rocco Sardone meurt dans l'explosion de la bombe qu'il s'apprêtait à déposer contre un concessionnaire Audi.

 En France, les prisonniers des NAPAP (Noyaux Armés Pour l'Autonomie Populaire) mettent fin à leur grève de la faim.


1980 :

 A Caluire-et-Cuire, le groupe révolutionnaire 'L'Affiche Rouge' attaque un convoi de fonds d'une agence BNP.


1981 :

 Mort de Georges Brassens.


2004 :

 A Athènes, Lutte Révolutionnaire fait sauter deux fourgons pénitentiaires qui devaient aller garder la prison de Korydallos.


2012 :

 Sur la ZAD de Notre-Dame-des-Landes, on est en pleine opération 'César' : grande journée d'affrontements contre la police autour de la Saulce.


2014 :

 A Mesolongi en Grèce, un groupe de personnes détruit de nombreux véhicules de police devant un commissariat suite à l'agression de deux anarchistes par la police un peu plus tôt.


2016 :

 - A

Marseille

, une manifestation de 300 personnes

investit un bâtiment vide

 de la rue Briffaut pour y créer un centre social.


 A Cukurca en Turquie, le PKK kurde a attaqué une base de l'armée turque au mortier, tuant trois soldats et en blessant cinq autres.

 A Oullins, en banlieue lyonnaise, un cocktail molotov est lancé sur le commissariat de police depuis une voiture en mouvement.

 du 29 octobre.

author: Sara Connors
title: Yukon photographer captures caribou’s extraordinary fight for survival
content:
It’s an incredible act of nature.


Two caribou. Their antlers locked in battle. One dead. The survivor, nearly immobilized by the weight of his opponent, preyed upon by a bear as foxes and birds scavenge the dead bull’s remains.


Yukon

 photographer

Peter Mather

 captured the remarkable images earlier this month while filming the Southern Lakes caribou’s rut, when up to a few hundred animals gather and males spar for females.


“I have never seen anything like that before,” Mather said. “Their horns are locked together, and one of them is dead. And the bear is like sitting 10 feet away, just watching, trying to figure out what to do. It was the strangest situation.”


Mather came across the rare sighting about 20 kilometres south of Whitehorse while filming content for the Kwanlin Dün First Nation as part of a project for the Southern Lakes Caribou Steering Committee. Kwanlin Dün is one of six First Nations governments represented on the committee.


With fewer than 1,000 animals in the early 1990s, the Southern Lakes caribou, which is composed of four woodland herds, has increased to about 4,000 today, thanks in part to voluntary harvest moratoriums by First Nations.


Yukon photographer Peter Mather. Photo: Jordan Haslbeck/APTN.


A rare encounter


Mather said he first became aware of the caribou after he and a friend helping him gather footage encountered an aggressive grizzly, something he said is not common around Whitehorse.


He said days later they saw another bear in the same spot, along with several ravens and eagles. Assuming a dead animal was nearby, he flew a drone to investigate.


He said he was shocked to see the two bulls locked together.


“Then you’d see the bear go in to try to get this big caribou, and the caribou would stand up, and the bear would go away scared, which is surprising because you would think a bear isn’t afraid of a bull caribou. But those bull caribou are so big they can take on a bear,” he said.


Mather figures the surviving caribou spent about a week weighed down in one spot while fending off bears and other predators.


After leaving the caribou some lichen, Mather said he appeared to gain back some strength.


He said scavengers and what he believes was a pack of wolves further helped free the animal by removing most of the dead caribou’s carcass, leaving just the head attached.


Mather said he and his friend resolved to remove what was left of the dead caribou with a hacksaw, but by that point the caribou was able to get up and leave.


“Last we saw, he was heading off in the mountains with two heads,” he said.


‘These herds are really special’


Lars Jessop, the steering committee’s project manager, said males are exhausted during the rut, leaving them vulnerable to predation.


He said while it can be a dangerous time for bulls, it’s rare for them to be unable to separate.


He said he’s only seen bulls locked together once before while both were alive, and that a colleague had previously found the skeletons of two locked bulls.


He said that makes the situation all the more remarkable as one bull died and the other survived.


“He would have been extremely vulnerable because he couldn’t move and somehow avoided predation until he managed to get away,” he said.


Lars Jessop, the project manager for the Southern Lakes Caribou Steering Committee. Photo: Jordan Haslbeck/APTN.


Despite the burden of an extra head, Jessop said the caribou has a good shot at survival. That’s because adult males typically shed their antlers after the rut.


“If he can make it another month or so, those antlers will drop. He’ll drop his antlers, and then he will have a good chance,” he said.


He noted that Mather’s images of the entangled caribou, as well as the herds themselves, have helped share the beauty of the

southern lakes caribou

 while also educating the public.


“These herds are really special,” he said.


For Mather, the surviving caribou is a reminder of what can happen when nature is allowed to thrive.


“I think he’s kind of the symbol of that recovery because that resilience that he’s got is indicative of what the herd has and how they’re growing again. They still need more work, but they’re coming back.”
